findings.title: Status parser takes the first Status: line, which can come from the verbatim operator quote
findings.body: The prompt tells the extractor to put the operator's last message verbatim under `## Last request`, with the real `Status:` line after it. The awk takes the first line matching `^Status:` and exits. If the operator's message contains its own `Status: Answered` line (for example a pasted status report), that line comes before the extractor's line and is shown to the operator as the handoff status. A pasted line starting with `## ` has the opposite effect: the awk exits before reaching the real Status, and the status is silently dropped. The injector therefore cannot always tell the extractor's verdict from quoted operator text, which conflicts with the goal that status parsing be reliable.
findings.fix: Keep the last `Status:` line in the section instead of exiting on the first. The extractor writes its Status after the quote, so the last match is the right one.

findings.title: Negative status tests do not go red if the section-boundary exit is removed
findings.body: The new cases in 2834 are meant to show that a Status: line from another section is ignored. Case 1 has no `## Last request` section, so `in_last_request` is never set and the boundary rule `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` is never exercised. Case 2 has the Status inside Last request with an unrecognized value. Test 50901 has a Last request section with a Status, followed by a Key Details section with no Status line. If the exit rule is deleted, every one of these still passes. A regression that leaks `Status:` from a later section (Key Details or Warnings) into the systemMessage would not be caught. This is the exact failure the goal says the tests must catch. The missing fixture is a Last request section with no Status line, followed by `## Key Details` containing `Status: Not answered`, expected to give goal-only output.
findings.fix: Add a fixture with `## Last request` and a quote but no Status line, then `## Key Details\nStatus: Answered`. Assert the systemMessage is goal-only.

findings.title: Status parser can read a Status: line from inside the verbatim operator quote
findings.body: The prompt (pre-compact.sh:319-321) asks the extractor to quote the operator's last message verbatim at the top of `## Last request` and to put its own `Status:` line after the quote. The message is bounded at 4000 chars and its JSON literal is decoded back into multi-line text. The session-start awk (session-start.sh:81-90) keeps the first `^Status:` line in the section and exits, and it also exits at the first `^## ` line. Two cases follow. A quoted line beginning `Status: Answered`/`Partially answered`/`Not answered` passes the allow-list and replaces the extractor's real status in the operator-facing systemMessage. A quoted markdown heading (`## ...`), common in pasted issue bodies or reports, ends the section scan early and silently drops the status. This only happens when the extractor copies those lines without a `> ` prefix, but the template's own layout shows the quote unprefixed. additionalContext is unaffected. No test puts a Status: line or a heading inside the quote ahead of the real Status line.
findings.fix: In the prompt template, put the `Status:` line directly after the `## Last request` heading, before the quote. Optionally also require the quote to be blockquoted (`> `), so a quoted `Status:` or `## ` line cannot match. The awk can stay as it is (first match wins) once Status comes first.

findings.title: No test pins the section boundary of the Status parser; deleting the heading exit stays green
findings.body: The awk in handoff-session-start.sh scopes the status to `## Last request` with two rules: the section-start rule and `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }`. The goal requires that a Status: line from another section is never picked up. The new tests cover only these cases. 50901 has a Status inside Last request and none in the following Key Details. The first 2834 negative has a Status in Key Details but no `## Last request` section. The second 2834 negative has an unrecognized value inside the section. None has a `## Last request` section without its own Status line, followed by a later heading that contains `Status: Not answered`. If the `/^## /` exit rule is deleted, every new test still passes. Only the missing-section guard is exercised, and that fails differently. A real handoff in that shape, for example a Last request section that omits the Status line and a Key Details line that says `Status: Not answered`, would then show the wrong status to the operator. The test-oracle gate (CLAUDE.md, semantic-regression-tests-over-source-shape) requires the test to go red when the behavior is removed.
findings.fix:
Add a 2834 case with `## Last request
Please continue.

## Key Details
Status: Not answered`. Assert the systemMessage has no Status line.

findings.title: Парсер принимает строку из цитаты запроса за его статус
findings.body: Контракт в executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh:319,337–338 требует дословно копировать декодированный запрос, включая переносы строк. Если оператор спрашивает «Explain this output:\nStatus: Answered\nWhy?», эта строка появляется внутри Last request перед настоящим `Status: Not answered`. Парсер выбирает первое совпадение и показывает оператору `Answered`, хотя запрос остался без ответа. Ошибка введена этим изменением: формат производителя не отделяет произвольную цитату от служебного поля потребителя.
findings.fix: Разместить служебный Status сразу после заголовка Last request, перед цитатой, и читать статус только из этой позиции.

findings.title: Status-parser tests do not cover the section-boundary exit, the exact cross-section leak the goal names
findings.body: The awk in handoff-session-start.sh stops at the next `## ` heading (`in_last_request && /^## / { exit }`). That line is the only thing keeping a `Status:` in a later section from being read when `## Last request` has no Status line of its own. The new negative cases do not exercise it. Case 1 has no `## Last request` heading at all, so it only proves the `in_last_request` guard. Case 2 has a Status line inside the section, with an unrecognized value, so it only proves the `case` filter. Delete the `/^## / { exit }` line and every test stays green. A handoff with `## Last request` holding a quote and no Status, followed by `## Key Details` containing `Status: Answered`, would then show a false status to the operator. Fix: add a fixture with a Last request section that has no Status line and a following section that has `Status: Answered`, and assert the goal-only systemMessage.
findings.fix:
In test_scripts_2834, stage a handoff with `## Last request
Please continue.

## Key Details
Status: Answered` and assert the systemMessage has no Status line.

findings.title: Prompt-contract assertions pass without the new prompt text
findings.body: `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` is satisfied by the transcript facts block, which always prints `Last user request: ...`. It says nothing about the new Last request instruction, which refers to "the facts block above". `<claim>, verify with: <exact command>` appears in two places in the prompt (Relevant Context and Key Details), so removing either instruction leaves the assertion green. 'Status:' is similarly loose. Only `## Last request`, the three status values and the 3-7 removal are real tripwires.
findings.fix: Drop the `Last user request` assertion. Assert the phrase twice, or per section, if both placements matter.

findings.title: Отрицательная фикстура не проверяет выход из Last request
findings.body: Новая фикстура содержит Status в Key Details, но не содержит предшествующего раздела Last request. Если удалить условие выхода из раздела в executable_handoff-session-start.sh:83, все добавленные проверки останутся зелёными. При этом handoff с Last request без статуса и последующим Key Details со строкой Status: Not answered покажет оператору статус из чужого раздела.
findings.fix: Добавить в эту фикстуру раздел Last request без Status перед Key Details. Сохранить положительный контроль из теста 50901.

findings.title: Prompt-contract assertions pass even when the new prompt text is removed
findings.body: The `<claim>, verify with: <exact command>` instruction is required in both Relevant Context (pre-compact line 316) and Key Details (line 325). Test 50900 checks the whole prompt with `assert_file_contains`, so deleting either copy leaves the test green because the other copy still matches. `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` can never fail: the transcript facts block always prints `Last user request: ...` (lines 113–265), and the new Last request instruction doesn't use that phrase at all. The `'Status:'` assertion is fine, since `Status:` appears only on the new line 320, and so are the heading, the three status values, 'what to check first' and the 3-7 removal check.
findings.fix: In test 50900, check the `<claim>, verify with:` instruction inside each section separately, for example by matching the line together with its neighboring section text or by counting two occurrences. Replace the `Last user request` assertion with one on the new instruction text, `Quote the operator's last real message verbatim`.

findings.title: Status parser takes the first `Status:` line in the Last request section, which can be inside the verbatim operator quote
findings.body: The prompt tells the extractor to put the operator's last message verbatim at the top of `## Last request`, before the model's own `Status:` line. The awk takes the first line matching `^Status:` and then exits. The quote comes from the transcript and can run to 4000 chars across many lines (`bounded_text`). If the operator's message has a line that starts with `Status: Answered`, the awk reads that line instead of the extractor's real status. This happens with pasted logs, a status report, or a template. The injector then shows a recognized but wrong status in the operator-facing systemMessage. It looks authoritative and is not caught by the allow-list, because the quoted value is itself one of the three accepted values. The opposite case fails safe: a quoted line starting with `## ` ends the section early and the status is dropped. The new negative tests cover a `Status:` in another section and an unrecognized value. None puts a recognized `Status:` line inside the quote ahead of the real one. I traced this by reading the awk and did not execute it against such an input, and it needs an operator message with a line-leading `Status:`. It only affects the display, and `additionalContext` is unchanged.
findings.fix: Take the last `Status:` line in the section instead of the first: drop the `exit` after `print` and keep the last value. The prompt places the model's Status after the quote, so the last match is the model's own line.

findings.title: Парсер принимает Status из дословной цитаты запроса за служебный статус
findings.body: Новый шаблон требует вставить декодированный запрос дословно перед служебной строкой Status. Если оператор написал «Проверь этот пример:\nStatus: Answered», допустимый handoff содержит эту строку перед фактическим «Status: Not answered». Парсер печатает первое совпадение и завершает работу, поэтому systemMessage показывает Answered для неотвеченного запроса. Аналогично строка «## …» внутри цитаты завершает поиск раньше служебного статуса. Это внесённая изменением неоднозначность формата; additionalContext сохраняется, но отображаемый оператору статус неверен или отсутствует.
findings.fix: Поместить служебный Status сразу после заголовка Last request, перед дословной цитатой, и читать статус только из этой позиции.

findings.title: No test turns red if the status parser stops at the end of the Last request section
findings.body: The goal says status parsing must not pick up a `Status:` line from another section. The session-start awk enforces that two ways: `in_last_request` is only set after `## Last request` (executable_handoff-session-start.sh:82), and `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` ends the scan at the next heading (line 83). The tests cover only the first. In the 2834 negative case, `Status: Not answered` sits in Key Details and there is no Last request section. In the other 2834 case, the Last request section has an unrecognized value. In 50901, the Status line comes before Key Details. If the line-83 exit is deleted, all three still pass. The case that would catch it is a handoff with `## Last request` and no `Status:` line, followed by `## Key Details` containing `Status: Answered`. A model that omits the Status line is a realistic output. With the exit gone, the operator would see a status that did not come from the Last request section. This is a gap in the new tests rather than a bug in the code.
findings.fix: Add a case to test 2834 with `## Last request` that has a quote but no `Status:` line, followed by `## Key Details` with `Status: Answered`. Assert that the systemMessage is the goal alone.

findings.title: No test goes red if the Status parser's section-boundary exit is deleted
findings.body: The awk in handoff-session-start.sh keeps the status scoped to `## Last request` with two rules: `in_last_request` is set only after that heading, and `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` ends the scan at the next heading. The new tests exercise only the first rule. The first negative case in test 2834 has a Status in Key Details but no `## Last request` section. The second has an unrecognized value inside the section. Test 50901 has a Status inside Last request and none in the following Key Details. If the `/^## /` exit line is deleted, every one of these still passes. A realistic handoff where the extractor leaves out the Status line in Last request, followed by `## Key Details` containing `Status: Answered` or `Not answered`, would then show the operator a status taken from another section. The goal names exactly this cross-section leak, and the test-oracle gate requires the test to fail when the behavior is removed.
findings.fix: Add a case to test 2834: `## Last request` with a quote but no Status line, then `## Key Details` with `Status: Answered`. Assert the exact goal-only systemMessage, and keep 50901 as the positive control.

findings.title: Verbatim last-request quote can conflict with the existing 400-word cap
findings.body: The change makes `## Last request` (pre-compact.sh:318-321) carry a mandatory verbatim quote of the operator's last message. That message is bounded only at 4000 chars by `bounded_text` (line 141), roughly 600+ words. `Maximum 400 words in the <handoff> section` (line 334) is still the only length rule, and it has no exception for the quote. When an operator message runs past a few hundred words (pasted reports or issue bodies), the extractor must break either the cap or the verbatim rule (line 337), and the prompt does not say which wins. Nothing in the hook enforces the word cap. So the visible failure is the extractor trimming or paraphrasing the quote, which defeats the purpose of the new section; a longer handoff would be harmless.
findings.fix: Add one line to the Constraints saying the Last request quote is exempt from the 400-word limit, or that it should be cut at a stated length with an explicit marker.

findings.title: Last request section has no instruction for the 'Last user request: None' case
findings.body: Line 319 says 'Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above', and line 320 requires `Status:` to be exactly one of three values. The facts block can say `Last user request: None` (lines 245, 260-261, 265). The prompt gives no branch for that case: the extractor may invent a quote or write a Status for a request that does not exist. The sibling 'no goal' case does have an explicit branch, so a branch here would match the file's own habit. The injector also ignores any Status line it cannot recognize, so an invented value just silently drops the status display.
findings.fix: Add a line such as '[If the facts block says Last user request: None, write None and omit the Status line]'.

findings.title: Prompt template puts the verbatim quote above Status: with no separator
findings.body: The template places the verbatim operator quote directly above the extractor's `Status:` line, with no delimiter between them. The injector's awk takes the first `^Status:` line in the section and exits at the first `## ` line. So a quoted line that starts with `Status:` or `## ` either replaces the real status or hides it. This is the producer-side half of the parser ambiguity reported against handoff-session-start.sh.
findings.fix: Put the `Status:` line first in the section, or require the quote to be blockquoted (`> `) so that only the extractor's own line starts with `Status:`.

findings.title: Last-request copy rule is stated twice
findings.body: Line 337 already says: 'Copy file paths, commit hashes and subjects, and the last user request exactly from <transcript_facts>'. The new template line 319 restates the same rule ('verbatim from the facts block above'). The two use different wording (quote vs. decode and copy), and the JSON-literal decoding rule on line 338 attaches only to the Constraints copy. Keep one source of truth, so the Last request line points to the rule or the Constraint carries it alone.
findings.fix: Shorten line 319 to the section's purpose and leave the copy and decoding rules in the Constraints.

findings.title: Engine refusal to queue tests returns exit code 1 instead of 2
findings.body: With SOURCE_ROUTINES_ENABLED=false, the engine returns HTTP 400 with key source_tree_tests_not_queued and leaves the version untested. Here that refusal becomes a VerdictReadFailed, and the generic catch in runCode then returns 1. Under the intended contract, an engine refusal should return 2, so the calling agent can tell 'could not run tests' apart from 'tests failed'. This behavior also existed before the change, but the change's new exit-code contract is left only partly implemented.
findings.fix: Handle source_tree_tests_not_queued at enqueue time: keep the refusal message and return 2.

findings.title: Verdict polling uses a hand-rolled wait loop the project's Effect rules forbid
findings.body: When the version stays pending, waitForVersion re-reads by hand and calls Effect.sleep through waitForNextPoll. This is new code, and it contradicts .claude/skills/effect-best-practices/SKILL.md:21 and :34, which require Effect.repeat with Schedule.spaced for this kind of polling. The separate helper hides the sleep from the syntactic lint rule, but the loop still manages its interval and stop condition by hand instead of using the agreed mechanism.
findings.fix: Replace the polling loop with Effect.repeat plus Schedule.spaced and an exit condition. Keep the shared deadline and the HTTP request cancellation.

findings.title: Timeout follow-up inserts workspace names without shell quoting
findings.body: Introduced by this change. Workspace selection accepts names containing spaces through workspaceMatches. If `code test --workspace 'Acme Europe'` times out, the suggested command contains `--workspace Acme Europe`. Running that command sets the workspace to `Acme`; `Europe` becomes an ignored positional argument. The suggested recovery therefore fails to read the original workspace's verdict.
findings.fix: Shell-quote workspace and session values when constructing the follow-up command.

findings.title: `code test --timeout N` with N ≤ 5 never reads the verdict
findings.body: `waitForVersion` sleeps `min(5000, remaining)` before each read, then breaks if the clock has reached the deadline. `code test` has no read of its own, because it uses the queue response. With `--timeout 5` (or anything lower) it sleeps to the deadline, breaks, and prints `still pending after N s` without calling `list-source-tree-versions` once. The same applies at the default 90 s. The last read is at 85 s, and the final 5 s of the budget are slept and never read. A verdict that landed in that window is reported as pending (exit 2). Fix: do one last bounded read when the sleep reaches the deadline, or poll before sleeping.
findings.fix: After the sleep, do not `break` on `now >= deadline`. Run a final read (it is already bounded by `readUntilDeadline`) before falling through to the pending message.

findings.title: Any 401/403 on the verdict read is reported as "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet"
findings.body: `isVerdictReadRefusal` treats every 401 or 403 as an old engine refusing the read, including the persistent-401 `rejectedCredentialError` ("Membrane rejected the stored credential. Sign in again"), which carries a 401 cause. It also matches a genuine permission denial. In those cases the command prints `pending — this engine cannot answer the verdict yet` and returns exit 2, the same code as "still pending, keep waiting". The agent is told to wait or retry when the real fix is to sign in again or fix access. The queue call succeeded with the same credential moments earlier, so the actionable message is lost. Goal item 4 only covers an old engine. The sign-in-expired check also matches on message text, which is brittle.
findings.fix: Keep the degrade-to-2 path for the old-engine refusal only. For a rejected-credential error, surface its message and return 1.

findings.title: `code test --json` output shape changed from `{version}` to the bare version object
findings.body: Before this change, `code test --json` printed the whole command result, `{ "version": {...} }`. Now `renderTestVersion` prints the bare version row, and the old-engine refusal path also writes it to stdout with the message on stderr. Any script that reads `.version.testsStatus` from this output breaks silently. The README, MANUAL and help text don't mention the change. If it is intended, document it. Otherwise print `{ version }`.
findings.fix: Print `{ version }` in JSON mode, or state the new shape in the plugin docs.

findings.title: Redundant Effect plumbing in the verdict read helpers
findings.body: `readUntilDeadline` ends with `.pipe(Effect.catchTag('VerdictReadFailed', (error) => Effect.fail(error))) as Effect.Effect<T, VerdictReadError>`. The catch re-fails with the same error, so it does nothing, and the cast hides the real error type. The same `new VerdictReadFailed({ cause, message: ... })` mapper is written out three times: in `codeTest`, in `listVersion`'s no-deadline branch, and in `readUntilDeadline`. `outcome.error as VerdictReadError` is cast three more times, and `timeoutSeconds` is a one-line wrapper that assigns to a variable and returns it. A single `tryRead(promise)` helper, plus typing the error channel properly, would remove the duplicated mappers and the no-op catch. Behavior stays the same.
findings.fix: Extract one `tryRead` helper for the `tryPromise` mapping. Drop the no-op `catchTag` and the casts. Inline `timeoutSeconds`.

findings.title: isVerdictReadRefusal reports an expired or rejected sign-in, or any 403, as 'this engine cannot answer the verdict yet' (exit 2)
findings.body:
`isVerdictReadRefusal` is meant to recognise one case: an old engine refusing a sessionless `list-source-tree-versions` read. An old engine refuses with AccessDenied, which is a 403 scope mismatch. The predicate returns true for much more than that: any 401 or 403 anywhere in the cause chain, and any error whose message matches /sign-in expired/.

Credential failures therefore match:
- `platform-token.ts:72` throws 'The Membrane sign-in expired… Sign in again.' when the refresh grant fails. This happens before any request reaches the engine, and a network failure during the refresh produces the same message.
- `rejectedCredentialError` ('Membrane rejected the stored credential. Sign in again…') carries the 401 as its cause.
- On the attached path, a session-token mint that is refused, or a `SessionClosedError` wrapping a refusal, also matches.

Concrete case: the operator's sign-in has expired and an agent runs `membrane-operator code status --workspace acme` (with or without `--wait`). The CLI prints 'this engine cannot answer the verdict yet' and exits 2 instead of exiting 1 with the 'Sign in again' message. Exit 2 is reserved for 'still pending / engine refuses', so an agent that follows the exit-code contract keeps polling and never recovers. `code test` hits the same path if the credential expires during its wait. The tests parameterised over [401, 403] (cli.code.verdict.test.ts:377, :396, :475) pin this behaviour. The 401 cases pass only because the OAuth refresh hits an unrouted 500 and takes the regex path.
findings.fix: Treat only the engine's own refusal of the list read as unavailable: a 403, ideally the access-scope-mismatch key, on the `list-source-tree-versions` response. Drop the 401 and /sign-in expired/ branches, and stop walking causes produced by token acquisition, so credential and session errors keep their message and exit 1. Update the [401, 403] test tables to match.

findings.title: `code test --json` output changed from `{ version: {...} }` to the bare version object
findings.body: Before this change, `code test --json` printed the whole command output, `JSON.stringify(result)`, which is `{ "version": { ... } }`. It now prints `renderTestVersion(context, result.version, true)`, the bare version, and that includes `--no-wait`. A script or agent that reads `.version.testsStatus` from `code test --json` now gets `undefined`. The goal does not ask for this change and no doc mentions it. I found no in-repo consumer that parses this output, so the impact is limited.
findings.fix: Either keep the `{ version }` envelope for `code test --json` (and use the same shape for `code status --json`), or note the new shape in the CLI docs and help text.

findings.title: An expired sign-in or any 403 is reported as 'this engine cannot answer the verdict yet' with exit 2 (pending)
findings.body:
`isVerdictReadRefusal` decides whether a failed verdict read means "an old engine cannot answer". It returns true for any 401, any 403, any error whose message matches /sign-in expired/, and anything whose `cause` chain holds one of those.

An old engine refuses a sessionless `list-source-tree-versions` on the platform credential with `AccessDenied`, and `AccessDenied.status` is FORBIDDEN (`engine/api/src/platform/errors/refusals.ts:152`). So 403 is the only status the degrade path needs. On the attached path the session's workspace token can already read versions on any engine, so an old engine is never the reason a read fails there.

The 401 and sign-in-expired cases are credential failures. On the unattached path, `callWithPlatformToken` retries a 401 after a refresh. When the retry also fails it throws `rejectedCredentialError` ("Membrane rejected the stored credential. Sign in again…", whose cause is the 401). When the refresh itself fails, `platform-token.ts:72` throws "The Membrane sign-in expired… Sign in again." Both match the predicate.

Concrete case: the operator's sign-in has expired and an agent runs `membrane-operator code status --tree-version X` (with or without `--wait`). The first call is the list read, so the CLI prints `this engine cannot answer the verdict yet` and exits 2. The goal defines exit 2 as "still pending / engine refuses". The agent never sees the "Sign in again" remedy, and an agent following the exit-code contract will keep polling. Without this predicate the error would surface through `runCode`'s catch with exit 1 and the real message.

The same applies to a session token expiring during `code test`'s wait. It also applies to any other 403 on the read, such as a `SessionClosedError` whose cause is a refusal, or a seat that is denied access to the tree: each is reported as an old engine. The tests pin this behaviour deliberately (`cli.code.verdict.test.ts:377`, `:396` and `:475`, parameterized over [401, 403]). That makes it a design choice, but the 401 half does not match what an old engine actually answers.
findings.fix: Treat only the old-engine refusal as unavailable. Match a 403 (ideally the access-scope-mismatch key the old engine sends) and drop the 401 and /sign-in expired/ branches, so credential failures go through the normal error path with exit 1 and their own message. Update the [401, 403] test tables to match.

findings.title: `code test --json` output changed from `{ version: {...} }` to the bare version object
findings.body: Before this change, `code test --json` printed `JSON.stringify(result)`, the `run-source-tree-tests` output `{ version: {...} }`. Every path, `--no-wait` included, now goes through `renderTestVersion`, which prints `JSON.stringify(version)` and so drops the `version` wrapper. A script or agent that reads `.version.testsStatus` from `code test --json` now gets `undefined`. No doc, help line or changelog mentions the change, and the goal does not ask for it. No in-repo consumer of this output was found.
findings.fix: Keep the `{ version }` envelope for `code test --json`, for example `JSON.stringify({ version }, null, 2)`. Otherwise, document the new shape in the help text and the plugin README.

findings.title: An expired or rejected sign-in is reported as "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet"
findings.body: `isVerdictReadRefusal` treats every 401, and any error whose message matches `/sign-in expired/i`, as an old engine refusing the read. Take `code status` (without `--wait`) when the operator's platform token has lapsed and refresh fails. `callWithPlatformToken` throws 'The Membrane sign-in expired and could not be refreshed. Sign in again.' The verb swallows that, prints 'this engine cannot answer the verdict yet' and exits 2, which the goal reserves for 'still pending/engine refuses'. The agent is told to wait or upgrade rather than to sign in again, so retrying `code status` never recovers. The comment on line 299 makes this conflation deliberate, but it reaches past the goal's case (an *old engine* refusing the read). An old engine refuses a non-sessionless command with an access denial (403), so the 401 and sign-in-expired branches only catch credential failures.
findings.fix: Treat only 403 (or the engine's access-denied refusal) as 'engine cannot answer'. Let a 401 or rejected-credential error propagate, so its 'Sign in again' message and exit 1 reach the user.

findings.title: The operator skill doesn't document `code test`/`status` exit codes, the 90 s wait, or `--wait`/`--timeout`
findings.body: The goal defines the verbs' contract by exit code: `code test` returns 0 passed/skipped, 1 failed, 2 still pending or engine refuses; `code status` adds 3 for untested. The agent-facing SKILL.md/MANUAL.md and claude-plugin/README.md only say `test` 'queues the tree's tests once and waits for the verdict' and `status` 'reads a verdict'. Nothing tells an agent that `test` gives up after 90 s with exit 2, that `status` reads once unless given `--wait`, or what each exit code means. An agent that reads exit 2 as a failure, or runs `code status` without `--wait` while the run is pending, has nothing in the skill to correct it. Only a stderr hint on timeout points to `code status --wait`. Separately, the README's verb list ('round-trips through seven verbs', README.md:240-248) still leaves out `test` (an omission that predates this change) and now also `status`.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to the SKILL/MANUAL paragraph and the README listing the exit codes and the `--wait`/`--timeout` flags. Add `code test` and `code status` to the README's verb block.

findings.title: The hint for an untested version drops the workspace and the requested tree version
findings.body: After `code status --workspace acme --tree-version ver_old --wait` finds an untested version, the CLI suggests `membrane-operator code test`. Without an attached session that command fails because `--workspace` is missing. With an attached session it tests the newest version, which may not be `ver_old`. Either way, the suggested command does not test the version whose status the user asked about.
findings.fix: Add the workspace or session flags to the hint via followUpFlags(options), plus `--tree-version ${version.id}`.

findings.title: The `code pull` example uses flags that `codePull` rejects
findings.body: The README lists `--tree-version` and `--latest` as valid flags for `code pull`, but `codePull` explicitly rejects both before reading the tree. A user who follows the example to fetch a specific version gets a refusal. `claude-plugin/skills/operate/SKILL.md:577` has the same example. The reviewer marked this as existing before the change under review.
findings.fix: Remove both flags from the examples, and say that a specific version is read through the `v/<version id>` tag inside the clone.

findings.title: isVerdictReadRefusal treats any 401/403 or 'sign-in expired' error, including local token-refresh failures, as an old-engine refusal
findings.body:
Observed: `isVerdictReadRefusal` returns true for any 401/403 ApiError anywhere in the cause chain, and for any Error whose message matches /sign-in expired/. `storedCredentialSource.get()` (claude-plugin/src/client/platform-token.ts:72) throws exactly that message when the stored OAuth token is expired and the refresh grant fails. The refresh is attempted before any request reaches the engine, and a network failure during the refresh produces the same message.

What follows: `code status` makes no earlier call. When the stored sign-in cannot be refreshed, the error is thrown from `platformToken.get()` inside `dispatch`. It is wrapped as VerdictReadFailed and classified as a refusal. The verb then prints `this engine cannot answer the verdict yet` and exits 2 instead of printing `Sign in again` and exiting 1. With an attached session, a session-token mint that is refused (401/403 from `tokens.get` / `remintAfterRefusal`) takes the same path. An agent following the documented contract reads exit 2 as 'still pending / engine refuses' and keeps polling instead of fixing its credential. `code test` is mostly shielded, because `run-source-tree-tests` runs first and surfaces auth errors normally. It is affected only if the credential expires during the wait.
findings.fix: Classify a refusal only when the list request itself was answered by the engine: check the ApiError status on the list command's own response. Do not match the refresh-failure message, and do not walk causes produced by token acquisition. Let local credential errors fall through to the normal exit-1 error path.

findings.title: `code test --json` now prints the bare version instead of the command output `{ version }`
findings.body: Before this change, `code test --json` wrote `JSON.stringify(result)`, where `result` is the run-source-tree-tests output `{ version: SourceTreeVersion }`. Now every path, including `--no-wait --json`, goes through `renderTestVersion`, which writes `JSON.stringify(version)`. That drops the `version` wrapper. Any script or agent reading `.version.testsStatus` from `code test --json` now gets `undefined`. Nothing in the diff or the docs mentions the shape change. I found no in-repo consumer, which is why this is minor.
findings.fix: Keep the wrapper for `code test` (`{ version }`). Alternatively, document the new shape in the help text and plugin README as an intended change.

findings.title: Each verdict poll re-fetches the full operator overview to resolve the same workspace
findings.body: Without an attached session, every `dispatch` goes through `dispatchUnattached`, which calls `loadOverview` → `getOperatorOverview()` before the actual command. Nothing caches the result. This change wraps `dispatch` in a polling loop (every 5 s, up to 90 s, plus one dispatch per cursor page), so one `code test` now makes about 19 extra overview calls. Each call returns every workspace the operator works in, with its jobs and inbox items, only to re-derive the same `orgWorkspaceId`.
findings.fix: Resolve the unattached workspace once per dispatcher: keep a lazily created `Promise<string>` for the `orgWorkspaceId` inside `createDispatcher` and reuse it in every `dispatchUnattached` call.

findings.title: `code status --wait --timeout 0` reports 'still pending' without making a single read
findings.body: With `--timeout 0`, `codeStatus` sets `deadline = now`. `readUntilDeadline` then finds `remaining <= 0`, aborts the request and fails with `VERDICT_READ_TIMED_OUT` before any response can count. So `codeStatus` prints `still pending after 0 s …` and exits 2 even when the newest version has passed (should be 0), is untested (3), or the tree is empty (1). The goal's status contract (0/1/2/3) is broken for that input. The test 'observes the aborted status read when the deadline is already spent' (cli.code.verdict.test.ts:262-302) expects `out: ''` and the 'still pending' line, so it locks in this behaviour and would stay green if it were wrong in any other way.
findings.fix: When the remaining time is already zero, allow one read without the abort (or let `codeStatus` do its first read without a deadline), then change the test to expect the real status of the version.

findings.title: No-op `catchTag` that fails again with the error it just caught
findings.body: `.pipe(Effect.catchTag('VerdictReadFailed', (error) => Effect.fail(error)))` catches `VerdictReadFailed` and fails again with the same value, so the error channel does not change. It adds an Effect layer and makes the reader look for a transformation that isn't there. Without it, `raceFirst` already has the error type `VerdictReadFailed | typeof VERDICT_READ_TIMED_OUT`, which the trailing cast still states.
findings.fix: Delete the `.pipe(Effect.catchTag(...))` call and keep the `as Effect.Effect<T, VerdictReadError>` cast on the `raceFirst` result.

findings.title: An expired or rejected sign-in looks like an old engine: "cannot answer the verdict yet", exit 2
findings.body:
The goal asks only that an *old engine* refusing the read fall back to exit 2. `isVerdictReadRefusal` goes much wider. It treats any 401 or 403 anywhere in the cause chain, and any message matching /sign-in expired/, as that engine refusal. So these credential failures, which the client already reports clearly, all become "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet" with exit 2:

- `platform-token.ts:72`: "The Membrane sign-in expired and could not be refreshed. Sign in again."
- `operator-client.ts:407`, `rejectedCredentialError`, whose cause is the 401: "Membrane rejected the stored credential. Sign in again to replace it."
- A `SessionClosedError` whose cause is a 401/403 mint refusal.

This bites hardest on `code status`, which never runs the queue call first. Example: an operator's refresh token has expired or been revoked, and they run `code status --workspace acme`. `platformToken.get()` throws the sign-in-expired error. `codeStatus` (line 705) prints "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet" and returns 2.

The goal defines exit 2 as "still pending / engine refuses". An agent that follows that contract will keep polling `code status` and never be told to sign in again; the "Sign in again" remedy is thrown away. The same happens in `waitForVersion` (line 665) when the credential expires partway through a 90 s wait in `code test`. The tests at cli.code.verdict.test.ts:377-493 only cover a bare 401/403 response, so they lock this behavior in rather than catching it.

Introduced by this change. Before it, `code test` surfaced these errors through `runCode`'s catch with exit 1.
findings.fix: Only treat the server's refusal of the read itself as an engine refusal. That is a 403 scope-mismatch (`ACCESS_SCOPE_MISMATCH`, or a bare 401/403 straight from the list call). Do not follow `error.cause`, and drop the /sign-in expired/ match. Errors the credential layer wraps (sign-in expired, rejected stored credential, closed session) should go through the normal error path, which exits 1 and keeps their "Sign in again" message.

findings.title: Флаг --no-wait возвращает успех для pending
findings.body: Когда `code test --no-wait` получает от engine статус `pending`, команда печатает его, но возвращает код 0. Вызывающий агент может принять это за прошедшие тесты, хотя вердикта ещё нет. Цель изменения задаёт код 2 для pending.
findings.fix: Возвращать код, полученный от renderTestVersion, вместо безусловного 0.

findings.title: Отказ engine поставить тесты в очередь возвращает код failed
findings.body: Если engine отказывает `run-source-tree-tests`, например с `source_tree_tests_not_queued`, ошибка выходит из `codeTest` во внешний обработчик `runCode`, который возвращает 1. По контракту код 1 означает проваленный тест, а отказ engine должен возвращать 2. Агент не может отличить отсутствие запуска от полученного отрицательного вердикта.
findings.fix: Обработать отказ постановки в очередь в codeTest и вернуть 2 с сообщением об ошибке.

findings.title: The untested follow-up hint drops the chosen version and workspace
findings.body: The untested hint at code.ts:727 prints `untested — queue with: membrane-operator code test` with no `--tree-version`, `--workspace` or `--session`. The timeout hints next to it do keep those flags through followUpFlags. With `code status --wait --tree-version <older id>`, following the hint queues tests on the newest version, not the one inspected. Without an attached session, the missing --workspace makes the suggested command fail.
findings.fix: Include the resolved version id and the original workspace/session flags in the hint.

findings.title: An expired or rejected sign-in is reported as "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet" (exit 2)
findings.body:
`isVerdictReadRefusal` treats three things as an old engine refusing the read: any 401/403 ApiError, any error whose message matches /sign-in expired/i, and any error with one of these in its `cause` chain. `codeStatus` (line ~705) and `waitForVersion` (line ~665) then print `this engine cannot answer the verdict yet` and exit 2. Exit 2 is the code for "still pending / engine refuses".

The regex matches the error `platform-token.ts:72` throws whenever the OAuth refresh fails. That includes the proactive pre-request refresh in `platformToken.get()` and a network failure during the refresh. No 401 and no old engine are involved. The cause-chain recursion also catches these:
- `rejectedCredentialError` ("Membrane rejected the stored credential. Sign in again to replace it"), which carries a 401 as its cause.
- A `SessionClosedError` whose cause is a 401/403 mint refusal.

The `auth: true` gate only checks that a credentials file exists, so it does not stop any of this.

Concrete case: an operator's refresh token has expired or been revoked, and they run `code status --workspace acme [--wait]`. The CLI prints "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet" and exits 2, instead of "Sign in again" and exit 1. An agent following the exit-code contract keeps polling and is never told to sign in. `code test` hits the same thing when the credential dies partway through the 90 s wait.

The comment above the regex ("A platform-token refresh reports this after the original 401") is wrong, because `get()` throws the same message with no 401 at all. The tests in cli.code.verdict.test.ts (~377-493, 'reports a %i list refusal…') only cover a bare 401/403 response, so they lock this behavior in. Before this change, these errors reached `runCode`'s catch and exited 1.
findings.fix: Classify as an old engine only the list call's own refusal: a 401/403 or ACCESS_SCOPE_MISMATCH ApiError returned directly by the read. Drop the /sign-in expired/ match and the recursion into `cause`, so credential errors go through the normal error path (exit 1, "Sign in again"). Add a test where the token refresh fails.

findings.title: `code status --wait` reports "still pending" when the first read timed out and nothing was read
findings.body: If the very first `listVersion` call hits the deadline, `version` is undefined and `timedOut` is true. The verb then prints `still pending after N s` and exits 2, although the version may already be passed, failed or untested. With `--timeout 0`, `readUntilDeadline` aborts the in-flight request at once, so `code status --wait --timeout 0` always claims pending. A short timeout on a slow link does the same.
findings.fix: When no version was read before the deadline, report that the verdict could not be read in time. Or perform the initial read without the deadline and apply the deadline only to the follow-up polls.

findings.title: `renderTestVersion` prints the bare version for `--json`, not the raw `{ version }` shape
findings.body: `renderTestVersion` prints `JSON.stringify(version)` on both the `--no-wait` and the waiting paths. Before, `code test --json` printed the raw `run-source-tree-tests` output `{ version: … }`, which matches the help line "Print the raw shape instead of the rendered summary" (cli.ts:71). Deployed agents or scripts reading `.version.testsStatus` now get undefined. The plugin is released from `main` to installed clients, and the change is undocumented.
findings.fix: Keep `{ version }` as the JSON shape for `code test` (and the same wrapper for `code status`), or document the change in the README and help text.

findings.title: Hand-rolled deadline race and error model contradict the repo's Effect rules
findings.body:
CODING_STANDARDS.md → Effect makes `.claude/skills/effect-best-practices/SKILL.md` binding. Its built-in table maps "`Promise.race` with a `setTimeout`" to `Effect.timeout` / `Effect.timeoutOrElse`. `readUntilDeadline` instead races `Effect.sleep(remaining)` against the read with `Effect.raceFirst`, and threads a hand-made `AbortController` through `CommandDispatch`. Effect's `tryPromise({ try: (signal) => … })` already provides an abort signal that fires on interruption. Other departures in the same block:

- The timeout is a bare `unique symbol` in the error channel rather than a `Data.TaggedError` ("The error channel names every failure"). It is then recovered with `Effect.match` plus `=== VERDICT_READ_TIMED_OUT` checks instead of `catchTag`.
- `.pipe(Effect.catchTag('VerdictReadFailed', (error) => Effect.fail(error)))` re-fails the same error, so it does nothing, and is followed by an `as Effect.Effect<T, VerdictReadError>` cast.
- `new VerdictReadFailed({ cause, message: cause instanceof Error ? cause.message : String(cause) })` is pasted three times (codeTest, readUntilDeadline, listVersion).
- The queue call's failure in `codeTest` is wrapped as `VerdictReadFailed` even though it is not a read.
- `listVersion` fires the dispatch before `readUntilDeadline` checks the deadline, so a spent deadline still issues a request and aborts it at once.
findings.fix: Make the timeout a `Data.TaggedError('VerdictReadTimedOut')`. Wrap each read as `Effect.tryPromise({ try: (signal) => dispatch(cmd, input, signal), catch: toVerdictReadFailed })`, piped through `Effect.timeoutOrElse({ duration: remaining, orElse: () => Effect.fail(new VerdictReadTimedOut()) })`, and recover with `catchTag`. This removes the manual AbortController, the no-op catchTag and the cast, and builds the request only after the deadline check.

findings.title: Отказ поставить тесты в очередь возвращает код failed
findings.body: Если engine не запускает source code, `run-source-tree-tests` отвечает 400 с ключом `source_tree_tests_not_queued` и не ставит запуск в очередь, как показано в `engine/api/src/workspace/source-tree/source-tree-tests-on-request.pg.test.ts:415`. Ошибка проходит в общий обработчик `runCode`, который возвращает 1. Контракт изменения назначает отказу engine код 2, а код 1 — проваленному тесту. Поэтому вызывающий агент принимает отсутствие запуска за отрицательный вердикт.
findings.fix: Распознать отказ постановки в очередь и вернуть код 2 с сообщением об отказе.

findings.title: The poll loop never reads at the deadline, so a test wait of five seconds or less reads nothing
findings.body: waitForNextPoll sleeps min(5000, remaining), and waitForVersion then breaks as soon as now >= deadline, so no read happens at the deadline. With `code test --timeout 5` or less, a `pending` queue answer leads to one sleep until the deadline and zero list reads. The command reports pending and exits 2 even if the verdict landed meanwhile. On longer waits the last read is up to 5 s before the deadline, so the final stretch of every timeout is never observed. `code status --wait` makes its first read before the loop, so for status only the follow-up poll is lost.
findings.fix: Allow a final read when the sleep reaches the deadline, for example by reading once at the deadline before giving up, or by sleeping slightly less than the remaining time.

findings.title: An expired sign-in or failed refresh during a verdict read is reported as "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet" (exit 2)
findings.body:
`isVerdictReadRefusal` treats any 401 or 403, anything whose message matches /sign-in expired/, and any error with such a cause as an old engine refusing the read. The dispatch promise the read wraps does more than call `list-source-tree-versions`. Without a session, `dispatchUnattached` first looks up the workspace, and `callWithPlatformToken` first calls `platformToken.get()`. `get()` refreshes an expired access token proactively, with no 401 involved, and throws 'The Membrane sign-in expired and could not be refreshed. Sign in again.' when the refresh fails. That includes a network failure on the refresh. `rejectedCredentialError` ('Sign in again to replace it') also carries a 401 `cause`, so it matches too.

The access gate only checks that a credentials file exists (`access-gate.ts:134`). So a real case: the access token has expired and the refresh token has been revoked, and the user runs `code status --workspace acme` (or the access token expires during a 90 s `code test` wait). The CLI prints 'this engine cannot answer the verdict yet' and exits 2, which is the exit code for 'still pending'. It never says to sign in again. An agent following the 0/1/2/3 convention will keep re-reading or give up, and never fixes the credential.

The comment above the regex, "A platform-token refresh reports this after the original 401", is wrong: `get()` raises the same message with no 401 at all. The tests in `cli.code.verdict.test.ts` ('reports a %i list refusal…') encode this mix-up and do not separate a rejected credential from an old engine.
findings.fix: Decide on the list call's own response only: check `isApiErrorWithStatus(error, 401|403)` on the error the list command returned, and drop the /sign-in expired/ match and the recursion into `cause`. A credential error from the token refresh or the workspace lookup should then surface through the normal error path ('Sign in again…', exit 1). Add a test where the token refresh fails and check that the sign-in message is printed.

findings.title: `code test --json` now prints the bare version object instead of the raw `{ version }` result, including with `--no-wait`
findings.body: Before this change, `code test --json` printed the raw `run-source-tree-tests` output `{ version: SourceTreeVersion }`. Now every path, `--no-wait` included, goes through renderTestVersion (code.ts:544), which prints the version alone. A consumer reading `.version.testsStatus` gets undefined. The `--json` help line still promises 'the raw shape' (cli.ts:71), and no doc mentions the change.
findings.fix: Keep `{ version }` as the JSON shape for `code test` on every path, or document the change in the help text and SKILL.md.

findings.title: The agent skill does not document `code status`'s flags, the new `--wait`/`--no-wait`/`--timeout` flags, or the 0/1/2/3 exit codes
findings.body:
SKILL.md is what agents work from. It now says `test` 'queues once and waits' and `status` 'reads a verdict without queuing'. But its `code` synopsis block (lines ~577-584) still lists neither `code test` nor `code status`, and nothing explains the following:

- `code test` now exits 1 on a failed verdict and 2 while still pending (it used to always exit 0).
- `code status` exits 3 for an untested version.
- `code status --wait [--timeout <s>]` exists to keep waiting.
- `--no-wait` keeps the old queue-and-return behavior.

An agent that reads exit 1 or 2 from `code test` as a command error may run `code test` again, and once a verdict has landed that queues a new run, which is the very loop this change is meant to stop. The stderr follow-up line only appears on timeout. `claude-plugin/README.md` has the same omission in its synopsis.
findings.fix: Add `membrane-operator code test [--tree-version <id>] [--no-wait] [--timeout <s>]` and `membrane-operator code status [--tree-version <id>] [--wait] [--timeout <s>]` to the synopsis block. Add one sentence on the exit codes: 0 passed/skipped, 1 failed, 2 pending or verdict unavailable, 3 untested.

findings.title: The untested-version hint (code.ts:727) leaves out workspace, session and version id, and the test locks it in
findings.body: `codeStatus` in claude-plugin/src/engine/verbs/code.ts:727 runs `--wait` on an `untested` version and prints `untested — queue with: membrane-operator code test` and nothing else. The two timeout hints in the same function do pass `followUpFlags(options)` and the version id. This hint does not, so the command it suggests can fail. Without an attached session, `code test` has no workspace to run against. With `--tree-version ver_2` given, `codeTest` (code.ts:517) sends no `versionId`, so the latest version gets queued instead of the one the user asked about. The new test here asserts the bare string and passes no `--tree-version`, so it fixes the wrong output in place. This change adds both the hint and the test.
findings.fix: In code.ts:727, build the hint the way the timeout hints are built: `${BINARY_NAME} code test${followUpFlags(options)} --tree-version ${version.id}`. In this test, pass `--tree-version` (and `--session`) and assert the full hint.

findings.title: isVerdictReadRefusal treats any 'sign-in expired' error and any 401/403 in the cause chain as an old engine refusing the read
findings.body:
Observed: `isVerdictReadRefusal` returns true for three things. (1) A 401 or 403 ApiError. (2) Any Error whose message matches /sign-in expired/i. (3) Any error with one of these in its `cause` chain. `codeStatus` (line 705) and `waitForVersion` (line 665) turn each of them into `this engine cannot answer the verdict yet` and exit 2. Exit 2 is the code for "still pending / engine refuses".

The regex matches the error `platform-token.ts:72` throws whenever the OAuth refresh fails. That includes the ordinary pre-request refresh in `platformToken.get()`, when the stored access token has expired and the refresh token is dead. No 401 and no old engine are involved. The CLI's `auth: true` gate (`cli.ts:134`) only checks that credentials exist, so it does not stop this case. Trigger: an operator whose sign-in has lapsed runs `membrane-operator code status --workspace acme [--wait]`. The read fails before any request goes out, and the CLI prints `this engine cannot answer the verdict yet` with exit 2, not `The Membrane sign-in expired… Sign in again.` with exit 1.

The cause-chain recursion causes the same thing in two more cases:
- `rejectedCredentialError` ("Membrane rejected the stored credential. Sign in again"), which wraps a 401.
- On the attached-session path, a 401 that survives the remint, or a `SessionClosedError` whose cause is a 401/403.

Inferred consequence: the goal makes exit 2 mean "pending / old engine". An agent following the documented contract waits or retries `code status --wait`. It is never told to sign in again or restart the session, so it can loop on exit 2 with a credential that will never work. `code test` mostly avoids this because the queue call fails first with the real message. `code status` and a credential that dies mid-wait do not.
findings.fix: Narrow the refusal test to what an old engine actually returns for a non-sessionless command: a 401/403 ApiError on the read itself, ideally only on the platform-token (unattached) path. Drop the `/sign-in expired/` regex, and stop recursing into `rejectedCredentialError` / `SessionClosedError`, so real credential failures still print their own message and exit 1.

findings.title: Отказ поставить тесты в очередь возвращает код 1
findings.body: Когда движок не исполняет исходный код или не может поставить запуск в очередь, run-source-tree-tests возвращает source_tree_tests_not_queued. Этот код оборачивает отказ в VerdictReadFailed и передаёт его внешнему обработчику runCode, который возвращает 1. По целевому контракту отказ движка должен давать 2; вызывающий скрипт получает тот же код, что и при проваленных тестах.
findings.fix: Распознать отказ source_tree_tests_not_queued при постановке в очередь и вернуть 2.

findings.title: Ожидание до пяти секунд не читает вердикт
findings.body: При допустимом --timeout 5 или меньшем code test после постановки в очередь спит до истечения срока и выходит до первого вызова listVersion. Даже если тест завершился сразу, команда всегда сообщает pending и возвращает 2. Та же проблема возникает у code status --wait, если его первый ответ был pending.
findings.fix: Выполнить чтение до первого сна или запланировать первое чтение до истечения срока.

findings.title: Every unattached verdict poll repeats the full cross-workspace operator-overview fan-out
findings.body: Without an attached session, every `dispatch` goes through `dispatchUnattached`, and each call runs `loadOverview` → GET /operator/overview before `callInWorkspace`. `waitForVersion` polls every 5 s for up to 90 s, so one `code test` makes up to about 19 overview requests, plus one more per page of a `--tree-version` walk. On the engine, each request runs `getNativeOperatorOverview`, which fans out across every org workspace with `concurrency: 'unbounded'`. All of that only re-resolves the same `orgWorkspaceId`. Before this change, `code test` made one dispatch.
findings.fix: In `createDispatcher`, cache the orgWorkspaceId promise from the first `dispatchUnattached` lookup and reuse it for later dispatches in the same invocation.

findings.title: No test fails if the Last request section boundary is removed
findings.body: The goal says status parsing must not pick up a Status: line from another section. The code enforces that with `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` in executable_handoff-session-start.sh. The first new negative case in test 2834 has no `## Last request` heading, so `in_last_request` is never set and that exit line is never reached. The second case has `Status: Waiting for a reply` inside Last request, which tests value validation only. No test covers a Last request section with no Status line followed by a later section holding `Status: Answered` (for example under Key Details). If the exit line is deleted, every test still passes. A real handoff where the model omits Status in Last request but a later section contains a `Status: Answered` line would then show a wrong status to the operator, and no test would catch it. The fix is a fixture of that shape with no Status line under Last request.
findings.fix: Add a fixture with `## Last request` containing no `Status:` line, followed by `## Key Details` containing `Status: Answered`. Assert the systemMessage has no Status line.

findings.title: First `Status:` line in Last request wins, even when it comes from the quoted operator message
findings.body: The section holds a verbatim quote of the operator's message before the real Status line. The awk takes the first line starting with `Status:` and exits. If a multi-line operator message has a line beginning `Status:`, that line is read first. Its value will not be one of the three recognized values, so the status is dropped even though the extractor's own `Status: Answered` line follows. A quoted line starting with `## ` also ends the section early and drops the status. In both cases the failure is a silently missing status, not a wrong one. A quoted line that is exactly `Status: Answered` would show a spoofed status. This is rare, and it is a consequence of the design the goal describes.
findings.fix: Take the last `Status:` line in the section instead of the first, since the extractor's line comes after the quote. For example, store the match and print it in an END block.

findings.title: Status awk can take a `Status:` line or `## ` heading from the verbatim operator quote as metadata
findings.body: The new prompt puts a verbatim quote of the operator's last message in `## Last request`, above the extractor's own `Status:` line. The awk takes the first line starting with `Status:` and exits, and it ends the section at any line starting with `## `. It cannot tell quoted text, including fenced code, from metadata. Three failures follow. (1) If the quote contains a line `Status: Answered` and the real status after it is `Status: Not answered`, the operator banner shows Answered for an unanswered request. (2) If the quote contains a `Status:` line with an unrecognized value, the real status is silently dropped. (3) If the quote contains a `## ` heading, the section ends early and the status is dropped. The new tests quote only a single line, so none of these cases is covered.
findings.fix: Put the `Status:` line directly after the heading, before the quote, and parse it only from that position, updating the extraction prompt to match. Alternatively, keep the last `Status:` line in the section rather than the first, and print it in an END block.

findings.title: Prompt-contract assertion 'Last user request' passes without the new prompt text
findings.body: test_scripts_50900 payload has no transcript_path, so transcript_facts() (executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh:113) always emits the `Last user request: None` line into the prompt. `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` is therefore satisfied by the facts block itself, not by the new `## Last request` template. Deleting or rewording the new instruction "Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above" (the facts-block reference the goal says must hold) keeps this test green. Nothing in the test pins that wiring. The other new assertions (## Last request, Status values, verify with, no '3-7 bullet points') do bind to the changed text.
findings.fix: Replace it with an assertion on the new instruction text, e.g. 'verbatim from the facts block above'.

findings.title: Prompt assertion for the inferred-items instruction cannot detect its loss from one of the two sections
findings.body: Test 50900 searches the whole prompt once for '<claim>, verify with: <exact command>'. The contract requires this instruction in both Relevant Context and Key Details. If either occurrence is removed from executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh, the other still satisfies the assertion and the test stays green. The extractor would then lose the rule for that section without any test failing. This conflicts with the guidance in docs/solutions/design-patterns/semantic-regression-tests-over-source-shape.md on choosing the contract boundary.
findings.fix: Extract the Relevant Context and Key Details blocks from the captured prompt and assert the full instruction in each one, so removing either occurrence turns the test red.

findings.title: No test pins the section boundary of the Status parser
findings.body: The goal says status parsing must not pick up a Status: line from another section. The awk in executable_handoff-session-start.sh stops at the next heading (`in_last_request && /^## / { exit }`). The new negative case at this line has no `## Last request` section at all, and the other negative case has an unrecognized value inside the section. Neither fixture puts a valid Status line in a later section after a Last request section. If the `exit` on the next heading were deleted, a handoff with `## Last request` holding no Status line and `## Key Details` holding `Status: Answered` would show 'Status: Answered' beside the goal, and every test would stay green. Add a fixture with that shape and expect the goal alone.
findings.fix: In test 2834, stage a handoff with `## Last request` (no Status line) followed by `## Key Details` containing `Status: Answered`, and assert the systemMessage has no Status line.

findings.title: Отрицательный пример не проверяет выход из секции Last request
findings.body:
В новом примере вообще нет `## Last request`, поэтому он проверяет только вход в секцию. Если удалить остановку на следующем заголовке из SessionStart, все представленные проверки статуса сохранят прежний результат. Регрессия останется незамеченной: для `## Last request
Please continue.

## Key Details
Status: Not answered` оператор увидит статус из Key Details, хотя требование разрешает читать его только внутри Last request.
findings.fix: Добавить рядом пример с секцией Last request без статуса и распознанным Status: в следующей секции. Проверить точный systemMessage без статуса.

findings.title: Проверка инструкции об inferred items не различает две секции
findings.body: Один поиск `<claim>, verify with: <exact command>` по всему prompt проходит, если удалить эту инструкцию из Relevant Context или из Key Details: второе вхождение удовлетворяет assertion. Поэтому новый тест не обнаружит потерю правила в одной из двух секций, хотя цель изменения явно требует его в обеих.
findings.fix: Проверять инструкцию отдельно в блоках Relevant Context и Key Details, чтобы удаление любого из двух вхождений делало тест красным.

findings.title: No test covers the Last request section boundary, so removing the `^## ` exit in the status awk stays green
findings.body: The new negative cases do not exercise the property the goal names: a Status: line from another section must not be picked up. Case 1 (around line 11692) has no `## Last request` heading at all, so `in_last_request` never turns on. Case 2 has the Status line inside Last request with an unrecognized value. The positive tests 50901 and 50902 have a Status line only inside Last request, and the next section (Key Details) has none. If `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` in executable_handoff-session-start.sh were deleted, every test would still pass. The gap is a Last request section with no or an unrecognized Status line, followed by `## Key Details` or `## Warnings` containing `Status: Answered`. In that case the operator would be shown a status the extractor never gave for the last request. This is the exact regression the tests are supposed to catch.
findings.fix: Add a fixture with `## Last request` holding only a quote, followed by `## Key Details` with `Status: Answered`. Assert the systemMessage shows the goal alone.

findings.title: Status awk reads the first `Status:` line in a section that holds a verbatim operator quote
findings.body: The prompt tells the extractor to put the operator's last message verbatim in `## Last request`, above the Status line. The awk takes the first line starting with `Status:` and exits, and it ends the section at any line starting with `## `. Both patterns can occur in the quoted operator text. Two failures follow, both inferred from the code and not run. (1) A multi-line operator message that includes a line like `Status: Answered` or `Status: Not answered` makes the operator banner show that value instead of the extractor's real verdict. (2) A pasted message containing a `## ` markdown heading ends the section early, so the real Status line is never reached and the banner silently drops the status. Case 2 is the more likely one and fails safe. Case 1 needs an operator quote with a line that starts with `Status:`, so it is uncommon. Taking the last matching line in the section would fix case 1. Case 2 is inherent to heading-delimited parsing.
findings.fix: Keep the last recognized `Status:` line in the section instead of exiting on the first, and print it in an END block.

findings.title: Строка Status: внутри цитаты принимается за служебный статус
findings.body: Новый prompt требует дословно вставить сообщение пользователя перед служебным Status:. Если сообщение содержит отдельную строку `Status: Answered`, например при обсуждении предыдущего handoff, awk выберет её и завершится до настоящего `Status: Not answered`. Оператор увидит Answered для неотвеченного запроса, хотя additionalContext сохранит настоящий статус. Аналогично заголовок `## ...` внутри сообщения преждевременно завершит поиск. Новые тесты используют однострочную цитату и не различают эти случаи.
findings.fix: Поместить служебный Status: перед цитатой и разбирать его только в этой позиции.

findings.title: No test covers the Last request section boundary, so deleting the `^## ` exit in the status awk stays green
findings.body: The awk added in executable_handoff-session-start.sh accepts a Status line only inside the Last request section, and the code comment says so. The rule that stops it at the next section, `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }`, is not covered by any test. In test 2834, the new negative case (scripts_test.sh:11692-11702) puts `Status:` in Key Details with no `## Last request` heading at all, so `in_last_request` is never set. The second case only checks value validation (`Waiting for a reply`), and no section follows it. In 50901 and 50902, Status appears only inside Last request. If the exit line is deleted, a handoff whose Last request has no Status line but whose later Key Details starts a line with `Status: Answered` would print `Answered` in the operator's systemMessage, and the suite would stay green. That is the false green this repository's test-oracle gate exists to catch. The damage is limited to the operator-only display, and it needs the extractor to leave out the Status the prompt asks for.
findings.fix: In test 2834, add one fixture: `## Last request` holding only a quoted message with no Status line, followed by `## Key Details` holding `Status: Answered`. Assert exactly that the systemMessage is the goal with no Status line. Prove it red by deleting the exit line, then restore it.

findings.title: Проверка допускает удаление правила об inferred items из одного раздела
findings.body: Тест ищет '<claim>, verify with: <exact command>' во всём prompt, хотя контракт требует эту инструкцию отдельно в Relevant Context и Key Details. Удаление любой одной из двух инструкций в executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh оставляет все проверки теста удовлетворёнными: второе вхождение сохраняется. Тест пропускает регрессию, при которой extractor больше не получает требование указывать команду проверки для предположений в одном из разделов.
findings.fix: Проверять полную инструкцию отдельно внутри каждого раздела переданного prompt. Подтвердить, что удаление любого из двух вхождений делает тест красным.

findings.title: Last request step has no defined outcome when the facts block says "Last user request: None"
findings.body: The facts block can emit `Last user request: None` (lines 260-261 and the fallback at 265). The new step says "[Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above]" and then "Status: [Use exactly one of: Answered, Partially answered, Not answered]". Neither says what to write when there is no message to quote. Haiku may invent a quote from the conversation, write "None", or pick one of the three statuses arbitrarily. If it picks a status, the SessionStart hook shows it as `Status: …` beside the goal, though there was no request to answer. The completion criterion for this section is undefined for the None branch, so runs diverge.
findings.fix: Add a branch to the section, e.g. "[If the facts block says Last user request: None, write None and omit the Status line]". The parser already treats a missing Status line as no status.

findings.title: Prompt places the verbatim quote before the Status line, which makes a quoted `Status:` line reachable by the parser
findings.body: The extraction prompt puts the verbatim operator quote (line 319) above the `Status:` line (line 320). The injector's awk in executable_handoff-session-start.sh takes the first `^Status:` line inside `## Last request` and exits. If the operator's last message has a line starting with `Status:`, the quote supplies the first match, and the shown status is wrong or dropped. The prompt layout is what makes this reachable.
findings.fix: Put the `Status:` line first in the section with the quote after it, or have the prompt format the quote as a blockquote or indented block.

findings.title: Two terminal paths can still discard their result without any test failing
findings.body: The goal says the tests must fail if a result is silently discarded again. Two `finish(...)` call sites have no notification assertion. (1) The outer `catch` in `runBrewAutoUpdate` (`index.ts` ~line 446, 'Pi update failed without blocking startup'), reached when `acquireLock` or the cleanup throws, e.g. an unwritable lock directory. Reverting that line to `return reportFailure(...)` leaves every test green. (2) The startup `PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0` skip. The 'disables startup only when PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE is zero' test still passes `fakeUi().ui` and never inspects notifications. The startup-silent-on-skip policy is therefore unpinned for the offline and disabled skips. Only the contended skip has a startup-silence control. A regression in either path is invisible to the suite.
findings.fix: Add a test where the lock directory cannot be created (or `deps.lockPath` is under a file) and assert one warning notification at startup and at manual. Assert `notifications` is empty in the startup offline and `PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0` cases, and assert one info notification in the manual offline case.

findings.title: Contention message reworded although the goal does not ask for it
findings.body: The message changed from 'another Pi process owns the update lock' to 'a Pi update is already running'. The goal does not require this; it only requires that the message reach `ui.notify`. The new text is also less accurate. `acquireLock` returns `acquired:false` for any lock directory that exists and is not stale, and also when stale-lock reclaim loses a race or runs out of attempts. It does not mean an update is running. A user who reads this after a crashed owner whose lock is still younger than the 20-minute stale window is told something false. The new message is the one the test now hardcodes, so the wording is not an independent oracle.
findings.fix: Keep the original wording unless there is a reason to change it, and update the test to match.

findings.title: Update failures stay invisible when Pi runs headless (print/JSON mode)
findings.body: In print/JSON mode the session_start handler still runs the update, but Pi binds `ctx.ui` to `noOpUIContext`, whose `notify` does nothing. A failure such as a non-zero exit from `brew update` therefore passes through `finish` and returns `failed`, yet the user is never warned: the handler discards the result and there is no other output channel. The reviewer traced this through the installed Pi: print-mode.js calls `bindExtensions` without a uiContext, and extensions/runner.js substitutes `noOpUIContext`. The change did not introduce this. The reviewer says it is an existing problem already recorded in the new issue 2026-09-02-007.
findings.fix: Add a diagnostic channel that headless consumers can see, and keep the chosen interactive notification policy.

findings.title: Тесты не защищают уведомление об ошибке получения блокировки
findings.body: Новый тест исключения выбрасывает ошибку из deps.exec и проверяет внутренний catch. Ни один случай не вызывает внешний catch в runBrewAutoUpdate. Если получение блокировки завершится EACCES или ENOTDIR, именно внешний catch должен сообщить об ошибке. Удаление finish из этой ветки снова сделает такой отказ невидимым, но существующие проверки этого не обнаружат. Это оставляет непокрытой явно заявленную цель защиты всех терминальных результатов от молчаливого отбрасывания.
findings.fix: Добавить случай ошибки получения блокировки и проверить результат failed вместе с уведомлением warning, содержащим причину ошибки.

findings.title: Outer-catch failure path and startup skip paths in runBrewAutoUpdate have no notification assertion
findings.body: The change routes every terminal result through finish(), but the tests only exercise some of those return sites. Covered: step exec throw, killed, nonzero code, manual offline, manual contention, startup contention, startup/manual success. Not covered: (a) the outer `catch` at index.ts:445-447, reached when acquireLock or the snapshot calls throw, so no test fails if finish() is removed there and that failure goes silent again; (b) the startup `PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0` skip and startup `PI_OFFLINE` skip, where silence is the specified policy. The 'disables startup only when PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE is zero' test still does not inspect notifications. The goal says tests must fail if a result is silently discarded again, and the outer catch is one place that could regress undetected. Tests that fail only on the later-step failures (brew upgrade, pi update) are also absent, though they share the same finish() call as step 1.
findings.fix: Add a test where the lock directory cannot be created (e.g. lockPath under a regular file) and assert a warning notification for both triggers. Add a startup-trigger assertion that the disabled and offline skips produce no notifications.

findings.title: Уведомление из внешнего catch не защищено регрессионным тестом
findings.body: Новые тесты ошибок вызывают только внутренние ветки обработки deps.exec. Ни один тест не вызывает внешний catch, например при невозможности создать каталог блокировки. Если здесь вернуть reportFailure напрямую, ошибки доступа снова станут невидимыми, а существующие проверки уведомлений этого не обнаружат. Это пробел покрытия изменённой ветки: ~/.claude/shared/testing.md требует проверять каждый путь ошибки, а docs/solutions/design-patterns/semantic-regression-tests-over-source-shape.md требует, чтобы тест менял вердикт при потере защищаемого поведения.
findings.fix: Добавить сценарий ошибки создания блокировки и проверить, что startup завершается результатом failed и отправляет одно уведомление уровня warning.

findings.title: Decision record cites a nonexistent agents-local directory for the warning convention
findings.body: The settled-policy text says `warning` "matches the convention already used by `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local`". No such directory exists. The extension is the single file `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local.ts`, which calls `ctx.ui.notify(warning, "warning")` at about line 53. The convention is real, but a reader who follows the cited path finds nothing.
findings.fix: Change the reference to `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local.ts`.

findings.title: Outer-catch failure path (lock acquisition throws) has no notification test
findings.body: The goal is that no terminal result is returned without passing `finish`, and the tests are meant to catch a silently discarded result. Every failure test (killed, nonzero exit, `exec` throwing) goes through the per-step returns. The outer `catch` in `runBrewAutoUpdate` is `finish(..., "Pi update failed without blocking startup: ...")`. It is reachable in real use, for example when the lock directory cannot be created, and nothing exercises it. If that `finish` call were reverted to `return reportFailure(...)`, the suite would stay green and the failure would be silent again.
