A fixture with an unwritable `lockPath` parent, asserting one `warning` notification for both startup and manual, would catch this.
findings.fix: Add a test where `acquireLock` throws, such as a `lockPath` under a regular file. Assert status `failed` and exactly one `warning` notification containing "Pi update failed without blocking startup".

findings.title: Startup-disabled test does not assert the silent-skip policy
findings.body: The policy says startup is silent on skipped outcomes, and manual reports them. The test "disables startup only when PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE is zero" never inspects notifications. A regression that notifies on a disabled startup would pass, and so would one that stops the manual path reporting. The offline case is checked for manual only, so no startup-silent control exists for either skip reason.
findings.fix: Assert `notifications` is empty for the startup-disabled and startup-offline cases, with the manual case as the control.

findings.title: Не проверяется уведомление при ошибке создания блокировки
findings.body: Новый тест исключения из deps.exec проверяет внутренний catch, но ни один сценарий не достигает внешнего catch в index.ts:445–447. Например, если родитель lockPath — обычный файл, mkdir завершится с ENOTDIR именно через внешний catch. Если убрать finish из этой ветки, ошибка снова станет невидимой пользователю, а существующие проверки этого не обнаружат. Это пробел в регрессионном покрытии нового поведения; текущая реализация уведомляет правильно.
findings.fix: Добавить в существующий describe сценарий с lockPath внутри обычного файла. Проверить результат failed, отсутствие вызовов executor и одно warning-уведомление с причиной ошибки.

findings.title: No test reaches the outer catch's finish() call, so it could be dropped without any test failing
findings.body: The goal requires that the tests fail if a result is silently discarded again. The new tests cover the exec-returns-failure, killed, exec-throws, offline, contended and complete paths. The outer `catch` at index.ts:445-447 has no test. That is the path where `acquireLock` or `deps.snapshotExtensions` throws, for example `mkdir` of the lock directory failing with EACCES or ENOSPC. If its `finish(...)` were reverted to a bare `return reportFailure(...)`, every existing test would still pass, and this path would silently drop the failure again. Failures there are the ones least likely to be noticed otherwise. This is a coverage gap on the changed code and not a defect in the shipped behaviour. The suite already injects `deps.lockPath` and `deps.snapshotExtensions`, so a case like this is cheap: point `lockPath` under a regular file, or make `snapshotExtensions` throw, then assert one `warning` notification for both triggers.
findings.fix: Add a test that makes `acquireLock` or `deps.snapshotExtensions` reject. Run it at startup, where only the failure policy forces a notification, and assert exactly one notification at level `warning`.

findings.title: Startup-silent policy for skipped outcomes (disabled, offline) is not pinned by any assertion
findings.body: The policy is that startup stays silent on skipped outcomes and the manual trigger reports them. Only the startup contended and up-to-date cases assert that `notifications` is empty. The 'disables startup only when PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE is zero' test passes `fakeUi().ui` and never inspects its notifications. The PI_OFFLINE test exercises only the manual trigger. If shouldNotify or finish began notifying on every startup skip, every test would stay green and each startup would show an info toast, which is the nagging the policy rules out.
findings.fix: In the 'disables startup only' test, keep the fakeUi from the startup call and assert `notifications` equals `[]`. Add a startup + PI_OFFLINE case that asserts no notifications, with the manual case as the control.

findings.title: Outer catch-all failure path and later-step failures are not exercised
findings.body: The change routes the outer `catch` (for example `acquireLock` throwing on mkdir/permission errors) through `finish`, giving 'Pi update failed without blocking startup: ...'. No test makes `acquireLock` throw. The failure fixtures also all fail at step 1 (`brew update`), so a failure in `pi update --extensions` is never checked. If the catch branch went back to returning an un-notified `reportFailure`, the suite would stay green. That is the silent-discard regression the goal names, in the one path with no coverage.
findings.fix: Add a test with an unusable lockPath (for example a parent path that is a file). Assert that a `failed` result produces one `warning` notification.

findings.title: Cites a non-existent agents-local directory
findings.body: The recorded decision points to `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local` as the warning-level convention. That path is a single file, `agents-local.ts`, not a directory. It does use `ctx.ui.notify(warning, "warning")`, so the claim holds but the path is wrong and a reader following it hits a missing directory. This is human-facing prose only.
findings.fix: Change the reference to `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local.ts`.

findings.title: No test reaches the outer catch's finish() call in runBrewAutoUpdate, so a silent-discard regression there goes undetected
findings.body: Issue 022 asks that the tests catch any regression that silently discards a terminal result again. Every new failure test fails inside `deps.exec`: a non-zero exit, a killed process, or exec throwing. Those all go through the inner handling around index.ts:408-422. No test reaches the outer `catch` at index.ts:445-447, which returns `finish(trigger, ui, reportFailure("Pi update failed without blocking startup: ..."))`. That path can be reached: `acquireLock` (index.ts:195-221) rethrows any mkdir/writeFile error other than EEXIST (EACCES, ENOTDIR, ENOSPC), and `deps.snapshotExtensions` may reject. If that `finish` went back to a bare `return reportFailure(...)`, every existing test would stay green and these failures would go silent again. The shipped code is correct today; the gap is in regression coverage for one of the failure exits.
findings.fix: Add a case where lock acquisition throws, e.g. `lockPath` under a regular file, or where `deps.snapshotExtensions` rejects. Assert status `failed`, no executor calls, and exactly one `warning` notification containing the failure reason, for both the startup and manual triggers. Confirm the test goes red when `finish` is removed from the outer catch.

findings.title: Were the new notification tests ever run red against the old silent-failure behaviour?
findings.body: The review materials do not show the new notification checks failing against the original implementation, which returned `failed` silently. The issue document explicitly requires that red run. The materials also do not show the checks passing on the current state. A red result before the fix and a green result after it would settle this.

findings.title: Outer catch path (unexpected throw) is never asserted to notify
findings.body: The goal requires that the tests fail if a terminal result is silently discarded again. Every failure test added here goes through `exec` (non-zero exit, killed, or `exec` throwing). None triggers the outer `catch` in `runBrewAutoUpdate` (index.ts:445-447), which returns `finish(..., reportFailure("Pi update failed without blocking startup: ..."))`. That path is reached when `acquireLock` or `deps.snapshotExtensions` throws. If that `finish` were reverted to a bare `return reportFailure(...)`, which is the original silent-failure pattern, every test would still pass. The startup-skip branch for `PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0` (index.ts:384-387) also has no notification assertion. The test named `disables startup only when PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE is zero` checks only calls, not that startup stays silent.
findings.fix: Add a test where `snapshotExtensions` (or the lock) throws and assert one `warning` notification for both triggers. Assert `notifications` is empty in the PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 startup case.

findings.title: Recorded convention points to a path that does not exist
findings.body: The decision says the `warning` level "matches the convention already used by `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local`". That path is not a directory. The extension is the single file `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local.ts`, which calls `ctx.ui.notify(warning, "warning")` at line 53. A reader following the cited path finds nothing. The convention itself holds, since the file does use `warning` for degraded conditions. Only the citation is wrong.
findings.fix: Cite `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local.ts`.

findings.title: No fixture tests that status parsing stops at the end of the Last request section
findings.body:
The goal requires that "status parsing cannot pick up a Status: line from another section" and that tests go red on real regressions. The new negative case in test_scripts_2834 (lines 11692-11702) uses a handoff with no `## Last request` section at all, so `in_last_request` is never set. test_scripts_50901 and the unrecognized-value case both put the Status: line inside Last request. No fixture has a `## Last request` section without its own Status: line, followed by another section that has one.

The regression this lets through: delete `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` from executable_handoff-session-start.sh:83, or make the parser match the first `^Status:` after the heading anywhere. Every test stays green. But a handoff like `## Last request
Can you check?

## Key Details
Status: Answered` would then show `Status: Answered` to the operator, a false "no need to answer first" signal. The hook code is correct today; the gap is that the section-boundary rule has no red-capable oracle.
findings.fix: In the 2834 negative block, add a fixture with `## Last request` holding a quote and no Status: line, followed by `## Key Details` with `Status: Not answered`. Assert the goal-only systemMessage exactly.

findings.title: The prompt-contract test never checks the verbatim-quote instruction, and its 'Last user request' check is always true
findings.body:
test_scripts_50900 checks `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'`. The pre-existing `transcript_facts` function always prints that string: on success, and in both `None` fallbacks (executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh lines ~246 and ~262). So this check passes no matter what this change does to the prompt.

No other check pins the main new instruction, `[Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above]`. Delete that line, or reword it to allow paraphrase, and the test stays green: `## Last request`, `Status:`, the three values and `what to check first` all remain. The goal names the verbatim quote from the facts block as a requirement. Prompt text that a model reads verbatim is a valid literal contract under the test-oracle gate, but this test does not hold that part of it.
findings.fix: Replace `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` with an assertion on the instruction itself, e.g. `assert_file_contains "$prompt" "Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above"`.

findings.title: Parser takes the first Status: line in Last request, which can come from the verbatim-quoted operator message
findings.body:
The prompt (executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh:319-322) asks for the operator's last message verbatim directly above the extractor's own `Status:` line. It gives no quote boundaries, and the decoded JSON literal can span many lines. The awk at executable_handoff-session-start.sh:81-90 prints the first `^Status:` line in the section and exits at the first `^## ` line.

- Pasted markdown with a `## ` heading closes the section before the real Status line, so the status is silently dropped. Feeding the awk a quote containing `## Steps` returned nothing.
- A pasted `Status: Answered` line is shown in place of the extractor's own value. An unrecognized pasted value makes the parser exit, and the case filter then blanks it.

The impact is limited to the operator's on-screen message. additionalContext is byte-for-byte unchanged, and the fallback is goal-only display. Pasted content is an expected input here, though, so the new status display can be lost or wrong on ordinary inputs.
findings.fix: Make the quote unambiguous in the prompt. Put `Status: [...]` first in the section and render the quote as a blockquote (`> ` on each line), so quoted lines cannot match `^Status:` or `^## `. Taking the last Status line alone would not fix the early `## ` exit.

findings.title: Verbatim last-request quote conflicts with the kept 400-word handoff cap
findings.body: This change adds a `## Last request` section (pre-compact.sh:319-322) that requires the operator's last message verbatim. Before it, the 'copy the last user request exactly' constraint (line 337) only applied if the request was included. bounded_text (line 141) allows that message to reach 4000 characters plus ` [truncated]`, which on its own can exceed the existing 'Maximum 400 words in the <handoff> section' (line 334). The prompt does not say which rule wins, so with a long pasted message Haiku may paraphrase or truncate the quote, or crowd out the other sections. Nothing enforces the cap mechanically, so if the model simply overruns it the result is harmless. The real risk is a paraphrased or cut request reaching the next agent.
findings.fix: Add one line to the prompt's constraints: exclude the Last request quote from the 400-word cap, or quote a bounded prefix and mark the cut with `[truncated]`.

findings.title: Проверка prompt остаётся зелёной без инструкции цитировать запрос
findings.body: Если удалить из prompt строку `Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above`, тест продолжит проходить: `## Last request` останется в шаблоне, а `Last user request` — в существующем блоке фактов. При такой регрессии extractor больше не получает требование передать последний запрос дословно, хотя тест заявлен как проверка этого контракта.
findings.fix: Проверять саму инструкцию о дословной цитате и её связь с блоком фактов.

findings.title: Negative fixture for 'Status outside Last request' has no Last request section, so the parser's section-end exit is never tested
findings.body:
The parser in executable_handoff-session-start.sh:81-90 relies on `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` (line 83) so it never reads a `Status:` line from a later section. The new negative case in test_scripts_2834 uses a handoff with no `## Last request` heading at all. `in_last_request` is never set, so the guard never runs. The positive fixtures (50901, 50902, 'Waiting for a reply') all put their Status line inside Last request, so the guard does not matter there either.

If line 83 is deleted, every test stays green. Then a handoff with `## Last request` (quote only, no Status line) followed by `## Key Details` containing `Status: Answered` or `Not answered` shows that Key Details text to the operator as the last-request status. One reviewer ran this mutant: the original prints nothing and the mutant prints `Answered`. The goal explicitly says status parsing must not pick up a Status: line from another section. Under semantic-regression-tests-over-source-shape.md, a test that stays green when the behavior is removed is a false green.
findings.fix: In test_scripts_2834, add or change a fixture to have `## Last request` with a quote and no Status line, followed by `## Key Details\nStatus: Not answered` (or `Answered`). Assert the exact goal-only systemMessage, and confirm the test goes red with line 83 removed.

findings.title: First Status: line in Last request wins, but the verbatim operator quote sits before it
findings.body: The extraction prompt (executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh:318-321) asks for the operator's last message to be quoted verbatim, decoded from the JSON literal, so it can span several lines. The prompt puts that quote above the extractor's `Status:` line. The awk takes the first `^Status:` line in the section and exits. If the operator's last message has a line beginning `Status: Answered` (for example a pasted earlier handoff), the operator sees that text as the status instead of the extractor's verdict. A `## ` line inside the quote fails more safely: the section ends early and only the goal is shown.
findings.fix: Keep the last matching Status: line in the section (assign instead of print+exit, print in END), or move the Status: line above the quote in the prompt template.

findings.title: Строка Status внутри запроса может подменить его состояние
findings.body: Промпт в home/private_dot_claude/hooks/executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh:318–320 требует дословно включить последнее сообщение оператора перед полем состояния. Если это сообщение содержит отдельную строку `Status: Answered`, а фактическое поле после него равно `Status: Not answered`, парсер выбирает первую строку и показывает оператору `Answered`. Аналогично заголовок `## ` внутри сообщения прекращает поиск до фактического поля. Формат не отделяет текст запроса от служебного состояния.
findings.fix: Задать для текста запроса однозначные границы или кодирование и извлекать поле состояния только за их пределами.

findings.title: Status parser can read a `Status:` line from the quoted operator message instead of the real status
findings.body:
The new prompt tells the extractor to quote the operator's last real message verbatim inside `## Last request`, above the `Status:` line (pre-compact.sh:319-321). That message comes from `last_user`, which can be up to 4000 characters and can span several lines (`bounded_text`, pre-compact.sh:140). The prompt does not say how to format the quote, for example with a `> ` prefix. The awk in session-start.sh takes the first line in the section that matches `/^Status:/` and then exits.

So if the operator's message has its own line starting with `Status:` (for example a pasted ticket or report line such as `Status: blocked on CI`), the parser reads that line instead of the extractor's real status:
- If the value is not one of the three, the `case` empties it and the operator sees no status, even when the real line says `Not answered`.
- If it is one of the three, the operator sees the wrong status.

A quoted line starting with `## ` ends the section early in the same way, so the status is dropped.

The goal requires that status parsing picks up only the extractor's line. The tests do not cover this case, because every fixture quotes a single line.
findings.fix: Take the last `Status:` line in the section instead of the first (store it, keep reading to the next `## ` heading, print it at END). Or tell the extractor to put `Status:` directly under the heading and quote the message after it with `> ` on each line.

findings.title: Test 50900's 'Last user request' assertion always passes, so the link to the facts block is untested
findings.body:
`assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` matches the `<transcript_facts>` block. Every path in `transcript_facts` prints that block, including both fallback printfs (pre-compact.sh:245, 262-263), and the older 'Copy … the last user request exactly from <transcript_facts>' constraint also contains it. The new instruction says 'from the facts block above', which does not contain that string.

So the assertion still passes if the `## Last request` instruction is deleted or stops pointing at the facts block. The goal names 'does not break … the facts-block reference' as a correctness condition, and no test would catch that regression.
findings.fix: Assert the new instruction line itself, e.g. `assert_file_contains "$prompt" "Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above"`, and drop the `Last user request` assertion.

findings.title: Verbatim-quote instruction conflicts with the kept 400-word cap for long operator messages
findings.body:
The new `## Last request` section asks for a verbatim quote of the last user request. The facts block allows that request to be up to 4000 characters (`bounded_text`), which can be roughly 600 or more words. The same prompt keeps 'Maximum 400 words in the <handoff> section'.

When the operator's last message is long, the extractor gets two instructions that cannot both be met. It must either:
- shorten the 'verbatim' quote, so the quote is no longer exact (the point of the section), or
- exceed the word cap, or
- drop Relevant Context or Key Details to make room.

The prompt does not say which instruction wins.
findings.fix: Say which instruction wins, e.g. 'If the quote alone exceeds the cap, quote the first and last sentences verbatim and mark the cut with […]', or exclude the quote from the 400-word count.

findings.title: Длинный запрос делает требования к handoff несовместимыми
findings.body: Промпт требует дословно включить последний запрос и одновременно ограничивает весь handoff 400 словами. В блок фактов может попасть запрос длиннее 400 слов, но короче предела в 4000 символов. В таком случае модель не может выполнить оба требования: ей придется сократить запрос или превысить лимит handoff. Следующий агент может получить неполный запрос.
findings.fix: Явно определить приоритет для длинных запросов и согласовать лимит handoff с требованием дословной цитаты.

findings.title: No test covers a Status: line inside the quoted operator request
findings.body: The fixture has only one Status line. Suppose the operator's last request, quoted verbatim, contains `Status: Answered`, and the real handoff status after the quote is `Status: Not answered`. The parser picks the first line and shows the wrong status. The current test stays green with that behavior.
findings.fix: Add a fixture whose quoted request contains a Status line. Assert that the handoff's own status is displayed, not the quoted text.

findings.title: Проверка промпта не защищает требование дословной цитаты
findings.body: Проверка «Last user request» проходит благодаря метке в блоке фактов, даже если из промпта удалить обе инструкции копировать запрос дословно. Остальные проверки также сохранят зеленый результат, хотя модель больше не получит требования перенести точный запрос оператора в handoff.
findings.fix: Проверить инструкцию о дословном копировании в секции Last request и ее связь с блоком фактов.

findings.title: No fixture puts a Status: line in a section after a Status-less Last request, so dropping the parser's section-end exit keeps every test green
findings.body:
The goal says status parsing must never pick up a `Status:` line from another section, and that the tests must fail on real regressions. The new negative case in test_scripts_2834 (the 'status outside Last request' fixture) has **no** `## Last request` section at all, so `in_last_request` is never set and the section-end rule `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` (executable_handoff-session-start.sh:83) is never exercised. The other fixtures (50901, 50902, and the 'Waiting for a reply' case) all have their Status line inside Last request.

I ran a mutant of the awk with that exit line removed on `## Goal / ## Last request (no Status) / ## Key Details: Status: Answered`. The original prints nothing. The mutant prints `Answered`, so the operator's systemMessage would show `Status: Answered` taken from Key Details. All of 50901, 50902 and 2834 stay green under that mutant, because none of their fixtures can tell the two apart. Under the repository's test-oracle gate this is exactly the 'green test that cannot fail when the behavior is removed' class. The one rule the goal names for the status parser has no oracle.
findings.fix: In test_scripts_2834, add a fixture with `## Last request` that has no Status line, followed by `## Key Details` containing `Status: Answered`. Assert that the systemMessage is the goal-only form.

findings.title: Prompt never says the Status line must hold only the bare value, or what to do when the last request is None
findings.body:
The injector accepts a status only when the rest of the `Status:` line exactly equals `Answered`, `Partially answered` or `Not answered` (session-start.sh:91-94). The prompt never says the line must contain nothing else. Models often merge the next-check note (`Status: Not answered — check the extractor first`), add a trailing period, or bold the label (`**Status:** Not answered`). A reviewer ran the merged form through the awk: the case filter rejects it and the display silently falls back to goal-only. The status is lost exactly when the request is not fully answered.

Separately, the facts block emits `Last user request: None` when no human message survives, and on the jq fallbacks. The section still asks for a quote and one of three statuses. The extractor may then invent a message, which line 337 forbids, or pick an arbitrary status.
findings.fix: In the prompt, require the Status line to be plain, holding only the value with no markup or punctuation, and put the next-check note on its own line. Add `[If the facts block says None, write None and omit Status]`. Optionally, have the parser accept a value followed by a separator.

findings.title: The verbatim last-request quote is unfenced, so `## ` or `Status:` lines inside the operator's message change the Last request section's boundaries
findings.body:
The prompt asks for the operator's last message to be quoted verbatim, directly under `## Last request` and before the `Status:` line. There is no fence or blockquote. The parser (session-start.sh:80-89) ends the section at the first `^## ` line and takes the first `^Status:` line.

Operator messages often contain pasted markdown (issue bodies, specs). Observed with the awk: a quoted message containing `## Steps` ends the section early, so the real `Status: Not answered` after it is never read and the status disappears. By the same mechanism, a quoted message that itself contains a line starting `Status: Answered` would be reported as the status ahead of the model's own line. That case needs an unusual message, so it is the rarer one. Both fail toward wrong or missing operator display only; additionalContext is unchanged.
findings.fix: Tell the extractor to quote the request as a `>` blockquote or in a fenced block, so that quoted lines cannot start with `## ` or `Status:`.

findings.title: The prompt-contract test asserts strings already present, so it stays green when the new 'verbatim from the facts block' and status-value instructions are removed
findings.body:
`assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` matches the `<transcript_facts>` block label, which was emitted before this change. It does not match the new instruction that tells the extractor to quote that fact. Removing `[Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above]` keeps the test green. `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Answered'` is implied by the `Partially answered` / `Not answered` assertions, so dropping `Answered` from the allowed values also stays green. The goal names 'the facts-block reference' as something the change must not break, and this test cannot detect that.

A related prompt problem: `bounded_text` allows a last request of up to 4000 characters (pre-compact.sh:140-141). The new section requires quoting it verbatim inside a handoff still capped at 400 words. For a long pasted request the extractor must break either the verbatim rule or the cap. The prompt does not say which wins.
findings.fix: Assert the new instruction text itself, e.g. 'verbatim from the facts block' and 'Use exactly one of: Answered, Partially answered, Not answered'. In the prompt, say how to handle a last request too long to quote within the cap.

findings.title: Парсер принимает строку Status из текста запроса за статус ответа
findings.body: Если последний запрос содержит отдельную строку `Status: Answered`, а извлекатель дословно цитирует его перед фактической строкой `Status: Not answered`, парсер выбирает первую строку и показывает оператору `Answered`. Аналогично заголовок `## ` внутри цитаты завершает поиск до фактического статуса. Это возможно при соблюдении нового требования дословно воспроизводить запрос.
findings.fix: Отделить цитату запроса от поля статуса однозначными маркерами и разбирать статус за пределами цитаты.

findings.title: Длинный запрос делает требования к handoff несовместимыми
findings.body: Для последнего сообщения из более чем 400 коротких слов, которое помещается в существующий предел фактов в 4000 символов, промпт одновременно требует дословно включить весь запрос и ограничить весь handoff 400 словами. Извлекатель не может выполнить оба требования: ему придётся сократить запрос или превысить предел.
findings.fix: Определить приоритет для длинных запросов, например исключить дословную цитату из лимита handoff.

findings.title: No test exercises the end-of-section guard, so a Status: line leaking in from a later section stays green
findings.body:
The goal requires that "status parsing cannot pick up a Status: line from another section". The thing that enforces this is the awk rule `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` at executable_handoff-session-start.sh:83. The new negative case in test_scripts_2834 uses a fixture (`## Goal … ## Key Details
Status: Not answered`) with no `## Last request` section at all, so it only catches the edit that drops the section requirement entirely. The fixtures in 50901 and 50902 put the real Status: line inside Last request and have no Status: in Key Details. Red-making edit that no test catches: delete line 83. Every new and existing test stays green, yet a handoff like `## Last request
<quote>

## Key Details
Status: Answered` (where the model left out the Status line, or wrote it as `**Status:**`, inside Last request) then shows the Key Details text `Status: Answered` to the operator as the last-request status. That is exactly the cross-section leak this negative case says it protects against ("A status outside Last request is ordinary handoff text").
findings.fix: In test_scripts_2834, change the 'status outside Last request' fixture so it does have a `## Last request` section (quote only, no Status: line), followed by `## Key Details\nStatus: Not answered`. Then check it goes red with line 83 removed.

findings.title: Status parser takes the first Status: line in Last request, which can be a line from the verbatim-quoted operator message
findings.body: The prompt tells the extractor to quote the operator's last message verbatim first, then write the `Status:` line (pre-compact.sh:318-320). last_user keeps newlines: it is JSON-encoded via tojson, and the model is told to decode it and copy it exactly. The parser prints and exits on the first `^Status:` line after the heading. If the operator's last message has a line starting with `Status:` (a pasted handoff, CI report or ticket, which is plausible in a repo whose operator works on these handoffs), one of two things happens. (a) A pasted `Status: Answered` gets shown although the model's real line says `Not answered`. That is a wrong status, and it misleads the operator exactly when the request is still open. (b) A pasted unrecognized value such as `Status: in progress` makes the parser exit, and the case filter then drops the status even though a valid one follows. This only happens if the model writes the quote without a `> ` blockquote prefix, which the prompt does not ask for.
findings.fix: Take the last Status: line in the section rather than the first. For example, keep a variable updated on each `/^Status:/` match and print it at the next `## ` heading or at END. The model's own Status line always comes after the quote.

findings.title: Prompt-contract test checks loose substrings that cannot catch a broken prompt/parser contract
findings.body: test_scripts_50900 checks loose substrings of the prompt. `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` is always satisfied by the pre-existing facts block (transcript_facts prints `Last user request:` on every path, pre-compact.sh:113-265) and the pre-existing constraint at :337. It goes red on no #509 edit and does not show that the new `## Last request` instruction refers to the facts block. The other checks (`'## Last request'`, `'Status:'`, `'Answered'`, …) are independent greps anywhere in the prompt. The one thing the injector relies on is a line beginning with `Status:` placed under `## Last request` and before the next `## ` heading. Red-making edits these checks miss: move the `Status: [...]` line under `## Key Details`, or turn it into a bullet (`- Status: ...`). Both keep the test green, but a model that follows the template then produces handoffs the parser at session-start.sh:82-84 never finds a status in, so the 🎯 status line silently never appears.
findings.fix: Drop the 'Last user request' assertion. Pull the `## Last request` block out of the captured prompt (from the heading to the next `## `) and assert_equal it against the exact four expected lines, which pins Status: to line start inside the section.

findings.title: Prompt-contract test 50900 never checks the verbatim-quote instruction; its 'Last user request' check always passes
findings.body:
test_scripts_50900 asserts `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'`. The `<transcript_facts>` block already contains that string on every path, including both `None` fallbacks (executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh ~245, ~262-265). So does the older 'Copy … the last user request exactly' constraint. The check therefore passes whatever this change does.

No assertion pins the main new instruction, `[Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above]`. You can delete it or reword it to allow paraphrase and the test stays green. The goal names the facts-block reference as a correctness condition.

The other checks are loose too:
- `'Answered'` is implied by the `Partially answered` and `Not answered` assertions.
- The checks are independent greps anywhere in the prompt. Moving the `Status:` line under `## Key Details`, or turning it into a bullet (`- Status:`), keeps the test green. A model following that template would then produce handoffs where the parser never finds a status.
findings.fix: Drop the 'Last user request' assertion. Assert the exact instruction text, e.g. "Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above" and 'Use exactly one of: Answered, Partially answered, Not answered'. Better still, extract the `## Last request` block from the captured prompt and assert_equal it against the expected lines.

findings.title: Positive status test covers only 'Not answered'; dropping 'Answered' or 'Partially answered' from the accepted set stays green
findings.body: Only test_scripts_50901 checks a recognized status, and it uses `Not answered`. The rejection case uses `Waiting for a reply`. If `Answered` or `Partially answered` is removed from the `case` allow-list in executable_handoff-session-start.sh, every test stays green, and the operator stops seeing the most common status values. This is partial coverage of an enum, not a vacuous test, and the fix is a few cheap fixtures at the test site.
findings.fix: Assert the systemMessage output for each of the three accepted values.

findings.title: Отрицательный случай не проверяет конец раздела Last request
findings.body: Фикстура помещает Status в Key Details, но не содержит раздела Last request. Поэтому удаление условия выхода из раздела в парсере оставит тест зелёным. В handoff с Last request без строки статуса и следующим разделом Key Details, содержащим Status: Not answered, оператор ошибочно увидит этот статус.
findings.fix: Добавить фикстуру с разделом Last request без статуса и строкой Status в следующем разделе.

findings.title: Prompt puts an unfenced verbatim quote above the Status: line, so `Status:` or `## ` lines in the operator's message change the parsed section
findings.body: The template asks for the operator's last message verbatim directly under `## Last request`, before `Status: [...]`, with no blockquote or fence. Line 338 makes the model decode the JSON literal, so a multi-line message comes back with real newlines. The injector (session-start.sh:81-90) takes the first `^Status:` line and stops at the first `^## `. A pasted markdown heading closes the section early, and the status is silently dropped; running the awk on such input confirmed this. A pasted `Status: Answered` line is shown ahead of the extractor's own value. Only the operator's systemMessage is affected; additionalContext is unchanged.
findings.fix: Put the Status line first in the section and render the quote as a blockquote, e.g. `Status: [...]` followed by `> [each line of the operator's last message, verbatim]`. Quoted lines then cannot match `^Status:` or `^## `.

findings.title: The verbatim-quote instruction conflicts with the kept 400-word handoff cap
findings.body: `[Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above]`, together with line 337 ("copy ... the last user request exactly"), requires the whole message. `bounded_text` (line 141) lets that message run up to 4000 characters plus ` [truncated]`, which is roughly 600 or more words. Line 334 still says "Maximum 400 words in the <handoff> section". When the operator's last message is long (pasted content is a supported case), the extractor has to break one of the two rules: truncate or paraphrase the quote, or overrun the cap and crowd out Relevant Context and Key Details. The prompt doesn't say which rule wins, so outcomes vary between runs. The added quote section makes this conflict concrete in the template.
findings.fix: State the precedence explicitly. For example, have the 400-word cap exclude the Last request quote, or tell the extractor to quote the first N lines verbatim and mark the cut with `[truncated]`.

findings.title: The Last request section has no instruction for `Last user request: None`, and the Status line has no plain-text constraint
findings.body: The facts block emits `Last user request: None` when no human message survives the filters, and on every jq fallback (lines 245 and 265). The new section still tells the extractor to quote "the operator's last real message" and to choose one of three statuses. None of the three fits when there is no request, so the extractor may invent a message from session memory (which line 337 forbids) or pick an arbitrary status. Separately, the parser accepts only the exact strings `Answered`, `Partially answered` or `Not answered` after a column-0 `Status:`. The prompt never says the line must be plain text. A haiku output such as `**Status:** Not answered` or `Status: Not answered.` drops the status without any signal. That failure is contained, because the display just falls back to goal-only. The section also uses three names for one thing: "Last request", "the operator's last real message" and the facts block's "Last user request".
findings.fix: Add `[If the facts block says None, write None and omit Status]`. Spell the line as `Status: <one of: Answered | Partially answered | Not answered>, written plain with no markup or trailing punctuation`. Refer to the source by its label: "the Last user request value in <transcript_facts>".

findings.title: Expired sign-in and genuine 403s are reported as "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet"
findings.body: `isVerdictReadRefusal` treats every 401 and 403, and any error whose message matches /sign-in expired/, as the old-engine refusal. In `waitForVersion` and `codeStatus` this prints "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet" and exits 2, which means still pending. Two cases get the wrong line. (1) The platform token expires and cannot be refreshed mid-wait: `platform-token.ts:72` throws 'The Membrane sign-in expired… Sign in again.', and this code swallows it. (2) A real permission refusal (403) on the read. An agent that sees exit 2 will keep waiting or retry instead of re-authenticating, and the actionable remedy is lost. The goal only asks for the old-engine case to degrade this way. I traced the code but did not confirm which status a real old engine returns. The tests only model 401 and 403, so I cannot tell whether a narrower match is possible.
findings.fix: Narrow the refusal match to what an old engine actually returns (for example the specific status and error code for an unrecognised sessionless command). Let the sign-in-expired and rejected-credential errors propagate so the user sees the sign-in remedy.

findings.title: The operator instructions incorrectly say tree tests run locally
findings.body: Pre-existing: “Tree tests are the exception — they run locally” contradicts the actual test path. `codeTest` dispatches `RunSourceTreeTestsCommand`, and the server enqueues a `SourceRunPayload` with `mode: 'test'` on the worker fleet (`source-trees.service.ts:3237–3253`). The CLI now waits for that remote verdict. An operator following this instruction gets the wrong picture of where tests run, which matters for fixtures and local changes. The same claim appears in SKILL.md:349 and MANUAL.md:335.
findings.fix: Correct all three occurrences to say that tree tests execute on the platform against the selected version, and the CLI waits for their verdict.

findings.title: Follow-up command prints the workspace name without shell quoting
findings.body: The new followUpFlags puts options.workspace into the printed follow-up command without quoting it. The CLI accepts a workspace selected by its full name, so after `code test --workspace 'Acme Inc'` the timeout prints `code status --workspace Acme Inc ...`. Run as printed, the parser reads the workspace as `Acme` and leaves `Inc` as an extra positional argument. The follow-up then fails to select a workspace, or it reaches a different workspace named Acme.
findings.fix: Shell-quote the workspace and session values as separate arguments when building the follow-up command.

findings.title: Code verb usage block omits `test` and the new `status`, so the exit-code and wait contract is not stated
findings.body: The changed paragraph (lines 589-592) tells the agent that `test` queues once and waits and that `status` reads without queuing. The usage block just above it (lines 577-584) lists `pull|diff|push|run|promote|import|drift` and neither `test` nor `status`. The block also gives no `--wait` or `--timeout` flags and no exit codes (0 passed or skipped, 1 failed, 2 pending, 3 untested). The goal depends on an agent reacting correctly to exit 2 by waiting with `code status --wait`, not by re-running `code test`. The CLI's own output prints that follow-up command (code.ts:681, 714), so an agent can recover at run time. But the skill text never states the contract. `test` was already missing from the block before this change; `status` is new in it.
findings.fix: Add `membrane-operator code test [--tree-version <id>] [--wait/--timeout]` and `membrane-operator code status [--tree-version <id>] [--wait]` to the usage block. Add one sentence giving the exit codes and saying that exit 2 means 'run `code status --wait`, not `code test` again'.

findings.title: Unchanged sentence says tree tests run locally, contradicting the changed text about queuing on a worker
findings.body: The changed paragraph above now says `code test` queues the run and waits for a verdict. The `run-source-tree-tests` description says the run executes on a worker. The next paragraph still says 'Tree tests are the exception — they run locally, because a test needs fixtures, not run authority.' An agent reading both cannot tell where tests run. The diff did not touch this sentence, but it sits directly beside the change, which makes the conflict sharper.
findings.fix: Reword to match the queue-and-wait behaviour, or delete the sentence if it is stale.

findings.title: Outer catch-all failure path (and manual unknown-extension outcome) has no notification test, so silencing it again stays green
findings.body: The goal requires that tests fail if a terminal result were silently discarded again. The outer catch at home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/brew-auto-update/index.ts:445-447 (reached when acquireLock throws, e.g. EACCES creating the state dir, or when deps.snapshotExtensions rejects) is the one failure exit that no test drives: every fixture's snapshotExtensions resolves and the temp lock path is always writable. Reverting line 447 to `return reportFailure(...)` (the pre-change shape) would leave the entire suite green while startup and manual both go silent on those failures — exactly the defect issue 022 fixed. Relatedly, the only test of the `complete` + "extension changes could not be verified" outcome was retargeted from manual to startup, so the manual-always-reports contract for that outcome is no longer covered, and the startup PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 / PI_OFFLINE skip tests never assert that startup stays silent.
findings.fix: Add a test with `snapshotExtensions: async () => { throw new Error("boom") }` (or an unwritable lock parent) for both triggers asserting exactly one `warning` notification containing "Pi update failed"; add a manual-trigger variant of the unknown-extension-state test expecting one `info` notification; assert `notifications` is empty in the startup-disabled case.

findings.title: Тесты не обнаружат потерю уведомлений об ошибках получения блокировки
findings.body: Если создание каталога блокировки завершается ошибкой, управление попадает во внешний catch. Добавленные тесты проверяют ошибки команд, но не этот путь. Если здесь снова вернуть результат без finish, пользователь перестанет получать предупреждение при каждой такой ошибке, а тесты останутся зелёными. Цель изменения и правила проекта требуют проверять этот путь отказа.
findings.fix: Добавить проверку ошибки получения блокировки, которая ожидает предупреждение для пользователя.

findings.title: Описание follow-up неверно утверждает, что уведомление отправляется для каждого результата
findings.body: Документ утверждает, что все конечные результаты передаются в ui.notify. При запуске skip, contention и up-to-date намеренно не вызывают ui.notify. Это противоречит политике, записанной в исходном issue, и может дать исполнителю follow-up неверное представление о текущем поведении.
findings.fix: Уточнить, что все результаты проходят через finish/shouldNotify, а ui.notify вызывается согласно политике для соответствующего триггера.

findings.title: Outer-catch failure path (lock/snapshot errors) has no test, so reverting it to silent passes the suite
findings.body: The goal requires that the tests fail if a terminal result is silently discarded again. Seven of the eight `finish` call sites have a test that pins their notification. The exceptions are line 386 (startup-disabled, which is silent by policy) and line 447, the outer `catch`. That catch is reached when `acquireLock` throws (for example, `mkdir` of the lock parent fails with EACCES/ENOTDIR on an unwritable or misconfigured XDG_STATE_HOME) or when `snapshotExtensions` throws. No test in tests/pi-brew-auto-update.test.ts reaches it: a search for 'without blocking startup' and for lock-path failure fixtures finds nothing, and every fixture uses a valid `temporaryLockPath()`. If line 447 went back to `return reportFailure(...)`, the whole suite would stay green. Meanwhile an unwritable state directory would fail silently on every startup, which is the defect issue 022 exists to fix.
findings.fix: Add a startup test whose `lockPath` sits under a regular file (so `mkdir` fails with ENOTDIR) or whose `snapshotExtensions` throws. Assert status `failed` and exactly one `warning` notification containing 'Pi update failed without blocking startup'.

findings.title: Startup-silence policy for `skipped` results is not asserted
findings.body: The settled policy says startup stays silent on non-failure outcomes. For `contended`, the cross-process lock test asserts `notifications` is empty. For `skipped`, nothing does. The `disables startup only when PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE is zero` test passes a throwaway `fakeUi().ui` and checks only status and calls, and there is no startup PI_OFFLINE test. If `shouldNotify` were changed to notify `skipped` regardless of trigger, everyone who set PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 or PI_OFFLINE=1 would get 'Pi startup update is disabled.' on every session, and no test would fail. Issue 022's scope asks to 'cover the selected startup notification policy with a nearby control'. This skipped-at-startup control is missing.
findings.fix: In the PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 test, keep the startup `notifications` and assert they are empty, mirroring the startup contention test at line 437.

findings.title: finish() is repeated at eight return sites, so "every result is notified" depends on discipline
findings.body:
The goal's invariant is that no terminal result is returned without going through finish/shouldNotify. Today it holds only because each of the eight `return` statements in `runBrewAutoUpdate` (lines 382, 386, 394, 410, 414, 421, 444, 447) wraps its result in `finish(trigger, ui, …)` and passes `trigger` and `ui` through by hand.

A future early return that forgets the wrapper brings back the silent-discard bug issue 022 fixed. The tests catch that only if the new branch happens to have a notification test.

Calling `finish` once would make the invariant hold by construction, and outputs, levels and `shouldNotify` decisions would stay the same. The only order change is that `ui.notify` would run after `lock.release()`, and nothing observes that order.
findings.fix: Move the current body into an inner `runSequence(trigger, deps)` that returns `{ result, installedUpdate }`, and have `runBrewAutoUpdate` call `finish` once on its return value.

findings.title: No test covers the outer-catch failure return, so that path could go silent again without any test failing
findings.body:
The change sends each terminal return through `finish`. One of them is the outer catch at `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/brew-auto-update/index.ts:445-447`: `return finish(trigger, ui, reportFailure(`Pi update failed without blocking startup: ${detail}`))`. No test reaches it. A search of tests/ for "without blocking startup" finds nothing. Every failure fixture makes `deps.exec` fail, and the inner per-step handlers catch those failures. Every fixture's `snapshotExtensions` resolves, and every fixture's temp lock path is writable.

The outer catch is reachable in real use. `acquireLock` throws on any mkdir error other than EEXIST, for example EACCES or ENOTDIR when `XDG_STATE_HOME/pi` is unwritable or is a regular file. A rejecting `snapshotExtensions` also lands there.

If line 447 went back to a bare `return reportFailure(...)`, which is the pre-fix shape, the suite would still pass. Startup would again fail silently on every run, and the manual command would show nothing. That is the defect issue 022 fixed. The goal requires the tests to fail if a terminal result is silently discarded again, and this return is not protected.

The manual-trigger variant of the `complete` + "extension changes could not be verified" outcome is also no longer tested, because that test was retargeted to startup.
findings.fix: Add a test whose `lockPath` sits under a regular file (e.g. `writeFile(join(root,'state'),'')`, then `lockPath = join(root,'state','pi','lock')`), or whose `snapshotExtensions` throws. Run it with both `startup` and `manual` and assert `status: "failed"` plus exactly one `warning` notification containing the error detail. Optionally add a manual-trigger variant of the unknown-extension-state test that expects one `info` notification.

findings.title: No test checks that skipped outcomes stay silent at startup
findings.body:
The settled policy keeps startup silent on non-failure outcomes. The startup skip branches return through `finish` at `index.ts:380-386`, and no test checks what the user sees from them.

- `disables startup only when PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE is zero` passes a throwaway `fakeUi().ui` and only asserts `status` and `calls`.
- The PI_OFFLINE test only uses the `manual` trigger.
- Only contention and up-to-date are asserted silent at startup.

Suppose a regression made skipped results notify at startup, e.g. a `status === "skipped"` clause in `shouldNotify`. A user who set PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 would then see "Pi startup update is disabled." on every Pi session, and the suite would stay green.
findings.fix: In the PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 test, keep the startup `notifications` and assert `toEqual([])`. Add a startup-trigger PI_OFFLINE case with the same assertion.

findings.title: The manual command can now show a failure message that mentions startup
findings.body:
The message text "Pi update failed without blocking startup: ..." already existed, but the old code always discarded it. The change now passes it to `ui.notify` for both triggers, including `/brew-auto-update-now`.

If `acquireLock` throws during a manual run (e.g. EACCES creating the lock directory), the user who asked for an update reads "Pi update failed without blocking startup: EACCES ...". The wording refers to a startup that did not happen.

The per-step failure messages are trigger-neutral, so this is the only terminal message whose wording depends on the trigger.
findings.fix: Make the message trigger-neutral (e.g. "Pi update failed: ${detail}"), or add the startup suffix only when `trigger === "startup"`.

findings.title: Нет проверки уведомления при ошибке получения блокировки
findings.body: Новые тесты ошибок вызывают сбой только внутри команды обновления. Если создание каталога блокировки завершится ошибкой, например из-за отсутствия прав, обработается внешний catch в runBrewAutoUpdate. Его можно снова изменить так, чтобы он возвращал failed без уведомления, и эти тесты останутся зелёными. Пользователь снова не увидит причину остановки обновления.
findings.fix: Добавить в этот набор сценарий с ошибкой создания блокировки и проверить предупреждение для пользователя.

findings.title: Follow-up issue wrongly says every terminal result is passed to ui.notify
findings.body: The follow-up issue says every terminal result, including skip, contention and up-to-date, is passed to `ui.notify`. In fact `shouldNotify` deliberately suppresses those outcomes at startup. The claim contradicts the notification policy recorded in the original issue 022 and later in this same issue. Anyone picking up the follow-up would start from a wrong picture of current behaviour.
findings.fix: Say that every result goes through finish/shouldNotify, and that `ui.notify` is called only for the results the policy allows for each trigger.

findings.title: Issue 022 is left open with no Resolution section even though this change implemented its scope
findings.body: Under the repository-issues convention (.claude/skills/repository-issues/SKILL.md:25), a closed issue keeps its `## Why this exists` section as filed and adds a `closed` date and a `## Resolution` section. Closed issues such as 2026-08-14-001 follow this pattern. The past-tense problem text is therefore expected, not stale. The actual gap is that issue 022 still has `status: "open"` and no Resolution, even though this change did the work in its Scope: it surfaces failures through finish/shouldNotify, removes `UpdateUi.setStatus` and replaces the assertions that expected no notifications. Follow-up issue 007 also states that 022 "fixed" the extension. As a result, a reader of 022 sees an open issue whose problem description no longer matches the code, and only the Open decisions section hints that the work landed.
findings.fix: Close 022 with `python3 scripts/issues close 2026-08-21-022 --resolution "..."`, recording the outcome: failures notify at warning on every trigger, manual results always notify, and setStatus was removed. Following the skill's close-time check, update the stale `short_description` with `scripts/issues edit`, and leave `## Why this exists` as filed.

findings.title: Outer catch-all failure path (`Pi update failed without blocking startup`) has no notification assertion
findings.body: The goal requires that tests fail if any terminal result is silently discarded again. Every inner failure return (exec throws, killed, nonzero code) now has a test asserting a `warning` notification. The outer `catch` at index.ts:445-447 is the exception: no test makes acquireLock or snapshotExtensions throw. `rg 'without blocking' tests/` returns nothing. If that line reverted to `return reportFailure(...)` without `finish`, which is exactly the shape the original defect had, the whole suite would stay green. The path is reachable in practice. For example, `mkdir(dirname(lockPath))` or `mkdir(lockPath)` throws EACCES/EROFS when the XDG state dir is not writable, and that failure would again be invisible on every startup. There is a related gap on the other side of the policy: startup silence for `skipped` (PI_OFFLINE=1 or PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0) is never asserted. The `disables startup only when PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE is zero` test discards `fakeUi().notifications`, so a regression that made startup nag on every skip would also go unnoticed. The production code is correct today; this only weakens the regression guard the goal asks for.
findings.fix: Add a test that points `lockPath` under a regular file (so `mkdir` throws ENOTDIR). For both `startup` and `manual`, assert `status: "failed"` and exactly one `warning` notification containing the error detail. In the PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 test, also assert that startup notifications are `[]`.

findings.title: Manual command can now show the catch-all message "failed without blocking startup"
findings.body:
The catch-all text "Pi update failed without blocking startup: ..." existed before, but it was always discarded. `finish` now sends it to `ui.notify` for both triggers, including `/brew-auto-update-now`.

If `acquireLock` throws during a manual run (e.g. EACCES on the state dir), the user who explicitly asked for an update reads a message about a startup that never happened. The per-step failure messages are trigger-neutral, so this is the only terminal message whose wording fits one trigger and not the other.
findings.fix: Make the prefix depend on the trigger, e.g. `trigger === "startup" ? "Pi update failed without blocking startup" : "Pi update failed"`, or make it trigger-neutral.

findings.title: Headless print/JSON mode gets the update result only through ui.notify, which does nothing there
findings.body: In Pi's print/JSON mode `ui.notify` does nothing, and the calling handler throws away the returned result. A failed startup update is therefore invisible to scripts. The reviewer says this existed before the change, and the new follow-up issue 007 records it.

findings.title: A failing later step hides an update that was already installed
findings.body: If Homebrew upgrades Pi and the following `pi update --extensions` then fails, the early return reports only the failure. The accumulated `installedUpdates` are left out of the notification, so the user is not told that the new Pi version needs a restart. The reviewer says this behaviour existed before the change.
findings.fix: Add the already-installed update and the restart requirement to the failure message.

findings.title: Описание утверждает, что уведомляются все результаты запуска
findings.body: В документе сказано, что каждый конечный результат передаётся через ui.notify. Однако shouldNotify намеренно подавляет при запуске результаты skipped, contended и up-to-date. Это противоречит записанной политике и может ввести читателя follow-up issue в заблуждение.
findings.fix: Уточнить, что через ui.notify передаются результаты, выбранные политикой уведомлений.

findings.title: No test checks that skipped outcomes (offline / PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0) stay silent at startup
findings.body:
The settled policy keeps startup silent on non-failure outcomes. Tests pin that for `contended`, `complete`/up-to-date and unknown-extension, but not for `skipped`. The only startup skip test, "disables startup only when PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE is zero", passes a throwaway `fakeUi().ui` and asserts only status and calls. The PI_OFFLINE test runs only with the manual trigger.

An edit like `if (trigger === "manual" || status === "skipped") return true` in `shouldNotify` would leave the suite green. Every user with updates disabled or offline mode on would then see "Pi startup update is disabled." or "Pi update skipped: offline mode is active." on every session. Issue 022 asks for the startup policy to be covered with a nearby control.
findings.fix: In the PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 test, keep the startup `notifications` and assert `toEqual([])`. Add a startup-trigger PI_OFFLINE case with the same assertion, next to the existing manual control.

findings.title: finish() is repeated at eight return sites; one exit point would guarantee no result skips it
findings.body: The goal's first condition is that no terminal result is returned without going through finish/shouldNotify. Right now that holds only because each of the eight `return` statements in `runBrewAutoUpdate` (lines 382, 386, 394, 410, 414, 421, 444, 447) wraps its result in `finish(trigger, ui, …)` and threads `trigger` and `ui` through by hand. If someone adds an early return later and forgets the wrapper, the silent-discard bug comes back, and the tests only catch it if that particular branch has a notification test. Simpler version: move the current body into an inner function that returns `{ result, installedUpdate }` (or derive `installedUpdate` from `status === "complete"` plus the update message), then make `runBrewAutoUpdate` a single `return finish(trigger, ui, …)`. Outputs, levels and the shouldNotify decisions stay identical. `finish` cannot throw because `notify` swallows errors, so the outer try/catch behaves the same. The one ordering change is that the synchronous `ui.notify` would run after the async `lock.release()` instead of before it. Nothing observes that order: release only removes this process's own lock directory, and no caller watches the notification relative to it.
findings.fix: Rename the current body to an inner `runSequence(trigger, deps)` that returns plain results, and have `runBrewAutoUpdate` call `finish` once on its return value.

findings.title: Failure-notification tests use substring matches where the exact message is deterministic
findings.body: The timeout, nonzero-exit, exec-throw and startup-failure tests check the notification with `toContain("Homebrew metadata refresh")` / `toContain("network failed")` / `toContain("timed out")`. The text is fully deterministic: for example "Homebrew metadata refresh failed: network failed" and "Homebrew metadata refresh timed out after 5 minutes." Nothing in it is unstable, so the loosening isn't justified. Edits that stay green: notifying with a message that drifts from `result.message` (for example a prefixed or duplicated detail), or a wrong timeout minute count such as `Math.round(deps.timeoutMs / 60)`. The success-path tests in the same file already compare `{ message, level }` exactly, so these tests are weaker than their neighbours for no reason.
findings.fix: Assert `expect(notifications).toEqual([{ message: result.message, level: "warning" }])` plus `expect(result.message).toBe("Homebrew metadata refresh failed: network failed")` (and the exact timeout string), matching the exact-equality style the success tests already use.

findings.title: Outer-catch failure path (and 3rd-step failure) of runBrewAutoUpdate has no notification test
findings.body: The goal says the tests must fail if a result is silently discarded again. The `finish(...)` in the outer `catch` of `runBrewAutoUpdate` (message "Pi update failed without blocking startup: …", index.ts ~447) is reached when something other than `deps.exec` throws, e.g. `acquireLock`'s mkdir failing or `deps.snapshotExtensions` rejecting. No test covers it: grepping the test file finds no "without blocking" assertion, and the throw test at line 351 throws from `exec`, which the inner try/catch handles. Reverting that one `finish` to a bare `return reportFailure(...)` would leave every test green, which is the silent-discard regression the goal names. Only the first step (`brew update`) is exercised for failure, timeout and throw. Failures in the `brew upgrade` and `pi update` steps are never asserted to notify.
findings.fix: Add a test where `snapshotExtensions` rejects (or the lock directory cannot be created) and assert one `warning` notification containing "Pi update failed without blocking startup". Optionally make the failure tests table-driven over all three steps.

findings.title: Startup silence for skipped outcomes (offline / disabled) is not asserted
findings.body: The policy says startup stays silent on skip, but nothing checks it. The PI_OFFLINE test uses the manual trigger only. The PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 test at line 303 passes `fakeUi().ui` and discards the notifications, so it checks only the status. If `shouldNotify` were changed to notify on startup skips, every test would still pass. The startup-contended silence is covered at line 424, so this is a partial gap in the policy matrix.
findings.fix: Keep the `fakeUi()` instance in the line 303 test and assert its notifications are empty for the startup case and contain the skip message for the manual case. Add a startup + PI_OFFLINE silence assertion.

findings.title: Unrequested removal of UpdateUi.setStatus from the exported interface
findings.body: The goal concerns routing outcomes through `ui.notify`. The diff also removes `setStatus` from the exported `UpdateUi` interface and from the test fake. Nothing under `home/` or `tests/` calls `setStatus` (grep finds no other use), and issue 022 records it as declared-but-never-called. Removing it is harmless for the real `ctx.ui`, which still satisfies the narrower interface, so this is a small bundled cleanup rather than a defect. The issue's Scope section does not list it.
findings.fix: Either keep it as a separate cleanup or mention it in the issue's recorded decisions.

findings.title: Positional boolean `installedUpdate` on finish() is unreadable at the call site
findings.body: `finish(trigger, ui, { status: "complete", message }, updateMessage !== undefined)` (line 444) passes a bare boolean as the fourth argument, defaulted to `false` on line 270. A reader of the call has to open `finish` and `shouldNotify` to learn what `true` means. The flag is only meaningful for one call site, and the other eight pass nothing. Deriving it inside `finish`, or naming it with an options object or a distinct status, would keep the notify policy readable. `levelForStatus` is a second small helper used only by `finish`.
findings.fix: Fold the flag into a named field (for example `finish(trigger, ui, result, { installed: true })`), or inline `levelForStatus` into `finish`.

findings.title: Startup silence for skipped outcomes (offline / disabled) is not asserted
findings.body: The policy in `shouldNotify` is that startup stays silent on skipped, contended and up-to-date results. Startup silence is asserted for up-to-date, unknown-state and contended. The `PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0` test (around line 303) only checks the call counts. No test runs `startup` with `PI_OFFLINE=1`. If the startup skip paths started notifying on every session, the exact nagging the policy comment rules out, no test would fail. The manual-offline test is the only coverage of the offline skip.
findings.fix: Add a `fakeUi` notifications check (`toEqual([])`) to the startup-disabled test, and a startup+`PI_OFFLINE=1` case.

findings.title: Не проверяется уведомление при ошибке захвата блокировки
findings.body: Новый тест с исключением из deps.exec достигает внутреннего catch, но не внешнего catch в index.ts:445–447. Все фикстуры создают доступный каталог блокировки; ни одна не вызывает ошибку acquireLock. Поэтому удаление finish из внешнего catch оставит тестовые утверждения выполненными, хотя ошибка доступа к каталогу состояния снова станет невидимой пользователю. Путь ошибки существовал раньше, но новое уведомление для него осталось без проверки. Это противоречит требованию покрытия каждого пути ошибки в ~/.claude/shared/testing.md и критерию регрессионного теста в docs/solutions/design-patterns/semantic-regression-tests-over-source-shape.md.
findings.fix: Добавить в существующий набор случай, где родительский путь блокировки занят обычным файлом. Проверить failed, отсутствие вызовов exec и одно уведомление warning с причиной ошибки.

findings.title: No test covers the outer catch path's finish(), the one failure return not driven by an exec result
findings.body: index.ts:445-447 turns any thrown error outside the per-step exec try/catch into a `failed` result with the message 'Pi update failed without blocking startup: ...'. A real case is `acquireLock` throwing because the state directory is unwritable (mkdir EACCES). Every new failure test uses `exec` returning a nonzero code, `killed`, or throwing inside the step try, so they all reach a different `finish` call. If the catch-branch `finish` were reverted to a bare `return reportFailure(...)`, which is the original silent-discard defect, every test would still pass. The goal says the tests must fail if a result is silently discarded again. A startup-trigger test with an unusable `lockPath`, or a `snapshotExtensions` that throws, should assert one `warning` notification containing 'failed without blocking startup'. The same gap applies to failures in steps 2 and 3 (`brew upgrade`, `pi update --extensions`). Only step 1 is tested for failure.
findings.fix: Add a startup-trigger test that makes acquireLock or snapshotExtensions throw and asserts a single warning notification. Optionally add one failure case at the `pi update --extensions` step.

findings.title: Startup-skip silence for PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 is not asserted; the notification sink is discarded
findings.body: The goal requires startup to stay silent on skipped outcomes. The 'disables startup only when PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE is zero' test calls `runBrewAutoUpdate("startup", fakeUi().ui, ...)`, which drops the notifications array. It never checks that nothing was notified, or that the manual caller was notified. The offline startup skip has no silence assertion either. The offline test now uses the manual trigger, and startup silence is asserted only for contention and up-to-date. A regression that notifies on the disabled-startup skip, such as a hard-coded `manual` trigger or a changed `shouldNotify` for that branch, would go unnoticed.
findings.fix: Keep the `fakeUi()` result in this test and assert `notifications` is empty for startup. Assert the info notification for the manual run if it is meant to report.

findings.title: Issue 022 still reads as an unfixed defect and refers to a name this change removed
findings.body: The change removes `UpdateUi.setStatus`, but the 'Why this exists' section (lines ~24-26) still says '`UpdateUi.setStatus` is declared but never called'. The Scope section still says 'Demonstrate the red state...' and the issue front matter stays `status: "open"`. The Open decisions section was rewritten as settled, so the document now mixes a fix-pending description with a fix-delivered decision record. The 'Why this exists' text is historical, so this is minor. A reader will not see that the interface member was dropped, or that the issue was completed by this commit. Also, the doc cites `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local` as the `warning` precedent, but the path is the single file `agents-local.ts`.
findings.fix: Note that `setStatus` was removed as dead code, correct the `agents-local.ts` path, and close the issue or state what remains open.

findings.title: Contended message rewording is a user-visible change not recorded in the issue docs
findings.body: The contended message changed from 'another Pi process owns the update lock' to 'a Pi update is already running'. The old text matched the code's meaning, since the lock is held by another process. The new text is now surfaced to the user at info level. The same message is also returned when stale-lock reclamation loses a race or the retry loop is exhausted, so 'already running' is not strictly guaranteed. The change is not mentioned in issue 022's recorded decisions. The wording is cosmetic and the impact is contained.
findings.fix: Optional: keep the original wording, or mention the new message in the issue.

findings.title: Ошибка получения блокировки осталась без проверки уведомления
findings.body: Добавленный тест с исключением из exec достигает внутреннего catch в index.ts:408. Ни один тест не достигает внешнего catch в index.ts:445, где этот diff тоже добавляет уведомление. Например, обычный файл вместо родительского каталога lockPath вызывает ошибку mkdir до запуска команд. Если вернуть прежний тихий return только во внешнем catch, существующие проверки этого не обнаружат, а пользователь снова не увидит причину остановки обновления.
findings.fix: Добавить в этот suite сценарий с файлом вместо родительского каталога lockPath. Проверить результат failed, отсутствие запущенных команд и одно уведомление warning с причиной ошибки.

findings.title: Startup gate silences the 'extension changes could not be verified' outcome, and a test pins that silence
findings.body: The terminal `complete` result for `extensionChangeUnknown` is passed to `finish` with `installedUpdate = (updateMessage !== undefined)`, which is false. At startup `shouldNotify` therefore returns false, and the message 'Pi package update completed; extension changes could not be verified.' is never shown. This is the case where `pi update --extensions` exited 0 but a snapshot failed, so an update may well have been installed. The user is not told to restart, and the only signal that something went wrong with verification is dropped. This is the same kind of silent discard the change is meant to remove. The test 'stays silent at startup on an unknown extension state…' asserts `notifications` is `[]`, so it locks the silence in. Observed: the gate returns false. Inferred: an update can be missed. It does match the literal policy 'silent unless something was updated', so this is a policy gap and not a bug against the stated goal.
findings.fix: Treat the unverified-extension outcome as notify-worthy at startup, for example by passing `true` for `installedUpdate` when `extensionChangeUnknown`, or by using `warning` for it. Alternatively, record it in the issue's settled policy as intentionally silent.

findings.title: Startup silence on skipped outcomes (PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0, PI_OFFLINE) is not asserted
findings.body: The policy in `shouldNotify` says startup stays silent on skipped results. The 'disables startup only when PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE is zero' test calls `runBrewAutoUpdate("startup", fakeUi().ui, ...)`, discards the notifications array and checks only call counts. The PI_OFFLINE test uses only the manual trigger, so no test runs startup with `PI_OFFLINE=1`. Startup silence is pinned only for the contended, up-to-date and unknown-state cases. If `shouldNotify` started notifying on startup skips (the nagging the policy rules out), or a branch hard-coded the `manual` trigger, no test would fail. Some added tests also compare notifications against `result.message` rather than literal expected text, so part of the assertion comes from the implementation itself.
findings.fix: Keep the `fakeUi()` instance in the disabled-startup test and assert `notifications` is `[]` for startup, plus the expected skip message for manual. Add a startup + `PI_OFFLINE=1` case asserting no notifications. Use literal expected messages where possible.

findings.title: The catch-all failure path and the startup skip path have no test that can go red
findings.body: Goal requires that no terminal result is returned without passing finish. Two of those exits have no notification assertion. (1) The outer `catch` at index.ts:445-447 (for example `acquireLock` throwing on mkdir EACCES) is exercised by no test. Changing that line to `return reportFailure(...)` without `finish` leaves the whole suite green, which is the silent-discard regression the change is meant to prevent. (2) The startup skip branches (`PI_OFFLINE=1`, `PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0`) are only tested with the manual trigger. The 'disables startup only when PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE is zero' test asserts call counts and never `notifications`. Making `shouldNotify` return true for a startup `skipped` result would therefore stay green, while the stated policy is that startup stays silent on non-failure outcomes. Only startup contention and startup up-to-date are pinned as silent. Failures at the second or third step (`brew upgrade`, `pi update`) are also untested, though they share the same `finish` helper.
findings.fix: Add a test where the lock directory is unwritable (or `deps.lockPath` sits under a file) and assert one warning notification. Add startup assertions for `PI_OFFLINE=1` and `PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0` that `notifications` is `[]`.

findings.title: Issue 022 cites a nonexistent agents-local directory and is out of date after the fix
findings.body: The recorded decision says the `warning` level 'matches the convention already used by `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local`'. That path is not a directory. The extension is the single file `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local.ts`, which calls `ctx.ui.notify(warning, "warning")`. The decision therefore cites a reference that cannot be opened as written. The doc is also stale in other places. 'Why this exists' (~lines 24-26) still says `UpdateUi.setStatus` is declared but never called, even though this change removes it. Scope still says 'Demonstrate the red state…'. The front matter remains `status: "open"` while Open decisions now reads as settled.
findings.fix: Change the reference to `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local.ts`, note that `setStatus` was removed as dead code, and close the issue or state what remains open.

findings.title: No test covers the notification from runBrewAutoUpdate's outer catch, or failures at steps 2 and 3
findings.body: The new throw test throws from `deps.exec`, which reaches the inner per-step catch (index.ts ~408). No test reaches the outer `catch` at index.ts:445-447, where this diff also routes the result through `finish(...)` with the message 'Pi update failed without blocking startup: …'. That path runs when something other than `exec` throws, for example `acquireLock` failing on mkdir (an unwritable state directory, or a regular file where the lockPath parent should be) or `deps.snapshotExtensions` rejecting. Every fixture creates a usable lock directory. Reverting that line to a bare `return reportFailure(...)`, which is the original silent-discard defect, would leave the whole suite green. The goal explicitly requires tests that fail if a terminal result bypasses `finish`. Failures at the second and third steps (`brew upgrade`, `pi update --extensions`) are also never asserted to notify. Only step 1 is exercised for non-zero exit, timeout and throw.
findings.fix: Add a case where the lockPath parent is a regular file (or `snapshotExtensions` rejects), next to a passing control. Assert `failed`, that no exec calls ran, and exactly one `warning` notification containing the failure reason, for both the startup and manual triggers. Optionally make the failure tests table-driven over all three steps.

findings.title: `code test --json` output changed from `{ version: … }` to the bare version object
