findings.body: Before this change, `codeTest` printed `JSON.stringify(result)`, where `result` is the `run-source-tree-tests` output `{ version: SourceTreeVersion }`. Now every path, including `--no-wait`, goes through `renderTestVersion`, which prints `JSON.stringify(version)`, so the `version` wrapper is gone. A script or agent that parses `code test --json` and reads `.version.testsStatus` now gets `undefined` and loses the verdict. The goal only asks for queue-once-and-wait plus exit codes; it never mentions changing the JSON shape. No doc or README notes the change, and no test pins the old shape: `cli.code.test.ts` dropped its `--json`-free assertion, and the new tests pin the bare shape. Searching the repo turned up no checked-in consumer of the old shape, so the impact is limited to external or agent callers.
findings.fix: In `codeTest`, print `{ version }` for `--json` (at least on the `--no-wait` path, which is otherwise unchanged), or document the new shape in the README/MANUAL where `code test` is described.

findings.title: Отказ поставить тесты в очередь возвращает код проваленного теста
findings.body: Если engine отвечает ошибкой `source_tree_tests_not_queued`, ошибка выходит из `codeTest` и общий обработчик `runCode` возвращает 1. По заданному контракту отказ engine должен возвращать 2; вызывающий процесс получает результат, который означает провал тестов, хотя запуск не состоялся.
findings.fix: Обработать отказ engine внутри `codeTest` и вернуть 2 с причиной отказа.

findings.title: Режим без ожидания сообщает успех для незавершённого запуска
findings.body: При `code test --no-wait`, когда engine возвращает `pending`, команда печатает этот статус, но всегда выходит с кодом 0. Контракт требует код 2 для незавершённого запуска, поэтому автоматизация может принять ещё не полученный verdict за успешный.
findings.fix: Вернуть код, который возвращает `renderTestVersion`, вместо безусловного 0.

findings.title: The final poll interval ends at the deadline without a read, so `--timeout` ≤ 5 s never reads a verdict
findings.body: In `waitForVersion` the loop calls `waitForNextPoll(effectiveDeadline)`, which sleeps `min(5000, deadline - now)`, then breaks as soon as `now >= deadline`. `readUntilDeadline` also fails immediately when no time is left. So the read that would follow the last capped sleep never happens. With `code test --timeout 5` or shorter, no verdict is read at all: the command reports `pending` and exits 2 even if the run finished within the window. With longer timeouts, the last stretch (up to 5 s) before the deadline is dead time. The same applies to `code status --wait` after its first `pending` read; the existing test at cli.code.verdict.test.ts:636 pins this behavior for `--timeout 5`.
findings.fix: After a sleep that reaches the deadline, take one final read with a short grace bound instead of breaking, or stop the last sleep short of the deadline so the read fits inside it. Reading immediately after queuing isn't useful for `code test`, since the run was only just queued.

findings.title: An expired or revoked sign-in is reported as "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet" and exits 2
findings.body: `isVerdictReadRefusal` returns true for any 401/403, for any error whose message matches /sign-in expired/, and for any 401/403 anywhere in the `cause` chain. The dispatch promise wraps more than the list request: `dispatchUnattached` resolves `--workspace` through `/operator/overview`, and `callWithPlatformToken` calls `platformToken.get()`. `get()` throws "The Membrane sign-in expired and could not be refreshed. Sign in again." (`platform-token.ts:72`) before any request when a stale token can't be refreshed. Both sit inside the dispatch, so a dead sign-in on `code status --workspace acme` prints `this engine cannot answer the verdict yet` and exits 2, not the sign-in message with exit 1. `code test` does the same if the token dies during the wait. A 401/403 from the overview lookup, wrapped by `rejectedCredentialError`, is misclassified the same way. The code comment is also wrong: refresh failure isn't only "after the original 401". Note that against a real old engine the refresh succeeds and the retried 401 arrives wrapped in `rejectedCredentialError`. So dropping the cause recursion, as originally proposed, would break the old-engine detection. The verdict tests only pass through the regex because their fake server has no refresh route.
findings.fix: Drop the `/sign-in expired/` regex: a refresh failure is a credential failure, not an engine refusal. Classify as a refusal only a 401/403 whose ApiError came from the `list-source-tree-versions` request itself (match on the request target the ApiError carries), whether direct or as the `cause` of `rejectedCredentialError`. Errors from the overview lookup and from token refresh then reach the `runCode` catch with their own "Sign in again" message and exit 1. Fix the comment to match.

findings.title: Verdict polling hand-writes its schedule, timeout race, symbol error and AbortController plumbing instead of using Effect
findings.body:
CODING_STANDARDS.md → Effect makes `.claude/skills/effect-best-practices/SKILL.md` binding, and the new code breaks several of its rules:
- `waitForVersion` is a `while` loop around `waitForNextPoll`, a thin wrapper over `Effect.sleep`. SKILL.md:21 and the `no-sleep-in-loop` lint rule ask for `Effect.repeat` with `Schedule.spaced`; moving the sleep into a helper hides the loop from the lint rule.
- `readUntilDeadline` builds its own `Effect.raceFirst` between the read and `Effect.sleep(remaining)`, with a `remaining <= 0` special case. SKILL.md:22 asks for `Effect.timeout` or `timeoutOrElse`.
- The timeout is the `unique symbol` `VERDICT_READ_TIMED_OUT`, matched by comparing `outcome.error === VERDICT_READ_TIMED_OUT` rather than recovered by tag. That forces the `as VerdictReadError` casts.
- The request promise is created eagerly, and one shared `AbortController` is passed by hand through `waitForVersion`, `listVersion` and `readUntilDeadline`.

`Effect.tryPromise({ try: (signal) => dispatch(..., signal), catch })` combined with `Effect.timeoutOrElse` aborts the request when it times out, with no manual controller. The repo already uses this pattern at engine/api/src/account/companies/logo-dev-discovery.ts:67-90. The current code works, so this is cleanup.
findings.fix: Use a `Data.TaggedError` for the timeout. Wrap each read in `Effect.tryPromise({ try: (signal) => dispatch(cmd, input, signal), catch })`, bound it with `Effect.timeoutOrElse`, and poll with `Effect.repeat(..., { schedule: Schedule.spaced('5 seconds'), until })`.

findings.title: A catchTag that re-fails the same error, a repeated error constructor, and a misnamed error for the queue call
findings.body:
`readUntilDeadline` ends with `.pipe(Effect.catchTag('VerdictReadFailed', (error) => Effect.fail(error)))`, which catches an error only to fail with it unchanged. It does nothing, and the cast after it is still needed.

`new VerdictReadFailed({ cause, message: cause instanceof Error ? cause.message : String(cause) })` is written out three times: in codeTest, readUntilDeadline and listVersion.

`codeTest` also wraps a failure of `run-source-tree-tests` (the queue call, not a read) in `VerdictReadFailed`, so the error's tag names the wrong operation.

`timeoutSeconds` assigns to a local and returns it on the next line. The behaviour is correct throughout; this is cleanup only.
findings.fix: Remove the no-op `catchTag`. Move the `VerdictReadFailed` construction into one `catch` helper, and give the queue failure its own tag or a neutral name.

findings.title: code test --no-wait возвращает успех для pending и failed
findings.body: Ветка --no-wait всегда возвращает 0 после вывода статуса. Поэтому вызывающий скрипт получает успешный код для pending и failed. Это нарушает заданный контракт code test: 2 для pending и 1 для failed. Тест cli.code.test.ts также закрепляет 0 для pending.
findings.fix: Вернуть результат renderTestVersion вместо безусловного 0.

findings.title: An expired sign-in (or any 401/403) is reported as "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet" with exit 2
findings.body:
`isVerdictReadRefusal` treats every 401, every 403, and any error whose message matches /sign-in expired/ (or carries such a cause) as an old engine refusing the read. Its comment says: "A platform-token refresh reports this after the original 401, so treat it as a verdict read refusal." That is not the only place the message comes from. `storedCredentialSource.get()` (`claude-plugin/src/client/platform-token.ts:84-85`) refreshes an expired access token *before any request is sent*, and on failure throws the same 'The Membrane sign-in expired and could not be refreshed. Sign in again.' error (`platform-token.ts:72`).

Concrete failure: an operator whose OAuth access token has expired and whose refresh token is no longer valid runs `membrane-operator code status --workspace acme`. The list dispatch is the first call: `dispatchUnattached` → workspace lookup → `platformToken.get()` → refresh fails. `listVersion` wraps that error as `VerdictReadFailed`, `isVerdictReadRefusal` matches the regex, and the CLI prints 'this engine cannot answer the verdict yet' and exits 2. The real remedy ('Sign in again') is swallowed. The same happens in `code test` when the token expires during the 90 s wait. It also happens when an attached session's workspace token is revoked (401 on the session path) and when the workspace lookup is rejected (`rejectedCredentialError` carries the 401 as its cause).

The goal defines exit 2 as 'still pending / engine refuses', so an agent will keep retrying or tell the operator the engine is too old. It will not re-authenticate. The 'clear line' the goal asks for is wrong in exactly the case where the operator could act.
findings.fix: Only classify the list read's own response as a refusal: a 401/403 `ApiError` from `list-source-tree-versions` after the credential has been shown to work (for example, `run-source-tree-tests` succeeded on the same credential). Drop the `/sign-in expired/` regex match, so a credential-refresh failure surfaces its own message and exit 1. At minimum, rewrite the comment so it no longer claims the message only follows a 401.

findings.title: The 401 refusal tests reach the refusal only through a failed token refresh, so the `cause` recursion is untested
findings.body: `verdictServer` has no route for `/oauth/token`, so a refresh gets a 500. In the sessionless `[401]` cases (cli.code.verdict.test.ts:377, :396 and the `code status` table at :474), `callWithPlatformToken` calls `refreshAfterRejection`, and the refresh throws 'The Membrane sign-in expired…' (platform-token.ts:72). `isVerdictReadRefusal` matches that through its regex (code.ts:560). The assertion `listRequests: 1` confirms that no retry ever happens. Against a real old engine the refresh succeeds and the retry gets a second 401. `callWithPlatformToken` then throws `rejectedCredentialError(retryError)`, a plain Error with a MembraneApiError 401 as its `cause`, and only the `cause` recursion at code.ts:561 classifies it. No test reaches that path, so removing the recursion would leave every 401 test passing. The 403 cases do hit the direct status check.
findings.fix: Route `/oauth/token` in `verdictServer` so the refresh succeeds, and give the retried list call a second 401. Assert the 'cannot answer the verdict' output and `listRequests: 2`. Keep a separate case for the failed refresh, since code.ts:559 classifies that as a refusal on purpose.

findings.title: README verb list leaves out the new `code status` and the wait flags and exit codes
findings.body: The README says the tree 'round-trips through seven verbs' and lists pull/diff/push/run/promote/import/drift in the code block. The change mentions `code status` only in the prose that follows. Neither the block nor the prose gives the `--wait`, `--no-wait` and `--timeout <s>` flags (default 90) or the exit-code contract: test exits 0 for passed/skipped, 1 for failed, 2 for still pending or engine refusal; status adds 3 for untested. Those exit codes are the point of the change. `SKILL.md`/`MANUAL.md`, which agents read, don't give them either. The 'seven' count was already wrong before this change, since `test` was never in the block; this change adds `status` to the gap.
findings.fix: Add `code test [--tree-version <id>] [--no-wait] [--timeout <s>]` and `code status [--tree-version <id>] [--wait] [--timeout <s>]` to the block, fix the verb count, and state the exit codes in one sentence.

findings.title: The `untested` queue hint drops the chosen `--workspace`, `--session` and `--tree-version`, and the test pins the bare hint
findings.body: When `code status --wait` finds an `untested` version, `codeStatus` prints `untested — queue with: membrane-operator code test` (claude-plugin/src/engine/verbs/code.ts:727). The hint passes on neither `followUpFlags(options)` nor `--tree-version`. The timeout hints at code.ts:681 and :714 do pass them on, which shows that keeping them is the intent. Running `code status --workspace acme --tree-version ver_old --wait` and then following the hint queues tests on the tree's newest version, because `codeTest` sends `versionId` only when it is given. Without `--workspace`, the hint also loses the workspace and the session the user named. The test at cli.code.verdict.test.ts:649 runs with `--workspace acme` and still expects the bare hint, so it locks in the defect.
findings.fix: In code.ts:727, build the hint as `code test${followUpFlags(options)}${options.version ? ` --tree-version ${options.version}` : ''}`. Update the test at cli.code.verdict.test.ts:649 to expect `--workspace acme`, and add a case with `--tree-version`.

findings.title: isVerdictReadRefusal treats every 401/403, and any 'sign-in expired' message, as the old-engine refusal
findings.body:
What I saw in the code: `isVerdictReadRefusal` returns true for any 401 or 403, for any error whose message matches /sign-in expired/, and for any error whose `cause` chain holds one of those. On the sessionless path, `callWithPlatformToken` turns a 401 that survives a refresh into `rejectedCredentialError` ("Membrane rejected the stored credential. Sign in again…"), with the 401 ApiError as its cause. A refresh that fails throws "The Membrane sign-in expired… Sign in again." Both match.

What follows: if the stored credential is revoked or expired and cannot be refreshed, `code status` (whose first network call is this read) prints `this engine cannot answer the verdict yet` and exits 2. `code test` behaves the same way when the credential expires partway through the 90 s wait. The real fix, signing in again, never appears in the output. The goal describes exit 2 as "still pending / engine refuses", so an agent reading it will keep polling `code status` and get the same misleading answer each time. A 403 from a real access denial gets the same treatment. This only matters when the credential goes bad, so the impact is contained, but it hides the remedy, which goes against the goal's "clear line".
findings.fix: Treat only the refusal an old engine gives for a non-sessionless route as 'cannot answer'. Let a credential rejection or expiry (rejectedCredentialError, or the platform-token refresh error) through unchanged so its 'Sign in again' message reaches the user. At minimum, drop the /sign-in expired/ match and stop recursing into the cause of rejectedCredentialError.

findings.title: One failed read during the wait ends it with exit 1, the same code as a failed verdict
findings.body:
What I saw: in `waitForVersion`, any read failure that is not a timeout or a refusal (a 500, a network reset) leads to `Effect.fail`. `runCode` catches it and returns 1. The test at cli.code.verdict.test.ts:452 pins this: a 500 gives exit 1. The goal gives exit 1 the meaning "failed". The loop also never retries, so one transient error during a 90 s wait drops the wait for a run that is still queued.

What follows: a caller that branches on the exit code reads a passing run as a test failure because of one upstream blip. The run is not re-queued, so the goal's main property still holds. The help text and docs don't document the exit codes, and stderr carries the API error, so the damage is limited to callers that go by exit code alone.
findings.fix: Map a non-refusal read failure during the wait to exit 2 (verdict unknown or pending), keep the error line on stderr, or retry the read until the deadline. Keep exit 1 for a `failed` verdict only.

findings.title: `code test --json` now prints the bare version object instead of `{ version }`
findings.body: Before this change, `code test --json` printed the `run-source-tree-tests` output, `{ "version": { … } }`. Now every path, including `--no-wait`, goes through `renderTestVersion`, which prints `JSON.stringify(version)` with no wrapper. A script or agent that reads `.version.testsStatus` now gets `undefined`, and a caller that treats undefined as not-failed misreads the verdict without any error. No doc or help text mentions the change, and the new test at cli.code.verdict.test.ts:403 pins the bare shape.
findings.fix: Keep the `{ version }` wrapper in `code test --json` output, or document the new shape in the README and MANUAL as a deliberate break.

findings.title: `code status --wait --timeout 0` aborts its only read and reports 'still pending' without reading anything
findings.body: What I saw: `validTimeout` accepts `0`. With `--wait`, `codeStatus` sets `deadline = now + 0`, and `listVersion` dispatches the request. `readUntilDeadline` then finds `remaining <= 0`, aborts the request and fails with VERDICT_READ_TIMED_OUT. `codeStatus` takes the `timedOut && !version` branch and prints `still pending after 0 s` with exit 2. That happens for every version, including one that has passed, one that is untested, and one that doesn't exist. A small positive timeout that ends during workspace resolution gives the same mislabel: the line says "still pending" when nothing was read. The input is unusual, so the impact is small.
findings.fix: In `codeStatus`, make the first read without a deadline (or allow at least one read before enforcing the deadline), and apply the deadline only to the wait loop. Otherwise word the timed-out-before-any-read message as "no answer within N s" rather than "still pending".

findings.title: Ожидание до первого опроса расходует весь короткий таймаут
findings.body: Если `code test --timeout 5` получает состояние `pending`, команда ждёт до истечения таймаута и выходит без единого чтения вердикта. То же происходит с меньшими таймаутами и с `code status --wait` после первоначального чтения `pending`. Даже если тест завершился сразу после постановки в очередь, команда сообщает, что он ещё выполняется.
findings.fix: Прочитать вердикт до первого ожидания и повторять чтение с интервалом, ограниченным оставшимся временем.

findings.title: Отказ в постановке теста возвращает код неуспешного вердикта
findings.body: Если engine не может поставить тест в очередь, например возвращает `source_tree_tests_not_queued`, ошибка выходит из `codeTest` и общий обработчик `runCode` возвращает 1. По заданному контракту отказ engine должен возвращать 2; код 1 означает, что тест завершился с ошибкой. Вызывающий агент поэтому получает неверный результат, хотя тест не запускался.
findings.fix: Обработать отказ постановки в очередь в `codeTest` и вернуть 2 с сообщением об отказе.

findings.title: Every verdict poll re-fetches the whole operator overview to resolve the same workspace
findings.body: Without an attached session, each `dispatch` goes through `dispatchUnattached` (run.ts:222). That calls `loadOverview` → `client.getOperatorOverview()` (operator-client.ts:82), and the result is not cached. Before this change a `code test` made one dispatch. Now `waitForVersion` polls every 5 s against a default 90 s deadline, and `listVersion` makes one dispatch per page. So `code test --workspace acme`, and `code status --wait`, now fetch the cross-workspace operator overview (health and jobs for every workspace the operator reaches) up to about 18 times per wait. Each fetch only re-resolves an `orgWorkspaceId` that cannot change during the invocation. The overview fetch also carries no signal, so it is the part of each poll the deadline cannot abort. The underlying `dispatchUnattached` behaviour is pre-existing; the new poll loop is what makes it repeat.
findings.fix: Resolve the workspace once per invocation: in `createDispatcher`, memoize the `orgWorkspaceId` lookup (e.g. cache the overview promise in the closure) and reuse it for every later dispatch.

findings.title: Hand-rolled deadline race and AbortController threading duplicate Effect's signal-aware tryPromise plus timeoutOrElse
findings.body:
`readUntilDeadline` builds its own race between the read Promise and a sleep that calls `abortController.abort()` and fails with a sentinel symbol `VERDICT_READ_TIMED_OUT`. It also special-cases `remaining <= 0` with `void read.catch(...)`. To feed it, one shared `AbortController` is created in `codeTest`/`codeStatus` and passed through `waitForVersion`, `listVersion` and `readUntilDeadline`. On top of that, `new VerdictReadFailed({ cause, message: ... })` is built three times (codeTest, readUntilDeadline, listVersion).

Effect 4 already provides this. `Effect.tryPromise({ try: (signal) => dispatch(cmd, input, signal), catch })` aborts `signal` when the fiber is interrupted, and `.pipe(Effect.timeoutOrElse({ duration: remaining, orElse: () => Effect.fail(new VerdictReadTimedOut()) }))` interrupts it at the deadline. The repo already uses exactly this pattern at engine/api/src/account/companies/logo-dev-discovery.ts:67-90 (also exa-company-discovery.ts:252-273). The result is the same: the in-flight read is aborted at the deadline, the read's rejection is observed inside Effect, and the loser timer is cleared. It removes the sentinel symbol, the shared mutable controller, the `remaining <= 0` special case, the `as Effect.Effect<T, VerdictReadError>` cast, and an `abortController` parameter on three functions. I could not open `node_modules/effect` (not installed) to confirm the v4 interrupt-wait semantics myself; the repo precedent relies on them.
findings.fix: Replace `readUntilDeadline` and the AbortController plumbing with `Effect.tryPromise({ try: (signal) => dispatch(..., signal), catch: toVerdictReadFailed }).pipe(Effect.timeoutOrElse({ duration: Math.max(0, deadline - now), orElse: () => Effect.fail(new VerdictReadTimedOut()) }))`. Use a `Data.TaggedError` instead of the symbol, and check the deadline before dispatching.

findings.title: A no-op `catchTag`, a repeated error constructor, and a misnamed error for the queue call
findings.body:
`readUntilDeadline` ends with `.pipe(Effect.catchTag('VerdictReadFailed', (error) => Effect.fail(error)))`. It catches the error and fails with the same value, so it changes nothing; the cast after it does the actual typing. Also:
- `new VerdictReadFailed({ cause, message: ... })` is written out three times, in codeTest, readUntilDeadline and listVersion.
- `codeTest` wraps a failure of the queue call `run-source-tree-tests` in `VerdictReadFailed`, so the error's tag names the wrong operation.
- `timeoutSeconds` assigns to a local and returns it on the next line.
findings.fix: Remove the no-op `catchTag`, build `VerdictReadFailed` in one shared `catch` helper, and give the queue failure its own tag or a neutral name.

findings.title: 'stops at the deadline…' test is covered by the 'aborts the in-flight…' test that follows it
findings.body: The edit that would turn this test red is removing the deadline race in `readUntilDeadline`, so a read that never resolves leaves `exit` unsettled. That same edit also turns the next test red ('aborts the in-flight code %s verdict read at the deadline', line 230): it uses the same never-resolving page and the same 10 s advance, then runs `await exit`, which would hang until vitest's real-timer test timeout. The second test additionally fails if only the abort is removed, which the first test does not catch. No edit fails the first test while the second passes, so the first adds two cases (test/status) and a hand-built race helper without covering anything extra, and neither test says which one owns the deadline behaviour.
findings.fix: Delete the 'stops at the deadline' `it.each`; the 'aborts the in-flight' test owns both the deadline and the abort.

findings.title: The README and SKILL.md synopsis blocks omit `code test`, `code status`, their wait flags and the exit codes
findings.body: The changed prose (SKILL.md:589 and its README copy) tells agents that `test` queues the tests once and waits for the verdict, and that `status` reads a verdict without queuing another run. The `bash` synopsis blocks above that prose (SKILL.md:578-586, README.md:241-249) still list only pull/diff/push/run/promote/import/drift. They give no usage line for `test` or `status`, and no `--tree-version`, `--no-wait`, `--wait` or `--timeout <s>` flag (default 90). Neither the README nor SKILL/MANUAL states the exit codes, which are the point of the change: 0 for passed/skipped, 1 for failed, 2 for pending or engine refusal, and 3 for untested on `status`. The README still says "round-trips through seven verbs" (README:239) and calls `credential` "A seventh verb" (README:307). Leaving out `test` predates this change, but this change adds `status` and makes `status --wait` the required way to wait without re-queuing.
findings.fix: Add `code test [--tree-version <id>] [--no-wait] [--timeout <s>]` and `code status [--tree-version <id>] [--wait] [--timeout <s>]` to both synopsis blocks, state the exit codes in one sentence, and fix the verb count and the "seventh verb" line.

findings.title: No test exercises the `## ` section exit in the Status awk; deleting it leaves the suite green
findings.body: The goal says status parsing must not pick up a `Status:` line from another section. In executable_handoff-session-start.sh, `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` enforces this, and no test reaches that line. The first new negative case in 2834 has no `## Last request` heading at all, so `in_last_request` is never set. The second negative case keeps its `Status:` inside Last request with an unrecognized value, so it tests only the allow-list. 50901 has a `## Key Details` after Last request, but that section has no `Status:` line. Delete the exit line and every test still passes. The real regression: the model writes `## Last request` with no Status line, and a later `## Key Details` contains `Status: Answered` or `Status: Not answered`. The operator then sees a false status next to the goal.
findings.fix: Add a negative fixture with a `## Last request` section that has a quote but no Status line, followed by `## Key Details` containing `Status: Answered`. Assert the systemMessage is the goal alone, and keep 50901 as the positive control.

findings.title: Status awk takes the first `Status:` line in Last request, which can sit inside the verbatim operator quote
findings.body: The new extractor prompt says to quote the operator's last message verbatim at the top of `## Last request` and to put the model's own `Status:` line after it. The injector awk prints the first `^Status:` line in the section and exits. Suppose the quoted message is multi-line and has a line starting with `Status: Answered`, `Status: Not answered` or `Status: Partially answered`, for example pasted CI or log output or a code block. That quoted line is then parsed as the verdict, the real `Status:` line is never read, and the operator banner shows the wrong status. A quoted line starting with `## ` instead ends the section early, so the real status is silently dropped and the banner shows only the goal. additionalContext still carries the full text. The defect is in the operator-facing systemMessage. The new tests use only a single-line request, so they cannot catch this.
findings.fix: Put the model's `Status:` line directly after the `## Last request` heading, before the quote, and read the status only from that position. Alternatively, keep the last `^Status:` match in the section (record each match and print it at END) instead of exiting at the first one.

findings.title: Status parser takes the first Status: line in Last request, which can be one inside the quoted operator message
findings.body: The extraction prompt tells the model to quote the operator's last message verbatim at the top of `## Last request`, and only afterwards write its own `Status:` line. The awk takes the first `^Status:` line in that section and exits. If the quoted message is multi-line and has a line starting with `Status:` (for example a pasted report such as `Status: Answered`), that quoted line is parsed. The operator's text then shows up as the model's verdict, and the real `Status:` line is never read. A quoted line beginning with `## ` has the opposite effect: it ends the section early and the status is dropped. That one fails safe. The goal says a Status: line from another section must not be picked up, and this is the closest remaining way a non-verdict line is picked up. The new negative tests cover only a `Status:` in a different section and an unrecognized value, not this case.
findings.fix: The model's own Status line comes after the quote, so keep the last `^Status:` match in the section (record it and print it in an END block) instead of exiting at the first match.

findings.title: 'Last user request' assertion in the prompt-contract test cannot fail when the new Last request instruction is removed
findings.body: In test_scripts_50900, `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` is meant to guard the facts-block reference of the new `## Last request` section. The existing `<transcript_facts>` block always prints `Last user request: ...` (executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh:245-265, plus :113 and :120), and prints `None` when there is no transcript. So the assertion stays green if the instruction `Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above` is deleted or reworded. The other new assertions are independent substring checks. They do not tie `Status:` or the three values to the `## Last request` section, and `Answered` also matches `Partially answered`.
findings.fix: Replace the assertion with one on the new instruction text, for example 'verbatim from the facts block'. Optionally extract the slice between `## Last request` and `## Key Details` and assert the Status values against that slice.

findings.title: Парсер принимает строку из цитаты запроса за итоговый статус
findings.body: Новый контракт производителя требует дословно цитировать запрос оператора перед служебным статусом (executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh:318–321; декодирование исходного текста требуется на строке 338). Если многострочный запрос содержит отдельную строку `Status: Answered`, она может попасть внутрь дословной цитаты без префикса. Парсер выберет её и завершится до настоящей строки `Status: Not answered`. В результате оператор увидит неверный статус выполнения запроса. Это введённая изменением неоднозначность интерфейса между генератором handoff и его потребителем; additionalContext при этом сохраняется.
findings.fix: Поместить служебный Status сразу после заголовка Last request, перед цитатой, и читать статус только из этой фиксированной позиции.

findings.title: No test fails if the Last request section stops ending at the next heading
findings.body: The status awk in executable_handoff-session-start.sh (line 83, `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }`) is the only thing stopping a `Status:` line in a later section from being read as the last-request status. No test exercises it. The 2834 negative case 1 has no `## Last request` section, so `in_last_request` is never set. Negative case 2 has `Status: Waiting for a reply` inside the section, which only tests the allow-list. 50901 has a `## Key Details` after Last request, but that section holds no `Status:` line. Deleting the exit line, or letting the scan run past the section, leaves every test green. Then a handoff with `## Last request` that has no status, followed by `## Key Details` containing `Status: Not answered`, would show a false status to the operator. The goal names this exact case: status parsing cannot pick up a Status line from another section. Add one fixture: a Last request section with no Status line, followed by a Key Details section with `Status: Answered`, expecting the goal-only message.
findings.fix:
Add a case with `## Last request
Please continue.

## Key Details
Status: Answered` and assert the goal-only systemMessage.

findings.title: Verbatim quote inside Last request can be mistaken for the status line
findings.body: The prompt tells the extractor to quote the operator's last message verbatim before the `Status:` line. The awk takes the first `^Status:` line in the section and then exits. If the operator's message has a line that starts with `Status: Answered` (for example a pasted report), that quoted line is parsed as the status and the real `Status:` line is never read. A quoted line starting with `## ` would instead end the section early. The result is a wrong or missing status in the operator banner. This needs a multi-line operator message with these exact line prefixes, so it is uncommon.
findings.fix: Take the last `Status:` line in the section instead of the first, since the prompt puts it after the quote.

findings.title: Verbatim, unbounded last-request quote before the Status line conflicts with the injector's parse format
findings.body: The new prompt puts a verbatim quote of the whole last operator message before the `Status:` metadata line. It says nothing about multi-line or long messages, and the quote competes with the 400-word cap on the whole `<handoff>`. Take an operator message like "Check this text:\nStatus: Answered". A faithful verbatim quote puts that line before the real `Status: Not answered`, and the injector (executable_handoff-session-start.sh:84–88) shows `Answered`. A quoted line starting with `## ` ends the section early and drops the status. The new tests use only a simple single-line request, so this format conflict goes undetected.
findings.fix: Put the `Status:` metadata line before the quote, or tell the extractor to prefix quoted lines. Say how a long quote is handled, and add a test request that contains its own `Status:` line.

findings.title: Отрицательный пример не проверяет выход из раздела Last request
findings.body: В примере со статусом из другого раздела вообще отсутствует ## Last request. Поэтому удаление ограничения `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` из инжектора оставит все новые проверки удовлетворёнными: положительные примеры находят статус до следующего заголовка, а этот отрицательный пример никогда не включает in_last_request. Регрессия, при которой статус из Key Details после Last request показывается как состояние запроса, останется незамеченной.
findings.fix: Добавить перед ## Key Details раздел ## Last request без строки Status: и сохранить ожидание сообщения только с целью.

findings.title: No test covers the section-boundary guard in the status awk; deleting it leaves the suite green
findings.body: The injector awk has `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }`, which is what stops a `Status:` line in a later section from being read. No test reaches that line. 50901 has the Status inside Last request, so it is found before any exit. The first new negative case in 2834 has no `## Last request` heading at all, so `in_last_request` is never set. The second negative case has the Status inside the section but with an unrecognized value. Mutation: delete the exit line and every test still passes. Real trigger: a handoff where the model writes `## Last request` with no Status line (the prompt makes that possible) and a later `## Key Details` contains `Status: Answered`. The operator would then see a wrong `Status: Answered` beside the goal. The goal says status parsing must not pick up a Status line from another section, and the test that claims to check this does not exercise the guard. The runtime defect is contained to an operator-facing banner. This is a test gap, not a code bug.
findings.fix: Add a case with `## Last request` that has no Status line, followed by `## Key Details` containing `Status: Answered`. Assert the systemMessage is the goal alone.

findings.title: Status awk takes the first `Status:` line in a section that holds a verbatim operator quote
findings.body: The prompt tells the extractor to quote the operator's last message verbatim inside `## Last request`, with the model's own `Status:` line after it. The awk prints and exits on the first line matching `^Status:`. If the quoted operator message has a line starting with `Status: Answered`, `Status: Not answered` or `Status: Partially answered` (for example pasted CI or log output), that line wins over the extractor's real verdict. The banner would then show the quote's value. Separately, a quoted line starting with `## ` ends the section early, so the real Status is silently dropped and the banner shows the goal alone. The first case needs operator text that happens to match exactly. The second only degrades the display. Observed: first-match and exit-on-heading logic. Inferred: the quote can contain such lines. The status awk also does not stop at `</handoff>`, unlike the goal awk beside it. This is harmless while Last request is followed by Key Details.
findings.fix: Take the last `Status:` line in the section instead of the first, by remembering each match and printing it at END. A stricter option is to require the Status line to be the section's final non-empty line.

findings.title: Парсер принимает Status: из дословной цитаты запроса за служебный статус
findings.body:
Новая инструкция требует дословно сохранять последнее сообщение оператора перед служебным Status:. Если оператор прислал «Объясни этот вывод:
```
Status: Answered
```», экстрактор может корректно сохранить этот текст и затем добавить настоящий `Status: Not answered`. Парсер не учитывает границы цитат или блоков кода: он выберет первый `Status: Answered` и завершится. В результате оператор увидит неверный статус. Новые тесты используют однострочный запрос без вложенного Status:, поэтому такое смешение текста запроса и метаданных оставляет их зелёными. Это введённый изменением дефект отображения; additionalContext сохраняет оба значения.
findings.fix: Разместить служебный Status: непосредственно после заголовка ## Last request, перед дословной цитатой, и читать статус только из этой позиции.

findings.title: No test covers the section-exit that stops Status parsing at the next heading
findings.body: The goal requires that status parsing cannot pick up a Status: line from another section. In executable_handoff-session-start.sh that guarantee comes from `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }`. Neither new negative case exercises it. The first has no `## Last request` heading, so `in_last_request` is never set. The second keeps its `Status:` line inside Last request, with an unrecognized value. Delete the exit line and every added test stays green. The real regression is a handoff whose Last request section has no Status line and whose later `## Key Details` contains `Status: Answered` or `Status: Not answered`. That would show a false status to the operator, and only this fixture catches it.
findings.fix: Add a negative fixture with `## Last request` and a quote but no Status line, followed by `## Key Details` containing `Status: Not answered`. Assert the systemMessage is the goal alone.

findings.title: Prompt-contract test has an assertion that passes without the change and does not pin the facts-block reference
findings.body: In test_scripts_50900, `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` is satisfied by the pre-existing `<transcript_facts>` block, which prints `Last user request: None` with no transcript. It stays green if the new Last request section is removed or reworded. The test also never checks that the new section tells the extractor to quote verbatim from the facts block. That link is the contract the goal calls out. Replacing the instruction with free-form text would still pass. The `Status:`, `Answered` and `what to check first` assertions do go red when the section is dropped. The `Last user request` line gives false assurance about the facts-block reference.
findings.fix: Drop the `Last user request` assertion. Assert the new instruction line instead, for example 'verbatim from the facts block above'.

findings.title: Inferred-items assertion still passes when the instruction is removed from one of its two sections
findings.body: The new check searches the whole prompt for '<claim>, verify with: <exact command>'. If the instruction is removed only from Relevant Context or only from Key Details, the test stays green because the other section still matches. So the test does not protect issue #509's requirement that inferred items carry a verification command in both sections.
findings.fix: Extract the Relevant Context and Key Details sections from the captured extractor prompt and assert the instruction in each one separately.

findings.title: Отрицательный пример не проверяет выход из Last request
findings.body: Новый пример со Status в Key Details вообще не содержит Last request. Если удалить строку 'in_last_request && /^## / { exit }' из injector, все добавленные примеры сохранят прежний результат. При этом handoff с Last request без Status и последующим '## Key Details\nStatus: Answered' начнёт показывать статус из другой секции. Это нарушает явно заданную границу разбора, которую отрицательный пример должен защищать.
findings.fix: Добавить в этот отрицательный пример секцию Last request без Status перед Key Details. Сохранить ожидаемый systemMessage без статуса и положительный контроль 50901.

findings.title: Last request instruction gives no guidance when the facts block says `Last user request: None`
findings.body: The new `## Last request` step asks for a verbatim quote from the facts block and then for exactly one of three statuses. It says nothing about the case where the facts block reads `Last user request: None`. That happens on the fallback paths (unreadable or malformed transcript, jq failure; lines 113, 120, 245, 265) or when no non-harness user message survives filtering. These paths are rare, because PreCompact normally supplies a readable transcript. In that case the extractor gets conflicting instructions and may still emit a status. The injector would then show the operator a `Status:` line for a request that was never captured. The result is a mildly misleading banner, not lost data, and the fork sees the full session anyway, so it can often still name the request.
findings.fix: Add one line under `## Last request`: when the facts block says `Last user request: None`, write `None` and omit the `Status:` line.

findings.title: Verbatim last-request quote is unbounded against the 400-word cap and can break the section the injector parses
findings.body: The prompt asks for a verbatim quote of the whole last message but says nothing about long or multi-line messages. The 400-word cap applies to the whole `<handoff>`, so the instruction conflicts with the cap, and the extractor has to choose which to break. A multi-line quote that contains a line starting with `## ` ends the `## Last request` section early in the injector's awk. A quoted line starting with `Status:` is picked up before the real status line. Either case drops or corrupts the operator-visible status.
findings.fix: State how a long quote is handled (for example, quote the first N words or lines). Put the `Status:` line before the quote, or tell the extractor to prefix quoted lines.

findings.title: `Last user request` assertion in the prompt-contract test cannot fail on this change
findings.body: `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` matches the facts-block label, which existed before this change. It stays green if the new `## Last request` section stops pointing at the facts block, or if that wording is removed. The test then does not cover the "facts-block reference" requirement in the goal. Likewise, `Answered` also matches the `Partially answered` line, so it only checks that the status line exists.
findings.fix: Assert the new instruction text, for example 'verbatim from the facts block'. Alternatively, drop the redundant assertion.

findings.title: No test checks that the Last request section ends at the next heading
findings.body:
The goal says status parsing must not pick up a `Status:` line from another section, and that the tests must go red on real regressions. The new fixtures cover three cases:
- 50901: a valid Status inside Last request, which is found before the boundary matters.
- 2834 case 1: a Status line in Key Details, but the handoff has no `## Last request` section at all, so `in_last_request` is never set.
- 2834 case 2: an unrecognized value.

No fixture has a Last request section with no valid Status line, followed by another section that has one. If you delete `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` (executable_handoff-session-start.sh:83), all three still pass. With that line removed, this handoff would show `Status: Not answered` to the operator even though the line comes from Key Details:
`## Last request\nquote\n\n## Key Details\nStatus: Not answered`

The one guard the goal names is therefore not protected by any test.
findings.fix: In test 2834, change the 'status outside Last request' fixture to include a `## Last request` section with no Status line before `## Key Details\nStatus: Not answered`. Keep the exact `assert_output` of the goal-only message.

findings.title: A required verbatim quote of up to 4000 characters conflicts with the 400-word handoff cap
findings.body:
The new section tells the extractor to quote the operator's last message verbatim. The facts block bounds that message at 4000 characters (`bounded_text`, line 141), which can be roughly 600 or more words. The prompt also keeps `Maximum 400 words in the <handoff> section`. Before this change, the facts constraint only required an exact copy if the request appeared; now the quote is mandatory.

When the last message is a long paste (a plan or a review brief), the extractor can only satisfy one instruction. It either truncates or paraphrases the quote, which breaks the verbatim and copy-exactly rules, or it spends the whole word budget on the quote and drops Relevant Context and Key Details. Either way the handoff gets worse in exactly the long-request case where the next agent needs it most.
findings.fix: Exclude the quoted request from the 400-word cap, or allow a bounded excerpt marked as truncated (for example, the first N words plus `[truncated]`).

findings.title: A Status: line inside the verbatim quote can be taken as the extractor's status
findings.body:
The awk prints the first line that starts with `Status:` anywhere inside `## Last request`, and the section now opens with a verbatim multi-line quote of the operator's message. If the quoted message has a line starting with `Status:`, the awk reads that line instead of the extractor's own status:
- If that line holds a recognized value (`Status: Answered`), the operator sees a status the extractor never assigned.
- If it holds any other value (`Status: blocked`), the real `Status: Not answered` line below is never reached, so the status is hidden.

The same applies to a quoted line starting with `## `, which ends the section early. This needs operator text with such a line, so it is uncommon. When it happens, the message shows a wrong status rather than none.
findings.fix: Use the last `Status:` line in the section, not the first, or tell the extractor to put the Status line before the quote, or to quote the request as `> ` blockquote lines.

findings.title: The 'Last user request' assertion is satisfied by the facts block, not by the new instruction
findings.body:
Test 50900 asserts the prompt contains `Last user request`, apparently to check that the new Last request instruction points at the facts block. But `transcript_facts` always emits a `Last user request: ...` line, even as `Last user request: None` on every fallback path. So this assertion passes whatever the new instruction says.

The new line reads `Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above`. If you remove or reword its facts-block reference, the test stays green. The goal names that reference as something the change must not break.
findings.fix: Assert the new instruction's own text instead, for example `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'verbatim from the facts block above'`.

findings.title: Текст последнего запроса может скрыть или подменить его статус
findings.body: Новый prompt требует дословно скопировать сообщение оператора перед Status:, но не задаёт границы цитаты. Если сообщение содержит строку `## Reproduction`, этот парсер завершает секцию до настоящего статуса, и systemMessage показывает только цель. Если сообщение содержит отдельную строку `Status: Answered`, парсер выбирает её вместо последующего `Status: Not answered`, который указал экстрактор. Оба случая возникают при выполнении инструкции о дословном копировании и дают оператору неверное представление о состоянии запроса.
findings.fix: Задать явные границы цитаты в prompt и пропускать её содержимое при поиске заголовков и строки Status:.

findings.title: 'Status outside Last request' fixture has no Last request section, so the section-end boundary is untested
findings.body: The negative case added to test_scripts_2834 is labelled "A status outside Last request is ordinary handoff text", but its fixture is only `## Goal` + `## Key Details\nStatus: Not answered`. It has no `## Last request` heading, so `in_last_request` is never set and the case passes no matter how the section is bounded. In every fixture that does have `## Last request` (50901, 50902, and the 'Waiting for a reply' case at 11704-11709), the Status: line sits inside that section, before any later heading. So deleting `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` (home/private_dot_claude/hooks/executable_handoff-session-start.sh:83) leaves every test green. After that regression, a real handoff in the prompt's order (Last request → Key Details → Warnings) where the extractor leaves out the Status line under Last request but writes e.g. `Status: Answered` under Key Details would show that status on the operator's screen. The goal names this criterion directly: "status parsing cannot pick up a Status: line from another section" and "tests go red on real regressions". The profile and the test-oracle gate rate a test that stays green after the protected behavior is removed as high-cost.
findings.fix:
Change the fixture (or add one beside it) to put a Status-less `## Last request` section before a later section that carries a status, e.g. `## Goal
ship the hook change

## Last request
Please continue.

## Key Details
Status: Not answered`, and keep the goal-only systemMessage assertion. 50901 is already the valid control.

findings.title: The prompt-contract assertion 'Last user request' is satisfied by the facts block, not by the new instruction
findings.body: test_scripts_50900 asserts `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'`, presumably to prove that the new Last request instruction references the facts block. But `transcript_facts` always emits `Last user request: ...`, including `Last user request: None` on every fallback path, and 50900 passes no transcript_path. The new instruction says "from the facts block above" and does not contain that string. So the assertion passes even if the new reference is removed or reworded, which the goal names as something the change must not break.
findings.fix: Assert the new instruction text itself, e.g. `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'verbatim from the facts block above'`, and drop or move the 'Last user request' assertion.

findings.title: Nothing goes red if the status parser stops ending at the next heading after `## Last request`
findings.body:
The goal requires that "status parsing cannot pick up a Status: line from another section" and that "tests go red on real regressions". The only negative fixture for this rule (2834, `## Key Details\nStatus: Not answered`) has no `## Last request` heading at all. That means `in_last_request` is never set, and the fixture passes whether or not the section-end rule exists. I traced each fixture with `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` (executable_handoff-session-start.sh:83) deleted:
- 50901 still finds its own `Status: Not answered` inside Last request.
- The first 2834 case never enters the section.
- The `Waiting for a reply` case is dropped by the `case` filter.

So all of them stay green. The regression is reachable in real use. Suppose the extractor writes `## Last request` but leaves out the Status line, or garbles it (for example `**Status:** Answered`), and a later `## Key Details` or `## Warnings` bullet starts with `Status: Answered`. The operator then sees a status the handoff never claimed for the last request. Under the profile's test-oracle rule, this negative case cannot fail when the behavior it names is removed.
findings.fix:
In the 2834 negative case, stage `## Goal
ship the hook change

## Last request
Please continue.

## Key Details
Status: Not answered`. A Last request section with no Status line, followed by another section that has one, reaches the section-end rule and goes red without it.

findings.title: The `Last user request` assertion in 50900 is satisfied by the facts block, not by the new prompt instruction
findings.body: 50900 sends `handoff_payload` with no `transcript_path`. That means `transcript_facts` takes its fallback and always prints `Last user request: None` into the prompt. The new Last request instruction says "from the facts block above" and never contains the string `Last user request`. So `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` passes even if the new `## Last request` instruction's reference to the facts block is deleted or reworded. The goal names exactly that case: "wording does not break ... the facts-block reference". Similarly, `'<claim>, verify with: <exact command>'` appears in both Relevant Context and Key Details, so losing it from either section is not detected.
findings.fix: Assert the instruction line itself, e.g. `[Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above]`. Drop the `Last user request` assertion, or move it to a test that checks the facts block.

findings.title: The first `Status:` line in Last request wins, including a line inside the verbatim operator quote
findings.body: The prompt tells the extractor to quote the operator's last message verbatim and then write the `Status:` line after the quote. The parser takes the first line in the section that starts with `Status:` and then exits. If the operator's last message is multi-line and one of its lines starts with `Status: Answered`, `Status: Not answered`, etc., the decoded verbatim quote puts that line first. Typical sources are a pasted earlier handoff or a status report. The operator then sees the quoted text's status instead of the extractor's verdict. The outcome is display-only and needs an unusual message, so the impact is contained.
findings.fix: Keep the last matching `Status:` line in the section, which is where the prompt puts the verdict, instead of exiting on the first one.

findings.title: Comments still say the operator sees only the goal, now that systemMessage can also carry Status
findings.body: The comment on the goal extraction says: "The operator never sees additionalContext, so show them the one block they can check: the goal the extractor settled on." The change now also adds `Status: <status>` to the same systemMessage (line 108). In the same touched test file, test 2831's comment says systemMessage rides "carrying the goal alone" (scripts_test.sh ~11602), and its title says "only the goal in systemMessage". Both describe the old contract. The comments are wrong, not the code.
findings.fix: Change "the one block" to say the operator sees the goal plus a recognized last-request status. Drop "alone" from the 2831 comment.

findings.title: Header still lists "Four deliberate departures from upstream" after the handoff structure changed again
findings.body: The vendored hook's header lists every departure from kylesnowschwartz/claude-handoff, because upstream is inactive and the departures are kept on purpose. This change makes another departure in the extraction prompt: a new `## Last request` section with a fixed Status vocabulary, the `<claim>, verify with: <exact command>` format for inferred items, and removal of upstream's "3-7 bullet points" cap. The list still says four, and none of them covers this. The session-start hook now parses that section, so the injector depends on it.
findings.fix: Add a fifth bullet saying that the prompt adds a `## Last request` section whose Status line the SessionStart injector parses, and that it drops the 3-7 bullet cap. Update the count.

findings.title: Тест пропускает удаление правила проверки предположений из одного раздела
findings.body: Новая проверка ищет '<claim>, verify with: <exact command>' во всём prompt. Если удалить инструкцию из Relevant Context (executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh:316), совпадение останется в Key Details (:325), поэтому тест продолжит проходить. Обратное удаление тоже останется незамеченным. Таким образом, тест не защищает требование #509 передавать модели это правило для обоих разделов. Это противоречит правилу репозитория о проверках, которые должны обнаруживать удаление защищаемого поведения.
findings.fix: Выделить Relevant Context и Key Details из захваченного prompt и проверить наличие инструкции отдельно в каждом разделе.

findings.title: Status parser takes the first `Status:` line and stops at the first `## ` line, so a verbatim operator quote can replace or hide the real status
findings.body: The new prompt tells the extractor to quote the operator's last message verbatim and then write `Status: ...`. The session-start awk enters at `^## Last request`, exits at the first `^## ` line, and prints the first `^Status:` line it sees. Nothing separates the quoted text from the status line. If the multi-line quote contains a line starting `Status: Answered` (for example a pasted earlier handoff banner), the operator sees `Answered` when the extractor wrote `Not answered`. If the quoted value is unrecognized, the case filter clears it and no status is shown at all. A quoted `## ` heading ends the section early, and the real status is silently dropped. The impact is limited to the operator-facing systemMessage.
findings.fix: Take the last `Status:` line in the section instead of the first. Or have the prompt put the Status line right after the heading, before the quote, and parse only that position.

findings.title: No fixture exercises the section-boundary exit; removing `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` keeps every test green
findings.body:
The new negative case "Status outside Last request" uses a handoff with no `## Last request` heading at all, so `in_last_request` is never set and the boundary rule is never reached. The other new cases (50901, and the 'Waiting for a reply' case in 2834) put the `Status:` line inside `## Last request`. If line 83 of executable_handoff-session-start.sh were deleted, a handoff like `## Last request
Please continue.

## Key Details
Status: Answered` would show `Status: Answered`, taken from Key Details, and no test would go red. The goal says the parser must not pick up a Status: line from another section, and that the tests must go red on real regressions. The one guard that enforces the first condition is the one the tests do not cover. The defect this would let through is display-only, so minor.
findings.fix: Change the 'Status outside Last request' fixture to include a `## Last request` section without a Status line, followed by `## Key Details` containing `Status: Not answered`, and keep the exact assert_output on the goal-only banner.

findings.title: Парсер принимает Status: из дословной цитаты запроса
findings.body: Новый prompt требует сначала дословно скопировать запрос пользователя, а затем записать вычисленный статус. Если многострочный запрос содержит пример со строкой `Status: Answered`, допустимый handoff сохранит эту строку перед настоящим `Status: Not answered`. Парсер выбирает первое совпадение и завершает обработку, поэтому оператор увидит `Answered` для ещё не выполненного запроса. Дефект введён этим изменением; он затрагивает отображаемый статус.
findings.fix: Поместить служебную строку Status непосредственно после заголовка Last request, перед цитатой, и читать её только в этой позиции.

findings.title: No fixture covers the end of the Last request section, so a parser that reads Status: from Key Details stays green
findings.body: The goal requires that status parsing "cannot pick up a Status: line from another section" and that tests go red on real regressions. The guard is `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` (executable_handoff-session-start.sh:83), and no test fails when it is deleted. The negative case in test_scripts_2834 labelled "A status outside Last request is ordinary handoff text" uses `## Goal` + `## Key Details\nStatus: Not answered` with no `## Last request` heading. `in_last_request` is never set, so the boundary rule is never reached. The other cases (50901, and the 'Waiting for a reply' / unrecognized-value case) keep the Status line inside the section, so awk finds it before any later heading. One reviewer ran the original awk and a version without the exit line on all fixtures and got identical output. Take a handoff where `## Last request` has no Status line and a later `## Key Details` contains `Status: Not answered`: the original shows nothing, and the mutant shows a false status in the operator's banner.
findings.fix:
In test_scripts_2834, change the first negative fixture to `## Goal
ship the hook change

## Last request
Please continue.

## Key Details
Status: Not answered`. Keep the exact assert_output of the goal-only systemMessage. 50901 already serves as the valid control.

findings.title: The inferred-item rule is asserted once, so deleting it from one of the two sections stays green
findings.body: The goal places the `<claim>, verify with: <exact command>` rule in both Relevant Context (pre-compact.sh ~316) and Key Details (~325). test_scripts_50900 checks it with a single `assert_file_contains` over the whole prompt, which passes if either copy exists. Deleting the rule from either section leaves the test green, so the requirement that both sections carry the rule is not protected.
findings.fix: Assert that the line appears twice (`run grep -c -F '<claim>, verify with: <exact command>' "$prompt"; assert_success; assert_output 2`), or extract each section and check each one separately.

findings.title: The single-line request fixture cannot catch a quoted Status: line being mistaken for the handoff status
findings.body: The new test uses a last request with no `Status:` or heading lines. If the verbatim quote contains `Status: Answered` and the real status after it is `Not answered`, the parser in executable_handoff-session-start.sh:84-88 picks the first line and shows `Answered`. The current fixtures cannot tell a status inside the quote from the handoff's own status line.
findings.fix: Once the status position and parser are fixed, extend this test with a multi-line request that contains a different recognized Status value.

findings.title: Проверка инструкции для предположений пропускает её удаление из одного раздела
findings.body: Требование задаёт инструкцию `<claim>, verify with: <exact command>` отдельно для Relevant Context и Key Details. Тест ищет её один раз во всём prompt. Удаление строки 325 из executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh оставляет все его проверки неизменными благодаря строке 316, хотя Key Details теряет обязательную инструкцию для следующего агента.
findings.fix: Извлечь Relevant Context и Key Details из захваченного prompt и проверить наличие инструкции отдельно в каждом разделе.

findings.title: Prompt puts the verbatim multi-line quote before the Status: line, so the parser can read the quote instead of the status
findings.body: The new template (executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh:318-320) asks for the operator's last message verbatim, then `Status: ...`, with nothing between them. The facts block stores that message as a decoded JSON literal of up to 4000 chars, and the constraints tell the extractor to copy it exactly, so it can span many lines. The session-start awk (executable_handoff-session-start.sh:81-90) exits at the first `^## ` line after `## Last request` and prints the first `^Status:` line. A pasted request with a markdown heading is common in this workflow. When the request has one, the section ends before the real Status line, and the banner shows no status. When the request has a line starting `Status: Answered`, the banner shows the wrong value. additionalContext is not affected. Only the systemMessage status the operator sees is missing or wrong.
findings.fix: In the prompt template, put `Status: [Use exactly one of: ...]` directly under `## Last request` and the verbatim quote after it. The current awk then finds the status before any quoted text.

findings.title: A required verbatim quote of the last request (up to 4000 chars) conflicts with the kept 400-word handoff cap
findings.body: The new `## Last request` section (executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh:319) requires the operator's last message verbatim. `bounded_text` (line 141) lets it reach 4000 characters plus ` [truncated]`, which is roughly 600-700 words. The constraint `Maximum 400 words in the <handoff> section` (line 334) is unchanged. Before this change the prompt did not require the request inside the handoff, so this conflict is new. Nothing in code enforces the cap. When the last request is long, the extractor has two conflicting rules: it can paraphrase or truncate the quote, which breaks the copy-exactly rule, or it can drop Goal and Context content to stay under the cap. The prompt does not say which rule wins. Long pasted requests are common here, so the handoff can lose the request's exact text or its context in exactly those sessions.
findings.fix: Add one line to the constraints: the quoted last request does not count toward the 400-word limit.

findings.title: Last request section does not say what to write when the facts block has `Last user request: None`
findings.body: `transcript_facts` sends `Last user request: None` when no non-harness user message survives. It also sends it on every jq fallback path (lines 245, 264). The new section still requires a verbatim quote and exactly one of Answered / Partially answered / Not answered, but gives no rule for this case. Some runs will quote `None` and pick a status at random, and the injector will then show that invented status in the operator's banner. Other runs will drop the section. Contained impact: it only affects the operator-facing systemMessage.
findings.fix: Add one line, e.g. `[When the facts block says Last user request: None, omit this section]`. The parser then shows the goal alone.

findings.title: No test covers the parser's stop at the next section after Last request
findings.body: The section boundary at executable_handoff-session-start.sh:83 (`in_last_request && /^## / { exit }`) is what stops a Status: line in a later section from being read. No test covers it. Delete that line and every new test stays green. In 50901 the real Status: comes first, so the parser picks it up before reaching the next section. 2834 case 1 has no `## Last request` at all, so the flag is never set. 2834 case 2 is caught by the allow-list `case`, not by the section boundary. The case no test covers: a handoff with `## Last request` and no Status: line, followed by `## Key Details` containing `Status: Answered`. Without the exit, the operator sees `Status: Answered` for a request that was not answered. The goal requires both 'status parsing cannot pick up a Status: line from another section' and 'tests go red on real regressions'; for this boundary the second does not hold.
findings.fix:
Add a case to test_scripts_2834: `## Goal
ship the hook change

## Last request
Please continue.

## Key Details
Status: Answered`, then check that systemMessage is exactly the goal-only form.

findings.title: Prompt-contract check for 'Last user request' can never fail
findings.body: `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` is always satisfied by the transcript_facts block. Every path that builds the facts block prints `Last user request: ...` (executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh:113,120,245,260-261,265, all present before this change). So the check stays green even if the new Last-request instruction 'Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above' is removed or loses its reference to the facts block. The goal names that facts-block reference as a correctness condition. This is the 'green test that cannot fail' class from semantic-regression-tests-over-source-shape.md.
findings.fix: Check the new instruction line instead, e.g. `Quote the operator'"'"'s last real message verbatim from the facts block above`, or drop the check.

findings.title: Status: comes after a multi-line verbatim quote that can end the section early or supply a false status
findings.body: The new template puts the verbatim quote of the operator's last message before the `Status:` line. That message can be up to 4000 characters (bounded_text) and span several lines once decoded. The session-start parser (executable_handoff-session-start.sh:81-90) stops at the first `^## ` line and takes the first `^Status:` line inside the section. Two failures follow. (1) An operator message that pastes Markdown with a `## ` heading ends the section before the real Status: line, so a valid status is silently dropped. (2) A pasted line starting with `Status: Answered`, for example from an issue or a log, is taken as the status. The operator then sees a wrong answered/unanswered state. If the model wraps the quote in `> ` blockquote lines, neither failure happens; I did not confirm how the model formats the quote.
findings.fix: Put the `Status:` line first in the `## Last request` template, before the quote, so the parser reads it before any quoted text.

findings.title: Verbatim quote of up to 4000 characters conflicts with the 400-word handoff cap
findings.body: The new Last request section tells the extractor to quote the operator's last message verbatim. The facts block allows up to 4000 characters plus ' [truncated]' for that message (bounded_text, line 140-141). The kept constraint is 'Maximum 400 words in the <handoff> section'. A long or pasted operator message of about 4000 characters is roughly 600-700 words, so following one instruction breaks the other. The model must either shorten the 'verbatim' quote, which undoes the exact-copy goal, or go over the cap and leave less room for Relevant Context and Key Details.
findings.fix: Exclude the Last request quote from the 400-word cap explicitly, or allow a bounded excerpt with a truncation marker.

findings.title: Строка Status внутри цитаты запроса подменяет статус ответа
findings.body: Новый prompt требует дословно цитировать последнее сообщение перед служебной строкой Status. Если пользователь попросил объяснить отчёт, содержащий строку `Status: Answered`, и extractor воспроизвёл отчёт в fenced code block, awk выберет эту строку раньше настоящего `Status: Not answered`. Оператор увидит неверный статус. Парсер не различает содержимое цитаты и служебные поля; аналогично заголовок `## ` внутри цитаты преждевременно завершает поиск. Проблема введена этим изменением.
findings.fix: Задать однозначный формат цитаты: например, потребовать префикс `> ` у каждой её строки, оставив служебную строку Status без префикса.

findings.title: Проверка prompt остаётся зелёной при удалении обязательных инструкций
findings.body: В новом test_scripts_50900 можно удалить инструкцию о дословном цитировании из секции Last request: проверка `Last user request` всё равно найдёт существующий текст facts block или Constraints. Можно также удалить инструкцию о проверке предположений из одной из двух секций: общий поиск найдёт вторую копию. Тест продолжит проходить при нарушении явных требований goal. Это новая недискриминирующая проверка, которую правила репозитория требуют исправлять.
findings.fix: Проверять инструкции в соответствующих секциях захваченного prompt, включая правило дословного цитирования и обе инструкции о проверке предположений.

findings.title: No fixture puts a Status: line after a real Last request section, so the section-boundary exit is untested
findings.body:
The goal requires that status parsing cannot pick up a `Status:` line from another section, and that the tests go red on real regressions. The injector has two guards. It starts reading only at `## Last request`, and `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` (executable_handoff-session-start.sh:~82-84) stops at the next heading. The new tests only exercise the first guard:
- The 'status outside Last request' negative fixture in test_scripts_2834 (`## Goal … ## Key Details\nStatus: Not answered`) has no `## Last request` heading. `in_last_request` is never set, so the result is empty whether or not the boundary exit exists.
- The unrecognized-value case in 2834 has no section after Last request, so it is caught by the allow-list `case`.
- In 50901 and 50902 the valid Status: line comes before `## Key Details`, so the scan exits on that line before it reaches the boundary.

If the boundary-exit line is deleted, every test stays green. In that state, take a handoff whose Last request section has no plain `Status:` line (the model skipped it, or wrote `**Status:**`), followed by `## Key Details` with `Status: Not answered` or `Status: Answered`. The operator sees a status taken from Key Details, which is exactly the cross-section leak the goal rules out. This is a rejection fixture without a discriminating control, the case that semantic-regression-tests-over-source-shape.md and source-greps-need-a-second-side.md describe.
findings.fix:
Add a case to test_scripts_2834, or replace the existing negative fixture with it: `## Goal
ship the hook change

## Last request
Please continue.

## Key Details
Status: Not answered`. Assert that systemMessage is exactly the goal-only form, and confirm the test goes red when the `/^## / { exit }` line is removed.

findings.title: Prompt-contract test 50900 checks loose substrings: 'Last user request' can never fail, and Status: is never tied to the Last request section
findings.body:
`assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` is always satisfied by the transcript_facts block. Every path that builds the facts block prints `Last user request: ...`, including the fallback `Last user request: None` (executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh ~113,120,245,260-266). The new instruction says 'from the facts block above' and never contains that phrase. So deleting the 'Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above' line, or removing its facts-block reference, leaves the test green, even though the goal names that reference as a correctness condition.

The other checks ('Status:', 'Answered', …) also match anywhere in the prompt. The SessionStart injector matches only `^Status:` at the start of a line, inside a `^## Last request` section, with the exact-case values. Moving the Status line under `## Key Details`, or changing it to `**Status:** [...]` or `- Status: [...]`, would silently drop the status from the systemMessage in real use, and 50900 would still pass.

CLAUDE.md asks for exact assertions on 'text that changes when the behavior breaks'. The neighbouring test_scripts_2844 already extracts its block and asserts the exact text, on the grounds that for a model consumer 'the instruction itself is the interface'.
findings.fix: Extract the `## Last request` block from the captured prompt (e.g. `sed -n '/^## Last request$/,/^## Key Details$/p'`) and assert_equal it against the exact instruction lines. Drop the 'Last user request' substring check, or replace it with the exact 'verbatim from the facts block above' sentence.

findings.title: A verbatim operator quote with a 'Status:' line is read as the handoff status
findings.body:
The prompt places the verbatim quote of the operator's last message before the `Status:` line. The parser takes the first `^Status:` line in the section and exits. The facts literal is decoded to its real text, so a multi-line operator message can contain a line that starts with `Status: Answered`, for example pasted tool output or a template. That line is matched first, and the operator sees the quoted text's status instead of the extractor's verdict.

A quoted line that starts with `## ` ends the section early instead. That case fails safe: no status is shown. Both cases are rare. The impact is limited to the operator-facing systemMessage.
findings.fix: Take the last `^Status:` line inside the section instead of the first: keep the value in a variable and print it at section end or END. Another option is to have the prompt put the Status line before the quote.

findings.title: 50902 duplicates 50901's fixture and run instead of strengthening the existing additionalContext owner
findings.body: The diff does not change the additionalContext path. test_scripts_50902 stages the same content under the same key and runs the same hook invocation as 50901. It then checks a different field of the response with an exact assert_equal. The additionalContext contract already has an owner, test_scripts_2831, which asserts only with `--partial '7731-ZARBLAX'`. CLAUDE.md and semantic-regression-tests-over-source-shape.md say to strengthen the best owner instead of duplicating the assertion. As it stands there are two fixture copies to maintain, and 2831's weak `--partial` check is left in place.
findings.fix: Add an exact `jq -r '.hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext'` + assert_equal against `$content` to 50901 (same response), or make 2831's check exact. Then delete 50902.

findings.title: Status parser can't tell lines inside the verbatim operator quote from the extractor's own Status: line
findings.body:
The new prompt (executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh:~318-320) puts the verbatim quote of the operator's last message, with no line prefix, before the real `Status:` line. The awk parser takes the first `^Status:` line inside `## Last request` and exits, and it stops at the first `^## ` line. It does not distinguish quoted content from the service field.
- If the operator's message contains a line like `Status: Answered`, for example an example in a code block, pasted CI output or an earlier handoff, that line is chosen. The real status written after the quote (e.g. `Not answered`) is never read, so the operator sees a false confirmation. If the quoted value is unrecognized, the real status is dropped instead.
- A quoted line starting with `## ` ends the section early, which falls back to the goal-only message.
This contradicts protected-slot-signal-extraction.md, which says a machine signal must occupy a protected position so examples inside text stay plain content.
