The comment at :79-80 says only the section's own Status: line is eligible, but the quote is inside the section. The impact is limited to the operator-facing systemMessage.
findings.fix: Make the prompt and parser agree on a protected slot. Either fix the Status line immediately after the `## Last request` heading, before the quote, and read only that position, or require the quote as a `> ` blockquote. Another option is to take the last `Status:` line in the section rather than the first.

findings.title: No fixture puts a Status: line after a real Last request section, so the boundary exit is untested
findings.body:
The parser stops scanning at the next heading with `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` (executable_handoff-session-start.sh:84). That line is the only thing that stops a Status: line in a later section, such as `## Key Details` or `## Warnings`, from being reported as the last-request status. None of the new fixtures reaches it:
- 50901 and 50902 put a recognized Status: inside `## Last request`.
- The first new 2834 case ("A status outside Last request…") has no `## Last request` section at all, so `in_last_request` is never set.
- The second 2834 case has an unrecognized value inside the section.

If line 84 is deleted, every test stays green. Yet a handoff like `## Last request\nPlease continue.\n\n## Key Details\nStatus: Not answered` would then show `Status: Not answered` to the operator. That is exactly the regression the goal names: "status parsing cannot pick up a Status: line from another section". The fixture that claims to cover it tests a different case, a missing section. So it gives a false signal for the boundary the comment describes.
findings.fix:
Change the 'status outside Last request' fixture in test_scripts_2834 to `## Goal
ship the hook change

## Last request
Please continue.

## Key Details
Status: Not answered`, keep the goal-only exact assertion, and confirm it goes red with line 84 removed.

findings.title: The prompt-contract assertion 'Last user request' is always satisfied by the facts block, not by the new instruction
findings.body:
`assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` is meant to check that the new `## Last request` instruction refers to the facts block. But transcript_facts always emits `Last user request: <literal>` or `Last user request: None` on every path, including both fallback printfs (executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh:245, 266). That line is part of `${facts_block}`, which is interpolated into every prompt. The new instruction itself says 'from the facts block above' and never contains the phrase. So if the 'Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above' line were deleted or changed to stop pointing at the facts, this assertion would still pass.

The other checks are loose substring matches ('Status:', 'Answered', …). The neighbouring test 2844 argues at :10724-10727 that for a model consumer 'the instruction itself is the interface: the exact sentence, not merely some text'. 50900 does not follow that rule, so the instruction it adds is guarded only by fragments.
findings.fix: Extract the `## Last request` block from the captured prompt (e.g. `sed -n '/^## Last request$/,/^## Key Details$/p'`) and `assert_equal` it against the exact three instruction lines. Drop the 'Last user request' substring check.

findings.title: Comment still says the operator is shown 'the one block they can check: the goal'
findings.body: The comment above the goal parser says: "The operator never sees additionalContext, so show them the one block they can check: the goal the extractor settled on." After this change, systemMessage also carries `Status: <status>` from the `## Last request` section (line 108). So the goal is no longer the only block shown. The comment describes the old behaviour of code that is still in use. Fix the comment; the code is right.
findings.fix: Reword it to say the operator is shown the goal, plus the last-request status when one is recognized. Or drop 'the one block' and let the new status comment at :78-80 cover the addition.

findings.title: A multi-line verbatim quote can supply or hide the Status: line
findings.body:
The prompt asks the extractor to quote the operator's last message verbatim (pre-compact.sh:319). The facts value is a decoded JSON literal, so it can span several lines. The prompt does not ask for a `> ` prefix on the quote. The parser takes the first line in the section that starts with `Status:` and exits, whatever the value. Two things can go wrong when the operator's message has a line like `Status: Answered`, for example pasted CI or tool output:
- A recognized value in the quote is shown as the extractor's verdict.
- An unrecognized value hides the real Status: line below it.
A `## ` line inside the quote ends the section early, but that only falls back to goal-only. The comment at :79-80 says only the section's own Status: line is eligible; the quoted message is inside the section, so the comment does not rule this out. In practice, models often blockquote such text, so this is uncommon.
findings.fix: Ask in the prompt for the quote as a `> ` blockquote, or have the parser take the last `Status:` line in the section rather than the first.

findings.title: Проверка prompt пропускает потерю инструкции о проверке выводов
findings.body: Новая проверка ищет '<claim>, verify with: <exact command>' во всём prompt только один раз. Если удалить инструкцию из Relevant Context или Key Details, оставшееся вхождение удовлетворит проверку. Регрессия останется незамеченной: extractor больше не получает требование снабжать выводы командой проверки в обоих разделах, как требует goal.md. Это противоречит правилу semantic-regression-tests-over-source-shape.md: проверка должна менять результат при потере защищаемого поведения.
findings.fix: Выделить Relevant Context и Key Details из переданного extractor prompt и отдельно проверить наличие полной инструкции в каждом разделе.

findings.title: Negative fixture for a Status outside Last request has no Last request section, so the section-boundary exit is never exercised
findings.body: The goal requires that "status parsing cannot pick up a Status: line from another section" and that tests go red on real regressions. The parser enforces this with two things: it only starts reading at `## Last request`, and it stops at the next heading (`in_last_request && /^## / { exit }`, executable_handoff-session-start.sh:82). The new negative case in test_scripts_2834 stages `## Goal` + `## Key Details\nStatus: Not answered`. That fixture has no `## Last request` heading, so `in_last_request` is never set and the result is empty whether or not the boundary exit exists. No other fixture has a Last request section without its own Status line followed by a later section that has one. I traced every fixture that mentions Last request (11628, 11646, 11707). If you delete the `/^## / { exit }` line, all three tests stay green. A handoff where the model drops the Status line under Last request and Key Details contains `Status: Answered` would then show the operator a status taken from Key Details. That is exactly the regression the goal names. This is the case `docs/solutions/design-patterns/source-greps-need-a-second-side.md` (severity: high) describes: "an absence assertion runs against a section the file never had, and cannot fail". The runtime harm is confined to the operator display. Major reflects the project's own severity rule for this class of test.
findings.fix:
Add or replace the fixture: `## Goal
ship the hook change

## Last request
Please continue.

## Key Details
Status: Not answered`, then assert the systemMessage is the goal alone. Prove it goes red with the boundary-exit line removed.

findings.title: Status parser can't tell lines in the verbatim operator quote from the model's own Status: line
findings.body: The prompt asks for the operator's last message to be quoted verbatim, with no line prefix. The facts block carries it as a JSON literal, and the extractor is told to decode it and copy it exactly, so a multi-line message keeps its line breaks in the `## Last request` section. The parser takes the first line starting with `Status:` and stops at the first line starting with `## `. It does not know which lines belong to the quote. Two consequences follow, both observed from the awk and inferred for real transcripts. (1) If the operator's message has a line starting with `## ` (pasted Markdown, common in this repo), the awk exits before reaching the real Status line, so a recognized status is silently dropped. (2) If the message has a line starting with `Status:` (pasted CI or handoff text), that line is chosen. If it is unrecognized, the real status is dropped. If it happens to read `Status: Answered` etc., the operator sees the quote's value instead of the extractor's judgement. The impact is limited to the operator-facing systemMessage, and additionalContext is unchanged.
findings.fix: Have the prompt ask for the quote with every line prefixed by `> ` so quoted lines can never start with `Status:` or `## `. Alternatively, have the parser take the last `Status:` line before the section ends rather than the first.

findings.title: Mandatory verbatim quote of a last request up to 4000 chars conflicts with the 400-word handoff cap
findings.body: `bounded_text` (line 141) allows the last user request in the facts block to be up to 4000 characters, roughly 600+ words. The new `## Last request` section requires that text to be quoted verbatim, and the constraints repeat "copy ... the last user request exactly". The 400-word cap on the whole `<handoff>` is kept. When the operator's last message is long, the extractor (haiku) must break one instruction. It can truncate or paraphrase the quote, which defeats the purpose of the facts block. Or it can exceed the cap, crowding out Relevant Context and Key Details. Which one it picks is unpredictable. This is inferred from the prompt text and was not observed in a run.
findings.fix: Exempt the quoted request from the word cap, or tell the extractor to quote at most the first N words, then mark the cut, when the request is long.

findings.title: Парсер принимает Status: из дословной цитаты запроса
findings.body: Новый шаблон помещает дословный запрос перед служебным Status:. Если оператор спрашивает о выводе хука и вставляет блок кода со строкой `Status: Answered`, awk принимает эту строку и завершает поиск. Настоящий статус `Not answered`, записанный экстрактором после цитаты, уже не читается. Оператор видит неверный статус; парсер не различает цитируемые данные и служебное поле.
findings.fix: Поместить служебный Status: перед цитатой в шаблоне либо задать отдельное представление статуса, которое парсер отличает от содержимого запроса.

findings.title: Проверка инструкции об inference не различает два обязательных раздела
findings.body: Контракт требует инструкцию `<claim>, verify with: <exact command>` в Relevant Context и Key Details. Новая проверка ищет её один раз во всём prompt. Удаление инструкции из любого одного раздела оставляет все утверждения теста истинными, хотя экстрактор получает неполный контракт. Это конкретный ложнозелёный путь, запрещённый правилом semantic-regression-tests-over-source-shape.md.
findings.fix: Проверять наличие инструкции отдельно внутри Relevant Context и Key Details.

findings.title: No fixture covers a Status: line in a section after Last request, so the section-boundary guard can be deleted with every test still green
findings.body:
The goal says status parsing must not pick up a Status: line from another section. The injector enforces this with two guards (executable_handoff-session-start.sh:82-83): it starts scanning only at `## Last request`, and `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` stops at the next heading. The new tests cover the first guard only. The negative case at 11692 has no `## Last request` section at all. The unrecognized-value case at 11703 has no section after Last request. In 50901/50902, the valid Status: line comes before `## Key Details`, so the scan exits on that line and never reaches the boundary.

Red-making edit: delete line 83 (`in_last_request && /^## / { exit }`). No test goes red. With that guard gone, take a handoff whose Last request section has no `Status:` line (for example the model wrote `**Status:** Answered`), followed by `## Key Details` with a line `Status: Not answered`. The operator would see `Status: Not answered` taken from Key Details. That is exactly the cross-section leak the goal rules out.
findings.fix:
Add one more case to the 2834 negative block: `## Goal
ship the hook change

## Last request
Please continue.

## Key Details
Status: Not answered`. Assert that systemMessage is exactly the goal-only message.

findings.title: Prompt-contract assertions pin text the change did not add, or pin it too loosely to catch an injector-breaking edit
findings.body:
`assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` (10758) cannot go red on any edit to the new instruction. The phrase comes from the transcript_facts block, which always emits it, even in the fallback `Last user request: None` (pre-compact.sh:261-266). If someone rewrites the new line `[Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above]` and drops the facts-block reference, the test stays green. The goal names that reference as a correctness condition.

`assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Status:'` (10759) is a weak substring check. The consumer is the awk in executable_handoff-session-start.sh. It matches only `^Status:` at the start of a line, inside a `^## Last request[[:space:]]*$` section, and only the exact-case values. A prompt edit to `**Status:** [...]` or `- Status: [...]` would make the model write a line the injector never recognizes. The status would then silently drop from the systemMessage, and 50900 would still pass, because 'Status:' and each value still appear somewhere in the prompt. Under the repository's test-oracle doc, this prompt text is consumed verbatim by a tool, so its literal shape is the contract and should be asserted exactly.
findings.fix: Replace the two loose checks with whole-line matches on the lines the injector depends on: `grep -Fxq 'Status: [Use exactly one of: Answered, Partially answered, Not answered]'` and `grep -Fxq '## Last request'`. Then assert the facts-block reference itself ('from the facts block above') instead of 'Last user request'.

findings.title: 50902 copies 50901's fixture and run instead of strengthening the existing additionalContext owner
findings.body: 50902 stages the same content under the same key, runs the same hook invocation, and checks another field of the same response as 50901. The additionalContext contract already has an owner: test_scripts_2831 (11591), which checks it only with `assert_output --partial '7731-ZARBLAX'`. CLAUDE.md says: "Search existing coverage first and strengthen its best owner instead of duplicating the assertion." The exact byte-for-byte check is worth having; its red-making edit is the injector rewriting or stripping the Status line from content. But here it is a second copy of a fixture and run, not an upgrade to the owner. 2831's weak `--partial` check is left in place.
findings.fix: Add `run jq -r '.hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext' <<< "$response"; assert_success; assert_equal "$output" "$content"` to 50901 (same response), or make 2831's check exact. Then delete 50902.

findings.title: Inference-instruction check does not distinguish the two sections that must each carry it
findings.body: The contract requires the `<claim>, verify with: <exact command>` instruction in both Relevant Context and Key Details. The new check searches for it once in the whole prompt. Deleting it from either section leaves every assertion true, because the other copy still matches. The extractor would then get an incomplete contract, and the obligation the goal and #509 require for that section would be gone. This is the false-green path that semantic-regression-tests-over-source-shape.md forbids.
findings.fix: Extract Relevant Context and Key Details from the captured prompt, and check for the full instruction separately in each, so that removing either copy turns the test red.

findings.title: Отрицательный пример не проверяет выход из Last request
findings.body: В новом примере со статусом в Key Details отсутствует секция Last request, поэтому парсер вообще не входит в неё. Удаление условия `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` из injector оставит все изменённые тесты зелёными. Однако для handoff с Last request без строки Status и последующей Key Details со строкой `Status: Not answered` такой парсер покажет чужой статус оператору, нарушая требование брать статус только из Last request.
findings.fix: Добавить к этому примеру Last request без статуса перед Key Details. Сохранить точное ожидание сообщения без статуса и проверить, что удаление условия выхода делает тест красным.

findings.title: Prompt places the verbatim quote above the Status: line without a delimiter, so quoted text can supply or hide the status
findings.body: The new template (executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh:319-320) puts '[Quote the operator's last real message verbatim ...]' before 'Status: [...]' and does not say how to delimit the quote. The decoded `last_user` value can be up to 4000 characters and span several lines. The parser in executable_handoff-session-start.sh:81-90 takes the first `^Status:` line in the section and stops at the first `^## ` line. Two failures follow. (a) A quoted line starting with `## ` ends the section before the real Status: line, so the status is silently dropped. (b) A quoted line starting with `Status: Answered`, `Status: Partially answered` or `Status: Not answered` is shown to the operator instead of the extractor's real status. This breaks the protected-slot rule in docs/solutions/design-patterns/protected-slot-signal-extraction.md. The impact is limited to the operator-facing systemMessage, because additionalContext still carries the full handoff. The tests use only a one-line quote. This duplicates 2c6f8daa94e8c3d6099cecf798647ed6, which covers the parser side.
findings.fix: Put the `Status:` line directly under `## Last request`, before the quote, so the parser's first-match-and-exit reads it first. Optionally also require the quote as a `> ` blockquote.

findings.title: A verbatim quote of a last request up to 4000 characters conflicts with the kept 400-word handoff cap
findings.body: Before this change, the prompt already had the 400-word cap and the 'copy the last user request exactly' constraint, and `bounded_text` (line 141) already capped the value at 4000 characters plus ' [truncated]'. What this change adds is a mandatory `## Last request` section that must quote that value verbatim (line 319). For a long operator message, such as one with pasted logs or diffs, the extractor must now choose between three outcomes. It can go over the 400-word cap. It can squeeze Goal, Relevant Context or Key Details to make room. Or it can truncate or paraphrase the quote, which defeats the exact-copy goal of this change. Going over a soft word cap is harmless here. Truncating or paraphrasing the quote is the real cost. The prompt states no precedence. This is inferred from the prompt text and was not observed in a run.
findings.fix: Add one constraint that states the precedence. Either exempt the Last request quote from the 400-word cap, or tell the extractor to quote at most the first N words and end with [truncated].

findings.title: No instruction for the case where the facts block says `Last user request: None`
findings.body:
The facts block prints `Last user request: None` when no qualifying user message exists, and also on every fallback path where fact extraction fails (lines 245 and 267). The new section always asks the model to quote the operator's message and pick one of three statuses. It gives no rule for the None case.

When this happens, some runs will quote "None". Others will pick a message from conversation memory, which the facts block exists to prevent. Others will drop the section. The chosen status (Answered or Not answered) is then arbitrary, and the injector shows it to the operator as if it were real.
findings.fix: Add one line: "When the facts block says None, write `None` and omit the Status line." The injector already shows the goal alone when no recognized status is found.

findings.title: "last real message" / "facts block" do not match the prompt's own names for the same thing
findings.body:
The rest of the prompt calls this source `<transcript_facts>` and the value `Last user request` (lines 251-262 and 337). The new line says "the operator's last real message ... from the facts block above". That gives one meaning two new names.

The word "real" also invites the model to judge whether the facts value counts as "real". It may pass over a short "continue" or a slash-command rendering and pick an earlier message from the conversation instead. That would contradict line 337's "copy ... exactly from <transcript_facts>". The harness filtering has already decided which message is real.
findings.fix: Reword as: "Quote the `Last user request` value from <transcript_facts> verbatim". Use the same leading word as line 337 and drop "real".

findings.title: A transient read failure while waiting exits 1, the code for a failed verdict
findings.body: `code test` has already queued the run when `waitForVersion` starts polling. If a poll then fails with anything that is not a 401/403 or a timeout, for example a 502 or a network reset, `return yield* Effect.fail(outcome.error)` rejects. `runCode` prints the bare error message and returns 1. The goal defines exit 1 as 'failed' and exit 2 as 'still pending / engine refuses'. The run is still queued and pending on the worker, but the agent sees exit 1 with no hint. It will either treat the tests as failed or run `code test` again. The second call is what the goal forbids, because it queues another run once the first has settled. The timeout path prints a `code status ... --wait` follow-up. This path prints none. `codeStatus` has the same shape at line 709, but that verb only reads, so a retry there is harmless. Fix: in `waitForVersion`, map a non-refusal read error to exit 2, with a stderr line such as `verdict read failed: <message> — wait with: code status --tree-version <id> --wait`. Alternatively, append that follow-up to the thrown message. I confirmed this by reading the code and did not run it. The tests in `cli.code.verdict.test.ts` that I listed do not cover a transient non-401/403 failure during polling.

findings.title: The `code pull` example suggests flags the CLI rejects
findings.body: The reviewer says this problem existed before the change under review. The README example allows `code pull --tree-version <id>` and `code pull --latest`. With either flag, `codePull()` returns 1 before it reads the tree or clones. The nearby tests in `cli.code.test.ts` assert that refusal. A user who follows the example to fetch a version gets no files.
findings.fix: Remove these flags from the `code pull` example. To read a version, point to `git show v/<version id>:<path>` after cloning.

findings.title: Every 401/403 and any "sign-in expired" error on the verdict read is reported as "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet"
findings.body: `isVerdictReadRefusal` maps any 401/403, and any error whose message matches /sign-in expired/i, to the old-engine degrade path. That path prints "pending — this engine cannot answer the verdict yet" and exits 2. The same refusal can come from a revoked membership, a closed session, or an expired login whose refresh failed. The queue call may have just succeeded under the same credential. Observed: the classifier does not distinguish the cause. Inferred: an agent told the engine is old keeps waiting instead of re-authenticating. The goal only requires the old-engine case to degrade clearly. Narrow it to the status and error key the old engine actually returns, or add the status to the line.
findings.fix: Include the HTTP status or the underlying message in the degrade line, and don't treat the platform-token refresh failure ("sign-in expired") as an engine refusal. Let it propagate as an error.

findings.title: `code test --json` output changes from the command output ({version}) to the bare version object
findings.body: Before this change `code test --json` printed the full `run-source-tree-tests` output, `{ "version": {...} }`. `renderTestVersion` now prints `JSON.stringify(version)`, so the object is the version itself. Observed: the shape differs for both `--json` and `--no-wait --json`. Inferred: a script reading `.version.testsStatus` gets undefined. No docs or tests in the diff mention the changed shape, so I did not confirm any consumer of it.
findings.fix: Print `{ version }` in `--json` mode, or state the new shape in the docs and help text.

findings.title: No test goes red if the Last request section-exit rule is removed
findings.body:
The goal requires that status parsing cannot pick up a `Status:` line from another section. The guard for this is `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` (executable_handoff-session-start.sh:83), and no fixture exercises it. The new negative fixture in test 2834 has no `## Last request` heading, so `in_last_request` is never set and the fixture passes whether or not the exit rule exists. Tests 50901 and 50902 put their recognized Status line inside Last request, so the first match exits before any later section is read. The second negative case checks only the value whitelist. One reviewer ran the mutant awk with line 83 removed. It printed nothing for the existing fixture but printed `Not answered` for `## Last request
Please continue.

## Key Details
Status: Not answered`. That second shape is the realistic one, because Key Details follows Last request in the prompt. So if the extractor leaves out the status, a later section's `Status:` line is shown to the operator as the request status, and every test still passes.
findings.fix: Change or extend the 2834 negative block with a fixture that has `## Last request` holding a quote and no Status line, followed by `## Key Details\nStatus: Not answered`. Assert the exact goal-only systemMessage, and check that the test goes red when line 83 is removed.

findings.title: Prompt puts an undelimited verbatim quote before `Status:`, so pasted `Status:` or `## ` lines take over or end status parsing
findings.body: The new prompt says `[Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above]` and places the `Status:` line after it. It does not say how to set the quote off, for example with a blockquote or a fence. The last user request can be up to 4000 characters of decoded text and often contains pasted output. The SessionStart parser takes the first `Status:` line in the section and ends the section at any `## ` line. One reviewer fed the awk a section whose plain quote contained `Status: Answered`, followed by the model's real status; the parser returned `Answered`. A quoted `Status: open` line makes the parser exit with an unrecognized value, and a quoted `## ` heading ends the section early. In both cases the real status is dropped. The result varies by run, depending on whether the extractor chooses to blockquote the message.
findings.fix: Put the `Status:` line first in `## Last request`, before the quote, or require a `> ` prefix on every quoted line so quoted text cannot match `^Status:` or `^## `.

findings.title: Prompt-contract test 50900 uses loose substrings; the 'Last user request' assertion always passes and the parsed section shape is not pinned
findings.body: `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` cannot fail because of this change. handoff_payload has no transcript_path, so the facts block always renders the pre-existing `Last user request: None` fallback, and the existing Constraints line already contains the phrase. The new instruction (`Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above`) could lose its facts-block reference or be deleted, and the test would still pass. The other assertions are unanchored substring greps that check fragments appear somewhere in the prompt, so prompt edits that break the injector stay green. Examples: moving the `Status:` line under `## Key Details`, changing it to `**Status:** ...`, renaming the heading to `### Last request` or `## Last Request`, or reordering sections. After any of these the status silently stops appearing to the operator.
findings.fix: Extract the `## Last request` block (up to the next `## `) from the captured prompt and assert it exactly, or use `grep -Fxq` for the exact `## Last request` and `Status: [Use exactly one of: ...]` lines. Replace the 'Last user request' check with one for the new 'verbatim from the facts block above' wording.

findings.title: The status parser does not stop at </handoff>, unlike the sibling goal parser
findings.body: The stored handoff_content is the extractor's entire output: <analysis>, <handoff>, and anything after it (pre-compact.sh:404). The goal awk stops at `^## ` or `^</handoff>`. The status awk stops only at `^## `. Warnings is optional, and the model may drop Key Details. If `## Last request` is then the last section and has no Status line, the awk keeps reading past `</handoff>`. It will take a `Status:` line from trailing text outside the handoff. This is an inconsistent boundary rather than a likely path.
findings.fix: Use the goal parser's terminator: `in_last_request && (/^## / || /^<\/handoff>/) { exit }`.

findings.title: Lines in the verbatim request quote are parsed as handoff markup, so they can fake or hide the status
findings.body: The prompt puts the operator's last message, quoted verbatim and decoded from JSON so multi-line text stays multi-line, before the `Status:` line in `## Last request`. The awk parser takes the first `^Status:` line in the section and exits at the first `^## ` line. If the quoted message contains its own line such as `Status: Answered`, for example a pasted hook systemMessage or an earlier handoff, while the real status after the quote is `Not answered`, the operator is shown `Answered`. If the quoted message contains a `## ` heading, for example a pasted plan, the parser exits before the real status line and the status is silently dropped. This affects only the operator-facing systemMessage. The trigger depends on the model quoting the message without a `>` prefix.
findings.fix: Give the quote an unambiguous boundary (for example, require a `> ` prefix on every quoted line) and parse the status from outside the quote. Alternatively, take the last `^Status:` line in the section, or put Status first.

findings.title: Prompt test checks the `verify with` inference rule once; deleting it from one of its two sections stays green
findings.body: The prompt has `[When an item is inferred rather than observed, write it as: <claim>, verify with: <exact command>]` twice, under Relevant Context (pre-compact.sh:316) and Key Details (pre-compact.sh:325). Test 50900 (scripts_test.sh:10764) runs `assert_file_contains` once against the whole prompt, so it passes while either copy remains. Deleting the instruction from one section leaves the test green. The extractor could then write inferred items in that section with no verification command. The test fails only if both copies are removed. The consequence is a softer prompt rather than broken parsing, so this is minor.
findings.fix: Count the occurrences (for example `grep -cF` and expect 2), or pull the Relevant Context and Key Details blocks out of the captured prompt and check that each one contains the rule.

findings.title: No test covers the end of the Last request section, so removing that boundary stays green
findings.body:
The goal requires that status parsing cannot pick up a `Status:` line from another section, and that tests go red on real regressions. The section boundary is `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` (executable_handoff-session-start.sh:83). None of the new fixtures put a `Status:` line in a section *after* `## Last request`:
- 50901 has `Status:` inside Last request.
- The first new negative case in 2834 has no `## Last request` heading at all, so `in_last_request` is never set.
- The second negative case uses an unrecognized value.

If someone deletes line 83, every test still passes. A real handoff that has `## Last request` with no Status line, followed by `## Key Details` containing `Status: Answered`, would then show `Status: Answered` to the operator. The test-oracle gate (docs/solutions/design-patterns/semantic-regression-tests-over-source-shape.md, symptom "A test stays green after the protected behavior is removed") calls this out. The damage is limited to the operator-facing systemMessage, so this is minor.
findings.fix:
Change the first negative case in test 2834 so it includes the heading, e.g. `## Goal
ship the hook change

## Last request
Please continue.

## Key Details
Status: Not answered`. It should still expect the goal-only systemMessage. Confirm it goes red when line 83 is removed.

findings.title: The `Last user request` assertion in 50900 always passes, whatever the new prompt says
findings.body: `handoff_payload` builds a payload with no `transcript_path`, so `transcript_facts` takes its fallback. That fallback always prints `Last user request: None` into the prompt, and it already existed before this change (pre-compact.sh lines 113/120/245/265 at 12681fb). So `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` passes even if the new instruction (`Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above`) is deleted or changed. That instruction is the only part of the new `## Last request` contract that tells the extractor where the quote comes from, and nothing checks it. This is a false-green assertion of the kind the test-oracle gate names ("A test stays green after the protected behavior is removed").
findings.fix: Assert the new instruction text instead, e.g. `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'verbatim from the facts block'`. Alternatively, drop the `Last user request` assertion.

findings.title: Строка Status в цитате запроса принимается за статус ответа
findings.body: Промпт требует дословно включить последнее сообщение оператора перед строкой статуса. Если сообщение содержит отдельную строку `Status: Answered`, а фактический статус после цитаты — `Status: Not answered`, парсер возьмёт первую строку и покажет оператору `Answered`. Пользователь увидит неверное состояние своего запроса.
findings.fix: Задать для цитаты формат с однозначными границами и извлекать статус только за пределами цитаты.

findings.title: Проверка промпта пропускает удаление правила для одного раздела
findings.body: Проверка ищет `<claim>, verify with: <exact command>` во всём промпте один раз, хотя правило требуется и в Relevant Context, и в Key Details. Если удалить его из любого одного раздела, тест останется зелёным, а агент перестанет получать требуемое указание для этого раздела. Это нарушает требование различающего теста из `docs/solutions/design-patterns/semantic-regression-tests-over-source-shape.md`.
findings.fix: Проверять правило отдельно внутри каждого из двух разделов промпта.

findings.title: No test fails if the Last request parser stops ending at the next heading
findings.body: The goal says status parsing must not pick up a `Status:` line from another section. The new negative fixture in test_scripts_2834 has no `## Last request` section at all (`## Goal` … `## Key Details\nStatus: Not answered`), so `in_last_request` is never set. That fixture goes red only if the section guard is removed completely. If someone deletes the terminator `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` (executable_handoff-session-start.sh:83), every test stays green: 50901/50902 have their Status line inside Last request, and 2834 never enters the section. With that regression, a handoff whose Last request section has no Status line, followed by `## Key Details` with `Status: Answered`, would show `Status: Answered` to the operator. That is the cross-section leak the goal rules out, and the suite would not catch it.
findings.fix:
Add one more fixture to the 2834 negative block: `## Goal
ship the hook change

## Last request
Please continue.

## Key Details
Status: Answered`. Assert the systemMessage is exactly the goal-only form.

findings.title: Prompt-contract test does not tie the Status: line to the ## Last request section the parser reads
findings.body: test_scripts_50900 checks each fragment with a separate `assert_file_contains`, so it only shows that each substring appears somewhere in the prompt. The injector only reads a `Status:` line that sits under `## Last request` and before the next `## ` heading. Suppose a later prompt edit moves the `Status: [Use exactly one of …]` line under `## Key Details`, or renames the heading to `## Last Request`. The second case still passes because `'Last user request'` and the other substrings match elsewhere. The status would then never appear on screen, and 50900 would stay green. Also, `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` matches the facts block's pre-existing `Last user request:` line (pre-compact.sh:254), not the new instruction. So it does not prove that the new section points the extractor at the facts block. This is the coupling the goal names ("prompt section order/wording does not break … the facts-block reference"), and the test cannot detect it breaking.
findings.fix: Extract the text between `## Last request` and the next `## ` heading from the captured prompt with awk. Assert that block exactly, or at least assert that it contains both the `Status: [Use exactly one of: Answered, Partially answered, Not answered]` line and `from the facts block above`.

findings.title: Verbatim last-request quote conflicts with the 400-word handoff cap
findings.body: The new `## Last request` section requires the operator's last message verbatim, and the existing constraints still say `Maximum 400 words in the <handoff> section`. `bounded_text` (line 141) passes up to 4000 characters plus ` [truncated]`, which on its own can exceed 400 words. The prompt does not say which rule wins. A model will usually let the soft cap slip, but some runs may shorten or paraphrase the quote, which breaks the copy-exactly constraint at line 337. Other runs may squeeze Relevant Context and Key Details instead.
findings.fix: State which rule wins, for example: the quote does not count toward the 400 words, or long quotes are explicitly truncated with a marker.

findings.title: Status parser can be fooled by a verbatim quote that contains `## ` headings or its own `Status:` line
findings.body: The prompt asks the extractor to decode the last user request and copy it verbatim into `## Last request`, ahead of the `Status:` line. The awk parser in executable_handoff-session-start.sh:81-91 exits at the first `## ` line and takes the first `^Status:` line in the section. If the operator's last message was multi-line markdown with a level-2 heading, the parser stops inside the quote and shows no status. That is quiet, and no worse than before this change. In the rarer case where the quoted message has a line that is exactly `Status: Answered`, `Status: Partially answered` or `Status: Not answered`, the operator is shown the quote's status instead of the extractor's. No fixture covers either shape: 50901 quotes a single plain line.
findings.fix: Make the quote unambiguous, for example by requiring a `> ` blockquote prefix or putting Status before the quote, and parse to match. Add a fixture whose quote contains a `## ` heading and a `Status:` line, and assert that the handoff's own status is shown.

findings.title: No fixture puts a Status: line in a section after Last request, so the section-exit rule is untested
findings.body:
The goal requires that status parsing cannot pick up a `Status:` line from another section, and that the tests go red on real regressions. The negative fixture at 11692-11702 has no `## Last request` heading at all, so `in_last_request` is never set. That fixture stays empty whether or not the boundary rule exists. Test 50901 does have a Last request section, but its own `Status:` line comes first, and its trailing `## Key Details` holds no Status line.

I traced the regression by hand: delete `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` (executable_handoff-session-start.sh:83). Test 50901, 50902 and both 2834 negative cases still pass. In the prompt, `## Last request` comes before `## Key Details` and `## Warnings`. So the realistic leak is forward: the handoff omits the status, or writes one the parser does not recognize, and a later section holds a `Status: Not answered` line. Without the exit rule, the operator sees that later line as the request status.

The code is correct today. What is missing is the oracle for the leak in that direction.
findings.fix: In the 2834 negative block, add a fixture with `## Last request` holding a quote and no Status line, followed by `## Key Details` containing `Status: Not answered`. Assert the goal-only systemMessage. Check that it goes red when line 83 is removed.

findings.title: Status parser reads the first `^Status:` line of the section, and the verbatim operator quote comes before the real Status line
findings.body:
What the code does: the prompt (pre-compact.sh:319-320) puts the verbatim quote of the operator's last message first in `## Last request`, then the `Status:` line. The awk takes the first line matching `^Status:` and exits at the first line matching `^## `. The facts block JSON-encodes the message, and the prompt tells the model to decode it and copy it exactly. So a multi-line operator message becomes multiple raw lines inside the section.

What follows from that, inferred rather than run: an operator message with a line starting `Status:` controls the status shown. For example, the operator pastes this hook's own systemMessage, or a prior handoff (`Status: Answered`). In that case the operator's text is shown instead of the extractor's verdict. An operator message with a `## ` heading line ends the section before the real Status line, so the status is silently dropped.

Only the operator-facing systemMessage is affected. additionalContext is unchanged. The trigger needs the model to quote the message without a `>` blockquote prefix. That is plausible in this repository, where the operator often pastes hook output, but not certain.
findings.fix: Take the last `^Status:` line in the section instead of the first, or have the prompt require the quote as a `>` blockquote so quoted lines cannot match `^Status:` or `^## `.

findings.title: `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` is already met by the facts block, so it does not test the new facts-block reference
findings.body: The goal lists "does not break the facts-block reference" as a correctness condition, and this looks like the assertion meant to guard it. But the string `Last user request` is already in the prompt from earlier code. It appears in the `<transcript_facts>` block (pre-compact.sh:260-261, and the fallbacks at 113/120/245/265). It also appears in the existing constraint line "Copy ... the last user request exactly from <transcript_facts>". If the new instruction at line 319 (`Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above`) lost its facts-block reference, or were reworded to let the model paraphrase, this assertion would still pass. The other new assertions do pin the new section. This one alone cannot fail for the regression it appears to cover.
findings.fix: Assert the new instruction text itself, e.g. `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'verbatim from the facts block above'`, or drop the assertion.

findings.title: Строки цитаты разбираются как разметка handoff
findings.body: Последний запрос может содержать собственную строку `Status: Answered` или заголовок `## ...`. Если извлекатель скопирует такой запрос дословно, парсер примет эту строку за статус handoff либо завершит поиск до настоящего статуса. Например, при последующем `Status: Not answered` оператор увидит `Answered`. Текущие проверки используют однострочный запрос и не выявляют это расхождение.
findings.fix: Задать для цитаты и статуса однозначный формат и разбирать статус вне текста цитаты.

findings.title: Дословная цитата длинного запроса конфликтует с лимитом handoff
findings.body: Если последний запрос содержит более 400 слов, но укладывается в лимит фактов по символам, извлекатель одновременно получает требование скопировать его целиком и ограничить весь handoff 400 словами. Выполнить оба требования невозможно: цитата или другие необходимые сведения будут сокращены либо лимит будет нарушен.
findings.fix: Определить правило для длинных запросов, например исключить дословную цитату из лимита или явно разрешить её сокращение.

findings.title: Проверка инструкции об inference не различает два раздела
findings.body: Тест ищет `<claim>, verify with: <exact command>` во всём prompt только один раз. Если удалить эту инструкцию из Relevant Context или Key Details, оставшаяся копия сохранит зелёный результат, хотя контракт требует её для обоих разделов.
findings.fix: Проверять инструкцию внутри каждого из двух разделов prompt.

findings.title: Negative case for 'Status outside Last request' cannot catch loss of the section-boundary exit
findings.body:
The new 2834 fixture puts `Status: Not answered` under `## Key Details` in a handoff that has no `## Last request` heading. `in_last_request` is never set, so the case passes even if `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` (executable_handoff-session-start.sh:83) is deleted. I ran the mutant awk without that line. It prints nothing for this fixture, so the test stays green. For `## Last request
Please continue.

## Key Details
Status: Not answered` it prints `Not answered`. That second shape is the one the extraction prompt produces, because Key Details follows Last request. So if the extractor drops the Status line, a `Status:` line under Key Details gets shown to the operator as the last-request status. 50901 does not catch this either, because its Status line is inside the section. The goal's requirement that status parsing must not pick up a Status: line from another section therefore has no test that fails when the guard is removed.
findings.fix: Change the fixture so it includes a `## Last request` section without a Status line, followed by `## Key Details\nStatus: Not answered`. Keep the exact goal-only systemMessage assertion.

findings.title: Prompt-contract test uses unanchored substrings, so it misses changes that break the injector parser
findings.body: test_scripts_50900 checks the captured prompt with `assert_file_contains`, which is an unanchored BRE grep. The injector only recognizes a status when the extractor writes `^## Last request[[:space:]]*$` and then a line starting `^Status:`. Two prompt edits would break that while the test stays green: changing the template line to `**Status:** [Use exactly one of: ...]` (it still contains `Status:`), or changing the heading to `### Last request` (it still contains `## Last request`). After either edit the extractor follows the template, the parser never matches, and the status silently stops appearing. Separately, `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` matches the `<transcript_facts>` label line. transcript_facts always emits that line, including its fallback, and tests 508 and the ones around it already cover it. This assertion cannot go red when anything in the new Last request instruction changes, including its reference to the facts block.
findings.fix: Use `grep -Fxq` for the exact template lines the parser depends on: `## Last request` and `Status: [Use exactly one of: Answered, Partially answered, Not answered]`. Replace the 'Last user request' check with an exact-line check for the new instruction that references the facts block.

findings.title: Тест не проверяет строку Status внутри цитаты запроса
findings.body: Последнее сообщение оператора может содержать отдельную строку «Status: Answered». Prompt требует скопировать сообщение дословно перед настоящей строкой состояния, а парсер выбирает первую строку Status в разделе. Поэтому при фактическом «Not answered» оператор увидит «Answered». Единственный положительный пример теста содержит Status только после цитаты и остаётся зелёным при этом сбое.
findings.fix: Добавить пример с распознаваемой строкой Status внутри дословного запроса и отделить цитату от состояния так, чтобы парсер выбирал состояние handoff.

findings.title: Проверка prompt не различает требования для двух разделов
findings.body: Если удалить инструкцию «verify with» из раздела Key Details, тест останется зелёным: он находит ту же строку в разделе Relevant Context. При этом следующему агенту могут передать предположения из Key Details без команды проверки, вопреки цели изменения.
findings.fix: Проверять требование отдельно в каждом разделе prompt, в пределах соответствующего раздела.

findings.title: Prompt leaves the verbatim quote's format open, so a pasted `Status:` or `## ` line in the operator's message takes over or ends status parsing
findings.body:
The new prompt says `[Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above]` and puts the `Status:` line right after it. It does not say how to set off the quote, for example with a `> ` blockquote or a fence. The last user request can be up to 4000 characters of decoded text (`bounded_text`), and it often holds pasted output. The SessionStart parser (`executable_handoff-session-start.sh:82-89`) takes the first line in the section that starts with `Status:` and exits. It also ends the section at any line starting with `## `.

I fed the parser's awk a `## Last request` section whose plain quoted message contained `Status: Answered`, followed later by the model's real status line. The parser returned `Answered`, so the operator sees a wrong status. A quote with a non-matching `Status: open` line makes the parser exit with an unrecognized value, and the real status is dropped. A quote containing a markdown `## ` heading ends the section before the real `Status:` line, and the status is silently dropped too. The goal says status parsing must not pick up a Status: line from another section. Here it picks one up from inside the quote. Runs differ depending on whether the extractor decides to blockquote the message.
findings.fix: Tell the extractor to set the quote off with a `> ` prefix on every line, and to put `Status:` on its own line after the quote. Or have the parser use the last `Status:` line in the section instead of the first.

findings.title: `Status:` template does not say the value must stand alone, but the parser rejects anything after it
findings.body: The prompt shows `Status: [Use exactly one of: Answered, Partially answered, Not answered]` and on the next line asks the extractor to name what to check first when the request is not fully answered. Nothing says the Status line must contain only the value. A natural output is `Status: Partially answered — check the parser first`, or `Not answered.` with a trailing period. The reviewer ran the parser's awk on the first form and got the whole string back, which the `case` at session-start.sh:91-94 rejects, so the status is silently left out. That happens exactly when the request is not fully answered, which is when the operator most needs to see it.
findings.fix: Change the template line to something like `Status: <one of Answered | Partially answered | Not answered, alone on this line>`, and put what to check first on the following line.

findings.title: Verbatim last-request quote conflicts with the 400-word handoff cap
findings.body: The new section asks for the operator's last message `verbatim`. The constraints keep `Maximum 400 words in the <handoff> section`. The facts block passes a last user request of up to 4000 characters plus ` [truncated]` (`bounded_text`, line 141). That is several hundred words before Goal, Relevant Context and Key Details are counted. When the message is long, the extractor has to break one rule, and the prompt does not say which wins. Some runs will truncate or paraphrase the quote, which also breaks the existing constraint to copy the last user request exactly. Other runs will go over the cap, or squeeze the goal-serving sections. The prompt gives no rule for this case.
findings.fix: State which rule wins. For example: the quote does not count toward the 400 words, or quotes over N words keep their first N words followed by `[…]`.

findings.title: No instruction for `Last user request: None`, so the extractor may invent a status for a request that does not exist
findings.body: `transcript_facts` writes `Last user request: None` when it finds no real user message, and also on both failure paths (lines 245 and 266). The new section always asks for a quote and one of three statuses. It does not cover the case with no request. The extractor may write `Status: Not answered`, `Status: Answered`, or leave the line out. For the first two, the SessionStart hook shows a recognized status beside the goal, telling the operator something about a request that does not exist. Severity is minor because the result is only a misleading line on the operator's screen.
findings.fix: Add one line, for example: `If Last user request is None, write None and omit Status.`

findings.title: The new line names the source differently from the existing constraint (`the operator's last real message` from `the facts block` vs `Last user request` in `<transcript_facts>`)
findings.body: Line 319 says `Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above`. The block is tagged `<transcript_facts>` and its field is `Last user request:`. The existing constraint (line 337) refers to `the last user request exactly from <transcript_facts>`. So the same input has two names. The word `real` also invites the extractor to judge the facts value and look back through the session for a different message. That would break the copy-exactly constraint. The local facts extraction exists to prevent that kind of second-guessing.
findings.fix: Write `[Quote the Last user request from <transcript_facts> verbatim]`.

findings.title: The `verify with` rule appears word for word in two sections
findings.body: `[When an item is inferred rather than observed, write it as: <claim>, verify with: <exact command>]` appears both under Relevant Context (line 316) and under Key Details (line 325). That breaks the single-source-of-truth rule in writing-for-agents: any change to the format must now be made in two places, and the repetition makes the rule look more important than it is. It applies to the whole handoff, so it belongs once in the Constraints list.
findings.fix: Move it once into Constraints, for example: `- Write any inferred item as: <claim>, verify with: <exact command>`.

findings.title: A verbatim operator quote can supply or cut off the Status: line the parser reads
findings.body:
The prompt tells the extractor to quote the operator's last message verbatim, and to put the quote before the `Status:` line (pre-compact.sh:318-320). The facts block JSON-encodes that message, and the extractor is told to decode it, so a multi-line message comes back as raw lines. The awk parser takes the first line in the section that starts with `Status:`, and it leaves the section at the first line that starts with `## `. Both kinds of line can come from the operator's own text:
- The operator pastes something like `Status: Answered\nwhy is CI still red?`. The parser returns `Answered` from the quote, and the systemMessage shows `Status: Answered` when the extractor actually wrote `Not answered`.
- The operator pastes markdown that has a `## ` heading. The parser leaves the section before it reaches the real Status line, so the status is silently dropped.
The goal requires that status parsing cannot pick up a Status: line that is not the status. In the first case the operator sees a wrong status, which defeats the point of the feature. Confidence is limited because the result depends on how the model formats the quote; a `> ` blockquote would avoid both cases.
findings.fix: Tell the extractor to prefix every quoted line with `> ` (or to put the Status line first in the section). Then make the parser skip lines that start with `>`, or read only the last `Status:` line in the section.

findings.title: No test covers the parser's section-end guard: deleting it leaves every test green
findings.body: The goal requires that status parsing cannot pick up a Status: line from another section, and that the tests go red on real regressions. The new negative case in test_scripts_2834 stages a handoff that has no `## Last request` heading at all. The awk never enters the section, so that case cannot tell whether the `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` guard (session-start.sh:83) exists. Tests 50901 and 50902 put the real Status line inside Last request, and the parser stops at that first match. If the guard is deleted, every fixture still passes. Yet the parser would then read `Status: Answered` from Key Details or Warnings when the extractor leaves the Status line out of Last request, which is exactly the leak the goal names.
findings.fix: Add one fixture to the 2834 negative block: `## Last request` with no Status line, followed by `## Key Details` and then `Status: Not answered`. Assert that the systemMessage is the goal alone.

findings.title: The prompt-contract test's 'Last user request' assertion is always true and does not guard the new facts-block reference
findings.body: test_scripts_50900 asserts `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'`. The `<transcript_facts>` block always emits that label, as `Last user request: None` in the fallback or with a value, and it did so before this change. The 508-series tests already pin that label. The new section's actual reference text is "verbatim from the facts block above" (pre-compact.sh:319), and nothing checks it, so removing or rewording it keeps 50900 green. Relatedly, the unanchored substring checks do not pin the `^Status:` line shape the injector matches: changing the template to `- Status:` or `**Status:**` stays green.
findings.fix: Assert the new instruction text, e.g. `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'verbatim from the facts block above'`. Anchor the section and Status template lines, e.g. `'^## Last request$'` and `'^Status: \[Use exactly one of: Answered, Partially answered, Not answered\]$'`. Drop the vacuous 'Last user request' assertion.

findings.title: Строка из цитаты запроса может подменить показанный статус
findings.body: Новый prompt требует дословно цитировать запрос перед вычисленным Status. Если оператор прислал многострочный запрос с примером `Status: Answered`, эта строка попадает в раздел Last request. Парсер принимает её первой и завершает поиск, даже внутри блока кода. Поэтому handoff с цитатой этого примера и последующим настоящим `Status: Not answered` покажет оператору `Answered`. Это новый дефект отображения; additionalContext остаётся без изменений.
findings.fix: Разместить вычисленный Status сразу после заголовка Last request, перед цитатой, и читать только эту позицию как метаданные.

findings.title: The status parser takes the first `Status:` line in Last request, which can be a line inside the verbatim operator quote
findings.body:
The new prompt (pre-compact.sh:318-320) asks the extractor to quote the operator's last message verbatim, decoded from JSON, before the `Status:` line. A multi-line message therefore comes back as raw lines. The awk prints and exits on the first line in `## Last request` that starts with `Status:`, and it leaves the section at the first line that starts with `## `. Both kinds of line can come from the operator's own text:
- The message contains a line `Status: Answered`, for example a pasted earlier handoff, a systemMessage, or a code-block example. The operator is shown `Answered` when the extractor actually wrote `Not answered`.
- The message contains a markdown `## ` heading. The parser leaves the section before the real Status line, and the status is silently dropped.
No test covers either case. The impact is limited to a wrong operator-facing systemMessage; additionalContext is unchanged.
findings.fix: Put the computed Status line directly after the `## Last request` heading, before the quote. Or have the prompt write the quote as a `> ` blockquote and make the parser skip lines that start with `>`, or read the last `Status:` line in the section.

findings.title: No fixture tests the end-of-section boundary of the status parser; removing the `/^## / { exit }` rule stays green
findings.body: The new negative case at 11692 puts `Status: Not answered` under `## Key Details` in a handoff that has no `## Last request` header. `in_last_request` is never set, so this fixture passes whether or not session-start.sh:83 (`in_last_request && /^## / { exit }`) exists. Test 50901 has its Status line inside the section, and the second negative only checks value validation. Regression that goes uncaught: delete line 83, and a handoff whose `## Last request` section has no recognized Status line, followed by `## Key Details` with `Status: Not answered`, now shows `Status: Not answered`. The goal says parsing must not pick up a Status: line from another section and that tests must go red on real regressions. The scope boundary that enforces this has no test that can fail.
findings.fix: Change the first negative fixture so it includes a `## Last request` section with a quote but no Status line, followed by `## Key Details` with `Status: Not answered`. Keep the same expected goal-only output.

findings.title: `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` checks text that was there before this change, so it does not guard the new facts-block reference
findings.body: `handoff_payload` (scripts_test.sh:10585) sends no `transcript_path`, so `transcript_facts` falls back and the prompt always contains `Last user request: None` from the `<transcript_facts>` block. That string was already in the prompt before this change. If someone rewrote the new `## Last request` instruction so it no longer points the extractor at the facts block (for example, dropping the line at pre-compact.sh:319), this assertion would stay green. The scope lists 'the facts-block reference' as part of the prompt contract this test protects. This assertion cannot fail for that regression.
findings.fix: Assert the new instruction text itself, e.g. `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'verbatim from the facts block'`, or drop the vacuous assertion.

findings.title: Required verbatim quote of the last request can exceed the 400-word handoff cap that was kept
findings.body: `last_user` is limited only to 4000 characters (line 141), which is roughly 600+ words. The new template requires a verbatim quote of that message inside `<handoff>`, and the constraint at 336-337 forbids paraphrasing it. Line 334 still caps the whole `<handoff>` at 400 words. When the operator's last message is a long paste (a review, a log, a spec), the extractor cannot follow both rules. It must truncate the 'verbatim' quote, push the handoff over the cap, or cut the Relevant Context and Key Details sections the goal depends on. The prompt does not say which rule wins, so the result depends on whatever choice Haiku makes.
findings.fix: State how a long request is handled. For example, exclude the quote from the 400-word count, or allow quoting the first N lines followed by `[truncated]`.

findings.title: Проверка инструкции об inference не различает два обязательных раздела
findings.body: Новый test_scripts_50900 ищет шаблон '<claim>, verify with: <exact command>' во всём prompt. Если удалить инструкцию из Relevant Context или Key Details, проверка продолжит проходить благодаря оставшемуся вхождению. Поэтому тест принимает prompt, который больше не требует помечать предположения в одном из обязательных разделов. Это противоречит docs/solutions/design-patterns/semantic-regression-tests-over-source-shape.md:77–81: проверка должна различать правильный и неправильный результат на выбранной границе.
findings.fix: Выделить Relevant Context и Key Details из перехваченного prompt и проверить инструкцию отдельно в каждом разделе.

findings.title: No test covers the Last request section-end guard; deleting `/^## / { exit }` leaves every test green
findings.body:
The goal requires that status parsing never reads a `Status:` line from another section. The only thing enforcing that is `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` at executable_handoff-session-start.sh:83. No fixture exercises it:
- The new negative case in test_scripts_2834 ("A status outside Last request…") stages a handoff with no `## Last request` heading at all, so `in_last_request` is never set and the case only tests entry into the section.
- 50901 and the second negative case put `Status:` inside Last request, so the parser exits there.
- 50902 never inspects systemMessage.

If line 83 is deleted, every test stays green. Yet a handoff like `## Last request\nPlease continue.\n\n## Key Details\nStatus: Answered` would then show `Status: Answered` to the operator, a status taken from the wrong section. Reviewers who ran the awk alone confirmed this: it prints `Answered` without the terminator and nothing with it. The negative case's comment claims coverage the fixture does not give.
findings.fix:
Change the first negative fixture in 2834 to `## Goal
ship the hook change

## Last request
Please continue.

## Key Details
Status: Not answered`, and assert the systemMessage is the goal alone. It then goes red when either the section-entry flag or the section-end exit is removed.

findings.title: Header still lists 'Four deliberate departures from upstream' after the prompt structure diverged again
findings.body: The header comment lists each deliberate departure from the vendored kylesnowschwartz/claude-handoff, and earlier changes kept it current (the transcript_facts and bare-/compact goal bullets were added as their changes landed). This change makes the extraction prompt diverge from upstream again: a new `## Last request` section with a machine-parsed `Status:` line, the `<claim>, verify with: <exact command>` format for inferred items, and the removed 3-7 bullet cap. The header still says 'Four deliberate departures' and does not mention any of these. The new section is also a cross-hook contract, because the SessionStart injector parses it. A maintainer re-syncing from upstream would treat the header as the complete list and could drop the section the injector depends on.
findings.fix: Change the count to five and add a bullet: the prompt asks for a `## Last request` section whose `Status:` line the SessionStart injector shows to the operator.

findings.title: The prompt asks for an unframed verbatim quote, so the operator's own text is parsed as handoff structure
findings.body: Line 319 tells the extractor to quote the operator's last message verbatim. That message can be up to 4000 characters and several lines long. The prompt asks for no framing such as a `>` blockquote or a code fence. The injector's comment promises that only the extractor's Status line in Last request is eligible, and an unframed quote breaks that promise. A quoted `## ` heading ends the section early, so the real status is dropped. A quoted `Status: Answered` line is shown as the handoff's status. The heading also appears in the additionalContext the next model reads, where it looks like a handoff section.
findings.fix: Tell the extractor to quote the message as a `>` blockquote (or a fenced block), so no quoted line can start with `## ` or `Status:`.

findings.title: New test 50902 duplicates the additionalContext check that 2831 already owns, instead of strengthening it
findings.body: CLAUDE.md's testing rule says: 'Search existing coverage first and strengthen its best owner instead of duplicating the assertion.' test_scripts_2831 (line 11590) already owns the claim that the handoff goes into additionalContext, but it only checks `--partial '7731-ZARBLAX'`. Instead of changing 2831 to an exact match, the change adds a separate test, 50902, with the same assertion on a different fixture. This change also never touches how `$context` reaches jq; only the new `--arg status` was added. So 50902 guards nothing that 2831 would miss if 2831 used an exact match, and 2831 keeps its weak `--partial` assertion.
findings.fix: Change 2831's additionalContext assertion to `assert_equal "$output" "<staged content>"` and drop 50902. Alternatively, fold the Last-request fixture into 2831.

findings.title: Тест не проверяет выход из раздела Last request
findings.body: Новый отрицательный пример вообще не содержит `## Last request`, поэтому проверяет только вход в раздел. Если удалить `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` из injector, все добавленные примеры по-прежнему пройдут. При этом handoff с `## Last request` без статуса и последующим `## Key Details\nStatus: Not answered` покажет оператору статус из другого раздела. Именно эту регрессию должен исключать контракт изменения.
findings.fix: Добавить в этот тест пример с разделом Last request без статуса, затем Key Details с распознаваемым Status, и проверить точное сообщение без статуса.

findings.title: No fixture tests the Last request section-end guard; deleting it keeps every new test green
findings.body:
The goal requires that status parsing never reads a Status: line from another section and that the tests fail when that breaks. The guard that enforces this is `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` at executable_handoff-session-start.sh:83. None of the new fixtures exercise it:
- 50901 puts Status inside Last request, so the parser exits at that line.
- The first negative case in 2834 ("A status outside Last request…") has no `## Last request` heading at all, so `in_last_request` is never set.
- The second negative case has an unrecognized value inside Last request.

I ran the parser with line 83 removed against all three fixtures. The results were the same: `Not answered`, empty, and `Waiting for a reply` (which the case filter drops). The real regression input is `## Last request` with no Status line, followed by `## Key Details` containing `Status: Answered`. Without the guard, that input yields `Answered`, so the operator sees a status taken from the wrong section and every test stays green. The comment on the negative case claims coverage the fixture does not give. The damage from the regression is contained (wrong operator-facing systemMessage only), so this is minor. The project profile still weights a green test that cannot fail heavily.
findings.fix: Change the first negative fixture in 2834 to include a `## Last request` section with no Status line before `## Key Details\nStatus: Not answered`. Then removing the section-end exit turns the test red.

findings.title: Prompt-contract test asserts 'Last user request', which the facts block always supplies, and checks the inference rule only once
findings.body:
`assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` passes on the old prompt too. The `<transcript_facts>` block always prints `Last user request: …`, including the `None` fallback at executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh:245/265. The new section never uses that phrase: it says "from the facts block above" (pre-compact.sh:319). So the assertion does not check the new section's reference to the facts field. Deleting or garbling that reference keeps 50900 green. The goal explicitly names that reference as a correctness condition.

In the same way, `'<claim>, verify with: <exact command>'` is asserted once, but the goal requires the rule in both Relevant Context and Key Details. Removing it from either section stays green. `Maximum 400 words` also passes on the pre-change prompt. That is deliberate (the cap is kept), so it is not part of this finding.
findings.fix: Assert the actual new instruction line, for example `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'verbatim from the facts block above'` (or reword the prompt to name `Last user request` in `<transcript_facts>` and assert that line). Count the inference-rule occurrences, for example `run grep -cF '<claim>, verify with: <exact command>' "$prompt"; assert_output 2`.

findings.title: The verbatim quote is not delimited, so its lines are parsed as handoff structure
findings.body:
The prompt tells the extractor to quote the operator's last message verbatim, decoded from the JSON literal, directly above the `Status:` line. The session-start parser (session-start.sh:81-90) reads that section line by line and has no quote boundary. Two cases follow:
- A last message with a line starting `## ` (common when the operator pastes Markdown, such as a review prompt or a doc) ends the section before the Status line, so the recognized status is silently dropped.
- A last message with a column-0 `Status: Answered` line wins, because the parser exits on the first match.

The heading also appears in the additionalContext the next model reads, where it looks like a handoff section. Observed: the parser behavior above. Inferred: whether it triggers depends on the model writing the quote without a `> ` prefix or a fence, which the prompt does not ask for.

The verbatim instruction also conflicts with the kept 400-word cap. `bounded_text` allows up to 4000 characters (about 600 words) for the last request, so a long last message cannot be quoted verbatim within the cap. The model must then break one of the two rules.
findings.fix: Ask for the quote as a Markdown blockquote (`> ` on every line) or a fenced block, and say that long requests may be shortened with an ellipsis. Optionally make the parser ignore lines starting with `>`.

findings.title: Парсер принимает Status: внутри цитаты за служебный статус
findings.body:
Новый шаблон требует дословно вставить запрос перед служебным Status:. Если запрос содержит пример «Объясни этот вывод:
```text
Status: Answered
```», его дословная вставка соответствует шаблону. Однако awk принимает строку внутри примера за статус и завершает поиск. Настоящий Status: Not answered ниже уже не читается, и оператор видит Answered. Дополнительный контекст модели сохраняется, поэтому последствие ограничено неверным статусом на экране.
findings.fix: Разместить служебный статус перед цитатой и читать его из фиксированной позиции либо отделить цитату форматом, который парсер однозначно различает.

findings.title: Общий поиск инструкции не различает два обязательных раздела
findings.body: Требование задаёт формат проверки предположений отдельно для Relevant Context и Key Details. Тест ищет соответствующую инструкцию только один раз во всём prompt. Если удалить её из Key Details на строке 325 extraction hook, совпадение останется в Relevant Context, а остальные проверки этого теста также сохранятся. Проверка останется зелёной при утрате обязательной инструкции для одного раздела. Это противоречит правилу semantic-regression-tests-over-source-shape.md о различающем оракуле; вывод установлен чтением, без запуска тестов.
findings.fix: Выделить оба раздела переданного prompt и проверить наличие инструкции отдельно в каждом.

findings.title: Negative cases never exercise the Last request section's end boundary, so deleting the `^## ` exit stays green
findings.body:
The goal's correctness bar includes "status parsing cannot pick up a Status: line from another section". The parser enforces this in two places in `home/private_dot_claude/hooks/executable_handoff-session-start.sh`: line 82 enters the section, and line 83 (`in_last_request && /^## / { exit }`) leaves it. The new negative fixture in test_scripts_2834 puts `Status: Not answered` under `## Key Details` with no `## Last request` section at all, so it only tests the entry flag. No test has a `## Last request` section without a Status line followed by a later section that does have one.

The edit that should turn the tests red: delete line 83. Fixture 1 still yields no status because the section flag is never set. Fixture 2, test 50901 and test 50902 all put Status inside the section, and 50902 never inspects systemMessage. So every test stays green. With that regression in place, a handoff like `## Last request
<quote>

## Key Details
Status: Answered` would show `Status: Answered` to the operator. The extractor never answered the status question, but the operator sees a status that a later section supplied. The test comment says "A status outside Last request is ordinary handoff text", so this test is meant to catch exactly that, but it only covers half of it.
findings.fix:
Make the first negative fixture in 2834 `## Goal
ship the hook change

## Last request
Please continue.

## Key Details
Status: Not answered`. Then it goes red both when the section flag is removed and when the end-of-section exit is removed.

findings.title: Prompt-contract test does not pin the `^Status:` line shape the injector parses, and its 'Last user request' assertion cannot fail because of this change
findings.body:
test_scripts_50900 checks the prompt with unanchored BRE substrings. `assert_file_contains` is `grep -q` (test-dsl.bash:428). The only contract between the extraction prompt and the injector is that the extractor writes a line starting with `Status:` under `## Last request`. The injector awk matches `/^Status:/`. Edit the prompt template line in `executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh` to `- Status: ...` or `**Status:** ...` and 50900 stays green, because `Status:` still appears as a substring. Haiku copies the template, so the injector stops recognizing any status and the operator never sees one. This is the one place where the prompt's literal shape is the contract (policy text consumed verbatim, as the oracle doc allows). The assertion is too loose to protect it.

Separately, `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` (line 10758) matches the facts-block line that existed before this change. The 508-series tests already pin that line exactly (e.g. 10799, 10833), so this assertion adds no new coverage. The prompt's new reference text is "from the facts block above", and nothing checks it.
findings.fix: Anchor the assertions: `assert_file_contains "$prompt" '^## Last request$'` and `assert_file_contains "$prompt" '^Status: \[Use exactly one of: Answered, Partially answered, Not answered\]$'`. Drop the 'Last user request' line, since the 508 tests own it.

findings.title: The inference-rule check searches the whole prompt, so losing the rule from one of its two required sections stays green
findings.body: test_scripts_50900 searches the whole prompt for `<claim>, verify with: <exact command>` once. The requirement places that instruction separately in Relevant Context and in Key Details. If it is removed from either section (for example Key Details at pre-compact.sh:325), the match in the other section keeps the test green. The test therefore accepts a prompt that no longer requires inferences to be marked in one of the required sections. That goes against the discriminating-oracle rule in semantic-regression-tests-over-source-shape.md.
findings.fix: Extract Relevant Context and Key Details from the captured prompt and check the instruction in each separately. Or count occurrences, e.g. `run grep -cF '<claim>, verify with: <exact command>' "$prompt"; assert_output 2`.

findings.title: Отрицательный сценарий не проверяет окончание Last request
