findings.body: Новый сценарий со статусом вне Last request вообще не содержит этого раздела. Поэтому удаление правила `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` из инжектора не нарушит ни один приведённый сценарий. При такой регрессии handoff с Last request без Status, затем Key Details со строкой `Status: Not answered`, покажет оператору статус из другого раздела. Запрет этого поведения прямо входит в цель изменения.
findings.fix: Добавить Last request перед Key Details в отрицательную фикстуру, оставив распознаваемый Status только в Key Details и сохранив ожидание сообщения без статуса.

findings.title: The required verbatim quote of the last request conflicts with the 400-word handoff cap that was kept
findings.body: Line 319 now requires a verbatim quote of the operator's last message. Line 337 forbids paraphrasing it. Line 334 keeps "Maximum 400 words in the <handoff> section". `bounded_text` (line 141) caps the message only at 4000 characters, which is about 600 words. A pasted log or review reaches that easily. When the last message is that long, the extractor cannot follow every rule. It must break the cap, cut or summarize the quote, or squeeze the other sections. The prompt does not say which rule wins. No code enforces the cap (the output goes to the store unchanged, lines 401-405), so nothing breaks. The cost is inconsistent handoffs: sometimes the quote is paraphrased, and sometimes Relevant Context or Key Details is thinned out.
findings.fix: State which rule wins. For example: "The verbatim quote does not count toward the 400-word limit", or "If the quote would exceed N words, quote its first N words and append [truncated]".

findings.title: No instruction for the `Last user request: None` case the facts block emits
findings.body: `transcript_facts` emits `Last user request: None` when no eligible user record exists and on both jq fallback paths (around lines 120, 245 and 265). The new section tells the extractor to quote that message verbatim and then choose exactly one of Answered, Partially answered or Not answered. None of these fits a request that does not exist, and the prompt gives no instruction for this case. Runs will diverge: some drop the section, some quote "None", some invent a request. Some will emit `Status: Answered`. The injector accepts that value, so the operator sees a confident status for a request that was never captured.
findings.fix: Add the case inline, e.g. "If the facts block says `Last user request: None`, write `None` and omit the Status line."

findings.title: The prompt does not pin the Status line format the injector parses, so a well-meant variant silently drops the status
findings.body: `handoff-session-start.sh` (lines 81-95) accepts only a line that starts with `Status:` and whose trimmed remainder is exactly `Answered`, `Partially answered` or `Not answered`. The template shows `Status:` on its own line but does not say that the value must stand alone. Line 321 ("name what to check first") comes right after it, so the model can write `Status: Not answered — check X first`. Markdown forms such as `**Status:** Answered` cause the same problem. In each case the case statement clears the value, and the systemMessage shows no status and no sign that one is missing. additionalContext is not affected.
findings.fix: Pin the contract in the template: "Write the Status line as `Status: <value>` with nothing else on the line; put what to check first on the next line."

findings.title: Three names for one fact, plus an undefined "real" filter on an already-filtered value
findings.body: Line 319 says "the operator's last real message ... from the facts block above". The block is labelled `<transcript_facts>`, and its field is `Last user request:`. Line 337 calls it "the last user request" from `<transcript_facts>`. So one fact has three names, which breaks the one-source-of-truth rule. The word "real" also invites the extractor to filter again: `is_harness` has already removed meta, compact and hook records. The extractor may decide the supplied message is not "real" and quote an earlier one from its own memory of the session. Line 337 forbids exactly that ('do not paraphrase or infer replacements').
findings.fix: Use the facts block's own label: "[Copy `Last user request` from <transcript_facts> verbatim]".

findings.title: No test covers the outer-catch failure path, so dropping its finish() would leave the suite green
findings.body: Issue 022 requires that the manual command report every terminal outcome. The tests cover the inner exec failure paths (throw, killed, nonzero) and lock contention. The outer `catch` at index.ts:445-447 has no test. That catch reports infrastructure failures: acquireLock or reclaimStaleLock throwing (mkdir/write of the lock directory failing), and an injected snapshotExtensions rejecting. Every test uses a fresh temp lockPath with non-throwing snapshotExtensions, and no test asserts "Pi update failed without blocking startup". If someone removed the finish() wrapper on line 447, the suite would stay green. Lock or state-directory failures would then go silent on startup and in the manual command, which is the regression issue 022 is meant to prevent. The current code behaves correctly; what is missing is the regression guard.
findings.fix: Add a manual-trigger test and a startup-trigger test where lock acquisition fails (e.g. deps.lockPath under a regular file so mkdir throws ENOTDIR) or snapshotExtensions throws. Assert status "failed" and that notifications equals exactly one `warning` entry carrying the failure detail.

findings.title: Manual command now shows a failure message that says "without blocking startup"
findings.body: The outer-catch message is the startup-specific text `Pi update failed without blocking startup: ${detail}`. Before this change the result was thrown away, so no user saw it. Now `finish` sends it to ui.notify for both triggers. A user who runs `/brew-auto-update-now` and hits a lock or filesystem error mid-session gets a warning about startup, which does not describe what they did. The notification still goes out, so the impact is limited to confusing wording.
findings.fix: Make the message depend on the trigger, or drop the clause, e.g. `Pi update failed: ${detail}`.

findings.title: Update failures stay invisible in headless mode (pi -p / --mode json)
findings.body: The reviewer marks this as pre-existing and already tracked in new issue 2026-09-02-007. In headless mode, runPrintMode binds extensions without a uiContext, so finish's ui.notify falls through to a no-op noOpUIContext. The session_start handler discards the returned `failed` result, so a nonzero `brew update` shows the user nothing. This change fixed the interactive path, but the headless path still loses the result.
findings.fix: Add a failure-reporting channel for headless mode, e.g. stderr, while keeping the chosen notification policy.

findings.title: The manual command now shows a failure message that says "without blocking startup"
findings.body: The outer catch builds "Pi update failed without blocking startup: ${detail}" no matter what the trigger is. Before this change failure results were never notified, so nobody saw the wording. Now `finish` sends it to ui.notify at `warning` for `trigger === "manual"` as well. A user who runs `/brew-auto-update-now` and hits a lock or state-directory error (e.g. EACCES creating `$XDG_STATE_HOME/pi`) is told the update failed "without blocking startup", even though no startup took place. The impact is wording only, but this change is what makes it user-visible.
findings.fix: Make the message trigger-neutral (e.g. `Pi update failed: ${detail}`), or add the "without blocking startup" clause only when trigger === "startup".

findings.title: Outer-catch failure path and manual 'could not be verified' outcome lack notification assertions
findings.body: The goal requires that the tests fail if a terminal result is silently discarded again, and issue 022's scope asks the manual command to report every terminal outcome. Two paths have no notification oracle. (1) The outer catch at index.ts:447, reached when acquireLock throws (e.g. the state directory can't be created): no test drives it, so reverting `return finish(trigger, ui, reportFailure(...))` to the old bare `return reportFailure(...)` keeps the suite green while that failure goes silent again. (2) The manual command's "Pi package update completed; extension changes could not be verified." outcome: the only test of it is now startup-only (silent), so dropping the notification for manual would also stay green. Separately, the PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 test at line 303 discards `fakeUi()` and asserts nothing about notifications.
findings.fix: Add a manual-trigger test whose lockPath parent is a regular file, so `mkdir` throws, and assert one `warning` notification. Add a manual-trigger case with `snapshotExtensions: async () => undefined` asserting the `info` "could not be verified" notification.

findings.title: Startup silence on `skipped` (offline/disabled) and the manual 'could not be verified' notification are never asserted
findings.body: Issue 022's policy says startup stays silent on non-failure outcomes and asks for a nearby control for each case. The change adds silent-startup controls for up-to-date, unknown-extension and contended, but none for `skipped`. The `disables startup only when PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE is zero` test passes `fakeUi().ui` and throws the notifications array away, and no test runs startup with PI_OFFLINE=1. If shouldNotify regressed to `if (status === "failed" || status === "skipped") return true;` (index.ts:260), every user with PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 or PI_OFFLINE=1 would get an info toast on every Pi start, and the suite would stay green. Separately, the test that used to cover "Pi package update completed; extension changes could not be verified." was switched from manual to startup. No manual test now checks that this outcome is reported, so if the manual path silently dropped it, no test would fail.
findings.fix: In the PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 test, keep the startup fakeUi and assert `notifications` toEqual([]). Add a startup PI_OFFLINE=1 case with the same empty assertion. Add a manual run with `snapshotExtensions: async () => undefined` that asserts one `info` notification with the unverifiable-extension message.

findings.title: Issue 022 is still `status: "open"` with no Resolution after the PR that fixes it lands
findings.body: This PR implements everything issue 022 scopes: failures notify at `warning` on every startup, the manual command reports every outcome, and the tests now assert notifications. But the issue keeps `status: "open"` (line 8), has no `closed` date and no `## Resolution` section, and the section heading is still `## Open decisions`, now opening with "Both decisions below are settled". Elsewhere in the repo, fix PRs close their issue in the same commit (e.g. 243fbd5 #125, 7283641 #116, d0bb59d #114 set `status: "done"`), and `scripts/issues` `finish_issue` adds the Resolution section. As it stands, `python3 scripts/issues list` (default filter: open/in-progress), which the repository-issues skill uses to pick work, still lists 022 as unresolved. An agent could redo the fix, and new issue 007 says 022 "fixed" index.ts, which contradicts 022's open status. If closure is deliberately waiting on the scope's "demonstrate the red state" step, the issue doesn't say so.
findings.fix: Move 022 through `python3 scripts/issues` to done with a resolution naming the finish/shouldNotify routing and the verifying tests, or mark it in-progress with a note on what remains. Rename the `## Open decisions` heading (e.g. `## Decisions`) since nothing in it is open.

findings.title: Уведомление из внешнего catch осталось без регрессионной проверки
findings.body: Новый тест с исключением из exec попадает во внутренний catch, а внешний catch в index.ts:445–447 не проверяет ни один сценарий. Если убрать finish только из внешнего catch, тесты не обнаружат возврат исходного дефекта: ошибка создания каталога блокировки, например EACCES, снова останется невидимой при запуске и ручном вызове.
findings.fix: Добавить сюда сценарий ошибки создания блокировки, например с обычным файлом вместо родительского каталога. Проверить failed и одно уведомление warning с причиной ошибки.

findings.title: The snapshot test would not catch losing the package.json read
findings.body: This gap predates the change and is already tracked in issue 2026-09-01-004. Between snapshots the test changes only package-lock.json. If captureExtensionSnapshot stopped reading package.json, the comparison would still pass because of the lock-file change. Updates that change only package.json would then go undetected, and the user would wrongly be told "Pi is up to date".
findings.fix: Add a case to the existing snapshot test that changes only package.json and leaves the lock files untouched.

findings.title: The timeout test does not check that the timeout is passed to exec
findings.body: This gap predates the change and is already tracked in issue 2026-09-01-004. The exec stub always returns killed: true and ignores its options. If the timeout were dropped or passed wrong, the test would not notice, and a hung update command could run without its limit.
findings.fix: Set a non-default timeoutMs and assert options.timeout on every exec call.

findings.title: The manual-command registration test never invokes the handler
findings.body: This gap predates the change and is already tracked in issue 2026-09-01-004. The test saves commandHandler and only checks that it exists. If the /brew-auto-update-now handler stopped calling runBrewAutoUpdate, neither this test nor the direct calls in other tests would notice. The user's manual command would then run no update and report nothing.
findings.fix: Invoke the saved commandHandler and assert the observed command sequence and the final notification.

findings.title: Follow-up issue 007 wrongly says every terminal outcome is sent through ui.notify
findings.body: The first sentence says every terminal result, including skip, contention and up-to-date, goes through ui.notify. But shouldNotify (index.ts:260-263) deliberately suppresses those notifications at startup. Every result passes through finish, but not every result calls ui.notify. The description contradicts the adopted policy and gives the next fix the wrong starting behavior.
findings.fix: Say that every result passes through finish/shouldNotify, and that ui.notify runs per the policy: all manual outcomes, startup failures, and installed updates.

findings.title: Two terminal outcomes have no notification oracle: startup `skipped`, and manual unverifiable-extension `complete`
findings.body:
Two of the routing rules in `shouldNotify` have no test that checks what gets notified.

(1) Startup `skipped`. The `disables startup only when PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE is zero` test (line ~303) builds its UI with `fakeUi().ui` and throws the `notifications` array away. No test runs startup with `PI_OFFLINE=1`. Contention is the only startup non-failure outcome whose silence is checked (line ~428). Suppose `shouldNotify` regressed so it notified on `skipped` at startup. A user who set `PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0` to silence the updater would then see "Pi startup update is disabled." on every launch, and the suite would stay green. That breaks the settled policy that startup stays silent on non-failure outcomes. Issue 022's scope also asks for a nearby control covering the startup policy.

(2) Manual `complete` where extension changes could not be verified. The test that used to cover this case (`reports an unknown extension state…`) was switched from `manual` to `startup`. No manual test now checks that "Pi package update completed; extension changes could not be verified." is reported. If the manual path dropped this result silently, no test would fail. The goal explicitly requires tests that catch that.
findings.fix: In the PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE test, keep the startup `notifications` and assert it equals `[]`. Add a startup `PI_OFFLINE=1` case asserting silence. Add a manual run with `snapshotExtensions: async () => undefined` asserting one `info` notification with the unverifiable-extension message.

findings.title: The catch-all failure message says "without blocking startup" and is now shown to manual-command users
findings.body: The outer `catch` builds the message "Pi update failed without blocking startup: …" no matter what `trigger` is. Before this change, failure results were never notified, so nobody saw this text. Now `finish` always notifies failures. Example: the user runs `/brew-auto-update-now`, and `acquireLock` throws because `mkdir` on the state directory fails with EACCES or ENOSPC. The user sees a warning about not blocking startup after a manual command that had nothing to do with startup. This is only wording, but the change is what makes it reachable.
findings.fix: Choose the message based on the trigger, e.g. `trigger === "startup" ? "Pi update failed without blocking startup: …" : "Pi update failed: …"`.

findings.title: No test covers the outer-catch failure path, so dropping its finish() leaves the suite green
findings.body: index.ts:447 is the only terminal path that reports infrastructure failures: acquireLock throwing (mkdir EACCES/ENOSPC on the state dir), snapshotExtensions rejecting, or any other unexpected throw. No test reaches it. Every test uses a fresh temp lockPath, and no snapshotExtensions override ever throws. Red-making edit: revert line 447 to `return reportFailure(`Pi update failed without blocking startup: ${detail}`)`. Startup and the manual command would both go silent on that failure again, and every test would still pass. The goal requires that the tests fail if any terminal result is silently discarded again. This path is the one terminal result with no owner.
findings.fix: Add a manual-trigger test with `snapshotExtensions: async () => { throw new Error("snapshot boom") }` (or a lockPath under a read-only/file parent). Assert result.status === "failed", then assert notifications equals [{ message: "Pi update failed without blocking startup: snapshot boom", level: "warning" }].

findings.title: Startup silence on `skipped` outcomes (offline / disabled) is never asserted
findings.body: Policy says startup stays silent on skip, but nothing checks it. The PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 test passes a throwaway `fakeUi().ui` and never looks at notifications. The PI_OFFLINE test only runs the manual trigger. The only startup-silence test for a non-complete status is the contention test at line 424. Red-making edit: add `if (status === "skipped") return true;` to shouldNotify (index.ts:260). Every Pi start with PI_OFFLINE=1 or PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 would then nag with an info toast, and no test would go red.
findings.fix: In the disable test, keep the startup fakeUi and assert `notifications` toEqual([]). Add a startup PI_OFFLINE case with the same empty assertion, next to the existing manual control.

findings.title: Failure-notification tests use substring matches where the exact message is known
findings.body: The timeout, nonzero-exit, exec-throw and startup-failure tests (lines ~328-330, 345-348, 365-367, 379-381) assert `toContain("Homebrew metadata refresh")` plus a fragment. The deps are fixed (timeoutMs 300_000, stderr "network failed", error "spawn brew ENOENT"), so each message is fully determined: e.g. "Homebrew metadata refresh timed out after 5 minutes." and "Homebrew metadata refresh failed: network failed". An edit that breaks the user-facing text still passes. Examples: a wrong minutes computation (`deps.timeoutMs / 1000` → "after 300 minutes") or a detail duplicated or misattributed in the message. Nothing in the output is unstable enough to need loosening.
findings.fix: Replace the toHaveLength/toContain/level triples with `expect(notifications).toEqual([{ message: "Homebrew metadata refresh timed out after 5 minutes.", level: "warning" }])` and the equivalent exact literal for each failure case.

findings.title: finish() is repeated at eight return sites instead of applied once around the sequence
findings.body: Every return in runBrewAutoUpdate (lines 382, 386, 394, 410, 414, 421, 444, 447) is wrapped in `finish(trigger, ui, ...)`. The invariant "no terminal result is returned without passing finish/shouldNotify" depends on every future return remembering the wrapper. A new early return that forgets it brings back the exact silent-failure defect, and per the outer-catch finding above, the tests would not catch it. Alternative: rename the body to an inner function returning `{ result, installedUpdate }` and call `finish` once in `runBrewAutoUpdate`. Outputs, levels and messages stay the same. The only ordering change is that notify runs after `lock.release()` instead of before. release cannot throw (readOwner swallows errors and removeLockDirectory is `.catch(() => {})`), and the notify is synchronous and in-process, so the reordering has no observable effect. This removes seven duplicated wraps and makes the invariant structural.
findings.fix: Move the current body into `async function runSequence(trigger, deps): Promise<{ result: UpdateResult; installedUpdate?: boolean }>` with plain returns. Make `runBrewAutoUpdate` do `const { result, installedUpdate = false } = await runSequence(trigger, deps); return finish(trigger, ui, result, installedUpdate);`.

findings.title: Уведомление из внешнего catch не защищено тестами
findings.body: Новый тест с исключением deps.exec попадает во внутренний catch на строке 408. Ни один тест не вызывает внешний catch, например через ENOTDIR при создании каталога блокировки. Если здесь вернуть reportFailure напрямую, все существующие проверки сохранят прежний результат, но ошибка блокировки снова станет невидимой: оба обработчика отбрасывают возвращённый результат. Это пробел в покрытии изменённой ветки, которая должна сообщать пользователю о сбое.
findings.fix: Добавить сценарий с обычным файлом вместо родительского каталога блокировки. Проверить статус failed и одно уведомление warning с причиной ошибки; существующий успешный сценарий оставить контролем.

findings.title: No test asserts a notification on the outer-catch failure path, so it could go silent again with every test still passing
findings.body:
The goal requires that "the tests would fail if a result were silently discarded again". `runBrewAutoUpdate` has a ninth terminal return at `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/brew-auto-update/index.ts:447`: the outer catch that wraps `acquireLock`, `deps.snapshotExtensions()` and everything else outside the per-step exec try. Examples that reach it: `mkdir` of the lock parent failing with EACCES, a non-EEXIST error from `mkdir(lockPath)`, or `snapshotExtensions` throwing. No test reaches it. The suite has no test that throws from `snapshotExtensions` or the lock path, and no test matches "without blocking startup". The only throwing fixture (line 351) throws from `exec`, and the inner catch at line 410 handles that.

Regression that stays green: put line 447 back to `return reportFailure(...)` without `finish(...)`. Every test still passes, and a broken lock directory or a throwing snapshot fails silently at startup and on the manual command, which is the defect issue 022 is about.

A smaller related gap: no test checks that startup stays silent for the two `skipped` outcomes. The `PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0` test (around line 303) checks status but not `notifications`, and the offline test only runs `manual`. The startup-silence half of `shouldNotify` is covered only for `contended`, `complete` and the unknown-extension-state case.
findings.fix: Add a test where `snapshotExtensions` throws (or `lockPath` sits under a regular file so `mkdir` fails) and assert `status: "failed"` plus exactly one notification at level `warning`. In the PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 test and an offline startup case, assert `notifications` is `[]`.

findings.title: Manual command now shows a failure message that wrongly mentions startup
findings.body: The outer-catch message "Pi update failed without blocking startup: <detail>" was written for the startup path. It used to be discarded, so the wording never mattered. Now `finish` sends it through `ui.notify` for every trigger. A user who runs `/brew-auto-update-now` while the lock directory can't be created (e.g. EACCES on `$XDG_STATE_HOME/pi`) sees a warning about not blocking startup, even though no startup is happening. The other failure messages name the failed step and fit both triggers. This change made the wrong wording visible.
findings.fix: Drop the trigger-specific wording, e.g. `Pi update failed: ${detail}`, or choose the suffix from `trigger`.

findings.title: В follow-up неверно описана политика уведомлений
findings.body: Документ утверждает, что каждый конечный результат передаётся через ui.notify. Однако shouldNotify оставляет запуск без уведомления при пропуске, занятой блокировке, отсутствии обновлений и неизвестном состоянии расширений. Это противоречит установленной политике и может ввести читателя в заблуждение относительно того, какие результаты должны доставляться.
findings.fix: Указать, что через ui.notify передаются результаты, для которых уведомление предусмотрено политикой запуска или ручной команды.

findings.title: Outer-catch failure path (lock/setup throws) has no notification test, so re-silencing it stays green
findings.body: `index.ts:445-447` routes any exception from `acquireLock` (e.g. `mkdir(dirname(lockPath))` failing with ENOTDIR/EACCES at index.ts:196) or from `deps.snapshotExtensions()` through `finish(..., reportFailure("Pi update failed without blocking startup: …"))`. None of the new tests reach this branch: the failure tests all fail inside `deps.exec` (caught at index.ts:408-421), and every fixture uses a writable temp `lockPath`. If line 447 reverted to the bare `return reportFailure(...)`, which is the exact silent-discard defect issue 022 fixes, no test would fail. The goal says tests must fail if a result were silently discarded again, and CLAUDE.md requires semantic regression coverage. That leaves one of the five failure returns unguarded.
findings.fix: Add a test where `lockPath` sits under a regular file, or `snapshotExtensions` throws. Assert `status: "failed"` and one `warning` notification containing "without blocking startup", for both startup and manual triggers.

findings.title: `finish(trigger, ui, …)` is repeated at every return instead of one exit point
findings.body: The rule that no terminal result bypasses `finish`/`shouldNotify` holds only because each of the roughly eight return sites (382, 386, 394, 410, 414, 421, 444, 447) was wrapped by hand. `trigger` and `ui` are fixed for the whole call. Four sites wrap `reportFailure(msg)`, which now appears only as `finish`'s argument. A future early return that forgets the wrapper would bring back the silent-discard defect this change exists to prevent.
findings.fix: Either bind local helpers (`const done = (r, installed = false) => finish(trigger, ui, r, installed)` and `const fail = (m) => done(reportFailure(m))`), or move the body into an inner function that returns a bare `UpdateResult` plus the installed flag, and call `finish` exactly once in `runBrewAutoUpdate`.

findings.title: New issue says 'Open decisions: None.' while its Scope leaves the delivery channel undecided
findings.body: The Scope section offers alternative fixes: "persisting the terminal result to session state (such as an appendEntry-style call) … or another mechanism Pi's extension API exposes". So which delivery channel to use is still an undecided, costly choice. In issue 022, which this one follows up, that kind of choice went under `## Open decisions` until it was settled (see the diff to 022's section). Writing `None.` tells whoever picks up 007 that nothing needs deciding. This is a prose defect only.
findings.fix: List the channel choice under `## Open decisions`, e.g. "Which headless delivery channel to use (session entry via appendEntry vs. another print/JSON-mode mechanism)."

findings.title: No test covers the outer-catch failure path, so a silent discard there would pass
findings.body: `runBrewAutoUpdate` has eight terminal returns. The outer `catch` at index.ts:447 (`return finish(trigger, ui, reportFailure(`Pi update failed without blocking startup: ...`))`) is the only failure return that no test reaches. Nothing makes `acquireLock` throw (for example EACCES creating the lock directory, or a rename failure while reclaiming a stale lock), and nothing makes `snapshotExtensions` reject. A search of the test file finds no `without blocking`, no rejecting `snapshotExtensions`, and no permission fixture. If line 447 went back to `return reportFailure(...)` (the exact silent-discard defect this change fixes), the whole suite would still pass. A broken state directory or a throwing snapshot would then fail silently again on every startup and on `/brew-auto-update-now`. The goal says the tests should fail if a result were silently discarded again, and this path is not held to that.
findings.fix: Add a manual-trigger test whose `snapshotExtensions` throws (or whose lock parent path is a regular file so `mkdir` fails). Assert status `failed` and exactly one `warning` notification containing the thrown detail.

findings.title: No test checks that startup stays silent for `skipped` results (PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 / PI_OFFLINE)
findings.body:
The policy says startup stays silent on non-failure outcomes. Tests pin that silence at startup for `contended`, up-to-date and unknown-extension-state, but not for `skipped`. The PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 test passes `fakeUi().ui` inline and never reads its notifications. The PI_OFFLINE test runs only the `manual` trigger.

If `shouldNotify` started returning true for `skipped` (or if an early skip branch called `notify` directly), every test would still pass. Meanwhile users with PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 or PI_OFFLINE=1 would see "Pi startup update is disabled." or "offline mode is active" every time Pi starts.
findings.fix: In the PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 test, keep the startup `fakeUi()` and assert `notifications` equals `[]`. Add a startup PI_OFFLINE case with the same assertion, next to the existing manual control.

findings.title: The manual command now shows a failure message that wrongly mentions startup
findings.body: The outer-catch message `Pi update failed without blocking startup: ${detail}` was written for the startup path. That result used to be discarded, so the wording never mattered. Now `finish` sends it through `ui.notify` on both triggers. A user who runs `/brew-auto-update-now` and hits a lock or snapshot error (e.g. EACCES creating `$XDG_STATE_HOME/pi`) sees a warning about startup, but nothing started up. The same change rewrote the contended message for this very reason and left this one as it was. The impact is limited to wording.
findings.fix: Use wording that holds for both triggers, e.g. `Pi update failed: ${detail}`, or pick the prefix from `trigger`.

findings.title: Нет проверки уведомления при ошибке создания блокировки
findings.body: Тесты ошибок моделируют только сбои `deps.exec`. Если каталог для блокировки недоступен, `acquireLock` выбрасывает исключение, которое обрабатывает внешний `catch`. Удаление уведомления из этого обработчика оставит все текущие тесты зелёными, хотя пользователь снова не узнает, что обновление не запустилось.
findings.fix: Добавить в этот набор тест с недоступным путём блокировки и проверить статус `failed` и уведомление уровня `warning`.

findings.title: Описание утверждает, что уведомление отправляется для каждого результата
findings.body: Документ утверждает, что каждый конечный результат проходит через `ui.notify`. Однако при запуске `shouldNotify` подавляет уведомления для пропуска, занятой блокировки и отсутствия обновлений. Это противоречит политике, записанной в том же документе на строке 18.
findings.fix: Уточнить, что каждый результат проходит через `finish` и `shouldNotify`, а вызов `ui.notify` зависит от политики уведомлений.

findings.title: When a later step fails, the earlier Pi-upgrade result is dropped and the user is not told to restart
findings.body: `installedUpdates` fills up step by step. Step 2 (`brew upgrade pi-coding-agent`) adds "pi" when its output shows an upgrade. If step 3 (`pi update --extensions`) then exits non-zero, times out or throws, the returns at lines 410/414/421 call `finish(trigger, ui, reportFailure(...))` with only the failure message. `installedUpdates` is never read on that path, so "Pi updated. Restart Pi to use the new version." is lost. The Homebrew binary has already been replaced under the running Pi, but the user sees only the package-update warning. The drop existed before this change, but the change rebuilt these exact return sites and kept it. No test covers an upgrade followed by a failure.
findings.fix: On the failure returns inside the step loop, append `installedUpdateMessage(installedUpdates)` to the failure message when it is defined, so the warning also says a restart is needed.

findings.title: No test checks that startup stays silent for `skipped` results (PI_OFFLINE / PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0)
findings.body:
The goal says startup stays silent on non-failure outcomes. The tests pin that silence for startup `contended` (cross-process lock test), up-to-date, and unknown-extension-state. They never pin it for startup `skipped`:
- The PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 test passes a throwaway `fakeUi().ui` and never reads its notifications.
- The PI_OFFLINE test only runs the `manual` trigger.

If `shouldNotify` gained `if (status === "skipped") return true` (or the disabled/offline early returns called `notify` directly), every test would still pass. Meanwhile a user who turned startup updates off with PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0, or works offline, would get an info toast every time Pi starts. That nagging is what the policy is meant to prevent, and the suite would not catch it.
findings.fix: In the PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 test, keep the startup `fakeUi()` and assert `notifications` equals `[]`. Add a startup PI_OFFLINE case that asserts `[]` next to the existing manual control.

findings.title: Catch-all failure message says "without blocking startup" even on the manual command
findings.body: Before this change, the outer catch result was thrown away. Now `finish` sends it to the user on both triggers. When `acquireLock` throws on `/brew-auto-update-now` (e.g. `mkdir` of `$XDG_STATE_HOME/pi` fails with EACCES/ENOSPC, or `removeLockDirectory` throws ENOTEMPTY while reclaiming a stale lock), the manual user sees "Pi update failed without blocking startup: …". No startup happened in that case, so the text points the user at the wrong context. The impact is limited to wording.
findings.fix: Build the prefix from the trigger, e.g. `trigger === "startup" ? "Pi update failed without blocking startup" : "Pi update failed"`.

findings.title: Notifications go only through ui.notify, which does nothing in Pi's headless print/JSON mode
findings.body: In Pi print/JSON mode `ui.notify` does nothing. A startup update that fails in that mode is still not delivered to the user. This behaviour existed before the change, and the change's new follow-up issue 007 tracks it.

findings.title: При ошибке последнего шага теряется сведения об уже установленном обновлении
findings.body: Если `brew upgrade pi-coding-agent` успешно обновил Pi, а следующий `pi update --extensions` завершился с ненулевым кодом, функция сразу сообщает только об ошибке последнего шага. Пользователь не узнаёт, что Pi уже обновлён и его нужно перезапустить. Это поведение существовало до изменения.

findings.title: Follow-up issue 007 says every terminal result goes through ui.notify, which contradicts the notification policy
findings.body: The issue says every terminal result is delivered through `ui.notify`. At startup, `shouldNotify` deliberately suppresses notifications for `skipped`, `contended`, up-to-date and unknown-extension-state outcomes. So the statement contradicts both the code and the policy written later in the same document (around line 18), and could mislead readers about which results should be delivered.
findings.fix: Say that every result passes through `finish` and `shouldNotify`, and that `ui.notify` is called only for the results the notification policy selects.

findings.title: No test reaches the outer-catch failure path (lock or snapshot throws), so silently discarding its result again would still pass
findings.body:
The goal requires the tests to fail if a terminal result is silently discarded again. `index.ts:445-447` sends any exception thrown outside the per-step exec through `finish(trigger, ui, reportFailure("Pi update failed without blocking startup: ..."))`. Examples: `acquireLock`'s `mkdir` of the lock parent failing with EACCES/ENOTDIR/ENOSPC, a non-EEXIST `mkdir(lockPath)` error, a rename or remove failure while reclaiming a stale lock, or `deps.snapshotExtensions()` throwing. No test reaches this branch. Every failure test fails inside `deps.exec`, which the inner catch around line 410 handles. Every fixture uses a writable temp `lockPath`. Nothing asserts on "without blocking startup".

Regression that stays green: change line 447 back to the bare `return reportFailure(...)`, which is the pre-change silent-discard defect. Every test still passes. A startup with an unwritable state directory, or with a throwing snapshot, would then fail silently on every launch and on `/brew-auto-update-now`.
findings.fix: Add a test whose `lockPath` sits under a regular file (so `mkdir` throws ENOTDIR), or whose `snapshotExtensions` throws. Assert `status: "failed"` and exactly one `warning` notification containing the thrown detail, for both the startup and manual triggers.

findings.title: Startup silence on skipped outcomes is never asserted
findings.body: The policy says startup stays silent on skipped/contended/up-to-date. Contended (cross-process lock test) and up-to-date are pinned at startup, but skipped is not: "disables startup only when PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE is zero" passes fakeUi().ui inline and never inspects notifications, and the PI_OFFLINE test only uses the manual trigger. Red-making edit nothing catches: make shouldNotify return true for status "skipped" (or call notify directly in either early skip branch). Users with PI_OFFLINE=1 or PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 would then get "Pi startup update is disabled." / "offline mode is active" on every Pi start with the suite green.
findings.fix: In the PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 test, keep a handle on fakeUi() for the startup run and assert notifications toEqual([]); optionally add the PI_OFFLINE startup case with the same assertion.

findings.title: finish(trigger, ui, …) repeated at eight return sites instead of one exit point
findings.body: The goal's invariant is that no terminal result bypasses finish/shouldNotify. As written, it holds only because each of the eight returns (lines 382, 386, 394, 410, 414, 421, 444, 447) was hand-wrapped; any future early return that forgets the wrapper reintroduces the silent-discard defect. An inner function (e.g. attemptUpdate(trigger, deps): Promise<{ result: UpdateResult; installedUpdate: boolean }>) returning bare results, with runBrewAutoUpdate doing `const { result, installedUpdate } = await attemptUpdate(...); return finish(trigger, ui, result, installedUpdate);`, would remove the repeated trigger/ui threading and make the invariant structural. Outputs, levels and messages stay the same. The one ordering difference is that notify (synchronous) would run after the finally block's lock release rather than just before it; no consumer here depends on that order.
findings.fix: Move the current body (offline/disabled checks, lock acquisition, steps, catch/finally) into an inner function that returns bare UpdateResult plus the installedUpdate flag, and call finish exactly once in runBrewAutoUpdate.

findings.title: Were the new notification regression tests shown to fail against the original silent-discard code?
findings.body: Nothing shows that the new notification tests (e.g. the one around line 370) went red against the original implementation, or against a minimal mutation that brings back the silent discard. Until that is shown, it is unproven that they catch the regression. The author could settle it by providing the red and green runs.

findings.title: No fixture fails when the Last request section-end guard is removed
findings.body:
The goal requires that status parsing cannot pick up a Status: line from another section, and that the tests go red on real regressions. The guard that stops this is `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` at home/private_dot_claude/hooks/executable_handoff-session-start.sh:83. No fixture exercises it. I ran the awk from the hook with and without that line on each new fixture. The results match on every one: 2834's 'Status outside Last request' fixture has no `## Last request` section, so the awk never enters the section in either version. 2834's unrecognized-value fixture and 50901 both put Status inside the section. A handoff of the form `## Last request
fix it

## Key Details
Status: Not answered` gives an empty status with the guard and `Not answered` without it. If someone deletes or breaks the guard, the operator sees a false `Status: Not answered` taken from Key Details, and the whole suite stays green. The profile weights a gate that cannot close very highly.
findings.fix: In test_scripts_2834, add a fixture with a `## Last request` section that has no Status line, followed by `## Key Details\nStatus: Not answered`. Assert the goal-only systemMessage. Prove it goes red with line 83 deleted.

findings.title: Prompt-contract assertion on 'Last user request' passes whether or not the change exists
findings.body: test_scripts_50900 asserts `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'`. That string comes from the `<transcript_facts>` block, which the hook prints on every path, including the fallback branches at executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh:113/120/245/265. It was already in the prompt before this change. So the assertion can never fail for this feature. The goal names the facts-block reference ('Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above', line 319) as a correctness condition, and no assertion covers that wording. If the line is deleted or stops pointing at the facts block, 50900 stays green. The separate `'Answered'` assertion is also implied by `'Partially answered'`, so it adds nothing.
findings.fix: Replace the 'Last user request' assertion with one on the instruction text, e.g. `assert_file_contains "$prompt" "Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above"`. Drop the redundant 'Answered' check.

findings.title: A Status: line inside the verbatim quote wins over the real status line
findings.body:
The prompt tells the extractor to quote the operator's last message verbatim, then write `Status:` below it. The awk returns the first line in the section that starts with `Status:` and exits. Suppose the operator's message spans several lines and one starts with `Status:`, and the model quotes it without a `>` prefix (the prompt does not ask for one). Then the quote's line is taken for the status. I simulated `## Last request
fix it
Status: Answered
more
Status: Not answered`. It returns `Answered`, so the operator is told the request was answered when the extractor said it was not. This trigger is rare, and the only effect is on what the operator sees.
findings.fix: Use the last `Status:` line in the section rather than the first: keep the latest match and print it at the section end or at END. Or tell the extractor to prefix quoted lines with `> `.

findings.title: Verbatim last-request quote can exceed the retained 400-word handoff cap
findings.body: `bounded_text` (line 140) lets the last user request run up to 4000 characters, roughly 600+ words of English. The new section requires a verbatim quote of that message inside `<handoff>`, while line 334 keeps 'Maximum 400 words in the <handoff> section'. With a long last request, the extractor cannot follow both rules. It will either cut the quote (breaking 'verbatim') or overrun the cap, and maybe squeeze out Relevant Context or Key Details to make room. The extractor is a model that runs against this prompt as a contract, so the conflict changes what it writes. The old prompt already said to copy the last request exactly, so this is partly pre-existing, but the new required section makes the conflict certain whenever the message is long.
findings.fix: Exempt the Last request quote from the 400-word cap, or allow it to be cut with an explicit marker.

findings.title: Status parser scans the verbatim operator quote before the Status line, so a quoted `## ` or `Status:` line wins
findings.body: The prompt (executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh:318-321) puts the verbatim quote of the operator's last message first in `## Last request` and the `Status:` line after it. The facts literal is decoded and copied exactly, so a multi-line message can stay multi-line. The awk in executable_handoff-session-start.sh:81-90 exits at the first `^## ` line after the heading and takes the first `^Status:` line in the section. Both can come from the quote. A quoted markdown heading hides the real status. A quoted `Status: Answered` line replaces a real `Status: Not answered`. A quoted `Status: Running` is dropped by the case filter, and the real status is lost with it. The trigger needs the extractor to copy the quote as bare lines, not as a `> ` blockquote, so whether it fires depends on the model's formatting. This is the threat that docs/solutions/design-patterns/protected-slot-signal-extraction.md covers: read one protected slot, never scan. additionalContext is not affected. The wrong or missing status shows only in the operator systemMessage, and that status line is the only purpose of the feature.
findings.fix: Read one protected slot. For example, have the prompt put `Status:` as the first line of `## Last request`, before the quote, and have the awk read only the first non-blank line after the heading. Alternatives: take the last `Status:` line in the section, or prefix quoted lines with `> `.

findings.title: The mandatory verbatim quote of the last request conflicts with the 400-word handoff cap
findings.body: The new `## Last request` section (pre-compact.sh:319) always requires a verbatim quote of the last operator message. `bounded_text` lets that message run to 4000 characters plus " [truncated]". Line 334 still caps the whole <handoff> at 400 words, and no rule says which one wins. When a request is long or contains pasted content, the extractor must paraphrase or cut the quote, against line 337, or go over the cap at the cost of other sections. The old prompt already said to copy the request exactly, but it did not require the request in the handoff. The new mandatory section makes the conflict certain for long messages. The impact is uneven handoffs on long requests only.
findings.fix: State the priority. For example, exclude the Last request quote from the 400-word cap, or allow a bounded quote with an explicit [truncated] marker.

findings.title: Status parser takes the first `Status:` line in Last request, which the verbatim operator quote that comes before it can spoof
findings.body: The prompt tells the extractor to quote the operator's last message verbatim first and to write the `Status:` line after it (pre-compact.sh:320-322). The parser then picks the *first* line inside `## Last request` that starts with `Status:` and exits. Operator messages can span several lines (the facts block carries up to 4000 characters, and the model decodes them into real lines). If the quoted message contains a line such as `Status: Answered`, the parser picks that line and never reaches the real one. This is likely in this repo, where the operator works on this very hook. I reproduced it: running the hook's awk program on `## Last request / The banner says / Status: Answered / but nothing ran / Status: Not answered / ## Key Details` prints `Answered`. The operator then sees `Status: Answered` when the extractor actually said `Not answered`, and that hides the exact signal this change adds. The damage stays on screen: additionalContext is unchanged. This is the case `docs/solutions/design-patterns/protected-slot-signal-extraction.md` was written for (applies_when: "Extracting a machine-readable signal ... from an LLM's free-text output" / "prose that can quote the signal's own format"). Its rule 1 is to read one protected position and never scan.
findings.fix: Read one protected slot instead of the first match. For example, take the last `Status:` line before the section ends, or ask the model to put `Status:` as the first line of the section, before the quote, and read only that line.

findings.title: No test covers the end-of-section boundary in the status parser: deleting the `/^## / { exit }` rule keeps every test green
findings.body: The goal requires that "status parsing cannot pick up a Status: line from another section". The new negative case stages a handoff that has *no* `## Last request` section, so `in_last_request` is never set and the case passes whether or not the section-end rule exists. The other fixtures (50901, 50902, and the 2834 'Waiting for a reply' case) all put `Status:` inside the section, so the parser prints and exits before it reaches the next heading. I ran the hook's awk with and without `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` on `## Last request / q / ## Key Details / Status: Not answered`. With the rule it prints nothing. Without it, it prints `Not answered`. No current fixture tells these apart. So the guard that stops a later section's Status line from leaking (exactly the regression the goal names) can be removed and the suite stays green. That breaks the test-oracle gate (semantic-regression-tests-over-source-shape.md). The neighbouring goal parser (line 76) also stops at `</handoff>`, and this one does not.
findings.fix: In test_scripts_2834, change the 'status outside Last request' fixture so it does include a `## Last request` section with no Status line, followed by `## Key Details\nStatus: Not answered`. Assert that the systemMessage shows the goal alone.

findings.title: Строка Status из запроса оператора может заменить статус ответа
findings.body: Промпт в home/private_dot_claude/hooks/executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh:319 требует дословно включить последнее сообщение оператора перед строкой статуса. Если это сообщение содержит отдельную строку `Status: Answered`, а фактический статус ниже — `Status: Not answered`, парсер выбирает первую строку и показывает оператору неверный статус. Это нарушает требование промпта различать содержание запроса и статус его обработки.
findings.fix: Задать для цитаты однозначные границы или кодирование и извлекать статус только из поля за пределами цитаты.

findings.title: The prompt puts an undelimited verbatim quote before the Status: line, so quoted text decides what the status parser sees
findings.body: The new section asks for the verbatim quote first and the `Status:` line after it. It does not say how to set the quote off (for example, as a `> ` blockquote). The decoded facts literal can span many lines, and pasted markdown is unwrapped on purpose. A quoted line starting with `## ` makes the injector's awk leave the section before the real status, so the status disappears. A quoted line starting with `Status:` is read in place of the extractor's verdict. This is the prompt-side cause of the parser spoofing in session-start.sh.
findings.fix: Put `Status: [...]` as the first line of `## Last request`, before the quote, or tell the extractor to prefix every quoted line with `> `.

findings.title: No fixture tests that the status parser stops at the heading after Last request
findings.body:
The goal requires that "status parsing cannot pick up a Status: line from another section". The guard is `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` at executable_handoff-session-start.sh:83. No fixture exercises it:

- The new negative case in 2834 has no `## Last request` header at all, so `in_last_request` is never set and the boundary line never runs.
- 50901/50902 put the recognized `Status:` inside Last request, before `## Key Details`.
- The other 2834 case is an unrecognized value inside the section.

Delete line 83 and every test stays green. But a real handoff like `## Last request\n<quote>\n\n## Key Details\nStatus: Not answered` would then show a false `Status: Not answered`. The prompt places Key Details right after Last request, so this layout is realistic.
findings.fix: Add a case to 2834: `## Goal` / `## Last request` with a quote but no Status line / `## Key Details` with `Status: Not answered`. Assert the goal-only systemMessage. Prove it goes red with line 83 removed.

findings.title: A verbatim quote of up to 4000 chars conflicts with the 400-word handoff cap
findings.body: The new instruction asks for the operator's last message "verbatim from the facts block". `bounded_text` lets that message reach 4000 characters (about 600+ words), and pasted documents are unwrapped into it. The prompt still says "Maximum 400 words in the <handoff> section" (kept on purpose per the goal). With a long last request, the extractor has two choices. It can break the cap, or it can truncate or paraphrase the quote, which breaks both "verbatim" and the existing "copy ... the last user request exactly from <transcript_facts>" constraint. Either way, the extractor gets contradictory instructions on exactly the long-request case, and the handoff's other sections can get squeezed out.
findings.fix: State which rule wins. For example: exclude the Last request quote from the 400-word cap, or allow a marked truncation of quotes over N words.

findings.title: The 'Last user request' assertion in 50900 passes before the change and does not test the new facts-block reference
findings.body: `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` matches the facts block itself. The payload has no transcript path, so the prompt always contains `Last user request: None`. The parent revision's prompt contains this string 6 times. So the assertion stays green if the new `## Last request` instruction stops pointing at the facts block, or if the whole section is reworded away from it. The goal lists "does not break ... the facts-block reference" as a correctness condition, and this line looks like it covers that condition but cannot fail on it.
findings.fix: Assert the instruction line itself, for example `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'verbatim from the facts block'`, or remove the vacuous assertion.

findings.title: A comment still says the goal is 'the one block' the operator can check
findings.body: The comment `# The operator never sees additionalContext, so show them the one block they can check: the goal the extractor settled on.` was written when the systemMessage held only the goal. After this change, the systemMessage can also carry `Status: <status>` from the Last request section (line 108). The new comment at lines 78-80 describes the addition, but the older comment still claims the goal is the single block shown. The comment is stale; the code is right.
findings.fix: Reword the comment, for example: "show them what they can check: the goal the extractor settled on and, below, the last-request status".

findings.title: The status test does not cover a `Status:` line inside the quoted request
findings.body: The last request is kept verbatim and can contain a standalone `Status: Answered` line. If the real handoff status after the quote is `Status: Not answered`, the parser takes the first line and shows the operator the wrong status. The current test uses a request without such a line, so it cannot catch this failure.
findings.fix: Add a request containing a `Status: Answered` line to the test, and assert that the status written after the quote is the one shown.

findings.title: The byte-for-byte check does not cover trailing newlines that SessionStart strips
findings.body: SessionStart reads the handoff through command substitution, which strips trailing newlines. A handoff ending in a blank line is therefore changed before it reaches additionalContext. The fixture has no trailing newline, so the new byte-for-byte check stays green. The reviewer notes that the newline loss existed before this change; the new check only fails to detect it.
findings.fix: Use a fixture with trailing newlines, and compare the JSON value in a way that keeps them.

findings.title: Проверка prompt не защищает требование цитировать запрос
findings.body: Тест проверяет наличие заголовка и слов `Last user request`, но не проверяет инструкцию цитировать сообщение в разделе `Last request`. Если заменить её на инструкцию обобщить сообщение, эти проверки останутся зелёными: строка `Last user request` уже присутствует в блоке фактов. Такой регресс оставит следующего агента без дословного запроса оператора.
findings.fix: Проверить инструкцию о дословной цитате в контексте раздела `Last request`.

findings.title: Status parser scans the verbatim operator quote before the Status line, so quoted `## ` or `Status:` lines win
findings.body:
The prompt (executable_handoff-pre-compact.sh:318-321) tells the extractor to put the verbatim quote of the operator's last message first in `## Last request` and the `Status:` line after it. The extractor is also told to decode the JSON literal and copy it exactly, so a multi-line message stays multi-line. The awk parser stops at the first `^## ` line and takes the first `^Status:` line inside the section. Both of those can come from the operator's quoted text, not from the extractor's verdict. I ran the parser in memory:
- A quote that contains a markdown heading (`Please review this:\n## Findings\n- bug`, then `Status: Not answered`) gives an empty result. The real status is never read.
- A quote with pasted tool output (`Status:  Running`, then the real `Status: Not answered`) gives `Running`. The case filter drops it, so the real status is lost.
- A quote with a line that is exactly `Status: Answered`, followed by the real `Status: Not answered`, shows `Answered`. That is the wrong status, and the operator sees it.
Observed: the parser cannot tell quoted text from the status line. Inferred consequence: when the operator pastes markdown or a log, which is common, the status is silently dropped. In the rarer exact-match case the status is wrong. additionalContext is not affected, so impact is limited to the operator display. This is the same family as the goal's requirement that parsing "cannot pick up a Status: line from another section": here the stray line comes from untrusted text inside the right section.
findings.fix: Put `Status:` as the first line of the `## Last request` section in the prompt, before the quote. Then make awk read only the first non-blank line after the heading.

findings.title: No test covers the end-of-section boundary; dropping `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` stays green
findings.body:
The new negative case in test_scripts_2834 has a `Status:` line and no `## Last request` section at all. test_scripts_50901 has the Status line inside the section. Neither has a `## Last request` section without a Status line followed by a later section that has one. I removed the boundary rule from the awk program in memory and fed it `## Last request
hi

## Key Details
Status: Answered`. It printed `Answered`, while the real program prints nothing. All of the new tests would still pass with that regression. So the goal's requirements, that "status parsing cannot pick up a Status: line from another section" and that "tests go red on real regressions", are only half covered: section entry is tested, section exit is not.
findings.fix: In test_scripts_2834, add a fixture whose `## Last request` section has no Status line, followed by `## Key Details` with `Status: Answered`. Assert the goal-only systemMessage.

findings.title: `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'` matches the facts block, so it cannot fail when the new reference is removed
findings.body: The string `Last user request` is always in the prompt from the `<transcript_facts>` block. With no transcript, which is this fixture, the fallback prints `Last user request: None`. The new instruction says "from the facts block above" and never uses that string. So deleting or rewording the instruction's link to the facts block leaves this assertion green. The goal lists "the facts-block reference" as something the change must not break. This assertion looks like it guards that, but it does not.
findings.fix: Assert the instruction's own text, for example `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'verbatim from the facts block above'`.

findings.title: A mandatory verbatim quote of up to 4000 characters conflicts with the kept 400-word handoff cap
findings.body: `bounded_text` (line 141) lets the last user request reach 4000 characters, roughly 600-700 words. The new section requires a verbatim quote of it, and the constraints still say "Maximum 400 words in the <handoff> section". When the last message is a pasted log or a long spec, the extractor cannot meet both rules. Either it cuts or paraphrases the quote, which defeats the verbatim requirement, or the quote pushes Relevant Context and Key Details out of the budget. I inferred this from the prompt text; I did not observe model output.
findings.fix: Exempt the quote from the word cap, or let the extractor quote a bounded prefix and mark it as truncated.

findings.title: Парсер принимает строки цитаты за границы и статус секции
findings.body: Последний запрос вставляется в эту секцию дословно и может содержать Markdown. Если он содержит строку `Status: Answered`, парсер выберет её вместо следующего за цитатой фактического `Status: Not answered`. Если запрос содержит строку, начинающуюся с `## `, парсер остановится до фактического статуса. В первом случае оператор увидит неверный статус, во втором статус не будет показан.
findings.fix: Явно ограничить цитату запроса и извлекать статус вне неё, не принимая строки цитаты за разметку handoff.

findings.title: Дословная цитата запроса конфликтует с пределом handoff в 400 слов
findings.body: Запрос из более чем 400 коротких слов может целиком попасть в блок фактов, поскольку его предел составляет 4000 символов. Тогда инструкции требуют одновременно дословно скопировать запрос в handoff и ограничить весь handoff 400 словами. Выполнить оба требования невозможно: извлекатель должен либо обрезать запрос, либо нарушить предел, поэтому сохранение последнего запроса зависит от того, как модель разрешит конфликт.
findings.fix: Явно определить приоритет дословной цитаты относительно предела слов или исключить цитату из этого предела.

findings.title: No fixture exercises the Last request section-end guard; deleting `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` keeps every test green
findings.body:
The goal requires that status parsing cannot pick up a Status: line from another section. The guard for this is `in_last_request && /^## / { exit }` at executable_handoff-session-start.sh:83. The new negative fixture in test_scripts_2834 has no `## Last request` heading, so `in_last_request` is never set and the guard never runs. The positive fixtures (50901/50902) and the unrecognized-value case all put `Status:` inside the section. Reviewers ran the awk with and without the guard on `## Last request
q

## Key Details
Status: Not answered`. With the guard it prints nothing; without it, it prints `Not answered`. No current fixture tells the two apart, so this cross-section leak can come back without any test failing. That breaks the test-oracle gate. The fixture comment ("A status outside Last request is ordinary handoff text") also claims more than the fixture covers.
findings.fix: In test_scripts_2834, give the fixture a `## Last request` section with no Status line, followed by `## Key Details\nStatus: Not answered`. Assert the exact goal-only systemMessage, and confirm the test goes red with line 83 removed.

findings.title: Prompt-contract test checks loose substrings instead of the exact lines the injector parses
findings.body: Test_scripts_50900 checks the captured prompt with separate substring checks: `## Last request`, `Status:`, `Answered`, `Partially answered`, `Not answered`. The consumer of this prompt contract is the injector's awk, which only matches the heading line `^## Last request[[:space:]]*$` and a line that starts with `Status:`. Some prompt edits break that handshake and still pass every assertion. Examples: rename the heading to `## Last request (verbatim)` or `## Last requests`, make the template line `- Status:` or `**Status:**`, or move the three values onto a different line from `Status:`. The extractor copies the template's shape, so after any of these edits the injector never shows a status, and the test stays green. The `Last user request` assertion also does not cover the new instruction. That string comes from the existing facts block, which test 508 already owns. It goes red only if the facts block itself is removed.
findings.fix: Check the two lines the injector depends on with whole-line matches. Use `grep -Fx '## Last request'` and `grep -Fx 'Status: [Use exactly one of: Answered, Partially answered, Not answered]'` with assert_success. Drop the separate `Status:`, `Answered`, and `Last user request` substring checks.

findings.title: The prompt-contract test asserts loose substrings, and its 'Last user request' check cannot fail for this change
findings.body: test_scripts_50900 asserts `assert_file_contains "$prompt" 'Last user request'`. That string comes from the `<transcript_facts>` block, which is printed on every path; this fixture prints `Last user request: None`. It was in the prompt before this change. So deleting the new instruction to quote the last message verbatim from the facts block, or rewording it into a summary, leaves the test green, even though the goal names the facts-block reference as a correctness condition. The other checks are separate substrings (`## Last request`, `Status:`, `Answered`, `Partially answered`, `Not answered`); `Answered` is already implied by `Partially answered`. Edits that break the injector's handshake also pass: renaming the heading, writing `- Status:` or `**Status:**`, or moving the values to another line. The injector matches only `^## Last request[[:space:]]*$` and `^Status:`.
findings.fix: Assert the instruction text itself, e.g. `Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above`. Check the heading and the `Status: [...]` template line with whole-line matches (`grep -Fx`). Drop the redundant `Last user request`, `Status:` and `Answered` substring checks.

findings.title: The status test covers only one of the three allowed values
findings.body: The only positive fixtures (test_scripts_50901 and 50902) use `Status: Not answered`. The case whitelist at executable_handoff-session-start.sh:91-94 also accepts `Answered` and `'Partially answered'`, but no test sends either value through to the systemMessage. A regression that drops or misquotes either branch would leave the suite green, and the operator would stop seeing the status for two of the three values the prompt contract defines.
findings.fix: In test_scripts_50901, stage handoffs with `Status: Answered` and `Status: Partially answered` too, and assert the exact systemMessage for each one.

findings.title: Mandatory verbatim quote of the last request conflicts with the 400-word handoff cap
findings.body: Line 319 says "[Quote the operator's last real message verbatim from the facts block above]". The facts block gets that message from `bounded_text` (line 141), which allows up to 4000 characters plus " [truncated]", roughly 600–700 words. Line 334 still says "Maximum 400 words in the <handoff> section". Before this change the extractor chose whether to include the request at all. Now the quote is required, so a long or pasted operator message cannot satisfy both rules. Some runs will truncate or paraphrase the quote, which breaks "verbatim" and line 337's "exactly ... do not paraphrase". Other runs will go over the cap, or squeeze Goal, Relevant Context and Key Details to make room. The text names no priority between the two rules, so runs diverge on exactly the long-request sessions where the handoff matters most.
findings.fix: State which rule wins. For example, add "the Last request quote does not count toward the 400-word cap", or cap the quote explicitly ("quote verbatim up to N words, then write [truncated]").

findings.title: The Last request section has no instruction for `Last user request: None`
findings.body: The facts block emits `Last user request: None` on every fallback path (lines 113, 120, 245, 260, 265) and whenever no qualifying user turn exists. The new section only says to quote the last real message and pick one of three Status values. It does not say what to do when the fact is `None`, and it has no "omit if nothing applies" rule like Warnings has. Runs will diverge: some quote `None` with a status, some infer a message (against line 337), some drop the section. The SessionStart injector can then show a status such as `Status: Answered` for a request that was never identified.
findings.fix: Add one line to the section, e.g. "[If the facts block reports Last user request: None, write None and omit the Status line]".

findings.title: Quote format is unspecified, so a quoted multi-line message can corrupt the Status parse
findings.body: The prompt asks for a verbatim quote but does not say how to set it off (e.g. as a `> ` blockquote). The decoded facts literal can span several lines. If the extractor pastes it as bare lines, any quoted line that starts with `## ` (pasted markdown) makes the injector's awk (`in_last_request && /^## / { exit }`) leave the section before it reaches the real `Status:` line, so the status silently disappears. A quoted line that starts with `Status:` is picked up instead of the extractor's verdict. The section boundary holds, but the value can come from operator text. Impact is contained: the systemMessage shows the wrong status or none, and additionalContext is unchanged.
findings.fix: Tell the extractor to put every line of the quote behind a `> ` prefix. Then neither `^## ` nor `^Status:` can match quoted text.

findings.title: Same rules stated twice and one fact given two names
findings.body: "[When an item is inferred rather than observed, write it as: <claim>, verify with: <exact command>]" appears word for word at lines 316 and 325. It could live once under Constraints, where line 337 already states the cross-section copy rules. Line 319 also calls the same thing "the operator's last real message ... from the facts block above", while the block itself says `Last user request:` inside `<transcript_facts>` and line 337 says "the last user request exactly from <transcript_facts>". So one meaning has two sources of truth under two names. The extractor has to work out that they match, and a later edit to one copy can drift from the other. This changes no behavior today.
findings.fix: Point line 319 at the fact by its own label: "[Copy the Last user request from <transcript_facts>]". State the inferred-item format once under Constraints.

findings.title: Old-engine degrade path classifies any 401/403 (incl. dead sign-in) as "engine cannot answer" exit 2
findings.body: isVerdictReadRefusal treats any 401/403 anywhere in the cause chain as an old engine refusing the verdict read. rejectedCredentialError (operator-client.ts:406) wraps the original 401 ApiError as `cause`, so when the stored platform credential is dead, `code status` (or the wait loop in `code test`) prints "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet" and exits 2 — the documented 'still pending' code — instead of the 'Membrane rejected the stored credential. Sign in again' error with exit 1. An agent following the docs keeps waiting/retrying instead of surfacing the expired sign-in. The goal intends this degrade only for an old engine refusing the read.
findings.fix: Narrow the degrade to the specific refusal an old engine returns for a sessionless read on a non-sessionless command (its access-denied code), or exclude rejectedCredentialError/SessionClosedError before walking `cause`.

findings.title: `code status --wait` with a zero or short `--timeout` reports 'still pending' for a version it never read
findings.body:
In `codeStatus` with `--wait`, the deadline is computed before the first read, and the first `listVersion` call runs through `readUntilDeadline`. `validTimeout` accepts 0. With `--timeout 0` the deadline is now, so `readUntilDeadline` sees `remaining <= 0`, aborts the request it already sent, and fails with VERDICT_READ_TIMED_OUT. Any timeout shorter than a slow first read does the same. `codeStatus` then reaches the timed-out branch, prints 'still pending after N s — wait with: … --wait' and exits 2.

The version may really be passed (exit 0), failed (1), untested (3) or not exist, so this breaks the 0/1/2/3 contract of the status read. Plain `code status` would have answered correctly. The test 'observes the aborted status read when the deadline is already spent' (cli.code.verdict.test.ts:255-293) asserts this output, so it locks in the misreport.
findings.fix: Do the first status read without the deadline and bound only the polling after a pending answer, or treat a timeout of 0 as 'read once, don't wait'. Alternatively, report 'could not read the verdict within N s' when no version was read. Update the `--timeout 0` test to expect the real status.

findings.title: `code test --json` output shape changed from `{version: …}` to the bare version object
findings.body: Before this change `code test --json` printed the whole run-source-tree-tests result, `{ "version": { … } }`. renderTestVersion now prints only `version`, so a caller parsing `.version.testsStatus` from `code test --json` silently gets null/undefined. The goal does not call for this, and no doc notes the break.
findings.fix: In JSON mode for `code test`, print `{ version }` to keep the previous shape (or document the change deliberately).

findings.title: Отказ движка поставить тесты в очередь возвращает код 1
findings.body: Если движок не запускает исходный код, `run-source-tree-tests` отвечает ошибкой `source_tree_tests_not_queued`. Эта ошибка выходит из `codeTest` и общий обработчик `runCode` возвращает 1. По цели изменения отказ движка должен давать код 2; вызывающий агент вместо этого получает тот же код, что и для проваленного теста.
findings.fix: Распознать отказ `source_tree_tests_not_queued` в `codeTest` и вернуть 2 с сообщением об отказе.

findings.title: With a short timeout, the pause before the first poll uses up the whole wait, so the verdict is never read
findings.body: In `waitForVersion` (code.ts:654-656), each iteration sleeps `min(5000, remaining)` before it reads, then breaks if the deadline has passed. With `code test --timeout 5` or smaller, the first sleep uses up the whole wait. The loop exits without calling `listVersion`, prints the queued version as pending and exits 2, even if the tests finished right after being queued. More generally, the final stretch before any deadline is spent asleep instead of reading. `code status --wait` has already read once before this loop, so there the effect is only a missed second read. The default timeout is 90 s, so this only affects short timeouts the user chooses explicitly.
findings.fix: Read the status before the first pause, or cap each sleep so that a read happens before the deadline, and keep polling until the deadline.

findings.title: An expired or rejected sign-in is reported as 'this engine cannot answer the verdict yet' (exit 2) instead of 'Sign in again'
findings.body:
`isVerdictReadRefusal` treats any 401, any error whose message matches /sign-in expired/, and any error whose cause chain holds a 401 as an engine that is too old to answer. Those are exactly the errors the client raises when the stored credential is dead. `platform-token.ts:72` throws 'The Membrane sign-in expired and could not be refreshed. Sign in again.' `operator-client.ts:406` `rejectedCredentialError` wraps the retried 401 as its `cause`. The old-engine case this check is meant for arrives as a 403 AccessDenied (`check-command-scope.ts:83-87`), so the 401 branches only ever catch credential failures. The same goes for an unattached `dispatch`: the workspace lookup in `dispatchUnattached` runs inside that promise, so a refresh failure there is caught too.

Concrete case: the operator's sign-in has expired and they run `code status`. The verb prints 'this engine cannot answer the verdict yet' and exits 2. Exit 2 is the 'still pending' code, so an agent keeps polling. It never sees the 'Sign in again' remedy that every other verb prints through the `runCode` catch. `code test` does the same in the middle of a wait: it prints 'v3: pending — this engine cannot answer the verdict yet'.
findings.fix: Treat only a 403 (or the AccessDenied scope-mismatch code) as the old-engine refusal. Drop the 401 check and the /sign-in expired/ match, so credential failures reach `runCode`'s catch and print their own message with exit 1.

findings.title: `code test --json` silently changes shape from the command output `{ version: {...} }` to the bare version object
findings.body:
Before this change, `code test --json` printed `JSON.stringify(result)`, where `result` is the `run-source-tree-tests` output `{ version: SourceTreeVersion }`. That matches the help text for `--json`, 'Print the raw shape instead of the rendered summary' (`cli.ts:71`). It also matches how sibling verbs behave: `codePromote` prints the command's raw output (`code.ts:750-753`). `renderTestVersion` now prints `version` itself, with no wrapper. The new tests pin this (`cli.code.verdict.test.ts:404-424`), so the change is deliberate, but neither the goal nor any doc mentions it.

The plugin is a published artifact that agents drive. A script or agent that reads `.version.testsStatus` from `code test --json` now gets `undefined`. Combined with the new behaviour of waiting and exiting non-zero, that caller can no longer read the verdict it is waiting for.
findings.fix: Keep the existing `{ version }` wrapper for `code test --json` (for example, `JSON.stringify({ version })` when rendering for `test`), or document the shape change in the help text and the plugin docs.

findings.title: `code status --wait` with a short or zero `--timeout` reports 'still pending' for a version it never read
findings.body: In `codeStatus`, when `--wait` is set, the first `listVersion` call is itself bounded by the deadline. With `--timeout 0`, `readUntilDeadline` sees `remaining <= 0`, aborts the request and fails with VERDICT_READ_TIMED_OUT. A short timeout has the same effect if the first page is slow. `codeStatus` then reaches the `timedOut` branch and prints 'still pending after 0 s — wait with: …' with exit 2. The version may already be `passed` (exit 0), `failed` (exit 1) or `untested` (exit 3). The command reports a status it never read, and the follow-up line points the caller into another wait.
findings.fix: Do the first read without the deadline, or report 'could not read the verdict within N s' rather than 'still pending' when no version was read yet.

findings.title: Verdict polling hand-rolls a timeout, a sleep loop and a symbol error, against the repo's Effect rules
findings.body:
