CODING_STANDARDS.md → Effect makes `.claude/skills/effect-best-practices/SKILL.md` binding. This code departs from it in two places:

- `readUntilDeadline` builds its timeout from `Effect.raceFirst` against an `Effect.sleep` that fails. The skill (SKILL.md:22, :45) says to use `Effect.timeout` or `Effect.timeoutOrElse` instead.
- `VERDICT_READ_TIMED_OUT` is a bare `unique symbol` in the error channel, checked with `===` after `Effect.match`. The skill (SKILL.md:67) requires an in-process error to be a `Data.TaggedError`, recovered with `catchTag`.

The `while` loop in `waitForVersion` is allowed: SKILL.md:92 keeps a loop that breaks or returns early as a `while` loop. The no-op `catchTag` at line 607 and the three copies of `new VerdictReadFailed({ cause, message })` (lines 520, 603, 628) add some noise.
findings.fix: Make the timeout a `Data.TaggedError` and bound each read with `Effect.timeoutOrElse` instead of `raceFirst` with a failing sleep. Factor the repeated `VerdictReadFailed` construction into one helper, and drop the no-op `catchTag`.

findings.title: `code test --json` output changed from `{ version: {...} }` to the bare version object
findings.body: Before this change, `code test --json` printed the `run-source-tree-tests` result, `{ "version": { ... } }`. That matched the `--json` help text, 'Print the raw shape' (cli.ts:71). `renderTestVersion` (code.ts:543-550) now prints the bare version object, in both wait and `--no-wait` modes, and the new tests pin this. No help text or plugin doc mentions the change. A script or agent that reads `.version.testsStatus` or `.version.id` from `code test --json` now gets `undefined`. The exit code still reports the verdict, and the new shape matches what `code status --json` prints, so the damage is limited to existing JSON consumers.
findings.fix: Keep the `{ version }` wrapper for `code test --json` in both wait and `--no-wait` modes (for example `JSON.stringify({ version })`), or document the shape change in the help text and the plugin docs.

findings.title: Any 401/403 or expired sign-in is reported as "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet", which hides the sign-in or session remedy
findings.body:
`isVerdictReadRefusal` returns true for any 401 or 403, for any error whose message matches /sign-in expired/, and for any error whose cause chain holds one of those. `codeStatus` and `waitForVersion` then print "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet" and exit 2. That output is meant for an old engine, and exit 2 also means "still pending".

A concrete failure: an operator's OAuth access token has expired and the refresh grant fails. `code status --workspace acme` runs `dispatchUnattached` → `callInWorkspace` → `callWithPlatformToken` → `platformToken.get()`. That call throws `The Membrane sign-in expired and could not be refreshed. Sign in again.` (platform-token.ts:72) before any request is sent. The classifier matches the message, so the CLI prints `this engine cannot answer the verdict yet` and exits 2. The "Sign in again" instruction is lost. An agent following the documented exit codes reads 2 as "pending or engine refuses" and keeps polling instead of signing in.

The same happens on the attached path. A 401 retried into `rejectedCredentialError` ("Sign in again to replace it") is classified as an old engine. So is a closed session: `SessionClosedError` carries the refusal as its `cause`, and its own message names `session start` / `session stop`.

The comment at line 559 is also wrong. It says: "A platform-token refresh reports this after the original 401, so treat it as a verdict read refusal." But `get()` raises that message proactively, with no 401 at all (platform-token.ts:83-85).

On tests: the 401/403 cases in cli.code.verdict.test.ts:377-427 and :473-494 assert this conflation. Nothing checks that a genuine credential failure keeps its own message. So the goal's "old engine degrades to exit 2 with a clear line" is satisfied only by also swallowing every auth failure.
findings.fix: Narrow the classifier to the specific refusal an old engine sends for a non-sessionless route: the MembraneApiError status, plus a body or denial kind if it has one. Do not match the `sign-in expired` message, and do not treat `rejectedCredentialError` or `SessionClosedError` as a refusal. Let those reach the runCode catch, which prints their message with exit 1. Add a test where the token refresh fails and assert the sign-in message survives.

findings.title: `code status --wait --timeout 0` sends the read, aborts it unread and reports "still pending" even for a settled version
findings.body:
With `--wait --timeout 0`, `deadline` equals the current time. `listVersion` calls `dispatch` first, so the request goes out. `readUntilDeadline` (line 588) then sees `remaining <= 0`, aborts the request and fails with VERDICT_READ_TIMED_OUT. `codeStatus` prints `still pending after 0 s — wait with: … --wait` and exits 2 without having read anything. This happens even when the version is `passed` (it should exit 0), `failed` (exit 1) or `untested` (exit 3).

Plain `code status` reads the verdict, but `--wait --timeout 0` reports a wrong state. The test 'observes the aborted status read when the deadline is already spent' (cli.code.verdict.test.ts:255-293) asserts this output as expected. It locks the wrong answer in, though its real aim is checking for unhandled rejections.
findings.fix: Let the first status read go ahead even when the deadline has already passed, and apply the deadline only to the polling after it. Or treat a timeout of 0 as "read once, don't wait".

findings.title: Short --timeout never polls: the last wait slice ends at the deadline with no read (code.ts:653-655)
findings.body: The defect is in claude-plugin/src/engine/verbs/code.ts:653-655, `waitForVersion`. Each iteration sleeps for `min(5000, deadline - now)`. If the clock has then reached the deadline, the loop breaks before calling `listVersion`. With `code test --timeout 5`, or with `code status --wait --timeout 5` after a first `pending`, the single sleep runs right up to the deadline. The command then prints `pending` and exits 2 without ever reading the verdict, so a version that has already passed or failed is reported as still pending. Any timeout of 5 seconds or less is therefore useless. With longer timeouts, including the default 90, the final interval up to the deadline is never polled either. The new tests in cli.code.verdict.test.ts miss this because they only feed `pending` answers (line 181 uses 90 s, and line 628 uses 5 s but expects pending). The loop is new in this diff.
findings.fix: In code.ts, read the verdict once more when the sleep reaches the deadline: drop the `break` after `waitForNextPoll` and let `readUntilDeadline` handle the remaining time, or do one last `listVersion` before giving up. Add a test in cli.code.verdict.test.ts that uses `--timeout 5`, with a next list answer of `passed` or `failed`, and asserts exit 0 or 1, for both `code test` and `code status --wait`.

findings.title: isVerdictReadRefusal reports an expired or rejected sign-in as 'this engine cannot answer the verdict yet' (exit 2)
findings.body:
`isVerdictReadRefusal` returns true for any ApiError with status 401 or 403 and for any Error whose message matches /sign-in expired/i. It also walks `error.cause`. `codeStatus` and `waitForVersion` turn that into 'this engine cannot answer the verdict yet' with exit 2, which is the documented 'still pending' code.

Those errors are exactly the ones the client raises when the stored credential is dead. `PlatformToken.get()` throws 'The Membrane sign-in expired and could not be refreshed. Sign in again.' (platform-token.ts:72) before sending any request. `rejectedCredentialError` (operator-client.ts:406) wraps the retried 401 as its `cause`. `SessionClosedError` carries the remint refusal as its cause. A genuine 403 from a policy gate also matches. The old-engine case this check exists for arrives as a 403 AccessDenied scope mismatch (`check-command-scope.ts:83-87`).

Concrete case: the operator's refresh token has expired and they run `code status`, or the token expires partway through a `code test` wait. The CLI prints 'this engine cannot answer the verdict yet' (or 'v3: pending — this engine cannot answer the verdict yet') and exits 2. The 'Sign in again' remedy is never shown. An agent that follows the exit codes reads 2 as pending and keeps polling forever.

The comment at line 559 is also wrong: it says the refresh reports that message only after the original 401, but `get()` raises it proactively. The tests at cli.code.verdict.test.ts:377-427 and :473-494 assert the conflation, and no test checks that a real credential failure keeps its own message.
findings.fix: Treat only the old-engine refusal as 'cannot answer yet': a 403 whose error data is the scope-mismatch access denial for list-source-tree-versions. Drop the 401 check and the /sign-in expired/ match, and do not treat rejectedCredentialError or SessionClosedError as a refusal, so they reach runCode's catch and print their own message with exit 1. Add a test where the token refresh fails and assert the sign-in message survives.

findings.title: `code status --wait --timeout 0` sets deadline == now, so readUntilDeadline aborts the only read and reports 'still pending' without reading the verdict
findings.body:
Observed: `validTimeout` accepts 0. `codeStatus` computes `deadline = now + 0`. `listVersion` dispatches the request, then `readUntilDeadline` computes `remaining = deadline - now <= 0`. It aborts the request and fails with VERDICT_READ_TIMED_OUT. `codeStatus` then prints 'still pending after 0 s — wait with: … --wait' and exits 2.

This happens whatever the version's real status is: passed, failed or untested. So `code status --wait --timeout 0` gives exit 2 and 'still pending' for a version that already passed, and never shows its status. A plain `code status` would have answered 0. The test at cli.code.verdict.test.ts:255 locks this behaviour in rather than catching it.

Impact is limited to a user who explicitly passes `--timeout 0` (or a sub-millisecond value) together with `--wait`.
findings.fix: Always do the first read without the deadline, or treat a timeout of 0 as 'read once, don't wait'. Only bound the reads that come after a pending answer.

findings.title: A transient error during a poll ends the wait with exit 1, the same code as a failed verdict
findings.body:
Observed: in `waitForVersion`, any read failure that is not a refusal (a 5xx, ECONNRESET, a DNS blip) reaches `Effect.fail(outcome.error)`. runCode's catch prints the message and returns 1. Under the exit-code scheme this change introduces (0 passed/skipped, 1 failed, 2 pending), exit 1 means 'tests failed'.

How this triggers: after `code test` has already queued the run, a single 502 from the list read during the up-to-90 s wait drops the wait. The command exits 1, as if the tests had failed. The next 5 s poll would most likely have succeeded. The stderr line names the HTTP error, but a caller branching on the exit code reads a failed verdict. Re-running `code test` to recover would queue a new run, which is the re-queue the change exists to prevent.

`code status`, and the 'No version X in this tree' path at line ~721, have the same 1-means-failed ambiguity.
findings.fix: Keep polling until the deadline after a non-refusal read error, keeping the last error for the timeout message. Or exit with a code different from the failed-verdict code (for example 2, with the error line) once the run is known to be queued.

findings.title: Пауза перед первым опросом расходует весь короткий timeout
findings.body: При `code test --timeout 5` или любом меньшем положительном timeout команда получает статус `pending`, ждёт до дедлайна и выходит с кодом 2, ни разу не прочитав результат. Даже если тест завершился сразу после постановки в очередь, команда сообщает, что он всё ещё выполняется. То же происходит в `code status --wait`, если первый ответ был `pending` и оставшееся время не превышает пяти секунд.
findings.fix: Прочитать статус до первой паузы и повторять чтение до дедлайна.

findings.title: A failed credential refresh is reported as "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet"
findings.body:
`isVerdictReadRefusal` treats any error whose message matches `/sign-in expired/i` as an old engine refusing the read. That text comes only from `storedCredentialSource.refresh` (`claude-plugin/src/client/platform-token.ts:72`), which throws it when the OAuth refresh grant itself fails: a revoked or expired refresh token, or a network error reaching the token endpoint.

The old-engine case does not need this clause. An old engine answers the sessionless read with 401. `callWithPlatformToken` then refreshes successfully, retries, gets 401 again and throws `rejectedCredentialError` with the 401 `ApiError` as its `cause`. The recursive `error.cause` check already matches that. The regex therefore only catches real refresh failures.

Concrete failure: `code test --timeout 600` waits long enough for the access token to expire. If the refresh then fails, the command prints `v3: pending — this engine cannot answer the verdict yet` and exits 2, the code meant for "still pending / engine refuses". The agent is told the engine is too old when the actual fix is to sign in again. A plain `code status` with an expired refresh token shows the same misleading line.

The 401/403 clause has the same breadth on the attached-session path. There `list-source-tree-versions` was always allowed, so a 403 means a real denial, but it is also reported as "engine cannot answer".
findings.fix: Delete the `/sign-in expired/i` line. The old-engine refusal is already caught through `error.cause`. A real refresh failure then surfaces with its own "Sign in again" message and exit 1.

findings.title: `code status --wait` with a short timeout says "still pending" for a version it never read
findings.body:
`codeStatus` computes the wait deadline before its first read and passes it to `listVersion`. So the first read, the one that learns the version's status, runs through `readUntilDeadline`. If the deadline is already spent (`--timeout 0`, where `remaining` is `deadline - now <= 0`) or the read is slower than the timeout, the read is aborted. The command then prints `still pending after N s` and exits 2. The version might really be `passed` (should exit 0), `failed` (1) or `untested` (3).

This breaks the goal's contract that `code status` reports 0/1/2/3. With `--timeout 0` the command can never report anything else. The new test `observes the aborted status read when the deadline is already spent` (`cli.code.verdict.test.ts:255`) pins this output, so it keeps the misreport rather than catching it.
findings.fix: Bound only the polling in `waitForVersion` by the deadline. Do the initial lookup in `codeStatus` without it (call `listVersion` with `deadline` undefined), or start the deadline after the first read. Update the `--timeout 0` test to expect the real status.

findings.title: The `catchTag` in `readUntilDeadline` does nothing
findings.body: `.pipe(Effect.catchTag('VerdictReadFailed', (error) => Effect.fail(error)))` catches a `VerdictReadFailed` and fails again with the same value. The error, its type and the ordering are all unchanged, so the combinator adds nothing. The `as Effect.Effect<T, VerdictReadError>` cast right after it makes the no-op harder to spot.
findings.fix: Remove the `.pipe(Effect.catchTag(...))` call and keep the cast on the `raceFirst` result.

findings.title: Has the PRD-3488 regression test been shown to fail with the regression in place?
findings.body: The test covers the main PRD-3488 case: the command queues the tests once and gets the final status without running them again. Nothing provided shows that this test failed on code that still had the regression, so it is not yet confirmed that it would catch it. To settle this, run the test against the state with the regression reproduced, confirm it fails for the expected reason, and confirm it passes on the fix.

findings.title: Workspace-code synopsis block lists neither `code test` nor the new `code status` verb or their flags
findings.body: The prose under the block now reads "`test` queues the tree's tests once and waits for the verdict; `status` reads a verdict without queuing another run", but the ```bash synopsis directly above (lines 575-583) still lists only pull/diff/push/run/promote/import/drift. The skill never names the new `--wait`, `--no-wait` and `--timeout <s>` flags, or the exit codes (0 passed/skipped, 1 failed, 2 pending, 3 untested) that `cli.ts` help and `code.ts` add. An agent copying invocations from the block has no `code status` line, so it learns about `--wait` only from the CLI's stderr after a first pending exit. `claude-plugin/README.md:240-249` has the same gap: it still says "round-trips through seven verbs" over a block missing both verbs. The impact is contained because the CLI's pending line prints the exact `code status … --wait` follow-up.
findings.fix: Add `membrane-operator code test [--tree-version <id>] [--no-wait] [--timeout <s>]` and `membrane-operator code status [--tree-version <id>] [--wait] [--timeout <s>]` to the synopsis block in SKILL.md and README.md, and correct README's verb count.

findings.title: 'Tree tests … run locally' contradicts the edited text saying `code test` queues the run on a worker
findings.body: These lines were not touched by this change. SKILL.md:599 ('Tree tests are the exception — they run locally, because a test needs fixtures'), SKILL.md:349 and MANUAL.md:335 all say tree tests run on the local machine. The paragraph this change edited, `docs/code.md` and `codeTest`'s doc comment all say the run executes remotely on a worker. An agent reading the skill could try to run `*.test.ts` locally instead of using `code test`.
findings.fix: Reword it to 'Tree tests are the exception — `code test` runs them on a worker without a routine's run authority, because a test needs fixtures' in both SKILL.md sites and in MANUAL.md.

findings.title: No test reaches the outer catch's failure notification, so reverting it to a silent return stays green
findings.body: The goal requires that the tests fail if a result is silently discarded again. `runBrewAutoUpdate` has a separate terminal path for errors that are not step failures: the outer catch at index.ts:445-447, which returns `finish(trigger, ui, reportFailure(`Pi update failed without blocking startup: ...`))`. It runs when `acquireLock` throws (mkdir/writeFile/rename on the state dir fails with EACCES, ENOSPC, EROFS or ENOTDIR) or when an injected `snapshotExtensions` rejects. No test reaches it. Every fixture uses a writable temp `lockPath`, the default `snapshotExtensions` resolves, and nothing asserts the "without blocking startup" message. The exec-throw test at line 351 throws inside the inner try (index.ts:406-411), so it never reaches this catch. If line 447 went back to `return reportFailure(...)` without `finish`, the whole suite would stay green, and a broken `~/.local/state/pi` would fail silently on every startup and every manual run. That is the exact defect issue 022 fixes.
findings.fix: Add a manual and a startup test where `lockPath` sits under a regular file (so `mkdir` throws ENOTDIR), or where `snapshotExtensions` throws. Assert status `failed` and exactly one `warning` notification containing the error detail.

findings.title: A later step's failure hides that an earlier step already upgraded Pi, so the user gets no restart prompt
findings.body: Suppose `brew upgrade pi-coding-agent` succeeds and `installedUpdates` records "pi". Then `pi update --extensions` fails, times out or throws. The function returns early with `finish(..., reportFailure("Pi package update failed: ..."))`, so the user sees only the failure warning. The "Pi updated. Restart Pi to use the new version." outcome is dropped even though the binary was replaced, and the user keeps running the old in-memory version without knowing a restart is needed. The old code also dropped this outcome. The change rewrote these return sites to surface outcomes but still loses the partial-update one.
findings.fix: When a step fails after `installedUpdates` is non-empty, add `installedUpdateMessage(installedUpdates)` to the failure message, or send a separate info notification before returning the failure.

findings.title: Issue 022 is still `open`, and its short_description describes the defect this change fixes
findings.body: The change implements the whole scope of issue 022 and records its decisions as settled. The frontmatter still says `status: "open"`, has no `closed` date, and keeps a short_description ("Both Pi updater entry points discard failed results, and focused tests explicitly require empty notifications...") that is now false. The repository-issues skill requires short_description to reflect the current understanding. `python3 scripts/issues list` will keep showing 022 as an unfixed bug next to its follow-up 2026-09-02-007, which calls 022 fixed, so agents may re-investigate it.
findings.fix: Close it through the lifecycle, e.g. `python3 scripts/issues close 2026-08-21-022 --resolution "..."`, pointing to 2026-09-02-007 for the headless gap. If it stays open on purpose, at least update short_description via `scripts/issues edit`.

findings.title: Тесты не защищают уведомление об ошибке получения блокировки
findings.body: Новые тесты проверяют ошибки команд, но не ошибку из внешнего блока catch, например отказ mkdir при создании каталога блокировки. Если в этом блоке снова вернуть reportFailure напрямую, минуя finish, пользователь не получит предупреждение, а эти тесты останутся зелёными. Это не выполняет цель изменения: тесты должны обнаруживать повторное замалчивание каждого типа результата.
findings.fix: Добавить сценарий с ошибкой получения блокировки и проверить предупреждение через пользовательский UI.

findings.title: При ошибке после обновления Pi теряется сообщение о перезапуске
findings.body: Если brew upgrade успешно обновит pi-coding-agent, а следующий pi update --extensions завершится с ошибкой, ранний возврат сообщит только об ошибке пакетов. Записанное в installedUpdates обновление Pi не попадёт в уведомление, и пользователь не узнает, что нужно перезапустить Pi. Эта проблема существовала до изменения.
findings.fix: При формировании сообщения об ошибке также сообщать о ранее установленных обновлениях и необходимости перезапуска.

findings.title: The manual command's catch-all failure notice says "without blocking startup"
findings.body: The outer catch builds `Pi update failed without blocking startup: ${detail}` for both triggers. Before this change nothing displayed that text. Now `finish` sends it through `ui.notify` at `warning`, including for the `manual` trigger. A user who runs `/brew-auto-update-now` while `acquireLock` throws (e.g. EACCES on the state dir) gets a warning about blocking startup, which is not what they ran. Only the wording is wrong.
findings.fix: Choose the prefix by trigger (`trigger === "startup" ? "Pi update failed without blocking startup" : "Pi update failed"`), or use trigger-neutral wording.

findings.title: Every return site must remember to call finish; a single exit point would enforce it
findings.body: The rule this change enforces is that every terminal result passes through `finish`/`shouldNotify`. Today it holds only because each of the eight `return` statements in `runBrewAutoUpdate` (lines 382, 386, 394, 410, 414, 421, 444, 447) wraps its result in `finish(trigger, ui, …)` by hand. A future return path that leaves out the wrapper silently brings back the issue 022 defect, and only a test written for that new path would catch it. A single exit point would make the rule hold by structure and remove the repeated arguments. The code is correct today; this is a structural improvement only.
findings.fix: Move the body into an inner `runSteps(trigger, deps)` that returns `{ result, installedUpdate }` without notifying, and have `runBrewAutoUpdate` call `finish(trigger, ui, result, installedUpdate)` exactly once.

findings.title: Outer catch failure path is never exercised, so silently discarding it again would stay green
findings.body: Each inner step failure (exec throw, killed, nonzero exit) now has a test that checks the notification. The outer catch at index.ts:445-447 has none. That catch handles `acquireLock` throwing (for example EACCES/EROFS creating the lock directory) and `snapshotExtensions` rejecting. No test makes either of those throw. Nothing in the file matches "without blocking startup". If line 447 went back to `return reportFailure(...)` without `finish`, every test would still pass, and a lock directory that can't be written would fail silently on every startup. That is the exact defect issue 022 fixes, and the goal says the tests must catch a silently discarded result.
findings.fix: Add a test with `snapshotExtensions: async () => { throw new Error("boom") }`, or a lockPath under a read-only/non-directory parent. Assert the status is `failed` and that exactly one `warning` notification contains "boom". Add the same case for the startup trigger.

findings.title: Startup silence on `skipped` (offline / disabled) is not asserted
findings.body: The settled policy says startup stays silent on non-failure outcomes. Tests check startup silence for `complete` (up to date and unknown) and for `contended` (line 437). Neither `skipped` branch is checked. The PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 test at line 303 calls `fakeUi().ui` and throws away the notifications. The PI_OFFLINE test only runs `manual`. Suppose `shouldNotify` were changed to report skips at startup, for example `if (status === "skipped") return true` added to surface why nothing ran. A user who set PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 or PI_OFFLINE=1 would then get "Pi startup update is disabled." or the offline message on every session, and nothing in the suite would fail.
findings.fix: In the PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 test, keep the startup `fakeUi()` and assert `notifications` is `[]`. Add a startup PI_OFFLINE=1 case with the same assertion, next to the manual offline test.

findings.title: Issue 022 is still `open` and its short_description describes the defect this change fixes
findings.body: The change implements the whole scope of issue 022 and records both decisions as settled. The frontmatter is unchanged: `status: "open"`, and the short_description still says "Both Pi updater entry points discard failed results, and focused tests explicitly require empty notifications for timeout and command failure". After this diff, both halves of that sentence are false. The repository-issues skill says short_description must describe the current understanding and must be updated in the same lifecycle operation. `scripts/issues list` returns open issues to agents, so an agent picking work will see 022 as an unfixed silent-failure bug and may re-investigate or re-implement it. The headless gap now has its own issue (007), so nothing else keeps 022 open.
findings.fix: Run `python3 scripts/issues close 2026-08-21-022 --resolution "..."`, pointing to 2026-09-02-007 for the headless gap. If it is deliberately left open, at least update short_description through `scripts/issues edit`.

findings.title: Registration test drives a startup failure into ctx.ui but never checks it arrives
findings.body: Issue 022 points at the call sites (`session_start` discarding the result) as the place failures were lost. The fix depends on the handler passing `ctx.ui` into `runBrewAutoUpdate`. The registration test already sets up a failing exec (`code: 1, stderr: "stop"`) and a fakeUi-backed `ctx`. But it builds `ctx = { ui: fakeUi().ui }`, which throws away the notifications array. It also calls `finishExec()` without awaiting the run. Suppose the handler at index.ts:461 passed any other UI object, or wrapped `ctx.ui` in a no-op. No test would fail, and startup failures would be invisible to Pi users again. The direct-call tests can't catch this, because they hand `runBrewAutoUpdate` the UI themselves.
findings.fix: Keep the `fakeUi()` result. After `finishExec()`, wait until `notifications.length === 1`, then assert that one notification is a `warning` containing "Homebrew metadata refresh" and "stop".

findings.title: Не проверяется уведомление об ошибке создания блокировки
findings.body: Тест исключения проверяет только ошибку запуска команды, которую обрабатывает внутренний catch. Если создание каталога блокировки завершается ошибкой, например из-за отсутствия прав, управление попадает во внешний catch. Тесты не проверяют его уведомление, поэтому удаление finish из этого пути вернёт тихий сбой при запуске и ручном вызове, не нарушив приведённые проверки.
findings.fix: Добавить в этот набор тест с недоступным путём блокировки и проверить результат failed и уведомление уровня warning.

findings.title: Follow-up issue 007 claims every terminal result is sent through ui.notify
findings.body: The follow-up says every terminal result is sent through `ui.notify`. At startup, `shouldNotify` deliberately suppresses `skipped`, `contended` and up-to-date results. The statement contradicts the notification policy recorded in issue 022, which this document references, and misleads readers about current behavior.
findings.fix: Say that every result passes through `finish`/`shouldNotify` and that a notification is sent according to the startup or manual policy.

findings.title: Issue 022's problem description is still in the present tense after the fix
findings.body: The issue still says `ui.notify` is called only on update and that tests require empty notifications on failure. After this change both statements are false: failures notify the user, and the tests assert those notifications. Readers get an outdated description of current behavior.
findings.fix: Mark the description as historical and record what the fix changed.

findings.title: No test asserts a notification from the outer-catch failure path (index.ts:445-447)
findings.body: The goal requires the tests to fail if any terminal result were silently discarded again. Every `finish(...)` call site has a test asserting a notification, except the outer `catch` at index.ts:445-447. That catch handles errors from `acquireLock` (for example `mkdir` of `~/.local/state/pi` failing with EACCES/ENOTDIR, or `rename` failing during stale reclaim) and errors thrown by `deps.snapshotExtensions`. I searched the test file: no test makes the lock path unwritable or makes `snapshotExtensions`/lock acquisition throw, and nothing asserts the "Pi update failed without blocking startup" message. Because the new exec-throw test (line 351) throws inside the inner `try` at index.ts:406-411, it never reaches this catch. Concrete case: change line 447 back to `return reportFailure(...)` and the whole suite stays green. A broken lock directory would then fail silently on every startup and every manual run, which is the exact defect issue 022 set out to fix. The policy itself is fine. The gap is in the oracle.
findings.fix: Add a test where `snapshotExtensions` throws, or where `lockPath` sits under a regular file so `mkdir` fails with ENOTDIR. Assert `status: "failed"` and exactly one `warning` notification for both the manual and startup triggers.

findings.title: Outer-catch failure message says "without blocking startup" and is now shown to manual-command users
findings.body: Before this change, the `reportFailure("Pi update failed without blocking startup: ...")` result was never shown to anyone. Now `finish` sends it to `ui.notify` for both triggers. When a user runs `/brew-auto-update-now` and lock acquisition or snapshotting throws, they see a warning about "blocking startup", even though no startup is happening. The text is trigger-specific but the code path is shared. The impact is limited to misleading wording in a warning that is otherwise correct.
findings.fix: Drop the startup-specific phrase (for example "Pi update failed: ${detail}"), or pick the wording based on `trigger`.

findings.title: Ошибка последнего шага скрывает ранее установленное обновление Pi
findings.body: Если `brew upgrade pi-coding-agent` установил новую версию, а следующий `pi update --extensions` завершился с ошибкой, функция возвращает только предупреждение об ошибке. Накопленный `installedUpdates` не используется, поэтому пользователь не получает сообщение о необходимости перезапустить Pi. Этот дефект существовал до изменений.
findings.fix: При возврате ошибки также сообщать об уже установленных обновлениях и необходимости перезапуска.

findings.title: Follow-up утверждает, что уведомляется каждый результат
findings.body: В описании сказано, что каждый конечный результат передаётся через `ui.notify`. Но `shouldNotify` намеренно подавляет при запуске результаты `skipped`, `contended` и успешный результат без установленного обновления. Это противоречит политике, записанной в исходном issue, и может ввести читателя в заблуждение о текущем поведении.
findings.fix: Уточнить, что через `ui.notify` передаются результаты, разрешённые политикой уведомлений.

findings.title: Outer-catch failure path (lock/setup errors) has no test, so dropping its finish() stays green
findings.body: The change routes the outer catch in runBrewAutoUpdate (home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/brew-auto-update/index.ts:445-447, message "Pi update failed without blocking startup: …") through finish(), so failures before or around the steps should now produce a warning. Examples are acquireLock throwing EACCES/EROFS on the state dir, or an injected snapshotExtensions rejecting. None of the new tests reaches this branch. The failure tests cover only exec throwing (line 410), killed (413-418) and non-zero exit (420-421). Red-making edit that no test catches: change line 447 back to `return reportFailure(...)` without finish(). Every test still passes, and a persistently unwritable lock directory silently swallows every startup and manual update again. That is the exact regression the goal says these tests must catch ("the tests would fail if a result were silently discarded again").
findings.fix: Add one case with a deps override whose lockPath sits under a regular file (e.g. write a file at the parent path), so mkdir rejects with ENOTDIR/EEXIST. Assert status "failed", then exactly one notification at level "warning" whose message contains the expected prefix. Run it for both startup and manual.

findings.title: finish() repeated at 8 return sites instead of one choke point around the run
findings.body: The goal's invariant is that no terminal result is returned without passing through finish/shouldNotify. Right now that holds only because each of the eight `return` statements in runBrewAutoUpdate (lines 382, 386, 394, 410, 414, 421, 444, 447) remembers to wrap its result in `finish(trigger, ui, …)`. A future early return that forgets the wrapper silently brings back the defect this change fixes. Alternative: move the body into an inner function that returns the plain UpdateResult plus the installed-update flag, and call finish() once in runBrewAutoUpdate. That keeps the same outputs, levels and messages and removes seven duplicate call sites. It also makes the invariant hold by structure. The one ordering difference: the notification would fire after `lock.release()` in the finally block instead of just before it. Nothing the user sees depends on that order.
findings.fix: Rename the current body to an internal `runSteps(trigger, deps)` returning `{ result, installedUpdate }` with no finish() calls, then implement `runBrewAutoUpdate` as `const { result, installedUpdate } = await runSteps(trigger, deps); return finish(trigger, ui, result, installedUpdate);`.

findings.title: Регрессионные тесты уведомлений не откалиброваны
findings.body: Для изменённых тестов уведомлений не предоставлен результат запуска против прежней реализации, которая молча возвращала ошибки. Поэтому не подтверждено, что тесты стали красными именно из-за отсутствия уведомлений и стали зелёными после исправления. Это оставляет непроверенным покрытие основного дефекта, который должна обнаруживать эта группа тестов.
findings.fix: Запустить изменённые тесты против прежней реализации или с минимальной мутацией, возвращающей молчаливое поведение, затем подтвердить успех на рассматриваемом состоянии.

findings.title: Expired sign-in or a real 401/403 on the verdict read is reported as 'this engine cannot answer the verdict yet'
findings.body: `isVerdictReadRefusal` maps every 401, every 403 and any error whose message matches /sign-in expired/ (or that has such an error as its cause) to the old-engine fallback. That covers `platform-token.ts:72` ("The Membrane sign-in expired and could not be refreshed. Sign in again.") and `rejectedCredentialError` (its cause is an ApiError 401). Example: an operator whose login has lapsed runs `code status --workspace acme`. Sessionless dispatch fails the platform-token refresh, and `codeStatus` (around line 712) prints `this engine cannot answer the verdict yet` and exits 2. The actionable "Sign in again" message is dropped, and exit 2 is documented as 'still pending / engine refuses', so an agent will retry or wait instead of asking for a sign-in. The same thing happens mid-wait in `waitForVersion`, which prints `vN: pending — this engine cannot answer…`. A genuine 403 with an attached session (for example a revoked seat) is misreported the same way. The goal only asks for an old engine refusing the read to degrade to exit 2. Credential failures are a separate state, and a consumer cannot tell the two apart.
findings.fix: Treat only the server's refusal of the read as the old-engine case: a 403 or 401 ApiError on the list call itself. Let `rejectedCredentialError` and the platform-token refresh failure propagate to runCode's catch, so it prints "Sign in again" and exits 1. At minimum, drop the /sign-in expired/ match and stop recursing through `cause` into credential errors.

findings.title: `code test --json` output changed from `{ version: {...} }` to the bare version object
findings.body: Before this change, `codeTest` printed `JSON.stringify(result)`, where `result` is the RunSourceTreeTestsCommand output `{ version: SourceTreeVersion }`. Now every path goes through `renderTestVersion(context, result.version, json)`, which prints the version object without the wrapper. This includes `--no-wait`, which otherwise keeps the old queue-and-return behaviour. A script or agent that read `.version.testsStatus` from `code test --json` now gets `undefined`. The goal does not mention this change, and no doc records it. It was probably done to match `code status --json`, but it is a silent break in a machine-read CLI output.
findings.fix: Keep the `{ version }` envelope for `code test --json` (print `{ version: current }`), or record the new shape in the plugin README / `--help` as an intended change.

findings.title: An expired or rejected sign-in is reported as "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet" and exits 2 (pending)
findings.body:
`isVerdictReadRefusal` returns true for any 401 or 403, for any error whose message matches /sign-in expired/, and it follows `error.cause` recursively. An old engine refusing the sessionless read answers 403 scope-mismatch: `AccessDenied` has status FORBIDDEN in `engine/api/src/platform/errors/refusals.ts:148-153`. A 401 does not mean an old engine, though. It means the credential is gone.

On the unattached path, `callWithPlatformToken` turns a 401 it cannot refresh into one of two errors:
- `rejectedCredentialError` ("Membrane rejected the stored credential. Sign in again…"), with the 401 ApiError as its cause (`operator-client.ts:406`);
- `platform-token.ts:72` "The Membrane sign-in expired and could not be refreshed. Sign in again."

The classifier matches both. So when an operator's login expires, `code status`, `code status --wait` or the polling phase of `code test` prints "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet" and exits 2. That message is the old-engine line, and the "Sign in again" remedy is never shown. Exit 2 means "still pending" in this verb's contract, so an agent following the documented exit codes will keep waiting or re-running `code status` and never re-authenticate. The attached path has the same problem: a session token that is refused again after remint (for example, a stopped session) also reads as "old engine".

The goal asks only that an old engine refusing the read degrade to exit 2. That refusal is a 403, so treating 401 and credential expiry as the same case goes beyond it and hides the actionable error. The tests at `cli.code.verdict.test.ts:377,396,475-478` pin 401 as an "unavailable verdict", so this behaviour is deliberate, but it is still wrong.
findings.fix: Treat only a 403 scope-mismatch (or 403) as the old-engine refusal. Let 401s and the credential-rejected or sign-in-expired errors propagate to `runCode`'s catch, which prints the "Sign in again" message and exits 1. Drop the `/sign-in expired/` match and the recursion into `cause` for 401.

findings.title: `code test --json` output shape changed from `{ version: {...} }` to the bare version object
findings.body: Before the change, `code test --json` printed `JSON.stringify(result)`, which is the `run-source-tree-tests` output `{ version: SourceTreeVersion }`. `renderTestVersion` now prints the `SourceTreeVersion` on its own, on every path including `--no-wait`. A caller that reads `.version.testsStatus` from `code test --json`, such as an agent script or jq pipeline, now reads `undefined`. Neither the goal nor the docs mention the change, and no test covers the JSON shape of `code test`.
findings.fix: Keep the `{ version }` envelope for `code test --json` (and use it for `code status --json` too, so both verbs agree), or document the shape change in the plugin README and help text.

findings.title: No-op `catchTag` rethrow and duplicated error-wrapping lambda in the verdict-read Effects
findings.body: `Effect.catchTag('VerdictReadFailed', (error) => Effect.fail(error))` catches the error and fails with that same error, so it does nothing. The `as Effect.Effect<T, VerdictReadError>` cast that follows covers for it. The same `catch: (cause) => new VerdictReadFailed({ cause, message: cause instanceof Error ? cause.message : String(cause) })` lambda appears three times (lines 520, 604, 632). `timeoutSeconds` assigns to a local only to return it. The code is correct, but this is dead structure.
findings.fix: Remove the `catchTag` pipe and the cast. Extract a single `toVerdictReadFailed(cause)` helper and use it at all three sites.

findings.title: An expired, rejected or closed sign-in or session is reported as "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet" and exits 2 (pending)
findings.body:
`isVerdictReadRefusal` returns true for any 401 or 403, for any error whose message matches /sign-in expired/, and it follows `error.cause` recursively. The old-engine case the goal names is a 403 scope-mismatch refusal of the sessionless read. The classifier catches much more than that:
- `platform-token.ts:72` throws "The Membrane sign-in expired and could not be refreshed. Sign in again." when the refresh grant fails. That can happen up front in `storedCredentialSource().get()` with no 401 involved, so the comment saying the message follows the original 401 is wrong.
- `rejectedCredentialError` ("Membrane rejected the stored credential. Sign in again…") has a 401 ApiError as its cause.
- `SessionClosedError` wraps a 403 mint refusal as its cause. A session closed before or during the wait loses its "run `session start …`" message.
- A genuine permission 403, such as a revoked seat, is caught too.

Failure case: an operator whose login has lapsed runs `code status --workspace acme`. `dispatchUnattached` fails on the workspace lookup, `listVersion` wraps the error as `VerdictReadFailed`, and the classifier matches it. The CLI prints "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet" and exits 2, which the verb's contract uses for "still pending". The "Sign in again" remedy is never shown, and an agent following the exit codes keeps waiting or polling instead of re-authenticating. `code test` mid-wait prints `vN: pending — this engine cannot answer…` in the same situation.

The tests in `cli.code.verdict.test.ts` (`it.each([401, 403])`, around lines 377, 396 and 475-478) lock this in. Their 401 case passes only through the 'sign-in expired' regex, because the token-grant double returns 500. No test checks that a credential failure still shows its sign-in message.
findings.fix: Count only the engine's direct 403 (scope-mismatch) refusal of the list call as the old-engine case. Drop the `/sign-in expired/` match, and stop following `cause` into `rejectedCredentialError` and `SessionClosedError`. Let those errors reach `runCode`'s catch, which prints their own message and exits 1. Add a test that an expired sign-in on `code status` prints the sign-in message.

findings.title: Workspace-code usage blocks leave out `code test`/`code status` and their new flags
findings.body: The README's usage block opens with 'round-trips through seven verbs' and lists pull/diff/push/run/promote/import/drift. It has no `code status` line, and none of the new `--wait`, `--no-wait`, `--timeout <s>` or `--tree-version` flags for test/status. The same gap is in the `## Workspace code` block of `claude-plugin/skills/operate/SKILL.md` (around lines 576-584). Yet the prose under both blocks now tells the reader to use `code status`. The `code test` line was already missing before this change. `code status` is new here, and the change added it to the prose but not to either usage block. The 0/1/2/3 exit-code meanings are also not written down anywhere except as stderr hints. `--help` does list the flags, so the damage is limited.
findings.fix: Add `membrane-operator code test [--tree-version <id>] [--no-wait] [--timeout <s>]` and `membrane-operator code status [--tree-version <id>] [--wait] [--timeout <s>]` to both blocks, and update the verb count.

findings.title: The guide wrongly says tree tests run locally
findings.body: This predates the change. The sentence "Tree tests are the exception — they run locally" contradicts the code: codeTest in claude-plugin/src/engine/verbs/code.ts:516 calls RunSourceTreeTestsCommand, and SourceTreeTestRunsService queues the run on a remote worker. The guide tells the agent the wrong place the tests run. The same error appears at SKILL.md:349 and MANUAL.md:335.
findings.fix: Correct all three mentions: the tests run on a platform worker, and the CLI waits for the result recorded on the version.

findings.title: The code pull example suggests flags the command rejects
findings.body: This predates the change. The example offers --tree-version and --latest for code pull, but codePull in claude-plugin/src/engine/verbs/code.ts:362 rejects either flag before reading the tree and exits 1. A user who follows the example to fetch a specific version gets no clone. cli.code.test.ts pins both rejections. The same example appears at operate/SKILL.md:577.
findings.fix: Remove these flags from both examples, and point to `git show v/<version id>:<path>` for reading a version after cloning.

findings.title: waitForVersion breaks at the deadline without a final read, so `code test --timeout` ≤ 5 never reads the verdict
findings.body: `waitForNextPoll` sleeps `min(5000, deadline - now)`. The check right after it, `if (now >= effectiveDeadline) break`, leaves the loop before any `listVersion` call once that sleep reaches the deadline. With `code test --timeout 5` or lower, the only sleep runs to the deadline and the loop exits without reading the verdict. The command prints `v3: pending` and the "still pending after N s" hint, then exits 2, even if the run settled meanwhile. With the default 90 s, the last read happens at 85 s, so a verdict that lands between 85 and 90 s is also reported as pending. `code status --wait` is not affected because it reads once before the loop. No test covers a `code test --timeout` below the 5 s poll interval.
findings.fix: Do one last read after the final sleep with a short grace period past the deadline (readUntilDeadline fails immediately once remaining <= 0, so just moving the deadline check after the read is not enough), or read before sleeping on each iteration so the last poll happens before the deadline.

findings.title: `code test --json` output changed from `{ version: {...} }` to the bare version object
findings.body: Before this change, `code test --json` printed `JSON.stringify(result)`. That is the `run-source-tree-tests` output, `{ version: SourceTreeVersion }`. `renderTestVersion` now prints the inner version object on every path: `--no-wait`, settled at queue time, after the wait, and on timeout. A script, jq pipeline or agent that reads `.version.testsStatus` now gets `undefined`. SKILL.md tells agents to prefer `--json` when reading data. The goal, the README, SKILL.md and MANUAL.md say nothing about the change, and no test covers the JSON shape of `code test`. The new `code status --json` uses the same bare shape, so the two verbs agree, but the existing verb's machine-read output broke silently.
findings.fix: Keep the `{ version }` envelope for `code test --json`, and use it for `code status --json` too. Otherwise, document the new shape in the plugin README and SKILL code-verb section.

findings.title: isVerdictReadRefusal treats any 401/403, including a SessionClosedError cause, as "engine cannot answer the verdict yet"
findings.body: Observed: `isVerdictReadRefusal` returns true for any 401 or 403 and walks `error.cause`. `SessionClosedError` (api-error.ts:54) wraps the mint refusal as its `cause`, and `isClosedSessionApiError` accepts 403. So a session that closes during the wait (or before `code status` runs) gets its actionable message ("run `session start …` to bind again") replaced by `this engine cannot answer the verdict yet`, with exit 2. Exit 2 is the code the goal reserves for "still pending". A genuine permission 403 on the read gets the same message. Inferred impact: an agent following the exit-code contract keeps re-polling with `code status --wait` and is never told to rebind its session. This is contained: an old engine does reject with exactly this status (its gates return 403 for a non-sessionless command on a platform credential), so the classifier works for its intended case. It is just broader than that case.
findings.fix: Exclude `SessionClosedError` (and the closed-session denial) from `isVerdictReadRefusal` so it keeps its own message. Optionally, limit the refusal match to the scope-mismatch/unscoped access-denied body an old engine returns.

findings.title: A genuinely expired sign-in is reported as "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet"
findings.body:
`isVerdictReadRefusal` treats any error whose message matches /sign-in expired/ as an old-engine refusal. That message is thrown only by `storedCredentialSource.refresh` in `client/platform-token.ts:72`, when the OAuth refresh grant itself fails, which means the operator's sign-in really is dead. It is not something an engine says when it refuses the read. An engine that refuses with a 401 after a successful refresh already surfaces as `rejectedCredentialError` with a 401 cause, and the recursion on `error.cause` on the next line catches that. So the regex adds only the misclassification.

The path: `PlatformTokenSource.get()` refreshes an expired access token up front, and `dispatchUnattached` (run.ts:222) calls `getOperatorOverview` → `callWithPlatformToken` inside the same `dispatch` promise that `listVersion` wraps. The CLI auth gate only checks that a credentials file exists (cli.ts:134); it does not validate the token. Failure case: an operator whose refresh token has expired or been revoked runs `membrane-operator code status --workspace acme`. They get `this engine cannot answer the verdict yet` and exit 2 ('still pending / engine refuses') instead of the 'Sign in again' error and exit 1. An agent following the documented exit codes will wait or retry, and is never told to sign in. The same happens to `code test` if the sign-in dies mid-wait: it prints `vN: pending — this engine cannot answer the verdict yet`.
findings.fix: Delete the `/sign-in expired/` line. That lets a dead sign-in propagate as its own error (exit 1 with the sign-in message), and real engine refusals stay covered by the 401/403 status check and the `cause` recursion.

findings.title: Each verdict poll re-fetches the whole operator overview to resolve the same workspace
findings.body: `code test` and `code status --wait` now call `dispatch(ListSourceTreeVersionsCommand, …)` every 5 s until the deadline (90 s by default, about 18 polls). With no attached session, which is the case this change targets (the command became `sessionless` for exactly that), every dispatch goes through `dispatchUnattached`. That calls `loadOverview` → `get-operator-overview` before the list call. `get-operator-overview` is the cross-workspace cockpit aggregate: every workspace the user touches, with its jobs, waiting inbox items and health (admin-hub.ts:926). So one wait sends up to ~18 heavy aggregate requests whose only use is to map `--workspace acme` to the same `orgWorkspaceId` each time. It also doubles the round trips inside every poll's deadline budget. dispatchUnattached was already written this way before this change, but the new polling loop is what makes it run repeatedly.
findings.fix: Resolve the workspace once per dispatcher: in `createDispatcher`, memoize the `orgWorkspaceId` promise from the first `dispatchUnattached` lookup, then call `client.callInWorkspace` directly on later dispatches. This keeps the same errors on the first call and the same target workspace for the rest of the invocation.

findings.title: `code status --wait --timeout 0` reports "still pending" without ever reading the verdict
findings.body: In `codeStatus`, `deadline = now + 0`. `listVersion` creates the request, and `readUntilDeadline` sees `remaining <= 0`, so it aborts the request and fails with `VERDICT_READ_TIMED_OUT` before the read can settle. `codeStatus` then prints `still pending after 0 s — wait with: … --wait` and exits 2, with nothing on stdout, even when the newest version has already passed (exit 0) or failed (exit 1). A read-only verb ends up claiming a status it never observed. The new test 'observes the aborted status read when the deadline is already spent' locks in this output (`out: ''`, exit 2), so the suite treats the misreport as correct. By contrast, `code test --timeout 0` at least prints the status it got back when it queued the run.
findings.fix: Bound only reads that follow the initial one: in `codeStatus`, call the first `listVersion` without a deadline (or skip the abort when `remaining <= 0` on the first page). Pass `deadline` only to `waitForVersion`, so `--timeout 0` means 'read once, do not wait'.

findings.title: Each verdict poll re-fetches the whole operator overview to resolve the same workspace
findings.body: `code test` and `code status --wait` call `dispatch(ListSourceTreeVersionsCommand, …)` every 5 s until the deadline: about 17-18 polls at the default 90 s, and more if there are several pages. With no attached session, which is the case this change targets, every dispatch goes through `dispatchUnattached`. That calls `loadOverview` → `get-operator-overview` before the list call. `get-operator-overview` is the cross-workspace aggregate of jobs, waiting inbox items and health for every workspace the user can access (admin-hub.ts:926, operator-overview.service.ts). Its only use here is mapping `--workspace acme` to the same `orgWorkspaceId` each time. Each poll's deadline budget also pays for an extra round trip. The lookup already existed; the new polling loop in code.ts (around line 657) is what makes it run repeatedly.
findings.fix: Resolve the workspace once per dispatcher or CLI invocation: memoize the `orgWorkspaceId` from the first `dispatchUnattached` lookup, then call `client.callInWorkspace` directly on later dispatches. The engine still checks access on every request.

findings.title: Workspace-code verb blocks omit `code test`/`code status` and their wait flags while the edited prose documents them
findings.body: The edited paragraph says "`test` queues the tree's tests once and waits for the verdict; `status` reads a verdict without queuing another run." The ```bash block it explains (SKILL.md 576-584) lists only pull/diff/push/run/promote/import/drift. The same gap is in claude-plugin/README.md, lines 236-252, which says "round-trips through seven verbs". Neither block has `code test`, `code status`, or the flags that decide how they wait: `--wait`, `--no-wait`, `--timeout <s>`, `--tree-version`. The 0/1/2/3 exit-code meanings appear nowhere except as stderr hints. `code test` was already missing before this change; `code status` is new here, and the change added it only in prose. `--help` and the stderr hint after exit 2 limit the damage.
findings.fix: Add `membrane-operator code test [--tree-version <id>] [--no-wait] [--timeout <s>]` and `membrane-operator code status [--tree-version <id>] [--wait] [--timeout <s>]` to both blocks, and update the README verb count.

findings.title: Pre-existing: "Tree tests are the exception — they run locally" contradicts the edited text saying `code test` queues tests on the platform
findings.body: This is on an unchanged line two paragraphs below the edited text. The `code run` paragraph says tree tests run locally, while the changed paragraph (line 589) and docs/code.md say `code test` queues the tests and a worker records the verdict on the version row. An agent may run the `*.test.ts` files locally and treat that as the verdict.
findings.fix: Change the sentence to something like "Tree tests run on the platform through `code test`, not through `code run`.", or delete it.

findings.title: No test reaches the outer-catch failure path (index.ts:445-447), so a silent discard there would still pass
findings.body: Issue 022 asks for tests that fail if a terminal failure is silently discarded again. The new failure tests only reach the step-level exits inside the `deps.exec` loop: the exec throw at index.ts:410, the timeout at 414 and the nonzero exit at 421. No test reaches the outer `catch` at home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/brew-auto-update/index.ts:445-447. That catch handles errors from `acquireLock`, such as `mkdir` failing with ENOTDIR, EACCES or EROFS on an unwritable or blocked state directory, and errors from a rejecting `snapshotExtensions`. `rg 'without blocking' tests/` finds nothing. If line 447 went back to the pre-fix `return reportFailure(...)`, every test would still pass. A broken lock directory would then fail silently on every startup and on every manual run, which is the defect issue 022 exists to fix. The code at line 447 is correct today, so this is a coverage gap rather than a live bug. A related gap: the unknown-extension-state result, "Pi package update completed; extension changes could not be verified.", is only tested with the startup trigger (line 275). No test checks that the manual command reports it.
findings.fix: Add a test where `lockPath` sits under a regular file, e.g. write a file at `join(root, "state")` and use `join(root, "state", "pi", "lock")` so `mkdir` throws ENOTDIR, or where `snapshotExtensions` rejects. Assert `status: "failed"`, that no exec calls run, and exactly one `warning` notification containing the error detail, for both `startup` and `manual`.

findings.title: Update failures stay invisible in headless (print/JSON) mode
findings.body: This problem existed before the change and is already recorded in the new issue 2026-09-02-007. When Pi runs in print/JSON mode, a brew failure passes through `finish`, but the notification is lost: the SDK sets up print mode without a uiContext, and the runner substitutes a noOpUIContext whose `notify` does nothing. The session_start handler also discards the UpdateResult. So someone running Pi from a script still gets no message when an update fails.
findings.fix: Add a failure-reporting channel for the no-UI mode, for example stderr, while keeping the chosen notification policy.

findings.title: Тесты не защищают уведомление из внешнего catch
findings.body: Новый тест исключения вызывает throw из deps.exec, который перехватывает внутренний catch. Ни один тест не вызывает внешний catch на строках 445–447 реализации. Например, если родитель lockPath является обычным файлом, acquireLock завершится с ENOTDIR именно через эту ветку. Возврат там к прежнему reportFailure без finish оставит все текущие тесты зелёными, хотя пользователь снова не увидит ошибку. Это оставляет невыполненным требование цели защищать каждый терминальный результат от молчаливого отбрасывания.
findings.fix: Добавить сценарий с родителем lockPath, являющимся файлом, и проверить failed, отсутствие запуска команд и одно warning-уведомление.

findings.title: Manual-command failure notification says the update failed "without blocking startup"
findings.body: The outer catch at index.ts:445-447 builds `Pi update failed without blocking startup: ${detail}` whatever triggered the run. Before this change that result was thrown away by both call sites, so nobody saw the string. Now it goes through `finish`, and `shouldNotify` always returns true for `failed`. So when a user runs `/brew-auto-update-now` and lock acquisition throws (e.g. EACCES creating `$XDG_STATE_HOME/pi`) or `snapshotExtensions` throws, the warning they see talks about startup for a run they started mid-session. The string is old; this change is what makes manual users see it.
findings.fix: Make the message trigger-neutral, e.g. `Pi update failed: ${detail}`, or include the startup wording only when `trigger === "startup"`.

findings.title: Outer catch-all failure path has no test, so a silent discard there would stay green
findings.body: The goal says the tests must fail if a terminal result is silently discarded again. The failure paths tested are a step that throws (index.ts:410), a timeout (414), and a nonzero exit (421). No test reaches the outer `catch` at index.ts:445-447: neither `acquireLock` (e.g. an unwritable lock parent) nor `deps.snapshotExtensions` ever throws in this file, and the dependencies fixture's default snapshot never rejects. If line 447 went back to `return reportFailure(...)`, failures from an unwritable state dir or a throwing snapshot would be silent again, which is the defect issue 022 fixes, and every test would still pass. The same gap applies at startup in the other direction. The `disables startup only when PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE is zero` test (lines 303-311) passes a throwaway `fakeUi().ui` and never checks notifications. No startup test runs with `PI_OFFLINE`. So if the startup skip paths began nagging, contrary to the settled policy, nothing would catch it. Issue 022's scope asks for every terminal outcome to be covered, with a control case for the startup policy.
findings.fix: Add a test where `snapshotExtensions` rejects (or `lockPath` sits under a regular file so `mkdir` throws). Assert `status: "failed"` and exactly one `warning` notification, for both startup and manual. In the PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 startup case, also assert `notifications` stays empty.

findings.title: Nothing tests the outer-catch failure path, so it could go silent again unnoticed
findings.body: `index.ts:445-447` is the only failure exit outside the step loop. It is reached when `acquireLock` throws an error other than EEXIST (for example `mkdir` of the lock's parent directory fails with EACCES, or XDG_STATE_HOME points at a read-only filesystem), or when an injected `snapshotExtensions` rejects. It returns `finish(trigger, ui, reportFailure("Pi update failed without blocking startup: …"))`. `rg "without blocking" tests/` finds no matches: every new failure test reaches the step-level exits at lines 410, 414 and 421 through `exec`. If line 447 went back to a bare `return reportFailure(...)`, which is exactly the silent discard issue 022 fixed, the whole suite would still pass. A broken lock directory would then fail quietly on every startup and on `/brew-auto-update-now`. The goal says the tests must fail if a result were silently discarded again, and this exit has no such oracle. Nothing is broken today; the gap only lets a regression of this path through.
findings.fix: Add a test whose lock parent cannot be created (for example `lockPath` under a regular file, so `mkdir` fails with ENOTDIR) or whose `snapshotExtensions` rejects. Assert `status === "failed"` and one `warning` notification containing "failed without blocking startup", on both `startup` and `manual`.

findings.title: No test checks that startup stays silent on `skipped` outcomes (disabled/offline)
findings.body: The settled policy keeps startup silent on non-failure outcomes. Only contention, complete/up-to-date and unknown-extension-state have a startup silence assertion. The `PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0` test (lines 303-311) passes a throwaway `fakeUi().ui` and never looks at `notifications`, and no test runs `PI_OFFLINE=1` with the `startup` trigger. Several regressions would pass every test: `shouldNotify` starting to notify every `skipped` result, the `trigger === "manual"` gate being dropped, or the wrong trigger being passed to `finish`. A user who set `PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0`, or who runs offline, would then see 'Pi startup update is disabled.' or 'offline mode is active.' on every start, which is the nagging the policy rules out.
findings.fix: In the `PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0` test, keep the startup `fakeUi()` and assert `notifications` equals `[]`. Add a matching `startup` + `PI_OFFLINE=1` case that asserts `[]`.

findings.title: Issue 022 stays `open` after the fix lands, and its description is now stale
findings.body: This commit implements everything in 022's scope and records both decisions as settled, but the front matter still says `status: "open"` and there is no `## Resolution`. `python3 scripts/issues list` still defaults to open/in-progress issues, so agents using the repository-issues workflow will see a finished problem as active. The body also describes code this change removed or rewrote, for example: "`UpdateUi.setStatus` is declared but never called at all (the focused tests assert `statuses` stays empty)". `setStatus` and `statuses` are gone from `index.ts:22-24` and from the tests. The cited `tests/pi-brew-auto-update.test.ts:276-305` empty-notification assertions no longer exist either. Smaller slip: the level decision cites `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local`, but the file is `agents-local.ts`. It does use `"warning"` at line 53, so the convention claim itself holds. This may be left open on purpose until it is closed through the issue CLI, hence the moderate confidence.
findings.fix: Move 022 through `python3 scripts/issues` to `in-progress`, then close it as `done` with a Resolution pointing to #135. Or, if it stays open, say what remains (for example the red-state demonstration).

findings.title: Уведомление об ошибке захвата блокировки осталось без регрессионного теста
findings.body: Новый тест с исключением из deps.exec проверяет внутренний catch в index.ts:408–410. Ни один тест не достигает внешнего catch в index.ts:445–447, который теперь тоже должен уведомлять пользователя. Например, если родитель lockPath является обычным файлом, mkdir отклоняется до запуска команд. Возврат прежнего reportFailure без finish в этой ветке снова сделает такую ошибку незаметной при startup и ручном запуске, а существующие тесты этого не обнаружат. Это пробел в покрытии исправления ранее существовавшего дефекта.
findings.fix: Добавить в эту же suite случай с файлом вместо родительского каталога lockPath. Проверить результат failed, отсутствие запущенных команд и одно уведомление warning с причиной ошибки.

findings.title: Outer-catch failure branch's finish() call has no test; reverting it to a bare return stays green
findings.body: The goal requires that tests fail if a terminal result is silently discarded again. Six of the seven failure/terminal branches have a notification assertion (offline skip, contention, exec throw, timeout, non-zero exit, complete). The outer `catch` at line 445-447 is not covered. That branch catches errors from `acquireLock` (for example `mkdir(dirname(lockPath))` hitting EACCES/ENOSPC under `~/.local/state/pi`) and errors thrown by `deps.snapshotExtensions`. `rg 'without blocking' tests/pi-brew-auto-update.test.ts` finds nothing, and no test makes `acquireLock` or `snapshotExtensions` throw. Observed: changing line 447 back to `return reportFailure(...)` would not fail any test. Consequence (inferred): an unwritable lock directory breaks every startup, which is the 'persistent break' issue 022 exists to surface, and it would go silent again without any test noticing.
findings.fix: Add a test where `snapshotExtensions` throws, or where `lockPath`'s parent cannot be created (e.g. the parent path is a regular file). Assert `status: "failed"` and exactly one `warning` notification containing the thrown detail, for both startup and manual.

findings.title: Startup-silence policy for the disabled/offline skip results is never asserted
findings.body: The settled policy is that startup stays silent on non-failure outcomes. That silence is only asserted for complete/up-to-date, unknown-extension-state and contention. The `PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0` test (lines 303-310) checks `status` and `calls`, but it passes a throwaway `fakeUi().ui` and never looks at notifications. No test runs `PI_OFFLINE=1` with the `startup` trigger. Observed: if `shouldNotify` regressed to notify every `skipped` result, or someone dropped the `trigger === "manual"` gate for skips, every test would still pass. Consequence (inferred): a user who deliberately set `PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0`, or runs offline, would see 'Pi startup update is disabled.' / 'offline mode is active.' on every Pi start. That is the nagging the policy rules out.
findings.fix: In the PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 test, capture the startup `fakeUi()` and assert `notifications` equals `[]`. Add a matching startup case for PI_OFFLINE=1.

findings.title: Outer-catch failure message says 'without blocking startup' and is now shown to manual-command users
findings.body: Before this change the outer-catch result was returned and thrown away by both call sites, so its wording was never visible. Now `finish` sends it to `ui.notify` for both triggers. So when a user runs `/brew-auto-update-now` and lock acquisition fails (e.g. EACCES creating `~/.local/state/pi`), they get the warning 'Pi update failed without blocking startup: ...' for a run that had nothing to do with startup. The message is misleading but the impact is contained. The wrapped line is part of this diff, and the diff is what makes the text reachable.
findings.fix: Make the message trigger-neutral, e.g. `Pi update failed: ${detail}`, or build it from `trigger`.

findings.title: Stale-lock reclaim renames the lock path without checking which generation it holds
findings.body: This problem existed before the change. After a Pi crash, two new processes can both find the stale lock and both decide to reclaim it (lines 224-228). Process A renames the old directory, deletes it and takes a fresh lock. Process B then runs its rename on the same path and moves A's new lock aside, because `reclaimStaleLock` does not receive the identity of the owner it checked. B deletes A's lock and also acquires successfully, so both processes run the update sequence and the single-owner guarantee is broken. Unique stalePath names prevent collisions at the rename destination, but they do not stop the source directory from being swapped underneath.
findings.fix: Serialize reclaim and re-acquire behind a mutual-exclusion mechanism that every contender respects. Re-checking owner.json just before the rename does not close the race.

findings.title: Outer-catch failure path (index.ts:447) has no test, so the silent discard can come back unnoticed
findings.body: The goal requires the tests to go red if a terminal result is silently discarded again. Every `finish(...)` call site except one has a test that drives it: offline (382), contention (394), exec throw (410), timeout (417), non-zero exit (421) and complete (444). The outer `catch` at `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/brew-auto-update/index.ts:447` (`Pi update failed without blocking startup: ...`) is never reached by any test. No test makes `acquireLock` or `deps.snapshotExtensions` throw, and `rg 'without blocking'` finds nothing in the test file. Here is the edit that should turn the suite red but doesn't: revert line 447 to `return reportFailure(...)`, the exact pre-fix shape. The suite stays green, and lock-directory errors (EACCES/EROFS from `mkdir`/`writeFile` in `acquireLock`) go back to being silent at both startup and manual.
findings.fix: Add a test where `deps.snapshotExtensions` throws, or where `lockPath` sits under a non-directory file so `mkdir` throws. Run it with trigger `startup` and assert `notifications` equals one entry whose message starts with `Pi update failed without blocking startup:` at level `warning`.

findings.title: `finish(trigger, ui, …)` is threaded through eight return sites instead of wrapping the function once
findings.body: The goal's first condition is that no terminal result returns without passing through `finish`/`shouldNotify`. Right now that holds only by convention: each of the eight `return` statements in `runBrewAutoUpdate` has to remember `finish(trigger, ui, ...)`. The missing test above shows this can slip through unnoticed. One wrapper does the same job. Move the body into a helper that returns `{ result, installedUpdate }`, and make `runBrewAutoUpdate` call `finish` once on it. That removes seven duplicate `trigger, ui` threadings and makes the guarantee structural, so a future early return can't skip notification. Behavior stays the same except for ordering: the notify would run after `lock.release()` in the `finally` instead of before it. `release` can't throw in practice (`readOwner` and `removeLockDirectory(...).catch` both swallow errors), and `notify` is a synchronous UI call, so callers can't observe the reordering.
findings.fix: Rename the current body to an inner `runUpdateSteps(trigger, deps)` that returns `{ result, installedUpdate }` and has no `ui` argument. Make `runBrewAutoUpdate` do `const { result, installedUpdate } = await runUpdateSteps(trigger, deps); return finish(trigger, ui, result, installedUpdate);`.

findings.title: "startup reports a failure notification every time" runs once and has no red-making edit of its own
findings.body: This test calls `runBrewAutoUpdate("startup", …)` a single time, despite its name. Any edit that silences startup failures, such as removing `if (status === "failed") return true` from `shouldNotify`, also turns the next test red ("startup notifies again on a second consecutive failure", lines 386-400), which runs startup twice and checks both warnings. The message-content assertions don't add anything either: the message is built the same way for every trigger, and the manual non-zero-exit test (lines 337-349) already pins it. The test duplicates another test's contract without saying which one owns it, and its "every time" name claims coverage it doesn't give.
findings.fix: Delete it, or fold its message/level assertions into the two-run startup test so one test owns the startup-failure contract.

findings.title: Failure-notification assertions check `toContain` fragments where the exact message is known
findings.body: In the timeout test `deps.timeoutMs` is fixed at 300_000, so the full message is the known string `Homebrew metadata refresh timed out after 5 minutes.`. The test checks only the substrings `Homebrew metadata refresh` and `timed out`. If the minutes calculation at index.ts:417 broke (e.g. `0 minutes`, `NaN minutes` or `5000 minutes`), the test would still pass. The non-zero-exit and exec-throw tests (around lines 346-347, 365-366 and 380-381) do the same, even though their full messages are also deterministic.
findings.fix: Assert the whole notification, e.g. `expect(notifications).toEqual([{ message: "Homebrew metadata refresh timed out after 5 minutes.", level: "warning" }])`, and use exact literals in the other failure tests as well.

findings.title: Тест исключения не защищает уведомление во внешнем catch
findings.body: Новый тест вызывает исключение из deps.exec, которое перехватывает внутренний catch в index.ts:408. Ни один тест не достигает внешнего catch в index.ts:445. Если заменить его возврат на прежний reportFailure(...) без finish, существующие проверки этого не заметят. При ошибке создания каталога блокировки пользователь снова получит молчаливый отказ. Эта ветвь входит в заявленный контракт уведомления о каждом отказе.
findings.fix: Добавить сценарий ошибки acquireLock, например разместить обычный файл на месте родительского каталога lockPath. Проверить результат failed, отсутствие вызовов exec и одно уведомление warning с причиной ошибки.

findings.title: Проверка тайм-аута пропускает неверную длительность
findings.body: Для этого сценария timeoutMs равен 300000, но тест проверяет только наличие слов «timed out». Замена вычисления длительности в index.ts:417 на 0 оставит эти проверки успешными, хотя пользователь увидит неверное сообщение «timed out after 0 minutes». Окружающий текст в данном сценарии полностью определён.
findings.fix: Проверять уведомление целиком: сообщение «Homebrew metadata refresh timed out after 5 minutes.» и уровень warning.

findings.title: No evidence was provided that the new notification tests fail against the old silent implementation
findings.body: No run of the changed notification tests against the previous, notification-suppressing implementation was provided, and the task document explicitly requires that red-state confirmation. From the available material, there is no proof that the tests catch the original regression. This is a gap in the evidence, not a claim that the author never ran the checks. Running the same suite before and after the fix (red before, green after) would settle it.

findings.title: The outer catch's failure notification has no test, so it could go silent again without any test failing
findings.body:
`runBrewAutoUpdate` has one terminal failure path that no test reaches: the outer `catch` at index.ts:445-447, which returns `finish(trigger, ui, reportFailure("Pi update failed without blocking startup: …"))`. Two things reach it:
- `acquireLock` throwing, e.g. `mkdir(dirname(lockPath))` failing with EACCES or ENOTDIR on `~/.local/state/pi`, or `writeFile` of the owner file failing.
- An injected `snapshotExtensions` that rejects.

No test uses either. `rg 'without blocking' tests/` finds nothing. If that line went back to `return reportFailure(...)`, which is the exact pre-fix shape, every test would still pass. A broken lock directory would then fail silently on every startup and on every manual run. That is the defect issue 022 exists to fix, and the goal requires that "the tests would fail if a result were silently discarded again".

A smaller gap of the same kind: nothing checks that the manual command reports the `complete` result "Pi package update completed; extension changes could not be verified." The test at :275 checks only that startup stays silent there. Issue 022's scope asks the tests to "require the manual command to report every terminal outcome".
