findings.fix: Add a manual-trigger test where `lockPath` sits under a regular file (so `mkdir` throws ENOTDIR), or where `snapshotExtensions` rejects. Assert `status: "failed"` and exactly one `warning` notification containing the error detail. Add a matching startup case, and a manual-trigger version of the "could not be verified" test that asserts an `info` notification.

findings.title: The manual command now shows "failed without blocking startup", which is wrong for a command run mid-session
findings.body: The outer catch builds its message as `Pi update failed without blocking startup: ${detail}`, whatever the trigger. Before this change, manual results were thrown away, so a user never saw this string. Now `shouldNotify` always returns true for `failed`, so `/brew-auto-update-now` shows it as a warning. Example: a manual run fails because the lock directory cannot be created. The user, mid-session, reads that the update failed "without blocking startup", which suggests a startup run they did not start. The string itself is old, but this change is what makes it visible to manual users.
findings.fix: Make the prefix depend on the trigger, e.g. `trigger === "startup" ? "Pi update failed without blocking startup" : "Pi update failed"`, or drop the startup wording.

findings.title: The recorded decision cites a path that does not exist (`extensions/agents-local`)
findings.body: The settled decision justifies the `warning` level as "the convention already used by `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local`". Nothing exists at that path. The extension is the single file `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local.ts`, which calls `ctx.ui.notify(warning, "warning")` at line 53. Anyone checking the cited convention will not find it at the stated path, although the convention itself is real.
findings.fix: Change the path to `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local.ts`.

findings.title: Nothing asserts that startup stays silent for `skipped` results (PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 / PI_OFFLINE)
findings.body: The settled policy says startup stays silent on non-failure outcomes. Startup silence is asserted for up-to-date, unknown-extension and contended results, but not for the two `skipped` exits, which now go through `finish` (index.ts:382, 386). The "disables startup only when PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE is zero" test (lines 303-311) passes a throwaway `fakeUi().ui` and never checks notifications. The PI_OFFLINE test runs only with the manual trigger. If `shouldNotify` began reporting `skipped` at startup, users would see "Pi startup update is disabled." or "offline mode is active" on every Pi start, and no test would fail. Related gap: the only test of the `complete`/"could not be verified" outcome was switched from manual to startup (line 278), so the manual command's report of that result is no longer asserted.
findings.fix: In the PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 test, keep the startup `fakeUi()` and assert `notifications` equals `[]`. Add a startup PI_OFFLINE case that asserts `[]`, with the manual PI_OFFLINE test as the control. Keep a manual-trigger assertion for the "could not be verified" message.

findings.title: Recorded decision cites a non-existent path for the agents-local warning convention
findings.body: The settled decision justifies the `warning` level by citing `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local`. That path does not exist. The extension is the single file `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local.ts`, where `notifyWarningsOnce` calls `ctx.ui.notify(warning, "warning")` at line 53. The convention is real, but a reader or agent following the reference reaches a missing path.
findings.fix: Change the reference to `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local.ts` (optionally `:53`).

findings.title: Recorded decision cites a non-existent path `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local` as the warning-level authority
findings.body: The settled-decision text justifies the `warning` level by pointing at `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local`, but no such directory exists; the extension is the single file `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local.ts` (its `notifyWarningsOnce` calls `ctx.ui.notify(warning, "warning")` at line 53). A reader following the citation to verify the convention finds nothing at that path. Human-facing prose, so contained impact; the convention it cites is real.
findings.fix: Change the reference to `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local.ts` (optionally `:53`).

findings.title: No test covers the outer-catch failure path (index.ts:445-447), so it could go silent again without any test failing
findings.body: `runBrewAutoUpdate` sends every terminal result through `finish`. The new tests check notifications on the inner failure returns (exec throws, killed, nonzero exit), but none reaches the outer `catch` at index.ts:445-447. That branch handles errors from `acquireLock` and from a throwing `deps.snapshotExtensions()`. Examples are `mkdir` of the lock parent failing with EACCES or ENOTDIR (XDG_STATE_HOME read-only or pointing at a file) and `rename`/`rmdir` errors during stale-lock reclaim. The only throwing fixture is `exec`, and the inner catch at line 410 handles it first. Changing line 447 back to `return reportFailure(...)` would leave the suite green, and a broken lock directory would again fail silently on every startup and on the manual command. The goal says the tests must fail if a result is ever silently discarded again, and this path breaks that.
findings.fix: Add a case next to "notifies a manual caller when the update command itself throws" that makes lock acquisition throw. For example, put a regular file at `dirname(deps.lockPath)` so mkdir fails with ENOTDIR, or make `snapshotExtensions` throw. For both startup and manual triggers, assert `status: "failed"`, that no commands ran, and exactly one `warning` notification containing the thrown detail.

findings.title: Issue 022 is still `status: "open"` after the PR that fixes it, and the new issue 007 says 022 is fixed
findings.body: This change implements the fix described in issue 022 and rewrites its "Open decisions" as settled. The frontmatter still says `status: "open"`. The new issue 2026-09-02-007 starts with "Repository issue 2026-08-21-022 fixed home/dot_pi/.../index.ts so every terminal update result ... is routed through ui.notify". The two documents now disagree. `scripts/issues` lists open/in-progress issues by default (scripts/issues:230), so an agent using the repository-issues workflow is pointed at work this PR already did. It may pick up 022 and redo or "fix" it.
findings.fix: Move 022 through `python3 scripts/issues` to `done` with a resolution that points to this PR and to follow-up 007, or reword 007 so it does not call 022 fixed while 022 is still open.

findings.title: Manual command now shows "Pi update failed without blocking startup" to a user who ran `/brew-auto-update-now`
findings.body: The outer-catch message was written for the startup path. Before this change it was never shown to anyone. Now `finish` notifies on every failure, manual trigger included. A user whose `/brew-auto-update-now` run fails during lock acquisition or snapshot (for example EACCES creating the state directory) sees a `warning` saying "Pi update failed without blocking startup: ...", although no startup happened. The string is old, but this change is what makes users see it. The impact is a misleading message only.
findings.fix: Remove the startup wording (e.g. `Pi update failed: ${detail}`) or pick the suffix based on `trigger`.

findings.title: Nothing asserts that startup stays silent for `skipped` results (PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 / PI_OFFLINE)
findings.body: The settled policy says startup stays silent on non-failure outcomes. The only startup-silence controls cover `complete` (no update / unknown state) and `contended`. The "disables startup only when PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE is zero" test throws away its `fakeUi()` notifications, and the PI_OFFLINE test runs only with `manual`. Suppose `shouldNotify` were changed to report `skipped` at startup, or `finish` were called with `"manual"` on the two early returns. A user who disabled the updater would then get "Pi startup update is disabled." on every Pi start, and no test would fail.
findings.fix: In the PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 test, keep the startup `fakeUi()` and assert `notifications` equals `[]` (and do the same for a startup PI_OFFLINE case), with the manual PI_OFFLINE test as the control.

findings.title: Уведомление об ошибке получения блокировки осталось без регрессионного теста
findings.body: Тест с исключением из deps.exec проверяет внутренний catch, но ни один тест не достигает внешнего catch в index.ts:445–447. Например, если родитель lockPath является обычным файлом, acquireLock завершится ошибкой до запуска команд. Если убрать finish из внешнего catch, такой сбой снова станет невидимым пользователю, а существующие тесты этого не обнаружат. Этот пробел относится к новому уведомлению, добавленному данным изменением.
findings.fix: Добавить в этот suite сценарий с обычным файлом вместо каталога блокировки. Проверить результат failed, отсутствие запущенных команд и одно уведомление warning с причиной ошибки.

findings.title: Outer-catch failure path routes through finish but no test exercises it, so reverting it stays green
findings.body: The outer `catch` at index.ts:445-447 is the only route for failures from lock acquisition and stale-lock reclaim, and from a throwing `snapshotExtensions`. Two examples: `mkdir(dirname(lockPath))` hitting EACCES because XDG_STATE_HOME is read-only, or `removeLockDirectory` hitting ENOTEMPTY during reclaim. No test reaches this branch. `rg 'without blocking' tests/` finds nothing. Every failure test in tests/pi-brew-auto-update.test.ts injects an `exec` that returns nonzero, returns killed, or throws, and those all hit the inner returns at 410/417/421. So if line 447 went back to `return reportFailure(...)`, the suite would still pass and a broken lock directory would again fail silently at every startup. The goal names this exact case: "the tests would fail if a result were silently discarded again". What I observed: the branch has no coverage. What follows: the regression would go undetected. The code is correct today.
findings.fix: Add a test whose deps make lock acquisition throw, for example a `lockPath` whose parent is an existing regular file, or a `snapshotExtensions` that throws. Assert `status === "failed"` and one `warning` notification, for both startup and manual triggers.

findings.title: Registration test passes a fake ctx.ui to session_start but never asserts that the startup failure reaches it
findings.body: In production, `session_start` passes `ctx.ui` to `runBrewAutoUpdate`. The registration test (starting at line 491) builds `ctx = { ui: fakeUi().ui }` at line 514 and drives a startup run that fails with code 1 "stop". It calls `finishExec()` at line 521 and ends without waiting for the run to settle or checking notifications. The startup-failure tests call `runBrewAutoUpdate` directly with their own `ui`, so nothing proves that a startup failure reaches the UI Pi hands to the handler. Issue 2026-09-01-004 says failure-notification behaviour stays under 2026-08-21-022, which this change implements. A regression in the two-line handler wiring is unlikely but would go undetected.
findings.fix: Keep the `notifications` array from `fakeUi()` in the registration test. Wait for the background run to settle, for example by polling until notifications has length 1, then assert one `warning` notification containing "Homebrew metadata refresh".

findings.title: Startup silence on skipped outcomes (PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0, PI_OFFLINE=1) is not asserted
findings.body: Policy says startup stays silent on non-failure outcomes. Silence is asserted for startup up-to-date, unknown-extension and contended, but not for the two `skipped` exits. The "disables startup only when PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE is zero" test (lines 303-311) passes a throwaway `fakeUi().ui` and checks only status and calls. The PI_OFFLINE test runs only the manual trigger. Now that both exits go through `finish` (index.ts:382,386), a change to `shouldNotify` that dropped the startup guard for `skipped` would pass every test. That regression would make every startup show "Pi startup update is disabled." or "offline mode is active". This is the nagging the policy is meant to prevent.
findings.fix: In the disable test, keep the startup `notifications` and assert it is `[]`. Add a startup PI_OFFLINE case that asserts `[]` as well, next to the existing manual case.

findings.title: Manual command now shows the user "Pi update failed without blocking startup"
findings.body: The outer-catch message was written for the startup path. Before this change no result was ever surfaced, so the wording never reached a user. Now `finish` notifies on every failure, including the manual trigger. If `/brew-auto-update-now` fails during lock acquisition (for example EACCES creating the state directory), the user sees "Pi update failed without blocking startup: …" even though no startup happened. The change is what makes this reachable. The impact is only a misleading message.
findings.fix: Make the prefix depend on the trigger. For example, use "Pi update failed: …" for manual runs and keep the "without blocking startup" wording for startup only.

findings.title: Outer-catch failure path has no test, so a silent discard there would stay green
findings.body: The goal requires the tests to fail if any terminal result is silently discarded again. Seven of the eight `finish(...)` sites are covered: offline/manual, contended/manual, exec throws, killed, nonzero exit, complete/manual and complete/startup. The catch-all at index.ts:447 is not. It reports failures from `acquireLock` (for example `mkdir` EACCES/ENOTDIR on `~/.local/state/pi`, or a `rename`/`rmdir` error while reclaiming a stale lock) and from a throwing `snapshotExtensions`. A test that goes red would need an edit like `return reportFailure(`Pi update failed without blocking startup: ${detail}`);` with `finish` removed. No test in tests/pi-brew-auto-update.test.ts reaches this branch: the only throwing fixture is `exec`, and line 410 catches that first. So a broken lock directory, which is a persistent failure that recurs on every startup, could go silent again with the suite still green. That is the defect issue 022 exists to prevent.
findings.fix: Add a test that makes `acquireLock` throw. For example, put a regular file at `dirname(deps.lockPath)` so `mkdir` fails with ENOTDIR. Run it with trigger "startup" and assert `status` is "failed" before checking for exactly one `warning` notification whose message starts with "Pi update failed without blocking startup:".

findings.title: Eight hand-threaded finish(trigger, ui, …) returns where one exit point would make the invariant structural
findings.body: `runBrewAutoUpdate` routes every terminal result through `finish` by repeating `return finish(trigger, ui, …)` at eight separate returns (lines 382, 386, 394, 410, 414, 421, 444, 447). The goal's correctness condition, that no terminal result skips finish/shouldNotify, holds only by convention. Any future `return { status: … }` added to the body would silently bring the original bug back. A smaller shape: move the current body into an inner function that returns `{ result, installedUpdate }` (or just the result plus the boolean), then call `finish(trigger, ui, …)` once in `runBrewAutoUpdate`. That removes seven duplicated call sites and the threaded `trigger, ui` arguments. The outputs, levels and the set of notified outcomes stay the same. The only ordering change is that `notify` would run after `lock.release()` rather than before. `release` cannot throw (`readOwner` swallows errors and `removeLockDirectory` is `.catch`ed), so the user can't observe the difference.
findings.fix: Extract the body into `attemptUpdate(trigger, deps): Promise<{ result: UpdateResult; installedUpdate: boolean }>` and have `runBrewAutoUpdate` return `finish(trigger, ui, outcome.result, outcome.installedUpdate)` once.

findings.title: Тест исключения не покрывает уведомление при ошибке захвата блокировки
findings.body: Новый тест вызывает исключение из deps.exec и проверяет только внутренний catch. Ошибка acquireLock, например ENOTDIR при наличии обычного файла вместо родительского каталога lockPath, попадает во внешний catch в index.ts:445–447. Если там заменить return finish(...) на return reportFailure(...), тесты продолжат проходить, хотя ошибка снова станет невидимой пользователю. Эта ветка уведомления добавлена изменением, но отдельного проверяемого сценария для неё нет.
findings.fix: Добавить сценарий с обычным файлом вместо родительского каталога lockPath. Проверить failed и одно уведомление warning для startup и manual.

findings.title: Were the new notification tests shown to fail against the original silent behavior?
findings.body: The materials include no run of the new notification checks against the original silent behavior. So the red → green transition required by docs/solutions/design-patterns/semantic-regression-tests-over-source-shape.md is unconfirmed. The question is whether the author ran the tests against the pre-fix code and saw them fail on the missing notification. This flags missing evidence; it does not claim the tests were never run.

findings.title: Outer-catch failure path (e.g. lock acquisition throws) has no notification test
findings.body: The goal says the tests must fail if a terminal result is silently discarded again. The new tests cover step-level failures (timeout, nonzero exit, exec throw) but nothing drives the outer `catch` in `runBrewAutoUpdate` (index.ts ~446-448). That path handles `acquireLock` or `snapshotExtensions` throwing, for example an unwritable lock directory. If that `finish(...)` were reverted to a bare `reportFailure(...)` return, the suite would stay green and the failure would be silent again. A fixture whose `lockPath` parent is a regular file, or a `snapshotExtensions` that throws, with a `warning` notification assertion, would close the gap. Startup-trigger skipped (`PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0` and `PI_OFFLINE`) also has no assertion that notifications stay empty.
findings.fix: Add a test where `acquireLock` or `snapshotExtensions` throws. Assert exactly one `warning` notification containing 'Pi update failed without blocking startup', and add a startup-trigger skipped case asserting no notifications.

findings.title: Issue 022 stays `status: "open"` and its problem narrative is unchanged after the fix
findings.body: The change implements the fix and records the settled decisions, but the front matter still says `status: "open"`. The body still describes the silent-failure defect and `setStatus` as present-tense facts (lines ~19-30). The repo has 108 issues marked `done`, so the lifecycle has a closing state. The decision text also cites 'the convention already used by `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local`' for `warning`. That path is actually the file `agents-local.ts`, which does call `ctx.ui.notify(warning, "warning")`, so the claim itself holds. This is documentation only and may be intentional if closing is a separate step.
findings.fix: Mark the issue done through `scripts/issues`, or note in the body that the defect is resolved by this change.

findings.title: Update failures stay invisible in headless (`pi -p` / `--mode json`) mode
findings.body: In headless mode finish's only channel is ui.notify. print-mode.js calls bindExtensions without a uiContext, so runner.js substitutes noOpUIContext, whose notify does nothing. The session_start handler also discards the returned UpdateResult. A failed `brew update` therefore reaches neither the output nor the session state. The reviewer marked this pre-existing and already recorded in the new follow-up issue 2026-09-02-007.
findings.fix: Add a diagnostic channel for headless mode, for example writing the result to stderr.

findings.title: No test reaches the outer catch in runBrewAutoUpdate, so dropping its finish() would stay green
findings.body: No test reaches the outer catch in runBrewAutoUpdate (home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/brew-auto-update/index.ts:445-447, 'Pi update failed without blocking startup: ...'). The failure tests (timeout, nonzero exit, exec throws) all make the first step's exec fail, and the inner catch handles those (index.ts:407-420). This path covers acquireLock throwing (for example mkdir EACCES, or a regular file where the lock directory's parent should be), snapshotExtensions rejecting, and lock-write errors. If its finish() reverted to a bare reportFailure, the issue-022 silent-failure defect would come back with the suite still green. Two related gaps are also real: no manual-trigger test covers the info notification for 'extension changes could not be verified', and the PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 startup skip test (tests:303-311) never checks that notifications stay empty. The production code is correct today; this is missing regression coverage.
findings.fix: Add a test where acquireLock throws, for example with lockPath's parent as a regular file, or where snapshotExtensions throws. Assert status failed, no exec calls, and exactly one `warning` notification containing 'Pi update failed without blocking startup', for both startup and manual triggers. Keep a nearby success control. Optionally add a manual-trigger unknown-extension-state case that expects `info`, plus startup skip cases that expect no notifications.

findings.title: No test covers the outer catch path, so dropping its finish() would still pass
findings.body: The goal requires that the tests fail if a terminal result is silently discarded again. Of the six `finish` call sites in `runBrewAutoUpdate`, the outer `catch` at index.ts:445-447 ("Pi update failed without blocking startup") has no test. Neither does the startup skip path for `PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0` (index.ts:384-387), whose silence is part of the policy. The new "update command itself throws" test throws from `deps.exec`, which the inner try/catch at index.ts:406-411 handles. If `acquireLock` rejected (for example a `mkdir` failure on the lock directory) and that catch reverted to a bare `return reportFailure(...)`, every test would still pass and a failure would go silent again.
findings.fix: Add a test where `lockPath` sits under a file so that `mkdir` rejects. Assert that startup produces one warning notification containing "Pi update failed without blocking startup". Add a startup test for `PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0` that expects no notifications.

findings.title: Issue 022 left open and unresolved after the change that fixes it
findings.body: PR #135 implements issue 022's scope: every terminal result goes through finish/shouldNotify, and the tests were updated. But the issue's front matter still says `status: "open"`, with no `closed:` date and no `## Resolution` section. In this repo, fix PRs normally close their issue in the same commit. For example, 243fbd5 (#125) set `status: "done"`, added `closed:`, and appended a Resolution section. The new follow-up issue 007 even states that 022 'fixed' the updater. So `scripts/issues list` will report 022 as open work, which misleads a maintainer. The Resolution should also mention two diff details the issue doesn't record: `UpdateUi.setStatus` was removed (it was never called, so spec 028's 'UI status identifies the active step' stays unimplemented), and the contended-lock message was reworded. Separately, the 'Open decisions' text calls `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local` a directory, but it is the file `agents-local.ts`. (The unverified-extension `complete` result was already silent at startup before this change, so that is not a new behaviour.)
findings.fix: Close 022 through `python3 scripts/issues close`, so it gets status done, a closed date and a Resolution section noting the setStatus removal. Correct the path to `home/dot_pi/agent/extensions/agents-local.ts`.

findings.title: Two terminal paths routed through finish() have no notification assertion, so silently discarding them again would stay green
findings.body: The goal is that no terminal result bypasses finish/shouldNotify and that the tests fail if a result is silently discarded again. Two such paths are not covered. (1) The outer `catch` in runBrewAutoUpdate (index.ts:445-447, `Pi update failed without blocking startup: ...`) is reached when acquireLock throws, for example from mkdir or reclaimStaleLock. No test makes acquireLock throw, so changing that line back to `return reportFailure(...)` would pass every test. That is exactly the original defect. The throwing-exec test only exercises the inner catch at index.ts:410. (2) The manual command's `complete` outcome with an unknown extension state ("extension changes could not be verified") is no longer asserted at all. The test was switched from `manual` to `startup`, so it only checks silence. The manual-notifies-info side of that message is untested. Add a test with an unwritable or file-blocked lockPath that expects a `warning` notification for both triggers. Add a manual-trigger case for the unknown-snapshot message.
findings.fix: Add a test where acquireLock throws (for example lockPath's parent is a regular file) and assert one `warning` notification for startup and for manual. Add a manual-trigger variant of the unknown-extension-state test expecting an `info` notification.

findings.title: Не защищено уведомление об ошибке получения блокировки
findings.body: Тест с исключением из deps.exec достигает внутреннего catch, а внешний catch в index.ts:445–447 не проверяется ни одним сценарием. Например, обычный файл вместо родительского каталога lockPath вызывает ошибку ещё до запуска команды. Если во внешнем catch вернуть reportFailure напрямую, все эти тесты сохранят прежний результат, хотя пользователь снова не получит уведомления о сбое при каждом запуске. Сам обработчик существовал раньше; его новое уведомление осталось без регрессионной защиты.
findings.fix: Добавить сюда сценарий с файлом вместо родительского каталога блокировки. Проверить результат failed, отсутствие вызовов exec и одно уведомление warning с причиной ошибки.

findings.title: Outer catch's finish() and the manual unknown-extension-state notification have no test
findings.body: Several of the new failure tests each pin one return site: step-1 throw, step-1 killed, and step-1 nonzero. The `catch` at index.ts:445-447 has no test. It wraps `acquireLock` errors, `deps.snapshotExtensions` rejections and lock-write errors. Revert that line to `return reportFailure(...)` and every test still passes. The goal says the tests must fail if a result is silently discarded again, so that path is a gap. Separately, the 'complete, extension changes could not be verified' result at index.ts:439-444 is only tested at startup, where it is silent. The manual notification for it, at `info` level, is never asserted. Nothing in the test file drives a failure from step 2 or 3. All of them rely on step 1. These are untested paths, not a wrong assertion. Each remaining `finish` call is protected only by review, not by an oracle.
findings.fix: Add a test whose `snapshotExtensions` or `acquireLock` setup throws and assert a `warning` notification with 'Pi update failed without blocking startup'. Add a manual-trigger case with `snapshotExtensions: async () => undefined` that asserts the 'could not be verified' info notification.

findings.title: Stale-owner check is not tied to the directory that gets renamed, so two claimants can both reclaim
findings.body: After the owner crashes, two Pi processes can read the same stale owner.json. A renames the old lock, creates a new one, and starts updating. B then continues reclaimStaleLock on its earlier read, renames the current directory at the same path (A's new lock), and also starts updating. This breaks the single-updater requirement. The recovery tests use only one claimant. The reviewer said this existed before the change and found it by reasoning, without running anything.
findings.fix: Serialize recovery with a separate atomic lock and re-check the owner after acquiring it, before renaming the directory.

findings.title: Outer catch path of runBrewAutoUpdate has no notification test
findings.body: The goal says no terminal result may bypass finish/shouldNotify and that the tests must fail if a result is silently discarded again. Two terminal branches have no test that asserts a notification. The first is the outer `catch` in `index.ts` (~line 447), which handles a failure in `acquireLock` such as an mkdir EACCES. The second is the manual `complete` branch with `extensionChangeUnknown`, whose message is 'extension changes could not be verified'. The only test that reaches the unknown-state branch runs it at startup and asserts silence. If someone changes the outer catch back to `return reportFailure(...)`, every test stays green and the original silent-failure defect returns on that path. A manual-trigger test where `deps.lockPath` is unusable (e.g. a file in place of the parent directory) would pin it.
findings.fix: Add a test that makes acquireLock throw (for example by pointing lockPath under a regular file) and asserts one `warning` notification with 'Pi update failed without blocking startup'. Optionally add a manual-trigger test for the unknown-extension-state message.

findings.title: Follow-up issue text has a garbled identifier
findings.body: The sentence reads 'resolves to the package's ., where notify is a literal no-op'. The `noOpUIContext` identifier was lost, probably stripped as a backtick span. The key claim about the Pi SDK behaviour is therefore unnamed and cannot be checked from the issue. The same paragraph also cites file names and function names without code formatting, so it is hard to scan.
findings.fix: Restore the identifier: 'resolves to the package's `noOpUIContext`, where notify is a literal no-op'.

findings.title: Проверка исключения не покрывает внешний обработчик ошибок
findings.body: Новый тест вызывает исключение из deps.exec, которое перехватывает внутренний catch. Ни один тест не вызывает внешний catch в runBrewAutoUpdate, например через ошибку создания каталога блокировки. Если в index.ts:447 убрать finish и вернуть reportFailure напрямую, все проверки уведомлений останутся зелёными, а пользователь снова не увидит ошибку блокировки. Для нового требования об уведомлении на каждом пути завершения эта ветка остаётся непроверенной.
findings.fix: Добавить сценарий, где родитель lockPath является обычным файлом, и проверить failed и одно предупреждение через UI. Рядом сохранить успешный контроль с доступным каталогом.

findings.title: Timeout notification test accepts a wrong duration in the message
findings.body: timeoutMs is fixed at 300000, but the test checks only the substring 'timed out'. If the production message's divisor changed from 60000 to 1000, users would see '300 minutes' instead of '5 minutes' and the test would stay green. The missing duration check predates this change, but this change modified the test to assert the user-visible notification.
findings.fix: Assert the whole notification: message 'Homebrew metadata refresh timed out after 5 minutes.' at level warning.

findings.title: Was the red run against the old silent behaviour performed?
findings.body: The origin issue requires showing that the changed notification tests fail against the old silent behaviour, and no such result was provided. On reading, the tests look sensitive to removed notifications, but their sensitivity is unconfirmed. The author can settle this by giving the focused test output against the old code (expected failures) and against the reviewed version.

findings.title: Failure-notification tests cannot detect a dropped finish() on the outer catch or on later steps
findings.body: Every failure test (timeout, nonzero exit, thrown exec) forces the first step, 'Homebrew metadata refresh', to fail. The outer `catch` in runBrewAutoUpdate (index.ts:445-447) is reached when acquireLock or snapshotExtensions throws, and no test reaches it. The killed, nonzero and thrown branches for steps 2 and 3 are also never exercised. If someone changes the outer catch to `return reportFailure(...)` without `finish`, the whole suite stays green. That is the 'result silently discarded again' regression the goal says the tests must catch. Separately, the silent-at-startup skip cases (PI_OFFLINE=1 and PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0 with trigger 'startup') are not asserted. The disabled-startup test discards its `fakeUi()` notifications, and the offline test only covers the manual trigger.
findings.fix: Add a test where `snapshotExtensions` or the lock path throws and assert one 'warning' notification, plus a failure in the third step. Also assert empty notifications for startup with PI_OFFLINE and with PI_BREW_AUTO_UPDATE=0.

findings.title: Issue text still describes setStatus as declared, but the change removes it; status stays 'open'
findings.body: The issue says `UpdateUi.setStatus` is declared but never called. This change deletes that member from `UpdateUi`, and the issue records neither the deletion nor the resolution. The front-matter `status` remains "open" even though the Open decisions section now says everything is settled and the code implements them.
findings.fix: Note the setStatus removal and update the status once the fix lands.

findings.title: `code test --json` output changed shape from `{version:{…}}` to the bare version object
findings.body: Before this change, `code test --json` printed `JSON.stringify(result)`, which is the full `run-source-tree-tests` output `{ "version": { …, "testsStatus": … } }`. Every `code test` path now goes through `renderTestVersion`, which prints `JSON.stringify(version)`. That covers `--no-wait`, an immediate verdict, the wait result, the timeout and the refusal. The top-level `version` key is gone. A script or agent that reads `.version.testsStatus` from `code test --json` now gets `undefined`. The goal does not mention this shape change and no doc records it. New `code status --json` uses the bare shape too, so the two verbs agree, but the existing verb's output changed without notice. No in-repo consumer was found, so the impact is contained.
findings.fix: Keep the old envelope for `code test --json`, i.e. print `{ version }`, or record the new shape in the plugin README/MANUAL.

findings.title: An expired sign-in during a verdict read is reported as "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet"
findings.body: `isVerdictReadRefusal` counts any 401/403 as an old-engine refusal. That includes the wrapped 401 inside `rejectedCredentialError`, and also the platform-token refresh failure 'The Membrane sign-in expired and could not be refreshed'. Take a sessionless `code status --wait` or `code test` whose platform sign-in expires or is revoked mid-wait, so the refresh fails. The command exits 2 with `pending — this engine cannot answer the verdict yet` or `this engine cannot answer the verdict yet`. The real cause and the 'Sign in again' instruction are dropped. Exit 2 means 'still pending', so an agent following the documented exit codes will keep retrying `code status`, which fails the same way. It never learns it has to re-authenticate. A real 403 from a current engine, for example a permission denial, is also reported as an engine-version gap.
findings.fix: Treat only a 403 scope/permission refusal as the old-engine case. Let credential-expiry errors (`rejectedCredentialError`, the sign-in-expired refresh error) propagate to runCode's catch with their own message and exit 1.

findings.title: An expired or rejected sign-in is reported as "this engine cannot answer the verdict yet" (exit 2)
findings.body:
`isVerdictReadRefusal` treats every 401 and 403 anywhere in the cause chain, plus any error whose message matches /sign-in expired/i, as an old engine refusing the verdict read. Real credential failures take the same path.

Trace for `membrane-operator code status --workspace acme` with a dead refresh token:
1. The access gate only checks that a credential file exists locally (cli.ts:134).
2. The first network call is `list-source-tree-versions` on the platform token. It returns 401.
3. `callWithPlatformToken` calls `refreshAfterRejection`, which throws 'The Membrane sign-in expired and could not be refreshed. Sign in again.' (platform-token.ts:72).
4. The regex matches, so `codeStatus` prints 'this engine cannot answer the verdict yet' and exits 2 (code.ts:705-707). `waitForVersion` (line 665) does the same.

A refresh that succeeds but is rejected again ends the same way: `rejectedCredentialError` wraps an ApiError 401 as its `cause`, and the classifier walks into `error.cause`. A refused attached-session token (403 after `remintAfterRefusal`) does too. So does a real permission-denial 403 from a current engine.

In this verb's contract, exit 2 means 'still pending'. An agent with a dead sign-in is told to wait or retry rather than to sign in again, and every retry fails the same way. Before this change, the same failure printed the sign-in remedy through `runCode`'s catch. `code test` is mostly shielded because its queue call fails first, with the correct message and exit 1. Sessionless `code status --wait` and verdict reads mid-wait are affected.

The regex also ties behaviour to human-facing message text in another module. Rewording that message silently changes the exit code.
findings.fix: Treat only the refusal an old engine actually returns as "cannot answer": the 403 scope-mismatch AccessDenied. Let 401s and the credential errors from `callWithPlatformToken` / `refreshAfterRejection` (`rejectedCredentialError`, the sign-in-expired error) propagate to `runCode`'s catch, so the sign-in remedy is printed with exit 1. At minimum, drop the `/sign-in expired/` match and the `error.cause` recursion over `rejectedCredentialError`.

findings.title: Bare symbol in the error channel next to a tagged error forces `as` casts; the failure wrapper is pasted three times
findings.body:
`VERDICT_READ_TIMED_OUT` is a plain `unique symbol` used as an Effect failure beside the `VerdictReadFailed` tagged error. You cannot `catchTag` on it, so each consumer:
- matches the whole effect into `{ok, error}`,
- compares the error by identity,
- casts back with `as VerdictReadError` (lines 423, 432, 665, 674, 705).

`verdictReadCause` exists only to unwrap this mixed union.

The `new VerdictReadFailed({ cause, message: cause instanceof Error ? cause.message : String(cause) })` mapper is copied at lines 520, 604 and 632. The first copy wraps the queue call (`run-source-tree-tests`) in codeTest, so a queue failure is labelled a verdict-read failure.

The plugin already uses `Data.TaggedError` here, and the repo's Effect guidance (engine/api/CLAUDE.md → Errors) makes every expected failure a tagged error. A `Data.TaggedError('VerdictReadTimedOut')` plus one shared `catch` function would remove the casts and the copies.
findings.fix: Replace the symbol with `class VerdictReadTimedOut extends Data.TaggedError('VerdictReadTimedOut')`. Recover with `Effect.catchTag`/`catchTags` and drop the `as VerdictReadError` casts and `verdictReadCause`. Hoist the tryPromise `catch` mapper into one function, and give the queue call its own error or plain `Effect.tryPromise` without the verdict-read name.

findings.title: No-op `catchTag` that re-fails with the same error, followed by a type cast
findings.body: In `readUntilDeadline`, `.pipe(Effect.catchTag('VerdictReadFailed', (error) => Effect.fail(error)))` catches the tagged error and fails with the same value. It changes neither behaviour nor type. The `as Effect.Effect<T, VerdictReadError>` cast after it is what actually sets the type. The `catchTag` is dead code that reads as if it recovers from something.
findings.fix: Delete the `.pipe(Effect.catchTag(...))`. Better, type the race properly once the timeout is a tagged error, so the cast is not needed either.

findings.title: The new verdict polling loop breaks the repo's required Effect rules (hand-rolled while + sleep instead of Effect.repeat/Schedule)
findings.body: For a pending version, the new `while` loop calls `waitForNextPoll`, which runs `Effect.sleep` (line 579). The rule in .claude/skills/effect-best-practices/SKILL.md:21 requires `Effect.repeat` with `Schedule.spaced` for this kind of polling, and lines 34–36 forbid new exceptions without a separate decision. The implementation brings back hand-written schedule and deadline management. Moving the sleep into a helper gets past the syntactic check but does not remove the violation.
findings.fix: Express the polling with Effect.repeat and a Schedule, and the wait bound with Effect.timeoutOrElse, keeping HTTP request cancellation.

findings.title: The follow-up command drops quoting, so a workspace name with spaces is lost
findings.body: After a timeout on a call with `--workspace 'Acme Inc'`, the printed follow-up command contains `--workspace Acme Inc` without quotes. Running it, the CLI receives workspace=Acme and cannot continue waiting in the original workspace. Full names are supported in client/operator-scope.ts:102–104. The package already has `shellQuote` in engine/git/credential-helper.ts:39, used for the workspace argument at line 52.
findings.fix: Use the existing shellQuote for the workspace and session values when building the follow-up command.

findings.title: Operate skill's code-verb usage block omits `code test` / `code status`, their wait flags and exit codes
findings.body: The skill an agent loads to drive the CLI lists the `code` verbs in a usage block (pull, diff, push, run, promote, import, drift) but not `code test` or `code status`. The prose below now says `status` reads a verdict without queuing, but nothing in the skill shows the syntax. It does not say that `code status` only waits with `--wait`, that `--timeout <s>` bounds the wait, that `code test --no-wait` returns at once, or what exit codes 0/1/2/3 mean. The same block in `claude-plugin/README.md` (around line 239, the "seven verbs" block) also omits both verbs. Impact is limited because `--help` documents the flags and a timeout prints the exact follow-up command.
findings.fix: Add `membrane-operator code test [--tree-version <id>] [--no-wait] [--timeout <s>]` and `membrane-operator code status [--tree-version <id>] [--wait] [--timeout <s>]` to the usage blocks in SKILL.md and README.md, with one sentence giving the exit codes.

findings.title: The docs wrongly say tree tests run locally
findings.body: The reviewer notes this predates the diff. The statement 'Tree tests are the exception — they run locally' contradicts the implementation. codeTest calls RunSourceTreeTestsCommand, and SourceTreeTestRunsService.requestRun enqueues the job through sourceRuns.enqueue with mode 'test', so tests run on a platform worker. An agent that follows the instruction to run them locally never gets the verdict recorded on the version, which the CLI now waits for. The same error appears at SKILL.md:349 and MANUAL.md:335.
findings.fix: Fix all three statements to say that code test runs the tests on a platform worker and reads the verdict from the version, and that fixtures must be part of the tested version.

findings.title: isVerdictReadRefusal classifies any 401/403 or 'sign-in expired' error as an engine that cannot answer the verdict
findings.body:
Observed: `isVerdictReadRefusal` returns true for any 401 or 403 found anywhere in the cause chain, and for any error message matching /sign-in expired/i. `codeStatus` (line 705) and `waitForVersion` (line 665) then print `this engine cannot answer the verdict yet` and exit 2. On the unattached path, `callWithPlatformToken` (operator-client.ts) turns a refused credential into `rejectedCredentialError` ('Membrane rejected the stored credential. Sign in again…', with the 401 as its cause). A failed refresh becomes 'The Membrane sign-in expired and could not be refreshed. Sign in again.' (platform-token.ts:72). Both match the classifier.

What follows: if an operator's login is revoked or its refresh token has expired, `code status` (with or without `--wait`) exits 2 and says the engine cannot answer yet. The real problem is the sign-in, and the 'Sign in again' instruction is dropped. Exit 2 is the 'still pending' code. An agent following the documented contract will keep waiting or polling a verdict that will never arrive, instead of signing in again. `code test` is mostly shielded because the queue call fails first, with the correct message and exit 1. A 403 for a real access problem is hidden the same way. Nothing is re-queued, so the goal's main invariant still holds. The impact is limited to a misleading diagnosis.
findings.fix: Detect an old engine more narrowly, for example by the engine's specific refusal body or by status 403 alone. Let `rejectedCredentialError` and the platform-token 'sign-in expired' error pass through to the generic error path (exit 1 with their own message). Alternatively, keep exit 2 but print the original error's message along with the 'cannot answer' line.

findings.title: The suggested command to run tests drops workspace, session and tree version
findings.body: After `code status --workspace acme --tree-version <id> --wait` on a version with status `untested`, the suggestion is just `membrane-operator code test`. Without an attached session that command fails for lack of `--workspace`. With an attached session it picks the newest version in that session's workspace. If an older version was the one checked, the command tests a different version and may re-queue a run that has already finished.
findings.fix: Add `followUpFlags(options)` and `--tree-version ${version.id}` to the suggested command.

findings.title: `code status --wait --timeout 0` sends its only verdict read after the deadline, cancels it and always reports pending
findings.body: `listVersion` sends `list-source-tree-versions` first and only then calls `readUntilDeadline`, which checks the deadline. `validTimeout` accepts `--timeout 0`, and with it `codeStatus` sets the deadline to the current time (line 694). By the time `readUntilDeadline` runs, `remaining <= 0`, so it cancels the request and fails with VERDICT_READ_TIMED_OUT. `codeStatus` then prints 'still pending after 0 s' and exits 2. The verdict is never read: a passed, failed, untested or missing version is reported as pending. Inside `waitForVersion`, a later page request in a paginated read can likewise be sent after the deadline and cancelled at once. The test at cli.code.verdict.test.ts:255 uses a fetch that never answers, so it cannot tell this apart from correct behaviour.
findings.fix: In `listVersion`, check the deadline before sending each page request, and stop without sending one once the time is spent. Also do the first `codeStatus` read before applying the deadline, or treat `--timeout 0` as one read.

findings.title: Every verdict poll reloads the operator overview for all workspaces
findings.body: Without an attached session, each `listVersion` call goes through `dispatchUnattached`, which reloads /operator/overview for the same `--workspace`. Over the default 90-second wait this adds up to 17 repeat loads after the tests are queued. `getNativeOperatorOverview` rebuilds jobs, inbox and health for every accessible workspace, while polling only needs the `orgWorkspaceId` it has already resolved. The new loop turns a one-off address resolution into a repeated load across all workspaces.
findings.fix: In the shared dispatcher, resolve the workspace once per CLI invocation and keep the selected `orgWorkspaceId`, for example with the existing `resolveWorkspaceTarget`. Keep reading the verdict on every request: the server-side sessionless check keeps the access check current, so permissions and results need no caching.
